One good example of self-sufficiency is growing your own food and making your own clothing. Secondly, self-reliance is the ability to depend on yourself to meet your own requirements. The capacity to rely on one’s own capabilities, and to manage one’s own affairs independetly. The concept of self-sufficiency is basically taken to mean the extent to which a country can satisfy its needs from its own domestic production. The difference between self sufficiency and self-reliance is that self-sufficiency relates to the fulfilment of a nation’s basic needs and proper use of its resources, while self reliance refers to control over decision making, which is the reliance on one’s own judgment, abilities, actions etc. Of all the needs that come under self-sufficiency concept, there are two elements for humans to survive. The first one is food, the second is water. Without food and water, human beings cannot live, but without other services humans can survive. How often does insufficiency of food and water supply come into Somaliland’s concern and consideration? Do Somaliland people hold any view of the extent to which their country can satisfy its food needs from its own domestic production, if global food scarcity or shortage will happen? A nation which fails to address its basic needs, encourage itself to improve its learning skills, arrange its ideas with the future challenges, protect the environment, and initiate projections to invest in getting its needs from its own domestic production is not succeeding. Taking life as it comes is simply never pursuing or predicting aspects of what the future would look like. It is a condition in which preparation for tomorrow is not part of one’s culture (How a society leads its own life). In such condition as this, things seem that going forward is unlikeliy to happen, because viewing the world through rose colored glasses is not the answer to overcoming adversity. What scope people wearing rose colored glasses see, determines what story they see and how they look at the world. Of course, seeing the world through different ways is about securing things, defending things, copying technology in order to save cost, as Chinese people do, controlling things, inventing things, protecting and preserving both renewable and non-renewable resources. It’s mostly a fear-based view of the world that is preparing for future events. This approach is humanly normal. Experience shows that developed countries always base their national strategies for their present and future needs on a fear-based stand to minimize the danger that may arise, for instances, from the occurrence of food scarcity or outbreak of world war, while underdeveloped nations mostly fail to set out strategies that can ensure the means to produce sufficient supply of their needs at the domestic level that will help them find a sweet space at which dependence on what others produce is minimized. The difference between the two approaches is that rich countries mostly utilise their mental mechanics for shaping their life as they want, while poverty-stricken countries neither use their effort nor their mental imagination for trying to tame their lives. The shame on Somaliland societies is that they take life as it comes to them. And taking life as it comes is fundamentally an “anti-change state.” That is, the way Somaliland people lead their lives is not about thinking in regards to the survival of the tribe. Nothing is more bitter than truth. Who among us can deny or disagree the fact that Somaliland has been, and still continues to be the dumping ground for the massively produced foreign goods? This reality goes further from this and probably begs the questions such as:- a) What do Somaliland people control? b) What do they own? c) What do they produce? e) What do they distribute? f) What are the goods that are the produce of Somaliland country that citizens of Somaliland consume? In fact Somaliland people are incredibly consumers and have no special creation. They never ever produced an iota of their basic needs in their entire life. Their food, their cloth, their cars, their tea, their phones, their mobiles, their lotion, their guns, all their white goods, etc, are not their own make, but all are made and controlled by people who don’t look like them, who may retain their goods for their own needs in hard times, who may not even be happy to see Somalis and their likes to survive. Academics had it right when they predicted 50 years ago on the prospect of parasite societies: “Non-productivity reduces output, represses levels of living standard for the masses and engenders strife.” A nation is alive only when it constantly revives and revitalises the way in which it manages its problems, aligns its national vision with what is going on in the world and discards its outdated traditions, habits, rituals and assumptions. Of all the problems Somaliland now faces, lack of local production is the elephant in the room. The old saying which goes to say “necessity is the mother of invention” is applicable to Somaliland. A bleak future is for he who knowingly ignores or escapes from this reality. How should Somaliland state get itself out of foreign-produce dependency? How Somaliland would deal with the lack of local production? The solution is simple. Doing what others did and still do, is the answer as to how Somaliland state can free itself from foreign goods and become self-reliant on its own resources rather than that of others. Apart from light, water and air, food is what makes humans survive; what provides human bodies with what they need to stay alive; what makes human beings grow, active, energetic, move and work; what keeps human bodies healthy and heal themselves; what every human who is born into this world requires. Thus, Somaliland must innovate and intellectuslise its weak policies towards its economic growth and come up with the ability, skill and knowledge to boost domestic yield to satisfy its basic needs from within its own domestic production without foreign produce? In the heat of these alarming moments, Somaliland must make sense of food insufficiency and insecurity, recognize climate change and global warming, protect its environment, dream of a regenerative agriculture, envision a green revolution, create an awareness throughout Somaliland, so that the population must plant sea and herd its animals, and dig the land for farms to produce more and better food. A lesson that sends a powerful message to every country that cannot stand on its feet without foreign aid is that, as a result of the sudden outbreak of the pandemic, Covid-19, rich nations have already started intensive researches on de-globalisation and indeed focused on setting up urgent objectives to develop their local production and measures to stop outsourcing supply chains. Remember, environment does not need humans to survive, but humans need it. So, let us get used to the truth that we are all connected to it and must like to live an environment-centered life. Nothing is more attractive than the reality to acknowledge that a healthy environment is the foundation for a healthy and sustainable society. This hope can only come true when all of us look ahead and always try to use our resources wisely for the sake of our future generations. Who knows what the nature will bring to us tomorrow? What matters to us is to get ready for how we can arrange our ideas with how we can shape the sense of tomorrow. By:JamaFalaag. Hargeisa, Somaliland. jamafalaag@gmail.com

items.title: Duqa Muqdisho oo si weyn loogu soo dhaweeyey dalka Jabuuti
items.description: Muqdisho (RaxanreebOnline) Guddoomiyaha Maamulka Gobolka Banaadir ahna Duqa Muqdisho, Dr. Xasan Maxamed Xuseen (Muungaab), ayaa safar ku tegay magaalada Jabuuti, kaddib markii uu casuumaad rasmi ah ka helay dhiggiisa Caasimadda Jabuut, Said Daoud Mohamed (Saïd Daoud). Wefdiga Duqa Muqdisho, Dr. Xasan Maxamed Xuseen (Muungaab), ayaa waxaa Garoonka Diyaaradaha Caalamiga ah ee Jabuuti-Ambouli, ku soo dhaweeyay Duqa Magaalada Jabuuti, Said Daoud Mohamed (Saïd Daoud), Danjiraha Jamhuuriyadda Jabuuti u fadhiya Soomaaliya, Ambassador Cusmaan Dubad Sugulle, Guddoomiyaha Rugta Ganacsiga Jabuuti, mas’uuliyiin reer Jabuuti ah iyo Diblomaasiyiin ka tirsan Safaaradda Soomaaliya ee dalka Jabuuti. Socdaalkan oo muhiim u ah xoojinta xiriirka walaaltinimo iyo iskaashi ee labada magaalo, ayey mas’uuliyiintu ku lafaguri doonaan sidii loo dhisi lahaa hannaan iskaashi oo joogto ah oo ku saleysan; xoojinta xiriirka ganacsi, dhiirrigelinta maalgashiga iyo khibrad-wadaagga ganacsatada labada dhinac. Wefdiga Guddoomiyaha Maamulka Gobolka Banaadir Duqa Muqdisho, Dr. Xasan Maxamed Xuseen (Muungaab), waxaa ka mid ah, mas’uuliyiin ka tirsan tirsan Rugta Ganacsiga iyo Wershadaha oo uu ku jiro Guddoomiyaha Rugta, Yaasiin Maxamuud Cibaar, Agaasimayaal ka tirsan waaxyaha Maamulka Gobolka Banaadir iyo xubno ka mid ah ganacsatada dalka. The post Duqa Muqdisho oo si weyn loogu soo dhaweeyey dalka Jabuuti appeared first on Raxanreeb Online .

items.title: Madaxweynaha Hirshabelle oo noqday musharaxa rasmiga ah JSP ee doorashada Hirshabelle
items.description: Urur Siyaasadeedka JSP ee Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu hoggaamiyo ayaa si rasmi ah Madaxweynaha Hirshabelle, Cali Cabdullaahi Xuseen (Cali Guudlaawe) ugu xushay inuu noqdo musharaxa uga qaybgelaya doorashada madaxtinimada Hirshabelle. Munaasabad lagu qabtay Xarunta Ururka Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka (JSP) ee Magaalada Muqdisho ayaa Axaddan lagaga dhawaaqay musharaxtinimada Cali Guudlaawe, iyadoona halkaasi lagu guddoonsiiyay kaarka Shimbirta Cagaaran 15 ee astaanta u ah ururka. Tallaabadan ayaa la filayaa inay sii hurin doonto khilaafka siyaasadeed ee ka dhashay, ka dib markii Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh uu habeenkii Khamiista uu Madaxweyne Kuxigeenka Hirshabelle, Yuusuf Axmed Hagar (Yuusuf Dabageed) u sheegay in Villa Somalia ay taageereyso dib-u-doorashada Cali Guudlaawe. Taageerada Villa Somalia ayaa Cali Guudlaawe siineysa guusha doorashada, bacdamaa aanu jirin hannaan daahfuran oo muuqda oo si xor iyo xalaal ah loogu tartamayo doorashada soo socota. Siyaasiyiinta Gobolka Hiiraan ayaa si adag uga horyimid in Cali Guudlaawe uu mar labaad u tartamo xafiiska, iyagoona Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ku eedeeyay in uu jebiyay heshiiskii siyaasadeed ee ilaalinayay in xilka hoggaanka sare ee maamulka uu si meerto ah ugu kala wareego labada gobol ee Hiiraan iyo Shabellaha Dhexe. Cali Guudlaawe ayaa 11-kii bishii November ee sanadkii 2020 loo doortay xilka Madaxweynaha Dowlad Goboleedka Hirshabelle, iyadoona tan iyo xilligaasi uu maamulayay maamulka.

items.title: Sawirro: Xasan Sheekh oo aqoonsaday wasaaradaha ugu wax qabadka badan DF
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Mudane Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa galabta ka qayb-galay bandhigga xiritaanka la-xisaabtanka sannadlaha ah ee Wasaaradaha Xukuumadda, kaas oo lagu soo bandhigay natiijooyinka waxqabadka iyo heerka ay ka gaareen fulinta qorsheyaashii loo dejiyay, gaarista bartilmaameedyadii loo asteeyay iyo gudashada waajibaadkooda sannadka 2026. Inta uu socday kulankan ayaa waxaa la sameeyay qiimeynta waxqabadka wasaaradaha Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, iyadoo la eegayo heerka ay ka gaareen milestones-ka, hawlaha loo qorsheeyay iyo shaqooyinka qabsoomay. Sidoo kale waxaa lasoo bandhigay shanta wasaaradood ee ugu horeeya, kuwaas oo kala ah:- 1. Wasaaradda Maaliyadda 2. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda 3. Wasaaradda Qorshaynta 4. Wasaaradda Hawlaha Guud 5. Wasaaradda Waxbarashada. Intaas kadib Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa intii ay socotay munaasabadda xiritaanka bandhigga xukuumadda Dan-Qaran, wuxuu billado guddoonsiiyay wasaaradaha maaliyadda iyo arrimaha dibadda, kuwaasi oo kaalmaha ugu sarreeya ka galay qiimeyntii la sameeyay sanadkan. Sidoo kale, wuxuu xafiiska ra’iisul wasaaraha ku abaalmariyay hirgelinta hannaanka danabaysan ee la socodka waxqabadka wasaaradaha oo markii ugu horreysay shaashad weyn laga shiday boqoleyda natiijada kasoo baxday qiimeynta wasaarad kasta, iyo waliba sida wasaaradaha kaalmaha u kala galeen. Dhanka kale Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya ayaa ku bogaadiyay xukuumadda dadaalka ay ku bixisay hirgelinta qorsheyaasha dowladda iyo horumarinta adeegyada bulshada, isaga oo adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay la-xisaabtanka hay’adaha iyo howl-wadeennada dowladda, hufnaanta shaqada iyo in si joogto ah loo qiimeeyo natiijooyinka waxqabadka. Waxaa kale oo uu ku booriyay wasiirrada iyo hay’adaha dowladda in natiijooyinka la gaaray ay noqdaan saldhigga lagu sii xoojinayo waxqabadka, laguna saxayo gaabisyada u baahan dardar galinta, si loo xaqiijiyo in qorshayaasha dowladda ay si muuqata uga tarjumaan baahiyaha iyo danta shacabka Soomaaliyeed. La xisaabtankan ayaa looga gol leeyahay in lagu qiimeeyo shaqadii qabsoontay sanadkan, iyada oo lala eegayo ballan-qaadyadii wasiir kasta uu saxiixay, isaga oo xusey in haddii ay soo baxaan caqabado shaqooyinka qaar u qabsoomi waayeen la sixi doono hadafyada iyo bar-hiigsiyada ku qoran jadwalka heshiisyada wasiiradda lala galay.   The post Sawirro: Xasan Sheekh oo aqoonsaday wasaaradaha ugu wax qabadka badan DF appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: JSP oo Cali Guudlaawe U Doortay Musharraxa Hirshabeelle
items.description: Cali Guudlaawe oo Si Rasmi ah u Helay Taageerada Xisbiga JSP ee Doorashada Hirshabeelle MUQDISHO, 13 Sebteembar 2026 — Madaxweynaha Hirshabeelle, Cali Cabdullaahi Xuseen (Cali Guudlaawe) , ayaa loo aqoonsaday musharraxa Xisbiga Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka (JSP) ee doorashada madaxtinimada Hirshabeelle, kaddib kulan ay xubnaha fulinta xisbiga ku yeesheen Muqdisho. Sida lagu sheegay xogta la helay, xubnaha fulinta JSP ayaa cod u qaaday in Guudlaawe noqdo musharraxa xisbiga, waxaana munaasabad ka dhacday xarunta xisbiga lagu guddoonsiiyay kaarka musharraxnimada ee JSP. Ra’iisul Wasaare Ku-xigeenka Labaad ee Soomaaliya, Jibriil Cabdirashiid Xaaji Cabdi, ayaa ka mid ahaa mas’uuliyiintii goob-joogga ka ahaa munaasabadda. Xoghayaha Guud ee JSP, Xuseen Sheekh, ayaa xubnaha xisbiga ugu baaqay inay taageeraan musharraxa loo doortay inuu matalo JSP ee Hirshabeelle.Guudlaawe ayaa isaguna sheegay in marxaladdii xifaaltanka siyaasadeed ay soo dhammaatay, isagoo ku baaqay in la isku soo wada dhowaado lana wada shaqeeyo. Go’aankan ayaa soo afjaraya hubanti-la’aantii ka jirtay su’aasha ahayd cidda JSP u meteli doonta doorashada Hirshabeelle. Guudlaawe ayaa hore, 28–29 Juun 2026, u sheegay inuu yahay musharrax u taagan inuu mar kale hoggaamiyo Hirshabeelle, isla markaana uu ka tirsan yahay JSP, balse xilligaas xisbiga ayaan weli si rasmi ah u shaacin musharraxiisa. Madaxweynaha Hirshabeelle ayaa xilka hayay tan iyo markii loo doortay hoggaanka maamulka bishii Nofeembar 2020. items.title: Somaliland seeks political leverage through Gaza troop offer
items.description: Somaliland seeks political leverage through Gaza troop offer For Somaliland’s leadership, the issue is about demonstrating that it can be a participant in regional and international security arrangements, rather than simply a political entity seeking recognition. Israel’s President Isaac Herzog and Somaliland’s President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi hold up glasses of beverage at the President’s Residence in Jerusalem, June 14, 2026. For Somaliland’s leadership, the issue is about demonstrating that it can be a participant in regional and international security arrangements, rather than simply a political WASHINGTON Somaliland’s initiative to offer up to 2,000 soldiers for deployment to Gaza appears less to be a straightforward military contribution to a proposed international force than an attempt by Hargeisa to leverage its strategic security and geographic position in pursuit of a wider political role. President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi said Somaliland was prepared to provide troops if requested to do so by the United States or Israel, making clear that Hargeisa was not currently volunteering to join the force but would be ready to respond if it received a formal request. The move comes at a sensitive time for Somaliland, which has sought international recognition of its independence since declaring a break from Somalia in 1991. Israel recognised Somaliland in December last year, becoming the first country to formally do so, but the decision has not so far triggered a wider wave of international recognition. That gives any potential Somaliland participation in an international force in Gaza significance beyond the number of troops Hargeisa could provide. For Somaliland’s leadership, the issue is about demonstrating that it can be a participant in regional and international security arrangements, rather than simply a political entity seeking recognition. If its forces were to take part in a multinational mission, Hargeisa could present itself to Western capitals as an actor capable of making a security contribution on an issue of exceptional sensitivity, potentially strengthening its political case with the United States and other countries. The United States is planning an international stabilisation force for Gaza that could eventually number around 20,000 troops. Its proposed tasks include maintaining security, training Palestinian police, facilitating the delivery of humanitarian aid and preventing Hamas from returning to military control of the Gaza Strip. Other countries have agreed or pledged to participate, including Uganda, with around 1,200 personnel, and Morocco, with up to 500, as well as personnel from Albania, Kazakhstan and Kosovo. But Somaliland’s offer differs from those of internationally-recognised states because it carries a sensitive political question: can participation in an international mission become one of the tools for building legitimacy? The presence of forces belonging to a territory that lacks broad international recognition in an international operation could give Hargeisa a level of visibility that traditional diplomatic channels have not provided. At the same time, accepting Somaliland’s participation could provoke objections from Somalia and regional states that remain committed to the country’s territorial unity. The issue is made more sensitive by Somaliland’s location. It lies on the Gulf of Aden, across from Yemen and close to one of the world’s most important maritime routes, making it a focus of growing interest from international and regional powers in recent years.The port of Berbera and its position on the Gulf of Aden give Hargeisa a geopolitical asset that it has sought to turn into security and economic partnerships. Amid instability in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab, that geography has become more important to the United States, Israel and other countries concerned with the security of maritime traffic. Somaliland’s offer of troops therefore cannot be separated from its efforts to develop relations with Washington. Abdullahi has said Israel’s recognition has raised international attention towards Somaliland, even though it has not so far been followed by other recognitions. Washington, meanwhile, faces more complicated calculations. Recognition of Somaliland could damage its relations with Somalia’s federal government, an important partner in combating Al Shabaab and jihadist organisations in the Horn of Africa. Turkey, a prominent military and political ally of Somalia, has also rejected Israel’s recognition of Somaliland and reaffirmed its commitment to Somalia’s territorial integrity. For that reason, accepting Hargeisa’s forces into a Gaza mission could become a political issue extending well beyond the borders of the Strip. Hargeisa is also seeking to avoid linking its initiative to more sensitive regional issues. Abdullahi has denied that there have been discussions with Israel or the United States about using Somaliland’s territory or airspace for operations against Houthi forces in Yemen. He has also denied any agreement to receive Palestinians from Gaza. The denials reflect an awareness of the sensitivity of Somaliland’s position in regional power balances and a desire to prevent its security partnerships from becoming a source of further regional isolation. The central question remains whether the offer to send 2,000 soldiers would actually produce political gains. Participation in an international force could give Somaliland the image of an actor capable of contributing to security, but it would not automatically translate into recognition. Deploying forces beyond its borders would also test the military and political capabilities of its army, which the president estimates at around 25,000 soldiers. Somaliland has not previously contributed troops to African Union operations. Even so, the initiative itself reveals a shift in the way Hargeisa is presenting itself. Rather than limiting its case to a demand for recognition, Somaliland is seeking to portray itself as an actor that can perform a role in regional and international security arrangements. From that perspective, Gaza is more than a distant conflict for Somaliland; it is a potential opportunity to demonstrate that an entity seeking recognition can also offer a political and security contribution in return. Hargeisa is therefore betting on a simple equation: strategic geography can be converted into influence, and influence can be converted into legitimacy. items.title: Maaliyadda iyo Arrimaha Dibadda oo Ku Guuleystay Qiimeynta Waxqabadka
items.description: Xasan Sheekh oo Abaalmarinno Guddoonsiiyay Wasaaradaha Ugu Waxqabadka Sarreeya Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa 13-ka Sebteembar 2026 Muqdisho kaga qaybgalay munaasabad lagu soo bandhigay natiijooyinka qiimeynta waxqabadka wasaaradaha Xukuumadda Federaalka, iyadoo lagu eegayay heerka ay wasaaraduhu uga soo baxeen qorshayaashii iyo bartilmaameedyadii loo dejiyay sannadka 2026. Wasaaradaha Maaliyadda iyo Arrimaha Dibadda ayaa galay kaalmaha ugu sarreeya qiimeynta, waxaana Madaxweynaha uu labada wasaaradood guddoonsiiyay billado lagu aqoonsanayo waxqabadkooda. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa sidoo kale Xafiiska Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ku ammaanay hirgelinta nidaamka danabaysan ee lagu cabbirayo laguna la soconayo waxqabadka wasaaradaha. Qiimeyntan ayaa daba socotay kulan la-xisaabtan ah oo Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre uu 12-ka Sebteembar la yeeshay wasiirrada Xukuumadda DanQaran. Kulankaas waxaa lagu eegayay qorshayaashii ay wasaaraduhu hore u dejisteen, heerka fulintooda iyo caqabadaha hortaagan qorshayaasha aan weli la dhammeystirin. Nidaamka cusub ayaa adeegsanaya hab dijitaal ah oo lagu soo bandhigayo natiijooyinka waxqabadka, taas oo Xamsa uu sheegay inay sahlayso in si joogto ah loola socdo shaqada wasaaradaha. Ra’iisul Wasaaruhu wuxuu sheegay in nidaam online ah uu u saamaxayo inuu si joogto ah ula socdo hawlaha ka socda wasaaradaha. Madaxweynaha ayaa xusay muhiimadda ay leedahay in hay’adaha dowladda ay yeeshaan isla-xisaabtan joogto ah, hufnaan iyo nidaam lagu cabbiro natiijooyinka shaqada, isagoo wasiirrada iyo hay’adaha dowladda ku boorriyay inay ka faa’iideystaan natiijooyinka qiimeynta si loo sii xoojiyo waxqabadka loona saxo meelaha uu gaabis ka jiro. Hannaanka qiimeynta iyo maamulka danabaysan wuxuu sidoo kale ku jiraa istaraatiijiyadda dowladda ee casriyeynta maamulka, taas oo dhigaysa in tiknoolajiyadda loo adeegsado hagaajinta maamulka iyo adeegyada dowladda, iyo la socodka waxqabadka hay’adaha. Qiimeynta ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli Xukuumadda DanQaran ay dib u eegis ku sameyneyso waxqabadkeeda iyo fulinta qorshayaasha qaranka. Golaha Wasiirrada ayaa 10-ka Sebteembar sidoo kale ka hadlay dib-u-eegista waxqabadka Xukuumadda iyo qorshayaasha dowladda. Munaasabadda Muqdisho ayaa sidaas ku muujisay isku dayga dowladda ee ah in waxqabadka wasaaradaha lagu saleeyo cabbirro iyo natiijooyin la qiimeyn karo, iyadoo kaalinta wasaaradaha lagu kala saaray natiijooyinka qiimeynta sannadlaha ah. The post Maaliyadda iyo Arrimaha Dibadda oo Ku Guuleystay Qiimeynta Waxqabadka first appeared on Radio Dalsan .

items.title: Xisbiga Towfiiq ee Sheekh Shaakir ‘oo laga reebay’ doorashada Galmudug
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Guddiga madaxa bannaan ee doorashooyinka qaranka ayaa galabta shaaciyay liiska ururrada siyaasadda ee ka qayb-galaya doorashada ku celiska ah ee maamulka Galmudug, taas oo la qorsheynayo inay dhacdo 30-ka bishaan September ee sannadka 2026-ka. Liiska ururrada la shaaciyay ayaa gaaraya illaa 12 urur, iyada oo ‘lga reebay Xisbiga Towfiiq ee uu hoggaamiyo Sheekh Maxamed Shaakir Cali Xasan’, kaas oo saameyn wayn ku leh gobollada dhexe. Xisbiga Towfiiq ayaa sabab u ahaa go’aankii kasoo baxay Maxkamadda Sare ee Dalka, ee lagu baab’iyay natiijada doorashadii horay uga dhacday Galmudug, kadib markii ay maxkamaddu shaacisay in aan loo maamulin, loona qaban si waafaqsan dastuurka iyo sharciga doorashooyinka dalka. Guddiga doorashooyinka oo warsaxaafadeed soo saaray ayaa xusay in liiska uu soo saaray isaga oo gudanaya waajibaadka shaqo ee loo igmaday, isla-markaana fulinaya jadwalka doorashada ee uu guddigu soo saaray 31 August. Qoraalka ayaa lagu sheegay in 12-ka urur ee la shaaciyay ay soo gudbiyeen musharrixiintooda, loona gartay inay ka qayb-galaan doorashada, taas oo ka dhigan in ururka Towfiiq aanu ka qayb-gelayn doorashada ku celiska ah ee Galmudug. Haddaba, ururrada siyaasadda ee soo gudbiyey liisaska murashaxiinta doorashada isku-sidkan ee Galmudug ayaa waxay kala yihiin: 1-Caddaaladda iyo Midnimadda Tiir 2-Madalsan, 3-Muwaadanniinta Soomaaliyeed 4- Dimuqraadiyadda Soomaaliyeed 5-Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka 6-Dadka Soomaaliyeed 7-Karaama 8-Saab 9-Dan Shacab 10- Sincad 11-Dhalinyarada Talo Qaran 12-Ramaas. Guddigu sidoo kale ku wargeliyay ururrada siyaasadda iyo daneeyeyaasha doorashooyinka isku-sidkan ee Galmudug in ay xirantay soo gudbinta liisaska murashaxiinta ka tartamaya doorashada ku-celiska ah ee Gamuug. Arrintan ayaa kusoo aadeyso, iyada oo maalmihii u dambeeyay xisbiga Towfiiq uu dhaleeceynayay habka uu wax wado guddiga doorashooyinka qaranka, wuxuuna soo jeediyay dhowr jeer oo hore in la dhowro shuruucda doorashooyinka iyo go’aankii dhawaan kasoo baxay Maxkamadda Sare. Liiska ururrada la shaaciyay ayaa gaaraya illaa 12 urur, iyada oo ‘lga reebay Xisbiga Towfiiq ee uu hoggaamiyo Sheekh Maxamed Shaakir Cali Xasan’, kaas oo saameyn wayn ku leh gobollada dhexe. Xisbiga Towfiiq ayaa sabab u ahaa go’aankii kasoo baxay Maxkamadda Sare ee Dalka, ee lagu baab’iyay natiijada doorashadii horay uga dhacday Galmudug, kadib markii ay maxkamaddu shaacisay in aan loo maamulin, loona qaban si waafaqsan dastuurka iyo sharciga doorashooyinka dalka. Guddiga doorashooyinka oo warsaxaafadeed soo saaray ayaa xusay in liiska uu soo saaray isaga oo gudanaya waajibaadka shaqo ee loo igmaday, isla-markaana fulinaya jadwalka doorashada ee uu guddigu soo saaray 31 August. Qoraalka ayaa lagu sheegay in 12-ka urur ee la shaaciyay ay soo gudbiyeen musharrixiintooda, loona gartay inay ka qayb-galaan doorashada, taas oo ka dhigan in ururka Towfiiq aanu ka qayb-gelayn doorashada ku celiska ah ee Galmudug. Haddaba, ururrada siyaasadda ee soo gudbiyey liisaska murashaxiinta doorashada isku-sidkan ee Galmudug ayaa waxay kala yihiin: 1-Caddaaladda iyo Midnimadda Tiir 2-Madalsan, 3-Muwaadanniinta Soomaaliyeed 4- Dimuqraadiyadda Soomaaliyeed 5-Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka 6-Dadka Soomaaliyeed 7-Karaama 8-Saab 9-Dan Shacab 10- Sincad 11-Dhalinyarada Talo Qaran 12-Ramaas. Guddigu sidoo kale ku wargeliyay ururrada siyaasadda iyo daneeyeyaasha doorashooyinka isku-sidkan ee Galmudug in ay xirantay soo gudbinta liisaska murashaxiinta ka tartamaya doorashada ku-celiska ah ee Gamuug. Arrintan ayaa kusoo aadeyso, iyada oo maalmihii u dambeeyay xisbiga Towfiiq uu dhaleeceynayay habka uu wax wado guddiga doorashooyinka qaranka, wuxuuna soo jeediyay dhowr jeer oo hore in la dhowro shuruucda doorashooyinka iyo go’aankii dhawaan kasoo baxay Maxkamadda Sare. Somalis rethink trade routes as Houthis disrupt Red Sea shipping
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Somalia’s business community is seeking alternative shipping routes due to disruptions and security concerns around the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Strait of Hormuz after Iran-backed Houthis captured a key port city and an island, sending thousands of Yemenis fleeing to neighboring Djibouti. Companies have traditionally imported goods from Asia through Gulf countries, such as the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Saudi Arabia. Now, some are trying a more direct approach. “The latest tensions in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, as well as those in the Strait of Hormuz , have negatively impacted us,” said Mohamed Ali Nur, director of Mogadishu Seaport. “But we have also taken measures to avoid that disruption.” Nur said his port has worked with exporters to find alternative routes. “For the first time, we brought a ship carrying sugar directly from Sri Lanka,” Nur said. “This could be a strategy we developed because of these tensions.” Yemen’s internationally recognized government and Saudi Arabia have been battling the Houthis for 12 years. The recent escalation has ended a ceasefire that had largely stopped civil war across Yemen since 2022. Now the number of people from Yemen fleeing the fighting is soaring. On Sunday, the International Organization for Migration said over 85,000 people have been displaced since the beginning of the month. More than 2,000 people have reached Djibouti, which neighbors Somalia, the agency said. At Mogadishu’s busy seaport, cargo ships continue to unload food and other commodities. Somalia is particularly dependent on maritime trade for many of the goods its people use every day. For ordinary Somali consumers, changes in shipping routes can eventually be felt in the markets, where imported food and other goods are sold. Longer or more complicated journeys can mean higher transportation costs and delays in getting products onto store shelves. Capt Ali Jemdi, who is originally from Syria and ships cargoes of sugar, said uncertainty in the region is already creating concerns for ships operating along the routes. “There is some trouble over there because of the war,” he told The Associated Press, referring to the Arabian Gulf and surrounding waters. “The Bab el-Mandeb may also have some issues for the vessel.” He said the instability could make maritime transportation and trade more difficult.

items.title: Ruushka oo Tareen Rakaab Ku Weeraray Xadka Poland
items.description: Boris Johnson oo cambaareeyay weerarka lagu qaaday tareen ku dhow xadka Poland Ra’iisul wasaarihii hore ee Britain, Boris Johnson, ayaa cambaareeyay weerar diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn ee Ruushka lagu qaaday tareen rakaab oo ku sugnaa gudaha Ukraine, meel ku dhow xadka Poland. Weerarka ayaa dhacay 13-ka Sebtembar 2026, gobolka Volyn, halkaas oo diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn ay ku dhufatay tareenka xamuulka jiidayay ee ku socda waddada u dhexeysa Kyiv iyo Warsaw. Shirkadda tareennada Ukraine ee Ukrzaliznytsia ayaa sheegtay in weerarku uusan sababin wax dhimasho ama dhaawac ah, kaddib markii shaqaalaha tareenka hore looga digay khatarta. Boris Johnson, oo ka hadlayay dhacdada bartiisa X, ayaa su’aal geliyay sababta Ruushku u bartilmaameedsaday tareen aan dhaqaaqayn, isaga oo weerarka ku tilmaamay mid aan macno lahayn oo ka mid ah weerarrada maalinlaha ah ee dadka reer Ukraine la kulmaan. Johnson wuxuu sidoo kale ku baaqay in Ukraine la siiyo nidaamyo dheeraad ah oo difaaca cirka ah. Wuxuu sheegay in dalalka reer Galbeedku ay u baahan yihiin inay qaadaan tallaabooyin dheeraad ah si loo yareeyo weerarrada lagu hayo kaabeyaasha rayidka iyo gaadiidka Ukraine. Weerarka tareenka ayaa ku soo beegmay weerarro kale oo ka dhacay agagaarka xadka Ukraine iyo Poland. Reuters waxay sheegtay in diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn ay ku dhufatay gaari xamuul ah meel u dhow isgoyska Yahodyn–Dorohusk, halkaas oo hawlihii xadka si ku-meel-gaar ah loo hakiyay. Masuuliyiinta Poland ayaa sheegay in weerarradu ka dhaceen gudaha Ukraine, isla markaana aan la xaqiijin in hawada Poland la jebiyay. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Ukraine ayaa weerarka ku tilmaantay mid khatar ku ah amniga Yurub, gaar ahaan maadaama uu ka dhacay meel aad ugu dhow xuduudda Midowga Yurub iyo NATO. Masuuliyiinta Ukraine waxay sheegeen in weerarrada noocan ah ay muujinayaan in dagaalku si isa soo taraysa ugu soo dhawaanayo waddamada taageera Kyiv. Dhanka Ruushka, weerarrada ayaa lagu sababeeyay in la bartilmaameedsanayo kaabayaal iyo waddooyin loo adeegsado gaarsiinta qalabka milatari ee reer Galbeedku u diraan Ukraine . Si kastaba, weerarka tareenka rakaabka ayaa walaac ka dhaliyay badbaadada dadka rayidka ah iyo sii socoshada adeegyada gaadiidka ee muhiimka u ah shacabka Ukraine. The post Ruushka oo Tareen Rakaab Ku Weeraray Xadka Poland first appeared on Radio Dalsan .

items.title: Colaaddii Soomaaliya uga Timid Qoriddii Farta Soomaaliga
items.description: Gumaystayaashii reer Yurub, kolka laga soo tago inay Afrika uga tageen colaado ku salaysan is-haysashada xuduudaha dhuleed, waxa kale oo ay uga tageen afafkoodii iyo dhaqamadoodii oo Afrika dacal ilaa dacal ku faafay. Dal kasta oo Afrikaan ah wuxuu qaatay afka gumaystihiisa. Soomaaliya waxaa kala qaybsaday Faransiis, Talyaani, Ingiriis iyo Itoobiyaan. Mid walba wuxuu doonayay, haddii uu meesha ka baxo, in afkiisu noqdo kan ugu muhiimsan qaybtii uu ku talin jiray. Talyaanigu, tusaale ahaan, wuxuu doonayay in af Talyaanigu noqdo afka hay’adaha dawladda iyo kan shacabkaba: afka wax lagu barto, wax lagu qoro, lagu xiriiro, laguna garto Soomaalidii Talyaanigu gumaystay. Ingiriiskuna sidaas oo kale ayuu doonayay. Af Soomaaliga waxaa lala damacsanaa inuu ku ekaado suuqa iyo guryaha oo keliya, sida ay noqdeen afaf badan oo kale oo Afrikaan ah. Soomaaliya waxay noqotay dalka keliya ee Afrikadii la gumaystay ee iska diidday doonitaankii gumaystayaashii. Markii ay xorowdayba, waxay guda gashay sidii ay u heli lahayd far qoran oo Soomaali ah. Dawladihii rayidka iyo dawladdii ciidamaduba mudnaanta koowaad ayay siiyeen qoridda farta af Soomaaliga. Markii ciidanku dalka qabsaday, wuxuu soo saaray bayaan uu ugu magac daray Xaashida Koowaad. Xaashidan waxaa lagu qeexay arrimaha mudnaanta u leh dawladda cusub iyo hiraalkeeda ku aaddan siyaasadaha gudaha iyo dibaddaba. Qodobka afraad wuxuu ahaa in la helo far u gaar ah afkeenna. Soomaalidu marnaba ma sawiran waxa ka dhalan kara markii ay u dhaqaaqeen hindisidda far u gaar ah afkooda. Warbixintii Guddiga Farta Soomaaliga marna laguma soo qaadin wax colaad ah oo laga filan karo qaadashada far u gaar ah af Soomaaliga. Wasiirkii Waxbarashada Soomaaliya ee xilka ugu muddada dheeraa, Aadan Maxamed Cali, ayaa qoray sidan: “Aniga oo haya Wasaaradda Waxbarashada, xafiiskayga waxaa iigu timid gabar Aljeeriya u dhalatay oo ka socotay wargeys ka hadla hiddaha iyo dhaqanka dalka Aljeeriya… Waxay iga waraysatay sidii farta af Soomaaliga loo qoray ee looga soo shaqeeyay, intii ka qaybqaadatay iyo mashaakilkii iyo dhibaatooyinkii innaga hor yimid. Arrimahaas oo dhan markii aan uga sheekeeyay, waxay igu tiri: ‘Marka ugu horraysa, waan idinku hambalyaynayaa.’ Dabadeedna waxay tiri: ‘Ma ogtihiin inaad miino ku dul taagan tihiin?’ Maye, ma ogi baan ku iri. Maxay se tahay miinadu? Waxay tiri: ‘Afrika laba dal baa isku dayay inay qoraan afkooda. Labadaas dal oo kala ah Kiinya iyo Itoobiya oo aad deris tihiin, labaduba kuma guulaysan, kamana gaarin meeshii la doonayay. Wayna shaqayn weyday. Inta kale, marka laga reebo dawladaha Carabta ee Waqooyiga Afrika deggan, waxay ku dhaqmaan afafkii gumaystayaashu kaga tageen dalalkaas: Ingiriis, Faransiis, Beljim iyo Holland/Netherlands. Waddamadaasina ma oggola in luqaddooda laga gudbo, dhaqankooda iyo hiddahoodiina laga tago. Weli waxay ku hawllan yihiin inay ummadda maskaxda ka sii haystaan. Arrintaasi waa miinada aad ku dul taagan tihiin. Sababtuna waa in aad arrimahoodii dhex gasheen dawlado waaweyn oo aqoon, dhaqaale, saamayn, miisaan, ciidan iyo taariikh dheerba leh. Maalin maalmaha ka mid ahna waxay noqon doontaa miino idinku qaraxda.’” Sida ay gabadhaasi tilmaantay, dawladihii awoodda lahaa ee dunida gumaystay ma doonayn in laga xarig furto. Waddamadii ay siiyeen xorriyadda waxay ka rabeen xorriyad magac-u-yaal ah, ee si buuxda ugama tegin. Dhaqan ahaan, hidde ahaan iyo dhaqaale ahaanba waxay rabeen in iyaga loo hoos joogo. Madaxdii Soomaalidu way ku saxnaayeen inay ka fekeraan, u hawlgalaan, ugu dambaynna meelmariyaan qoridda afkeenna. Dhabtii, dadkii hawshaas qabtay abaal aan la gudi karin ayay nagu leeyihiin. Haddii aysan iyagu ahaan lahayn, maanta maan qoreen sadarradan, adiguna maad akhrideen. Intaas oo keliya ma aha ee, waxaa dhici lahayd in Hargeysa af Ingiriisi looga hadlo, Xamarna af Talyaani looga hadlo, sidaasna laba qowmiyadood lagu kala noqdo, gobollada la haysto inta aan la gaarinba. Helitaanka far uu afkeennu leeyahay wuxuu udub u ahaa in afkeennu noqdo kan mideeya ee isku xira Soomaalida oo dhan, kuwii xor ahaa iyo kuwii gumaysiga ku hoos jirayba. Maanta afkeenna qoran ayaa sabab u ah in buugta ka soo baxda meel kasta oo geyiga Soomaaliyeed ka mid ahi si siman looga akhristo dhammaan dhulweynaha Soomaaliyeed, Jabuuti ilaa Siyeelloow. Hubaashii, waxaa laga yaabi lahaa in maanta dalkeennu u qaybsanaan lahaa qayb Ingiriisi ku hadasha iyo qayb Talyaani ku hadasha, dhinac kastana uu xoogga saari lahaa in tiisa la qaato, sidaasna iscolaadin iyo nacayb gacan ka hadal gaara uu ku dhalan lahaa. Ha u qaadan wax fog in la isku layn lahaa Talyaani baa lagu hadli iyo Ingiriis baa lagu hadli, waayo, waxaa jira waddamo Afrikaan ah oo arrintaas colaad uga aloosan tahay. Tusaale ahaan, dalka Kaamiruun waxaa ka socda dagaal u dhexeeya labada dhinac ee u kala hadla Ingiriis iyo Faransiis. Marka dagaalkaas la tilmaamayo, waxaa loogu yeeraa “Anglophone-Francophone War”, oo macnaheedu yahay dagaalka u dhexeeya kuwa af Ingiriiska ku hadla iyo kuwa af Faransiiska ku hadla. Dhinaca kale, madaxdeennii kuma baraarugsanayn dakanooyinka ay galeen. Miinada ay gabadhaas weriyaha ahi garatay, madaxdii hawsha farta loo xilsaaray warba kama hayn. Dagaal aad ogaal ku gashay waxba kaama dhimo. Waad u diyaargarowdaa, guul iyo guuldarrana midkood ayaad ku talagashaa. Midka se aad indho la’aan ku gasho ama gondahaaga ka dhasha, sahal uma haleeshid maarayntiisa. Wasiir Aadan wuxuu kaga jawaabay weydiintii inantu ahayd “Ma xasuusataan inaad miino ku taagan tihiin?” isagoo yiri: “Ma xasuusni, laakiin innagu waan diyaargarownay. Arrintaasi waxay na siinaysaa geesinnimo ah inaynu nahay ummad isku kalsoon, Ilaahayna ku kalsoon. Sidaas baynu ku qornay…” Waa adag tahay in la fahmo sida ay ugu diyaargaroobeen miinada uu qirayo inuusan warba u hayn. Waxay tusaale u tahay sida madaxda Soomaalidu u sahashato dhibaatooyinka dibedda kaga iman kara. Waa arrin kale oo tilmaamaysa sida dhaqankii miyigu saamayn baaxad weyn ugu yeeshay dhaqanka siyaasadeed ee dalka. Dhaqanka Soomaalida kuma jirin basaasnimo iyo raadinta xogta hoose. Colaadaha dhex mari jiray ma ahayn kuwo u baahnaa raadinta xogta hoose, ogaanshaha cududda ciidanka reerka kale ama soo jaajuusidda waxa ay damacsan yihiin. Wax la qariyaba lama aqoon. Dhaqankaasi markii dambe ayuu dawladnimadeennii galay, wuxuuna keenay in madaxda Soomaalidu aysan waxba ka soo qaadin xogaha iyo khataraha lala wadaago, kuwaas oo mararka qaarkood dalka gelin kara halis weyn. Qoridda fartu laba jiho ayay lahayd: mid farsamo iyo mid siyaasadeed. Jihada farsamo waa middii loo saaray guddigii loo yaqaanay Guddiga Farta Soomaaliga, oo mar Muuse Galaal guddoomiye ka ahaa, marna Shariif Saalax. Jihadaas si wacan oo hawlkarnimo leh ayaa looga soo shaqeeyay, halkii la rabayna waa la dhigay. Dhammaan farihii kala duwanaa ee la soo bandhigay ayay falanqeeyeen. Mid kasta wixii caqabad iyo culays ah ee uu lahaa ayay eegeen, ugu dambaynna middii la qumanaatay ayay qaateen. Jihada siyaasadeed waxay ahayd in xukuumadihii jiray xilliyadii farta lagu mashquulsanaa ay ka fekeraan maaraynta iyo u diyaargarowga colaadda ka dhalan karta madaxbannaanida afeed ee loo socday in la gaaro. Taasi ma dhicin. Sida hadalka wasiirka ka muuqata, wax shiddo lehba looma arag. Wasiirkani wuxuu ahaa ninkii mas-uulka ka ahaa meelmarinta farta, dejinta siyaasaddeeda, eegidda caqabadaha iman kara, sida looga gaashaaman karo wixii ka yimaadda iyo sida la isaga difaaci karo wixii soo kordha. In uu jawaabo u diyaariyo su’aalahaas iska daaye, xataa warba kama hayn in farta la qaatay ay abuuri karto cadaawad. Adiga oo aan qoorta dhiiban ayaa laga fekeraa sida aad isaga furdaamin lahayd dhibaatooyinka kaa soo gaari kara arrimo kuu gaar ah oo masiiri ah. Se dhaqankii geeljiruhu sidaas ma aha. Ma aha mid ka cabsada berri iyo cid maqan wax la jira! Kuwa ka carooday ee Soomaalida ku colaadiyay farta ay qoratay ma ahayn reer Galbeed oo keliya. Waddamadii Carbeedna waxay gaareen meel ay reer Galbeedku ka fogaayeen. Wasiirkii Waxbarashada Soomaaliya, Aadan Maxamed Cali, ayaa sheegay inay shir kaga qaybgaleen dalka Marooko. Shirkaas, oo dhex marayay waddamada ku midaysan Jaamacadda Carabta, waxaa Soomaaliya hoggaaminayay Madaxweyne Maxamed Siyaad Barre. Wasiir Aadan wuxuu sheegay inay haaraan iyo hujuun badan kala kulmeen waddamadii Carbeed ee halkaas yimid, kuwaas oo aad uga caraysnaa farta ay Soomaaliya qaadatay. Wuxuu sheegay in Madaxweyne Siyaad uu isaga xilsaaray ka hadalka arrimaha farta iyo taageero u raadinteeda. Wuxuu yiri: “Shirkaas oo Marooko ka dhacay aad ayuu noogu adkaa. Mashruuca aan wadnay wuxuu ahaa adkaynta iyo xoojinta afka Carabiga. Waxaan ku niri: ‘Annaga waddankayaga afka Carabiga waxaa lagu dhigtaa dugsiyada Qur’aanka iyo xalaqooyinka masaajidda. Dadkayagu waxay u badan yihiin xufaadul Qur’aan, diintuna aad ayay noogu dheer tahay. Laakiin duruufo gaar ah ayaa keenay in aan farta Laatiinka qaadanno.’ Arrintaas aad ayaan u difaacnay, waanna qancinnay oo ka dhaadhicinnay waddamadii intooda badnaa, marka laga reebo waddamada Khaliijka Carabta. items.fullContent: Gumaystayaashii reer Yurub, kolka laga soo tago inay Afrika uga tageen colaado ku salaysan is-haysashada xuduudaha dhuleed, waxa kale oo ay uga tageen afafkoodii iyo dhaqamadoodii oo Afrika dacal ilaa dacal ku faafay. Dal kasta oo Afrikaan ah wuxuu qaatay afka gumaystihiisa. Soomaaliya waxaa kala qaybsaday Faransiis, Talyaani, Ingiriis iyo Itoobiyaan. Mid walba wuxuu doonayay, haddii uu meesha ka baxo, in afkiisu noqdo kan ugu muhiimsan qaybtii uu ku talin jiray. Talyaanigu, tusaale ahaan, wuxuu doonayay in af Talyaanigu noqdo afka hay’adaha dawladda iyo kan shacabkaba: afka wax lagu barto, wax lagu qoro, lagu xiriiro, laguna garto Soomaalidii Talyaanigu gumaystay. Ingiriiskuna sidaas oo kale ayuu doonayay. Af Soomaaliga waxaa lala damacsanaa inuu ku ekaado suuqa iyo guryaha oo keliya, sida ay noqdeen afaf badan oo kale oo Afrikaan ah. Soomaaliya waxay noqotay dalka keliya ee Afrikadii la gumaystay ee iska diidday doonitaankii gumaystayaashii. Markii ay xorowdayba, waxay guda gashay sidii ay u heli lahayd far qoran oo Soomaali ah. Dawladihii rayidka iyo dawladdii ciidamaduba mudnaanta koowaad ayay siiyeen qoridda farta af Soomaaliga. Markii ciidanku dalka qabsaday, wuxuu soo saaray bayaan uu ugu magac daray Xaashida Koowaad. Xaashidan waxaa lagu qeexay arrimaha mudnaanta u leh dawladda cusub iyo hiraalkeeda ku aaddan siyaasadaha gudaha iyo dibaddaba. Qodobka afraad wuxuu ahaa in la helo far u gaar ah afkeenna. Soomaalidu marnaba ma sawiran waxa ka dhalan kara markii ay u dhaqaaqeen hindisidda far u gaar ah afkooda. Warbixintii Guddiga Farta Soomaaliga marna laguma soo qaadin wax colaad ah oo laga filan karo qaadashada far u gaar ah af Soomaaliga. Wasiirkii Waxbarashada Soomaaliya ee xilka ugu muddada dheeraa, Aadan Maxamed Cali, ayaa qoray sidan: “Aniga oo haya Wasaaradda Waxbarashada, xafiiskayga waxaa iigu timid gabar Aljeeriya u dhalatay oo ka socotay wargeys ka hadla hiddaha iyo dhaqanka dalka Aljeeriya… Waxay iga waraysatay sidii farta af Soomaaliga loo qoray ee looga soo shaqeeyay, intii ka qaybqaadatay iyo mashaakilkii iyo dhibaatooyinkii innaga hor yimid. Arrimahaas oo dhan markii aan uga sheekeeyay, waxay igu tiri: ‘Marka ugu horraysa, waan idinku hambalyaynayaa.’ Dabadeedna waxay tiri: ‘Ma ogtihiin inaad miino ku dul taagan tihiin?’ Maye, ma ogi baan ku iri. Maxay se tahay miinadu? Waxay tiri: ‘Afrika laba dal baa isku dayay inay qoraan afkooda. Labadaas dal oo kala ah Kiinya iyo Itoobiya oo aad deris tihiin, labaduba kuma guulaysan, kamana gaarin meeshii la doonayay. Wayna shaqayn weyday. Inta kale, marka laga reebo dawladaha Carabta ee Waqooyiga Afrika deggan, waxay ku dhaqmaan afafkii gumaystayaashu kaga tageen dalalkaas: Ingiriis, Faransiis, Beljim iyo Holland/Netherlands. Waddamadaasina ma oggola in luqaddooda laga gudbo, dhaqankooda iyo hiddahoodiina laga tago. Weli waxay ku hawllan yihiin inay ummadda maskaxda ka sii haystaan. Arrintaasi waa miinada aad ku dul taagan tihiin. Sababtuna waa in aad arrimahoodii dhex gasheen dawlado waaweyn oo aqoon, dhaqaale, saamayn, miisaan, ciidan iyo taariikh dheerba leh. Maalin maalmaha ka mid ahna waxay noqon doontaa miino idinku qaraxda.’” Sida ay gabadhaasi tilmaantay, dawladihii awoodda lahaa ee dunida gumaystay ma doonayn in laga xarig furto. Waddamadii ay siiyeen xorriyadda waxay ka rabeen xorriyad magac-u-yaal ah, ee si buuxda ugama tegin. Dhaqan ahaan, hidde ahaan iyo dhaqaale ahaanba waxay rabeen in iyaga loo hoos joogo. Madaxdii Soomaalidu way ku saxnaayeen inay ka fekeraan, u hawlgalaan, ugu dambaynna meelmariyaan qoridda afkeenna. Dhabtii, dadkii hawshaas qabtay abaal aan la gudi karin ayay nagu leeyihiin. Haddii aysan iyagu ahaan lahayn, maanta maan qoreen sadarradan, adiguna maad akhrideen. Intaas oo keliya ma aha ee, waxaa dhici lahayd in Hargeysa af Ingiriisi looga hadlo, Xamarna af Talyaani looga hadlo, sidaasna laba qowmiyadood lagu kala noqdo, gobollada la haysto inta aan la gaarinba. Helitaanka far uu afkeennu leeyahay wuxuu udub u ahaa in afkeennu noqdo kan mideeya ee isku xira Soomaalida oo dhan, kuwii xor ahaa iyo kuwii gumaysiga ku hoos jirayba. Maanta afkeenna qoran ayaa sabab u ah in buugta ka soo baxda meel kasta oo geyiga Soomaaliyeed ka mid ahi si siman looga akhristo dhammaan dhulweynaha Soomaaliyeed, Jabuuti ilaa Siyeelloow. Hubaashii, waxaa laga yaabi lahaa in maanta dalkeennu u qaybsanaan lahaa qayb Ingiriisi ku hadasha iyo qayb Talyaani ku hadasha, dhinac kastana uu xoogga saari lahaa in tiisa la qaato, sidaasna iscolaadin iyo nacayb gacan ka hadal gaara uu ku dhalan lahaa. Ha u qaadan wax fog in la isku layn lahaa Talyaani baa lagu hadli iyo Ingiriis baa lagu hadli, waayo, waxaa jira waddamo Afrikaan ah oo arrintaas colaad uga aloosan tahay. Tusaale ahaan, dalka Kaamiruun waxaa ka socda dagaal u dhexeeya labada dhinac ee u kala hadla Ingiriis iyo Faransiis. Marka dagaalkaas la tilmaamayo, waxaa loogu yeeraa “Anglophone-Francophone War”, oo macnaheedu yahay dagaalka u dhexeeya kuwa af Ingiriiska ku hadla iyo kuwa af Faransiiska ku hadla. Dhinaca kale, madaxdeennii kuma baraarugsanayn dakanooyinka ay galeen. Miinada ay gabadhaas weriyaha ahi garatay, madaxdii hawsha farta loo xilsaaray warba kama hayn. Dagaal aad ogaal ku gashay waxba kaama dhimo. Waad u diyaargarowdaa, guul iyo guuldarrana midkood ayaad ku talagashaa. Midka se aad indho la’aan ku gasho ama gondahaaga ka dhasha, sahal uma haleeshid maarayntiisa. Wasiir Aadan wuxuu kaga jawaabay weydiintii inantu ahayd “Ma xasuusataan inaad miino ku taagan tihiin?” isagoo yiri: “Ma xasuusni, laakiin innagu waan diyaargarownay. Arrintaasi waxay na siinaysaa geesinnimo ah inaynu nahay ummad isku kalsoon, Ilaahayna ku kalsoon. items.title: Somalia: Mogadishu could fall without AU troops, says ex-minister
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Mogadishu “cannot be defended” if African Union troops withdraw from the country by December, Somalia’s former Minister of Planning Abdirahman Aynte said, adding that US diplomats have told Somali officials Washington will not reverse its decision to end logistics funding for the African Union peacekeeping mission regardless of the outcome of ongoing political talks. The warning comes against a backdrop of confirmed fact: on July 1, the United States formally notified the African Union it would stop funding the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) after December 31, 2026 — the logistics mechanism that supplies AUSSOM with food, fuel, transport, medical care and communications. Washington has said it would not block the UN Security Council from renewing AUSSOM’s mandate itself, but would block any UN logistical or operational support for the mission — a distinction analysts say leaves the roughly 12,000-strong force operationally unsustainable without a replacement funding arrangement. Aynte, who served as Somalia’s minister of planning and international cooperation from 2015 to 2017 under President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s first administration and previously worked as a journalist for the BBC, Voice of America and Al Jazeera English, said that during recent talks between the political opposition and the Somali government, US diplomats mediating the discussions delivered that message directly to Somali officials. According to Aynte, the diplomats said that if Somalia’s rival political factions reached a settlement, Washington would not obstruct other countries from stepping in to fund AUSSOM’s logistics after the US withdrawal. But if no settlement was reached, he said, the diplomats warned that Washington would actively work to prevent other nations from filling that gap. Aynte said AUSSOM troops cannot remain in the country without logistical support, and that Mogadishu would fall if the mission’s forces withdraw from the country. He said this assessment is not merely his own opinion but one shared by President Mohamud himself. His account aligns with the public record of a summit Mohamud attended in Kampala on July 31, where leaders of countries contributing troops to AUSSOM concluded three days of talks by agreeing to seek 18 to 24 months of uninterrupted international support for the mission, and endorsed a phased, coordinated withdrawal. Aynte said Mohamud personally appealed to the troop-contributing countries at that summit to keep their forces in Somalia even after logistics funding ends. “If the Somali government believes it can defend Mogadishu, why would it ask AUSSOM’s troop-contributing countries to keep their forces in the country?” Aynte asked. He further said that if Somali leaders fail to reach a political agreement, the international community would be indifferent to who governs the country, and would not object even if Al-Shabaab took power, provided the group renounced its Al-Qaeda affiliation and expelled foreign fighters. “I swear, if al-Shabaab accepts those two conditions and respects the borders of Kenya and Ethiopia, the international community will hand over the country’s security to the group the very next morning,” Aynte said. His remarks follow weeks of public statements from Somali officials seeking to ease fears of a government collapse in the event of an AUSSOM withdrawal. President Mohamud, the Security Minister and the National Security Advisor have all said Somalia’s security forces are fully capable of defending the country and assuming security responsibilities if AUSSOM departs. Mohamud went further on August 16, telling a graduation ceremony for roughly 3,000 newly trained Somali National Army soldiers in Galmudug that the country no longer needed foreign peacekeepers and that it was time to send them home “with a bunch of flowers.” Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: Turkish Flag Burned in Puntland and Jubaland as Anger Grows Over Ankara’s Role in Somalia
items.description: EYL (WDN) — Anger over Turkey’s growing military and political role in Somalia has spilled into the streets, with protesters in Puntland burning the Turkish flag and similar displays of hostility reported in Jubaland, reflecting growing opposition to what critics describe as Ankara’s increasingly close alignment with the Federal Government in Mogadishu. In a coastal area near Eyl, Puntland, demonstrators burned the Turkish flag during a protest over the reported deaths of 13 people described by local residents as fishermen. The protesters accused Turkish forces of killing the men and demanded compensation for their families and for property they said was lost in the incident. Local Puntland officials, including Nugaal Governor Abdulkadir Osman Samatar (Food-cade), Deputy Governor Mukhtar Farah Jeer and Gen. Muxyadin Ahmed Muse, participated in the demonstration. The protesters warned that further demonstrations would follow unless Ankara addresses their demands. The incident is particularly significant because similar anti-Turkish sentiments have also surfaced in Jubaland, where the Turkish flag has reportedly been burned amid growing criticism of Ankara’s relationship with Mogadishu. Taken together, the demonstrations suggest that the controversy surrounding Turkey is developing beyond a single maritime incident and becoming part of a wider political debate over foreign military influence and Somalia’s internal political divisions. Turkish Military Role Under Scrutiny The Eyl protest follows conflicting accounts surrounding the reported deaths of 13 fisher men off the Nugaal coast. The Federal Government has described the men as suspected pirates killed during an operation involving Turkish naval forces. Local protesters, however, insist that the victims were fishermen. The circumstances surrounding the deaths, including the identities of those killed and the precise nature of the operation, is verified by the Puntland State. But the dispute has already intensified public scrutiny of Turkey’s military presence in Somali waters, particularly in Puntland, where relations with the Federal Government remain politically sensitive. From Security Partnership to Political Controversy Turkey has become one of Mogadishu’s most important international partners, providing military training, equipment and broader security assistance to Somali forces. Yet Ankara’s relationship with the Federal Government is increasingly being viewed through the lens of Somalia’s political divisions. Critics accuse Turkey of becoming too closely aligned with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration and argue that Turkish military support risks becoming entangled in disputes between Mogadishu and rival Federal Member States. They have also alleged that Turkish-supplied weapons and military capabilities have been used against political opponents and forces aligned with regional administrations. Those are allegations require independent verification. But the perception is becoming politically significant. For critics of Mogadishu, the concern is no longer simply whether Turkey is helping Somalia fight Al-Shabaab and other security threats. It is whether a foreign military power is becoming an actor in Somalia’s internal political struggle. Why Jubaland Matters The reported burning of the Turkish flag in Jubaland adds an important dimension to the controversy. Jubaland has been involved in repeated political and security disputes with the Federal Government, particularly over control of security forces, federal authority and political influence in the region. If anti-Turkish demonstrations emerge in both Puntland and Jubaland, that could indicate that opposition to Ankara’s role is increasingly connected to broader resistance to Mogadishu’s political strategy. The issue is therefore larger than Turkey itself. It concerns whether foreign military partnerships are strengthening Somalia’s national institutions—or unintentionally strengthening one political center against its rivals. A Growing Trust Problem The burning of the Turkish flag in Puntland and Jubaland is consequently more than an expression of anger over individual incidents. It reflects a growing trust problem. Turkey may regard its relationship with Somalia as a strategic partnership based on security, development and mutual interests. But if communities in different parts of Somalia increasingly perceive Turkish military assistance as support for the Federal Government’s political agenda, Ankara risks losing the image of neutrality that such a partnership requires. A foreign partner can provide weapons, training and military assistance without becoming politically neutral in the eyes of the public. Perception matters—particularly in a country where political legitimacy is already deeply contested. The Questions Ankara and Mogadishu Must Answer The latest controversy raises questions that deserve clear answers. Who authorized the operation off the Nugaal coast?  What exactly happened to the 13 men?   Were they armed pirates posing an immediate threat, or fishermen caught up in a disputed military operation? Was the operation conducted under a clearly defined Somali-Turkish legal framework? And what safeguards exist to ensure that Turkish-supplied weapons and military capabilities are not used in Somalia’s internal political conflicts? These questions matter because Somalia has legitimate security needs and requires international assistance. But that assistance must be transparent, accountable and governed by clear rules. The Wider Political Stakes The controversy comes as relations between Mogadishu and several Federal Member States remain strained over elections, constitutional amendments, security arrangements and the distribution of political authority. Turkey’s expanding military relationship with the Federal Government carries unavoidable political implications. For Puntland, Jubaland and other critics of Mogadishu, Ankara risks being seen not simply as a security partner but as a foreign power whose military support strengthens the federal government while Somalia’s political factions are confronting one another. Whether that perception is justified will ultimately depend on evidence, transparency and Turkey’s own conduct. But the political warning is already visible. When the Turkish flag is being burned in different parts of Somalia, Ankara should recognize that its Somalia policy is no longer being judged solely by the security assistance it provides. It is increasingly being judged by whose political power that assistance is perceived to strengthen. Turkey’s partnership with Somalia remains strategically important. But if Ankara wants that partnership to endure, it must convince Somalis that its military relationship is with Somalia as a country—not with one political faction within it. items.title: HirShabelle oo lagu kala baxay iyo Xasan Sheekh oo Guudlaawe siiyay kaarka JSP
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Waxaa si rasmi ah galabta loo soo afjaray dooddii muddada dheer ka taagnayd cidda noqonaysa musharraxa Xisbiga JSP ee doorashada maamulka HirShabelle, iyadoo ugu dambeyn kaarka musharraxnimada la siiyay Madaxweyne Cali Guudlaawe, kaas oo mar kale u taagan xilka madaxtinnimada Dowlad-goboleedka HirShabelle. Go’aankan ayaa ka dambeeyay kadib markii maanta xarunta dhexe ee Ururka Caddaaladda iyo Wdaajirka (JSP) uu ku qabsoomay kulanka guddiga fulinta kaas oo uu shir guddoomiyay xoghayaha guud ee JSP, Dr. Xuseen Sheekh Maxamuud. Kulanka oo ahaa mid xasaasi ayaa diiradda lagu saaray u diyaar-garowga doorashada soo socota ee Dowlad Goboleedka HirShabelle, waxaana guddiga fulinta uu go’aamiyay in Madaxweyne Cali Cabdullaahi Xuseen uu noqdo musharraxa rasmiga ah ee xisbiga ku metalaya doorashada HirShabelle. “Guddiga fulintu waxa uu si aqlabiyad leh ugu go’aamiyay in Mudane Cali Cabdullaahi Xuseen uu noqdo musharraxa rasmiga ah ee Urur Siyaasadeedka Caddaaladda iyo Wadajirka (JSP) ugu taagnaan doono doorashada hoggaamiyaha Dowlad Goboleedka HirShabelle,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraal kasoo baxay Ururka Caddaaladda iyo Wdaajirka (JSP) ee uu hoggaamiyo Xasan Sheekh. Go’aankan oo aad loo hadal-hayay, lana filayay ayaa xiisad horleh ka abuuray HirShabelle, iyada oo ay ka hor yimaadeen siyaasiyiinta reer Hiiraan oo markii horeba tabasho ka qabay dhismaha Maamul-goboleedka HirShabelle. Madaxweyne ku xigeenka HirShabelle, Yuusuf Axmed Hagar (Dabageed) oo kasoo jeeda beesha Xawaadle ee degta Hiiraan ayaa horay u sheegay in Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh uu si cad ugu sheegay in xilka maamulka HirShabelle uu u wado Cali Guudlaawe, taas oo maanta rumowday, maadaama la siiyay kaarka JSP, kuna metali doono doorashada guud ee HirShabelle. Madaxweyne ku-xigeenka dowlad-goboleedka HirShabelle, Yuusuf Axmed Hagar (Dabageed) ayaa sidoo kale Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ku eedeeyay inuu uga baxay ballan siyaasadeed oo uu la galay. Dabageed oo tilmaamay in Madaxweynaha ay horay ugu heshiiyeen, uguna ballanqaaday inuu hoggaanka HirShabelle isaga siiyo ayaa sheegay in Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu hadda waxba kama jiraan kasoo qaaday ballankaas, uuna kursiga siiyay Madaxweyne Cali Guudlaawe oo markale isa soo sharraxay. “Madaxweynihii xalay waxaan kala kulmay wax uu nin fiyow oo ehel iyo mas’uul ah oo Madaxweyne Soomaaliyeed uu dhihi karo aanan u qabin. Ballankii reer abtigay waa ka baxay ee kursiga iiga doon, oo iga nabad doonee ayuu igu dhahay,” ayuu yiri Dabageed. Waxa uu intaas kusii daray: “Intee geyni baa dhahay haddaan kasoo helo oo doono. Cali Guudlaawe ayaa siin buu yiri. Madaxweynaha uma badin ee waxaan dhahay arrintaas kama nabad dooneyn karo, nin hadda iga dambeeya oo ka nabaddooneyn kara inuu jiro ilama aha. Raalli ahow, wax aan ka filanayay oo reer abtiga ka sugayeen ma aha, oo xaqoodi ma aha.”   The post HirShabelle oo lagu kala baxay iyo Xasan Sheekh oo Guudlaawe siiyay kaarka JSP appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Hirshabelle Drifts Away as Sr. Figures Warn of Another Somali Government
items.description: Jowhar (WDN) — Somalia’s federal system is facing another potentially destabilizing political rupture after senior Hirshabelle figures openly challenged President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s handling of the regional leadership and electoral process. Hirshabelle Vice President Yusuf Hagar (Dabageed) and former National Intelligence and Security Agency chief and lawmaker Abdullahi Mohamed (Sanbalooshe) have critically come against the president’s proposed plan for Hirshabelle election. Sanbaloolshe sharply criticized the president’s decision to support Ali Gudlawe remaining in power despite what Sanbaloolshe said was opposition from the Hawadle community. Sanbaloolshe warned that if Hassan Sheikh is satisfied to control Jowhar and Balcad without broader political agreement, Somalis could ultimately establish another government. “If Hassan Sheikh and Gudlawe are satisfied with Jowhar and Balcad, Somalis will establish another government,” Sanbaloolshe said. The warning comes as tensions over Hirshabelle’s political future increasingly expose the limits of Mogadishu’s influence outside the capital. Dabageed: No Election Without Political Agreement Hirshabelle Vice President Yusuf Hagar Dabageed has separately challenged the proposed electoral process, saying no election should take place in Hiiraan without a prior political agreement acceptable to the relevant stakeholders. Abdullahi Sanbalooshe and Yusuf Dabageed He said the requirement applied even to individual villages, warning that those who attempt to conduct elections without political consensus would bear responsibility for any consequences. Dabageed’s remarks highlight the depth of disagreement over how Hirshabelle’s next political leadership should be chosen. He also called on the Hawadle community to collectively consider its political future, saying discussions should involve members of the community both inside Somalia and abroad. Hirshabelle Joins a Wider Federal Crisis The dispute is unfolding as relations between Mogadishu and several Federal Member States remain strained. Puntland and Jubaland have adopted increasingly independent positions in their disputes with the Federal Government, while Southwest State has faced its own political and security confrontation with Mogadishu. Hirshabelle now appears to be moving toward a similar standoff. The emerging pattern points to a broader problem for the Federal Government: political authority cannot easily be imposed from Mogadishu when regional leaders and influential communities do not accept the process through which that authority is exercised. The risk is therefore not necessarily an immediate formal breakup of Somalia. It is the gradual development of de facto political fragmentation, with regional administrations increasingly making decisions independently of the center. The Test for Hassan Sheikh For President Hassan Sheikh, the choice is becoming increasingly difficult. Attempting to impose a preferred political outcome could intensify resistance in Hirshabelle. But failing to reach agreement with regional stakeholders could further weaken Mogadishu’s influence. The most viable path is political negotiation, not coercion as coercion will sure fail like Baidoa. That means clarifying the constitutional basis of the electoral process, addressing the concerns of Hiiraan and other stakeholders, and creating a framework that competing political actors can accept. Dabageed and Sanbaloolshe’s warning should therefore be viewed as more than another political statement. It reflects a growing challenge to the Federal Government’s ability to maintain a unified political system when regional actors increasingly insist on determining their own political arrangements. If Hirshabelle follows Puntland, Jubaland in distancing itself from Mogadishu, Somalia’s federal crisis will no longer be a series of separate disputes. It will become a national question about whether the current federal model can survive without a new political settlement . The warning comes as tensions over Hirshabelle’s political future increasingly expose the limits of Mogadishu’s influence outside the capital. Dabageed: No Election Without Political Agreement Hirshabelle Vice President Yusuf Hagar Dabageed has separately challenged the proposed electoral process, saying no election should take place in Hiiraan without a prior political agreement acceptable to the relevant stakeholders. Abdullahi Sanbalooshe and Yusuf Dabageed He said the requirement applied even to individual villages, warning that those who attempt to conduct elections without political consensus would bear responsibility for any consequences. Dabageed’s remarks highlight the depth of disagreement over how Hirshabelle’s next political leadership should be chosen. He also called on the Hawadle community to collectively consider its political future, saying discussions should involve members of the community both inside Somalia and abroad. Hirshabelle Joins a Wider Federal Crisis The dispute is unfolding as relations between Mogadishu and several Federal Member States remain strained. Puntland and Jubaland have adopted increasingly independent positions in their disputes with the Federal Government, while Southwest State has faced its own political and security confrontation with Mogadishu. Hirshabelle now appears to be moving toward a similar standoff. The emerging pattern points to a broader problem for the Federal Government: political authority cannot easily be imposed from Mogadishu when regional leaders and influential communities do not accept the process through which that authority is exercised. The risk is therefore not necessarily an immediate formal breakup of Somalia. It is the gradual development of de facto political fragmentation, with regional administrations increasingly making decisions independently of the center. The Test for Hassan Sheikh For President Hassan Sheikh, the choice is becoming increasingly difficult. Attempting to impose a preferred political outcome could intensify resistance in Hirshabelle. But failing to reach agreement with regional stakeholders could further weaken Mogadishu’s influence. The most viable path is political negotiation, not coercion as coercion will sure fail like Baidoa. That means clarifying the constitutional basis of the electoral process, addressing the concerns of Hiiraan and other stakeholders, and creating a framework that competing political actors can accept. Dabageed and Sanbaloolshe’s warning should therefore be viewed as more than another political statement. It reflects a growing challenge to the Federal Government’s ability to maintain a unified political system when regional actors increasingly insist on determining their own political arrangements. If Hirshabelle follows Puntland, Jubaland in distancing itself from Mogadishu, Somalia’s federal crisis will no longer be a series of separate disputes. It will become a national question about whether the current federal model can survive without a new political settlement . items.title: Galkacyo Killing Renews Calls to End Somalia’s Cycle of Clan Revenge
items.description: Galkacyo (WDN) — Government officials in Mudug are conducting efforts to identify and arrest those responsible for the killing of Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Haamay, who was shot dead in Galkacyo several days ago, as the latest killing raises renewed fears of retaliatory violence. Regional officials said security forces are intensifying investigations and operations to locate the suspected perpetrators and establish both their identities and the motive behind the killing. The death has caused widespread grief and concern in Galkacyo, with residents and community leaders calling for the perpetrators to be brought before the courts and held accountable under the law. But the killing also highlights a much larger problem that Somalia cannot continue to ignore: the endless cycle in which one killing is followed by revenge, another death, another retaliation and eventually another round of clan violence. The immediate responsibility lies with the security authorities. Rather than allowing communities to pursue their own form of justice, the government must demonstrate that it has the capacity and determination to identify those responsible, arrest them and ensure that they face a transparent judicial process. A failure to do so creates a dangerous vacuum. When families and communities believe that the state cannot deliver justice, they may increasingly turn to traditional retaliation. What begins as an individual murder can then become a collective dispute involving entire clans. That is how isolated criminal acts become prolonged cycles of violence. Justice, Not Revenge Authorities have urged residents to provide information that could assist the investigation while warning against retaliatory actions. That message is critical. The murder of Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Haamay should not become the justification for another killing. If the perpetrators are identified, responsibility must remain individual. Innocent members of their families or communities should not be treated as responsible for a crime they did not commit. The principle is simple: a murder must be answered with justice, not another murder. A Test of State Authority The case presents the Mudug authorities with an important test: whether the government can ensure that those responsible for the killing are identified, arrested and prosecuted through lawful institutions. That requires effective investigation, reliable intelligence, cooperation from local communities and a judiciary capable of delivering credible justice. Community leaders also have a responsibility to discourage inflammatory rhetoric and prevent grief from turning into collective retaliation. The killing of Sheikh Ahmed Yusuf Haamay should end with an investigation and a court case—not another death. For Somalia to escape the cycle of clan revenge, responsibility for justice must rest with the state, while communities reject collective punishment and allow individual perpetrators to answer for their crimes. items.title: Eritrea Accuses UAE of ‘Port Colonialism’ as Abu Dhabi’s Regional Footprint Expands
items.description: Asmara (WDN) — Eritrea has accused the United Arab Emirates of pursuing what it described as “port colonialism” in Africa, warning that Abu Dhabi’s expanding commercial, political and military footprint along the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and East Africa deserves far greater scrutiny. Eritrea’s Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said the UAE’s growing presence in regional ports should not be viewed simply as a commercial enterprise. He argued that African governments should examine the broader strategic consequences of allowing a foreign power to establish long-term influence over critical maritime infrastructure. The criticism comes as UAE-linked companies, particularly DP World and AD Ports Group, have expanded their involvement in ports across Africa and the wider Red Sea region. Their interests include Berbera in Somaliland, Bosaso in Puntland, as well as port projects in countries including Egypt and Tanzania. For Eritrea, the concern is that commercial port investments can eventually create political and military leverage. From Ports to Power The UAE’s regional strategy illustrates how ports have become instruments of geopolitical influence. Control, management or long-term investment in strategically located ports can provide far more than commercial revenue. It can create logistical access, political relationships and influence over maritime trade routes that connect the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean. Dubai port, UAE That is why Eritrea has rejected proposals for a permanent UAE military presence on the Dahlak Islands. Abu Dhabi previously maintained a military facility at Assab, which it used during its involvement in the Yemen war. Asmara now says it does not want Eritrean territory or ports transformed into permanent foreign military platforms. The distinction between commercial investment and strategic influence has consequently become increasingly difficult to ignore. The UAE’s Troubled Regional Record The Eritrean warning also opens a much broader debate about the UAE’s role in conflict zones across the region and Africa. Critics of Abu Dhabi’s foreign policy point to its involvement, directly or indirectly, in conflicts and political struggles in Yemen, Libya and Sudan, among other theaters. They argue that UAE-backed actors and military relationships have frequently intensified existing rivalries rather than producing durable political settlements. The consequences have been particularly devastating in countries already suffering from institutional collapse and armed conflict. In Yemen, the UAE became a major participant in the Saudi-led military intervention and supported local forces pursuing their own political and territorial agendas. In Libya, Abu Dhabi has been accused of providing military and political backing to forces opposed to the internationally recognized authorities, contributing to the country’s complex fragmentation. In Sudan, the UAE has faced persistent allegations of supporting the Rapid Support Forces, accusations Abu Dhabi has repeatedly denied. The devastating war that erupted in 2023 has nevertheless transformed Sudan into one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises. These cases do not prove that the UAE alone caused the conflicts. Local political failures, rival regional powers, armed groups and international actors have all played significant roles. But they raise a legitimate question about Abu Dhabi’s model of foreign engagement: Does the UAE’s pursuit of strategic influence help stabilize fragile states—or does it deepen conflicts by empowering selected local actors? Eritrea Watches Ethiopia and Somalia Asmara is particularly concerned about the UAE’s growing relationship with Ethiopia, especially as Addis Ababa seeks reliable access to the sea. Eritrea also views with suspicion the strengthening relationship between Israel and Somaliland. From Asmara’s perspective, the convergence of UAE, Ethiopian, Israeli and Somaliland interests around ports and maritime access could fundamentally alter the strategic balance along the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. The concern is not simply who owns or manages a port. It is who ultimately gains strategic influence over the surrounding territory, maritime routes and security arrangements. The Red Sea and Horn of Africa are rapidly becoming a major arena of international competition. The UAE is only one of several external powers seeking influence. Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Iran, Israel, the United States, China and European states all have strategic interests in the region. Ports have consequently become much more than infrastructure projects. They are increasingly linked to military logistics, energy security, trade routes, fisheries, investment and geopolitical influence. This makes Eritrea’s warning particularly significant. Asmara is effectively arguing that African countries should not judge foreign port investments solely by the promised economic benefits. They should also examine what political and strategic obligations may accompany those investments over the long term. The Cost of Foreign Intervention The wider lesson from Sudan, Libya and Yemen is that foreign intervention can produce consequences far beyond the original strategic objective. When external powers support competing local factions, provide weapons or establish security partnerships, they can unintentionally—or deliberately—reshape domestic power balances in ways that make political compromise more difficult. The result can be prolonged conflict, fragmented authority and weakened national institutions. This is where the strongest criticism of the UAE emerges. Abu Dhabi has become exceptionally skilled at converting commercial relationships into strategic influence. The question is whether that influence ultimately produces stability—or simply gives the UAE greater leverage over countries already struggling to govern themselves. Africa Must Ask Harder Questions Eritrea’s accusation of “port colonialism” should therefore not be dismissed as simply another regional political dispute. African governments have every right to attract foreign investment and develop their ports. But they also have a responsibility to ensure that strategic infrastructure remains subject to transparent agreements, national oversight and clearly defined security arrangements. Port investments should not quietly evolve into permanent military footholds. Commercial partnerships should not become mechanisms for political dependency. And foreign security assistance should not empower armed actors at the expense of national institutions and peaceful political settlements. The UAE’s expanding footprint across the Red Sea and Africa is a reality. Whether it ultimately contributes to stability or deepens regional fragmentation will depend on how Abu Dhabi uses its growing influence—and how firmly African states insist on transparency and accountability. The real issue is no longer whether the UAE is investing in Africa. It is what Africa is becoming in return: a partner in mutually beneficial development, or a collection of strategic assets in someone else’s geopolitical competition.
