items.title: US plans Bosaso base for CIA operations, air strikes: report
items.description: Bosaso (Somalia Today) — The United States plans to expand CIA operations in Somalia’s Puntland region and turn its presence at Bosaso airport into a military base capable of launching air strikes and surveillance missions from the strategic Gulf of Aden port, Drop Site News reported . The planned expansion would mark a significant increase in the US security footprint in Puntland, Somalia’s semi-autonomous northeastern federal member state, where American air power has supported a major offensive against Islamic State militants. Five regional security officials told Drop Site News that the current US presence at Bosaso airport consists of an intelligence and liaison “office” used by US Africa Command (AFRICOM) and the Central Intelligence Agency. AFRICOM personnel there currently coordinate requests for air support between Puntland forces and the main US military hub in neighbouring Djibouti, they said. Once the new facility is complete, US aircraft would be able to conduct combat and surveillance missions directly from Bosaso. The CIA would also expand its operations there, according to the report. Puntland publicly announced the agreement on August 2 after President Said Abdullahi Deni met a US delegation headed by Major General Claude Tudor, commander of US Special Operations Command Africa. The Puntland presidency said the United States would expand its military presence in Bosaso to strengthen counter-terrorism operations and maritime security. The talks also covered security in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. But the five officials who spoke to Drop Site said Bosaso had not previously hosted a fully fledged US military base and that the agreement would effectively establish a new American military footprint. CIA role Drop Site reported that CIA personnel already play a significant role in Puntland’s campaign against Islamic State, including interrogating captured militants, particularly senior suspects and foreign fighters. The officials cited the case of Abdiweli Mohamed Yusuf, also known as Abdiweli Walalac, a senior Islamic State financier captured near Xumbeys in Bari region in July 2025. The US Treasury designated Yusuf a Specially Designated Global Terrorist in July 2023, describing him as the head of ISIS-Somalia’s finance office since at least late 2019 and accusing him of helping deliver foreign fighters, weapons and supplies for the group. Puntland initially described his capture as a joint US-Somali operation. The five officials who spoke to Drop Site said it was instead a US-led helicopter raid involving American forces, a Somali interpreter and commanders from the Puntland Intelligence and Security Agency. Two officials told the publication that CIA personnel took Yusuf to the agency-linked office at Bosaso airport for questioning before transferring him to Djibouti the following day. “Here they are like a big brother,” one Puntland security official told Drop Site , referring to the CIA’s influence over security decisions involving Islamic State. “What they say or do goes without any questions.” The planned Bosaso arrangement also includes a new US-supported Puntland counter-terrorism force, according to the report. The sides have not yet decided its size, but one official said Washington would oversee the unit’s salaries, equipment and training. “It’s been confirmed, but the numbers haven’t been decided yet,” the official said. Strikes resume The report came as suspected US drones carried out surveillance and air strikes in the Al-Miskad mountains on Thursday night, potentially ending a months-long pause in American attacks on Islamic State in Somalia. Puntland security officials told Drop Site that drones began reconnaissance missions shortly after sunset over Togga Miraale and Togga Baalade, two areas local authorities consider Islamic State strongholds. The aircraft spotted suspected militants travelling with a donkey cart near Togga Baalade before strikes began at around 8:30 pm, the officials said. Drones also conducted surveillance further northwest in the Al-Madow mountains, where Al-Shabaab operates. AFRICOM did not respond to Drop Site’s request for comment and had not publicly confirmed the September 3 strikes. The command last confirmed an attack on Islamic State in Somalia on May 6 in the Golis Mountains, about 75 kilometres southeast of Bosaso. AFRICOM said it conducted that operation in coordination with Somalia’s federal government. New America , which tracks US counter-terrorism operations, said in August that the United States had carried out no strikes against Islamic State for three months after the May 6 attack. American operations against Al-Shabaab continued elsewhere in Somalia. Islamic State established its Somali branch in 2015 after Abdulqadir Mumin and other militants broke away from Al-Shabaab. The group later entrenched itself in the Al-Miskad mountains and developed an important financial and logistical role within the wider Islamic State network. Puntland launched Operation Hilaac against the group in late 2024 with international air support and has since captured most of its established positions. Militants, however, remain in parts of the rugged mountain range. Federal authority The Bosaso agreement also comes amid a wider dispute over the division of power between Puntland and the federal government in Mogadishu. Under Somalia’s 2012 provisional constitution, foreign affairs and national defence fall under federal authority, while the constitution requires the federal government to consult member states on international agreements affecting their interests. Puntland has been at odds with Mogadishu over constitutional changes since 2024 and has increasingly asserted its authority independently of the federal government. The dispute deepened further this year amid disagreement over Somalia’s new constitutional framework and the legitimacy of federal institutions. Drop Site said Somalia’s defence and information ministries did not respond to questions about whether the federal government knew about the Bosaso agreement in advance. items.title: UN says Bosaso used as hub for arms, fighters to Sudan’s RSF
items.description: Bosaso (Somalia Today) — The United Nations says Somalia’s port city of Bosaso served as a recurring logistics hub for a transnational network moving weapons, military equipment and foreign personnel towards Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. The UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan said it had reasonable grounds to believe that a network spanning the United Arab Emirates, Chad, southeastern Libya and Puntland in Somalia facilitated RSF operations through interconnected air, land and maritime routes. Locations in Chad, southeastern Libya and Puntland served as transit and logistical hubs for weapons, personnel and other military supplies moving into RSF-controlled areas, the report said. The report provides particularly detailed findings on Bosaso, the commercial capital of Puntland, Somalia’s semi-autonomous northeastern federal member state. “The evidence identified Bosaso, Somalia, as a recurring logistical hub and transit point,” the mission said. The report said UAE-based individuals and entities were among external actors using Bosaso for personnel and cargo destined for RSF-held areas. Witnesses also described a military base in Bosaso through which foreign contractors transited. Arms and cargo flights Sources cited by the UN described Ilyushin-76 cargo flights linking Bosaso with Kufra and Benghazi in Libya and with Chad, before personnel and cargo moved onwards into Sudan . Witnesses described regional routes involving Bosaso that carried NORINCO AH-4 155mm howitzers, FK-2000 air-defence systems, radars, armoured vehicles, Land Cruisers, uniforms, ammunition, weapons and medical supplies. The mission said some of the material was consistent with equipment previously exported to the UAE. Investigators compared witness accounts with authenticated imagery and footage, confirming the presence of some of the reported weapons at RSF operational sites. These included NORINCO AH-4 howitzers, later recaptured by Sudanese government forces, and FK-2000 air-defence systems, documented in Dubeibat in February and July 2026. Witnesses also reported drone equipment moving through regional supply routes to the RSF, including CH-95 reconnaissance and strike drones, electronic warfare capabilities and related technical support. The report did not conclude that Puntland or Somalia’s federal government supplied the weapons or knowingly participated in the network. Instead, the mission said private companies, intermediaries and associated individuals operating across several countries, including Somalia, facilitated elements of the support network. Puntland under scrutiny The UN report did not make a finding on whether Puntland authorities knew of or approved the activities it documented through Bosaso. Somalia Toda y has learned from sources familiar with the arrangements that Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni was aware of and approved the UAE’s use of Bosaso as a logistics hub for supplies destined for the RSF. Deni has maintained close ties with the UAE for years, while authorities in Jubaland and Somaliland have also developed separate economic and security partnerships with Abu Dhabi amid persistent political divisions within Somalia. The disclosure comes against a backdrop of strained relations and limited security coordination between Somalia’s federal government and the Puntland administration. The UN mission said it contacted Somalia on June 11 seeking information about activities identified within or through its territory but received no substantive response before completing the report. Somalia’s federal government later told Reuters that it took the findings seriously and had not permitted its territory, airspace or ports to be used by parties to Sudan’s conflict for military purposes. It acknowledged, however, that there had been “gaps” in information-sharing between the federal government and regional administrations. Colombian mercenaries Bosaso also featured in routes used to deploy Colombian military contractors to Sudan. The mission said former Colombian military personnel had become a significant component of the network supporting the RSF. Estimates ranged from 350 to 2,000, with investigators assessing that the total could approach 2,000 as recruitment continued. Witnesses said initial groups travelled through the UAE, Bosaso and Benghazi before crossing southern Libya into Darfur. Later groups reportedly travelled through Bosaso or the UAE before transiting Chad and entering Sudan through Nyala airport. The contractors performed specialist military roles, including operating and maintaining surveillance and strike drones, supporting artillery and advanced weapons systems and providing intelligence, technical maintenance and military instruction. Some remained responsible for operating drone systems because the necessary expertise was not widely available within RSF ranks, the report said. The mission also found evidence that Colombian contractors were present around El-Fasher before, during and after the RSF captured the North Darfur capital in October 2025. Some reportedly operated artillery, drones and other technical equipment during the offensive. The mission has previously documented war crimes, crimes against humanity and conduct displaying hallmarks of genocide in El-Fasher. Wider supply network Bosaso was one part of a wider regional logistics network identified by UN investigators. In southeastern Libya, Benghazi, Kufra and Jufra were described as hubs receiving weapons, vehicles, fuel, food and military personnel before onward transfer towards Sudan. The mission also found evidence of training facilities in Benghazi and Kufra where RSF fighters received specialised instruction in operating and maintaining weapons. Foreign trainers, including Colombians, reportedly provided technical training before fighters deployed to Darfur, Kordofan and elsewhere. Jufra also hosted a military camp where fighters from Sudan, Chad and other countries reportedly trained for deployment with the RSF. Chad served as another logistical corridor. Witnesses described recurring cargo flights originating in the UAE, followed by the movement of military supplies, personnel and foreign contractors towards RSF-controlled areas. Chad denied that weapons or military equipment had passed through its territory and said it remained neutral in the conflict. The mission said, however, that its evidence showed private actors and transnational networks had used parts of Chadian territory for transit and logistical activities. Earlier Bosaso reports The UN findings add weight to previous reporting about Bosaso’s role in Sudan’s conflict. Somalia Today reported in November 2025 on allegations that Bosaso served as a transit hub for weapons, logistics and mercenaries destined for the RSF. Somalia Today had also reported that Colombian contractors had passed through an Emirati military facility at Bosaso airport before deployment to Sudan. A Reuters investigation in July tracked aircraft operated by companies linked to a US military contractor flying between Bosaso and other locations associated with RSF supply routes. The UAE has repeatedly denied providing military, financial or logistical support to the RSF. It told the UN mission that allegations involving arms transfers and foreign fighters were unfounded and maintained that it had remained neutral throughout Sudan’s war. The mission nevertheless found that individuals and entities operating from, registered in, or linked to the UAE played a significant role in networks involved in recruiting, financing, transporting, and deploying foreign military contractors, as well as in providing military-related support benefiting the RSF. The mission urged Somalia and other governments whose territories featured in the network to investigate and prevent illicit activity. It concluded that the transnational network provided the RSF with weapons, logistical assistance, training and foreign personnel, sustaining its military operations during a conflict marked by serious violations of international humanitarian and human rights law and international crimes. items.title: Overview of the Continuous Invasion of Djibouti Government on Awdal Region, Somalia
items.description: Dr. Ali Bahar The collapse of the Union (the Somali republic) in the 1990s has not only paved the way for the disintegration of the Somali society but also facilitated the emergence of merciless militia groups such as SNM in northern Somalia and opened doors for the nemeses of Somali republic. The SNM troops with the full support of Ethiopia and Djibouti have invaded the Awdal region in 1991. These wars are still burning today, and the ethnic cleanings continues where Djibouti with, the help Hargeisa troops, now declared all hell on Awdal people, trying to displace the natives of Awdal with new settlers of Issa tribe from Ethiopia and Djibouti. Israel style! But this is nothing new, as I reported back in 2023 on the following article: The exploded warfare in Awdal, Somalia, is the never-ending crisis in Awdal region; Crisis in Awdal: Violence, Poverty, and Border Restrictions , WardheerNews, 12/23/2023[ 1 ] The identity used here is based on the way individuals describe themselves and are defined by others. Identity, as tragically has negative impacts on psychic of our society of today, is still considered an important element and remains deeply rooted in our culture. The roots of the current tribal conflicts in Awdal today, however, are not so much about differences in race, ethnicity, religion, language and culture between fighting groups. But rather identity-based conflicts also occur when groups, or more accurately countries, vying for power, succeed to control others and deny their rights; and this has been documented in Djibouti during the French colonial occupation, and the practice continues after the transfer of power to Issa tribe in Djibouti. Some of these atrocities have been well documented in book, MA’NAXE (2 ). The government in Djibouti continued the oppression and the elimination of prominent Gadabursi Djiboutian citizens, born and educated in the country. People denied their citizenship, jobs and businesses, or even killed, jailed and deported from their birthplace, Djibouti, to Awdal region in Somalia or where else. These practices and illegal deportation continue even today. The Current Rewed Invasions from Djibouti to Annex Awdal Region As if the bloody crimes committed against Gadabursi in Djibouti were not enough, and destruction of lives to satiate their clan-driven hate towards the Gadabursi people never subsided, Djibouti openly started campaigning for the annexation of coastal areas in Awdal region back in 1970s. Case in point is the organized invasion carried out in 1991 in Awdal, where Djibouti joined SNM and Ethiopia, with their military forces, to occupy the Awdal region and annihilate the Gadabursi people, the dominant tribe in the region. Since then, Awdal remains occupied and suffers daily threats and killings of innocent civilians under this oppressive, illegal occupation of by the SNM in Hargeisa administration and the government of Djibout. On Tyranny, Timothy Snyder reported that history does not repeat, but it does instruct. Aristotle warned that inequality brought instability, while Plato believed that demagogues exploited people to install themselves as tyrants ( 3 ). We see that today in Djibouti government. The current escalated security crisis in Awdal are efforts from Djibouti to finally succeed in her long-time clan ambitions (Issa clan) to completely annex Awdal region and claim it as part of Djibouti. This is an open invasion by tribally financed and empowered forces traveling across the Djibouti and Ethiopian borders with a mere intention of establishing terror and control the Awdal region. Read more: Overview of the Continuous Invasion of Djibouti Government on Awdal Region, Somalia Dr Ali Bahar Email : alibahar731@gmail.com Awdal State Movement awdalstatemovement.com The post Overview of the Continuous Invasion of Djibouti Government on Awdal Region, Somalia appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Somalia says Ankara Declaration now governs Ethiopia ties
items.description: Mogadishu (Somalia Today) — Somalia says the Ankara Declaration now governs its relations with Ethiopia, playing down questions over whether Addis Ababa’s disputed 2024 memorandum with Somaliland remains formally in force. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar said the agreement reached by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed in Türkiye in December 2024 had established a new framework between the neighbouring countries. Omar told Saudi newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat that the declaration reaffirmed both countries’ commitment to sovereignty, unity, independence and territorial integrity. “I don’t see a need to spend much time debating whether the old memorandum is frozen or dead,” Omar said. Under the Ankara framework, he said, Ethiopia could pursue access to the sea through mutually beneficial commercial arrangements, but any agreement would have to remain under Somalia’s sovereign authority. His comments provide one of Mogadishu’s clearest recent assessments of the status of the January 2024 memorandum between Ethiopia and Somaliland, which triggered the most serious diplomatic dispute between Somalia and Ethiopia in years. Ankara framework Ethiopia signed the memorandum with Somaliland in January 2024, seeking access to the Gulf of Aden. Somalia rejected the agreement as a violation of its sovereignty because it considers Somaliland part of its territory. Somaliland, the self-declared republic in northwestern Somalia, has operated with its own government and institutions since declaring independence in 1991. The dispute sharply strained relations between Mogadishu and Addis Ababa before Türkiye mediated talks between the two governments. Mohamud and Abiy signed the Ankara Declaration on December 11, 2024 , agreeing to set their differences aside and pursue a new arrangement for Ethiopia’s access to the sea. The declaration acknowledges the potential benefits of reliable Ethiopian access to and from the sea while requiring any arrangement to respect Somalia’s territorial integrity. It provides for negotiations on commercial agreements, including contracts, leases and similar arrangements, that could give Ethiopia maritime access “under the sovereign authority of the Federal Republic of Somalia”. That framework differs fundamentally from the disputed memorandum, which Ethiopia signed directly with Somaliland rather than Somalia’s federal government. Technical negotiations Somalia and Ethiopia began technical negotiations under the Ankara framework in February 2025, with Türkiye again acting as facilitator. Omar led the Somali delegation, while Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos headed Addis Ababa’s team. The two sides discussed implementation of the declaration and arrangements intended to provide Ethiopia with commercial access to the sea while preserving Somali sovereignty. Omar said the negotiations showed that Ethiopia’s interest in reliable commercial maritime access could be addressed without compromising Somalia’s territorial integrity. The Ankara Declaration does not prevent Ethiopia from accessing Somali ports. Instead, it requires such access to come through an agreement with Somalia’s federal government. Relations between Mogadishu and Addis Ababa have since improved after the tensions caused by the Somaliland memorandum. Abiy visited Mogadishu in February 2025 , when the two governments reaffirmed their commitment to bilateral cooperation and welcomed the start of technical negotiations under the Ankara process. Omar’s comments indicate that Mogadishu now regards that framework, rather than the disputed Somaliland memorandum, as the basis for negotiations over Ethiopia’s pursuit of access to the sea. items.title: Waa kuma ninka Fahad sida dadban u sheegay in uu ka dambeeyey qaraxii taliye Shub?
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Agaasimihii hore ee Hay’adda NISA, Fahad Yaasiin Xaaji Daahir oo soo saaray qoraal xasaasi ah ayaa ka hadlay qaraxii ka dhacay guriga taliye Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub) ee degmada Doolow, isaga oo tilmaam ka bixiyay cidda ka dambeysay dhacdadaasi. Fahad Yaasiin ayaan si toos ah u magacaabin shaqsiga uu eedeynayo, balse wuxuu tilmaamay in weerarka oo loo adeegsaday diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn ee Drones-ka uu hoggaamiyay nin horay usoo noqday ku-simaha Taliyaha NISA, isla markaana mar kale noqday ku-simaha Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya. Waxaa kale oo uu Fahad ku andacooday in ninkaas uu horay u weeraray siyaasiga Cabdiraxmaan Cabdishakuur Warsame, isaga oo markaas ku sime ka ahaa Taliska Sirdoonka iyo Nabadsugidda Qaranka. Marka la eego, labada tilmaam, waxay u egtahay in Fahad ka hadlayo Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac) oo sidoo kale aad ugu dhow dowladda Turkiga. “Mar ayuu noqday Ku-simaha Taliyaha Nabad Sugidda, wuxuu hoggaamiyey weerarkii guriga Cabdiraxman Cabdishakuur. Mar labaad ayuu Ku-sime u noqday Madaxweyne xeer dhaaf ah, haddana wuxuu hoggaamiyey weerarkii Drone-ka ee Degmada Dooloow ee lagu shirqoolay Taliye Mahad Cabdiraxmaan (Shub),” ayuu Fahad Yaasiin ku yiri qoraalkiisa. Dhinaca kale, waxaa si degdeg ah usoo jawaabay Xildhibaan Cabdirashiid Jilley, oo ka mid ah saaxiibbada Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka, kaas oo isna Fahad Yaasiin ku eedeeyay inuu horay u gaystay gabood-fallo, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Marka aad xukunka joogtay jariimadii aad geeysatay, ma hilmaantay fahadow?! Meeqo Muwaadin ayaa kugu maqan, takanadii aad Soomaali ka gashay weli qalbiga shacabka soomaaliyeed kama bixin fahadoow, laguma ilaawin weli!!!!” ayuu ku jawaabay Xildhibaanku. Waxaa kale oo uu falcelintiisa ku daray su’aal uu ku yiri: “Yaa hadda Soomaaliya talo kaa weydiinaya?!”. Dhacdada Doolow ayaa dhalisay hadal-heyn xooggan iyadoo dowladda Soomaaliya ay iska fogeysay weerarkaas, waxayna tilmaamtay in qaraxyadu ka dhasheen waxyaabo qarxa oo lagu diyaarinayay guri, inkastoo baaritaan rasmi ah aan weli la soo gabagabeyn. Si kastaba, Is-dhaafsiga eedeymahan ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli khilaafka u dhexeeya dowladda federaalka iyo garabka Lafta-gareen uu sii xoogeysanayo, gaar ahaan kaddib iska-horimaadyadii iyo xiisadihii amni ee dhowaan ka dhacay Baydhaba. Fahad Yaasiin ayaan si toos ah u magacaabin shaqsiga uu eedeynayo, balse wuxuu tilmaamay in weerarka oo loo adeegsaday diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn ee Drones-ka uu hoggaamiyay nin horay usoo noqday ku-simaha Taliyaha NISA, isla markaana mar kale noqday ku-simaha Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya. Waxaa kale oo uu Fahad ku andacooday in ninkaas uu horay u weeraray siyaasiga Cabdiraxmaan Cabdishakuur Warsame, isaga oo markaas ku sime ka ahaa Taliska Sirdoonka iyo Nabadsugidda Qaranka. Marka la eego, labada tilmaam, waxay u egtahay in Fahad ka hadlayo Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac) oo sidoo kale aad ugu dhow dowladda Turkiga. “Mar ayuu noqday Ku-simaha Taliyaha Nabad Sugidda, wuxuu hoggaamiyey weerarkii guriga Cabdiraxman Cabdishakuur. Mar labaad ayuu Ku-sime u noqday Madaxweyne xeer dhaaf ah, haddana wuxuu hoggaamiyey weerarkii Drone-ka ee Degmada Dooloow ee lagu shirqoolay Taliye Mahad Cabdiraxmaan (Shub),” ayuu Fahad Yaasiin ku yiri qoraalkiisa. Dhinaca kale, waxaa si degdeg ah usoo jawaabay Xildhibaan Cabdirashiid Jilley, oo ka mid ah saaxiibbada Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka, kaas oo isna Fahad Yaasiin ku eedeeyay inuu horay u gaystay gabood-fallo, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Marka aad xukunka joogtay jariimadii aad geeysatay, ma hilmaantay fahadow?! Meeqo Muwaadin ayaa kugu maqan, takanadii aad Soomaali ka gashay weli qalbiga shacabka soomaaliyeed kama bixin fahadoow, laguma ilaawin weli!!!!” ayuu ku jawaabay Xildhibaanku. Waxaa kale oo uu falcelintiisa ku daray su’aal uu ku yiri: “Yaa hadda Soomaaliya talo kaa weydiinaya?!”. Dhacdada Doolow ayaa dhalisay hadal-heyn xooggan iyadoo dowladda Soomaaliya ay iska fogeysay weerarkaas, waxayna tilmaamtay in qaraxyadu ka dhasheen waxyaabo qarxa oo lagu diyaarinayay guri, inkastoo baaritaan rasmi ah aan weli la soo gabagabeyn. Si kastaba, Is-dhaafsiga eedeymahan ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli khilaafka u dhexeeya dowladda federaalka iyo garabka Lafta-gareen uu sii xoogeysanayo, gaar ahaan kaddib iska-horimaadyadii iyo xiisadihii amni ee dhowaan ka dhacay Baydhaba. items.title: Sawirro: Sidee Cirro loogu soo dhaweeyay Mareykanka?
items.description: Washington (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Somaliland, Mudane Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro) iyo wafdi uu hoggaaminayo ayaa maanta ka dagay garoonka Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) ee Magaalada Washington D.C, halkaas oo si diirran loogu soo dhaweeyay. Madaxtooyada Somaliland ayaa sheegtay in soo dhaweynta madaxweynaha ay ka qayb-galeen bulshada reer Somaliland ee ku dhaqan Maraykanka iyo saaxiibada Somaliland ee ku sugan dalkaasi. Cabdiraxmaan Cirro oo maalmo sii joogi doono Mareykanka ayaa waxa safarka ku wehelinaya Marwada Koowaad ee Somaliland iyo xubno kale oo ay ka mid yihiin;- 1-Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah 2-Wasiirka Duulista iyo Horumarinta Madaarrada, 3-Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga, 4-La-taliyaha Sare ee Madaxweynaha ee Arrimaha Dhaqaalaha, 5-La-taliyaha Sare ee Madaxweynaha ee Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah . Waxaa kale oo wafdiga Madaxweyne Cirro ku soo biiri doona Guddoomiyaha Golaha Wakiillada Somaliland, Wasiirka Madaxtooyada iyo La-taliyaha sare ee Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah, sida ay sheegtay madaxtooyadu . Inta uu Madaxweynaha Somaliland ku guda jiro safarkiisa dalka Maraykanka, waxa uu kulamo iyo wada-hadallo la yeelan doonaa mas’uuliyiin iyo dhinacyo muhiim ah, isaga oo diiradda saari doona xoojinta xidhiidhka diblomaasiyadeed, iskaashiga amniga iyo dhaqaalaha, maalgashiga, iyo taageerada qaddiyadda aqoonsiga Somaliland. Warsaxaafadeedka ayaa sidoo kale lagu sheegay in Madaxweynaha uu madaxda Mareykanka u gudbin doono aragtida Somaliland, muhiimadda ay leedahay iyo rabitaanka shacabka ee ku aadan inay helaan aqoonsi caalami ah. “Safarkani ma aha oo keliya booqasho diblomaasiyadeed, balse waa juhdi Qaran oo lagu horumarinayo danaha, sumcadda iyo himilada Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland, iyada oo Madaxweynaha iyo weftigiisu ay Washington u gudbin doonaan aragtida Somaliland, xaqiiqadeeda siyaasadeed, doorkeeda istaraatiijiga ah iyo rabitaanka shacabka Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland oo ah in dalkoodu helo aqoonsi iyo xidhiidh caalami ah oo ku salaysan dano-wadaag iyo iskaashi midho-dhal ah,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraalka kasoo baxay madaxtooyada. Booqashada Cabdiraxmaan Cirro oo ah tii ugu horreysay ee uu madaxweyne ahaan ku tego Mareykanka ayaa loo arkaa mid muhiim u ah xoojinta xiriirka diblumaasiyadeed, iskaashiga amniga iyo dhaqaalaha, dhiirrigelinta maalgashiga iyo horumarinta qaddiyadda aqoonsiga Somaliland. Somaliland ayaa haatan wadda dadaallo diblumaasiyadeed oo ay ku doonayso inay xoojiso xiriirkeeda caalamka, gaar ahaan Mareykanka. items.title: Kumaandooska Danab oo gurmad u fidiyay dad uu gaari la gaddoomay
items.description: Ciidanka Kumaandooska Danab ee Xoogga Dalka ayaa gurmad caafimaad u fidiyay dad shacab ah oo gaari rakaab uu kula rogmaday deegaanka Golweyn oo hoostaga Magaalada Marka ee Xarunta Gobolka Shabellaha Hoose. Wararka ayaa sheegaya in Kumaandooska Danab iyo Ciidanka Guutada 14-ka October oo ku guda jira hawlgal amni xaqiijin ah ay waddada Golweyn kula kulmeen shacabka oo gaariga uu kula gaddoomay waddada dhexdeeda. Muuqaal la soo dhigay baraha bulshada ayaa muujinaya ciidamada oo soo samatabixinaya dadkii ku dhex jiray gaariga. Dhakhaatiirta ka tirsan Ciidanka Danab ayaa gurmad caafimaad u fidiyay dadkii u baahnaa gargaarka degdegga ah. Ciidamada oo watay gaadiidka dagaalka ayaa sidoo kale gacan ka gaystay hagaajinta gaarigii qalibmay, si shacabka loogu fududeeyo inay sii wataan safarkooda. Lama sheegin cid ku dhimatay shilkan, marka laga soo tago in qaar ka mid ah rakaabkii gaariga la socday ay ku dhaawacmeen. Ciidamada Qalabka Sida keliya kuma eka difaaca dalka, balse waxay mar kasta u taagan yihiin inay safka hore ka galaan samatabbixinta iyo caawinta shacabka, xilliyada ay jiraan masiibooyinka dabiiciga iyo xaaladaha degdegga ah.

items.title: Somalia’s Expired Parliament: A Legislature Serving Villa Somalia at the Expense of the People
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — Somalia’s Federal Parliament has once again come under scrutiny after lawmakers voted down an opposition motion seeking to place the Doolow attack on the parliamentary agenda —a decision critics say exposes a legislature that has become more responsive to Villa Somalia than to the Somali public. The vote came during a tense parliamentary session in which opposition lawmakers sought to force a debate over the attack on former Custodial Corps Commander General Mahad Abdirahman “Shub” at his residence in Doolow. The motion was rejected by a decisive margin. According to the parliamentary session, 165 lawmakers were present. Of those, 118 voted against adding the Doolow incident to the agenda, while 45 supported the motion and two abstained. The result triggered loud exchanges and disorder in the chamber as government and opposition lawmakers confronted one another over the politically sensitive issue. But the significance of the vote extends beyond the Doolow incident. The residence of Gen Mahad in Doolow, attacked by Drones Somalia’s Federal Parliament has been operating beyond the expiry of its constitutional mandate since April 2026, yet it continues to exercise legislative authority amid an unresolved national political and electoral crisis. Critics argue that the legitimacy problem is compounded by the parliament’s record during the period in which it still held a valid mandate. Rather than functioning as an independent check on executive power, the chamber has became a political theatre serving the president. Its frequently been portrayed by opposition groups and civil-society critics as an extension of Villa Somalia, approving presidential initiatives no limited scrutiny. The latest Doolow vote has revived that criticism. The question is no longer simply whether Parliament can pass legislation. It is whether it is willing to hold the executive accountable when the government itself becomes the subject of serious allegations. During the tenure of former Speaker Sheikh Adan Mohamed Nur “Adan Madoobe,” critics frequently used the nickname “Approved” to mock what they described as Parliament’s readiness to endorse government-backed proposals. The label reflected a widespread perception that presidential initiatives could move through the chamber with no resistance. More seriously, critics have questioned whether parliamentary sessions and votes have complied with the required attendance and procedural thresholds. Such concerns strike at the heart of parliamentary legitimacy. A parliament is not supposed to exist merely to endorse decisions already made by the executive. Its fundamental functions include scrutinizing government policy, challenging executive decisions, representing constituents and protecting the public interest. When those functions are weakened, Parliament becomes an instrument of executive power rather than a check on it. The Politics of Patronage President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration has built political loyalty among lawmakers through patronage, including land allocations, financial benefits and other political favors. If lawmakers believe their political survival or personal interests depend on maintaining loyalty to the presidency, their ability to represent constituents independently is inevitably questioned. The result, is a parliament whose members have become more responsive to the interests of those controlling government patronage than to the citizens. That is the difference between representation and political dependency. The attempt to bring the Doolow attack before Parliament, was a test of principle and offered the lawmakers an opportunity to demonstrate responsibility and independence. Opposition MPs, including Yusuf Gamaadiid and Dahir Amin Jesow, reportedly pushed for the incident to be added to the agenda so Parliament could debate what happened and determine whether further action was required. They failed. The 118–45 vote against the proposal immediately became a political statement in itself. It does not establish who was responsible for the Doolow attack. That remains a matter for an independent investigation. But it does raise a separate question: Why would Parliament refuse even to debate an incident involving a former senior national security official who was reportedly wounded in an attack? Representing Constituents—or Themselves? The deepest criticism facing Somalia’s parliament is therefore not about one vote. It is about representation. Somali citizens expect their lawmakers to speak for communities facing insecurity, displacement, poverty, political exclusion and weak institutions. They do not elect MPs merely to protect government interests. Nevertheless, many believe that Somalia’s lawmakers are a product of the very corrupt political system that put them in office—a process in which ordinary citizens had no role, no voice, and no meaningful say in choosing those who claim to represent them. Parliamentary independence is measured not by speeches but by difficult votes. It is tested when the executive disagrees. It is tested when the government is accused of wrongdoing. It is tested when opposition lawmakers demand an investigation. And it is tested when a politically uncomfortable issue must be placed on the national agenda. The Doolow vote was precisely such a moment. The government and its supporters may argue that Parliament was simply exercising its procedural authority. That is a legitimate position. But a legislature unwilling to investigate allegations involving the national interest or the abuse of power is failing in its fundamental duty.. The distinction matters. Somalia cannot build a credible democratic system if its institutions are extensions of political power. it’s a cost to Somalia’s democracy. An expired parliament already faces questions about its legitimacy. A parliament accused of routinely following Villa Somalia’s direction faces a deeper crisis of public confidence. And a legislature that refuses to debate politically sensitive allegations risks reinforcing the perception that accountability ends where presidential power begins. That is dangerous for a country already struggling with disputes over elections, constitutional reform, federalism and the distribution of political authority. The Question Somalia Must Answer The Doolow motion may have been defeated, but the questions it raised will not disappear. Who does Somalia’s parliament represent? Does it represent the presidency? Does it represent the interests of individual MPs? Or does it represent the Somali people? The parliamentary mandate expired in April, 2026. The country still lacks a broadly accepted political settlement over the next electoral and constitutional order. Yet the same political machinery continues to operate. For critics, the latest vote is another indication that Somalia’s legislature has failed to develop the independence required of a genuine democratic institution. A parliament should not exist to say “approved” whenever the presidency points. It should exist to ask questions, demand evidence and hold power accountable. The Doolow vote has therefore become more than a parliamentary procedural dispute. It has become a test of whether Somalia’s legislature can still claim to represent the people—or whether it has become another arm of Villa Somalia. items.title: Saraakiisha Militariga oo u kuurgelaya caqabadaha horgudban hawlgalka deegaanka Basra
items.description: Wararka ka imanaya Magaalada Muqdisho ayaa sheegaya in Saraakiisha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ay ka arrinsanayaan, waxa u baahan in wax ka bedelka lagu sameeyo, si uu u guuleysto hawlgalka la doonayo in maleeshiyada Al Shabaab lagaga saaro deegaanka Basra, oo ku yaala xuduudda Gobolada Shabellaha Hoose iyo Shabellaha Dhexe, isla-markaana isku xira Magaalooyinka Afgooye iyo Balcad. Saraakiisha ayay wararku sheegayaan inay u kuurgelid iyo qiimaynba ku sameynayaan qaabka uu u socdo hawlgalka iyo caqabadaha ay tahay in xal degdeg ah loo helo. Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka oo kaashanaya Booliska Sida Gaarka ah u tababaran ee Haramcad ayaa 26-kii bishii hore ee August bilaabay hawlgal militari oo qorshuhu ahaa in maleeshiyada lagaga kiciyo deegaankaasi. Inkasta oo ciidamada ay u suurtagashay inay Shabaabka ka saaraan inta badan goobihii ay kaga sugnaayeen deegaanka, haddana dagaalka ayaa la arki karay in uu mid adag ku noqday, xilligii dhameystirka. Shabaabka ayaa salka la galay godad ay horey uga qoteen bannaanada Basra ee uu maro Webiga Shabelle, isla-markaana ah dhul cufan oo geedo badan leh oo gurmad-na ka heli kara Labada Shabelle. Gulufka dagaal ee ay ciidamadu ku hayeen maleeshiyada ayaad mooddaa in uu gaabis ku yimid amaba uu hakaday, wixii ka dambeeyay gelinkii dambe ee maalintii Arbacada. Taliska Militariga ayaa lagu dhalleeceeyay inay Shabaabka culeys ka soo saareen dhinaca Muqdisho oo keliya, iyadoo aanu cadaadis ka haysan jihooyinka kale ee Afgooye iyo Balcad ama Wanlaweyn iyo Qalimow. Wararka ayaa sheegaya in Saraakiisha sarsare ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ee ku sugan Magaalada Muqdisho ay hadda ka wada hadlayaan, sidii la isugu xiri lahaa ciidamada, isla-markaana uu hawlgalku u noqon lahaa mid dhowr jiho ka socda. Ilo wareedyo ayaa sheegaya in Saraakiisha Militariga ay eegayaan, sidii ay ciidamada uga wada hawlgeli lahaayeen duleedka Muqdisho iyo Gobolada Shabellooyinka. Deegaanka Basra oo deegaan beereed ah ayaa leh muhiimad weyn oo istiraatiiji ah, oo Shabaabka u sahla in ay si nabdoon isugu kala gooshaan Labada Shabelle. Lama oga waqtiga saxda ah ee ay qaadaneyso in la qorsheeyo guluf ballaaran oo wadajir ah, oo si buuxda Al Shabaab looga saarayo jiinka Webiga Shabelle ee Basra. Dhowrkii sano ee u dambeeyay oo ciidamada ay marar kala duwan hawlgalo ka sameeyeen deegaanka ayaa ku soo dhamaaday natiijo la’aan, sababtuna waa inaysan si dhameystiran uga wada saarin Shabaab, isla-markaana aysan ka sameysan saldhigyo joogto ah oo lagaga hortagayo inay ku soo laabtaan amaba lagu xakameynayo isu socodkooda gobolada deriska la ah Caasimadda Muqdisho.

items.title: Somalia: Fahad Yasin links Jama to Gen. Shub drone strike
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Somalia’s former intelligence chief Fahad Yasin has accused the Speaker of the House of the People, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur – widely known by the nicknames “Jama” and “Minister TikTok” – of directing the drone strike that hit the Doolow residence of former Custodial Corps commander Gen. Mahad Abdirahman Aden late Thursday. Gen. Mahad, popularly known as “General Shub,” survived the overnight attack in the Gedo region town near the Ethiopian border. Jubaland’s Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism said five people in total were hurt: Gen. Mahad, who sustained minor injuries, and four civilians, including his wife. The allegation In a Facebook statement, Yasin warned that the strike would carry “dangerous repercussions capable of spreading beyond Somalia to neighboring countries,” a remark he made in the context of accusing President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration of crossing a dangerous line. Yasin said Nur first demonstrated what he described as command responsibility for lethal operations in December 2017, when he served as acting head of the National Intelligence and Security Agency (NISA) and, according to Yasin, led the raid on the Mogadishu home of opposition politician Abdirahman Abdishakur Warsame. Yasin alleged that Nur – who is now serving as acting president while President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud is on an overseas trip – has again used that authority, this time to direct the strike on Gen. Mahad. Competing accounts of the attack Jubaland’s Ministry of Information, Culture and Tourism said Turkish military aircraft carried out the overnight operation, adding that two missiles were fired – one of which struck the home of Doolow’s district chairman. Other Jubaland officials and prominent political figures, including former presidents Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo and the opposition Somali Future Council, have echoed the drone-strike account and demanded an independent investigation. The Federal Government has denied involvement and disputed that a drone strike took place at all. Its preliminary investigation, officials said, indicates the blast at Gen. Mahad’s residence originated from explosives being handled inside the house rather than from an external strike. Turkey, which operates a military base in Mogadishu and trains and equips federal government forces, has not responded to the allegations that its aircraft were involved. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: Somalia’s Geopolitical Reset: Is the World Giving Up on One Somalia?
items.description: By Ahmed A. Yusuf For decades, the dominant international policy toward Somalia was built around a simple proposition: Somalia needed a functioning central government capable of governing the entire country. That proposition now appears to be under serious reconsideration. Across the Horn of Africa, a different geopolitical reality may be emerging—one in which international powers increasingly engage with Somalia not as a single effective political unit, but through its most strategically important and locally functional territories. If that shift is indeed taking place, it could represent one of the most consequential changes in international policy toward Somalia since the collapse of the state in 1991. The emerging question is no longer simply whether Somalia can rebuild a powerful central government. It is whether the international community has begun preparing for a Somalia in which regional political entities become the principal partners for security, trade, maritime access and strategic investment. That would fundamentally change the political equation in Mogadishu. From state-building to strategic partnerships. For more than three decades, billions of dollars have been invested in rebuilding Somali state institutions, training security forces, supporting elections and strengthening successive federal governments. Yet the results have remained deeply disappointing. Al-Shabaab continues to pose a major security threat. Federal authority remains uneven. Constitutional disputes repeatedly paralyze politics. Relations between Mogadishu and several federal member states have deteriorated, while political competition increasingly revolves around control of institutions rather than the construction of a genuinely national political settlement. For external powers, this creates a difficult calculation. Why continue pouring enormous resources into a central government that cannot reliably exercise authority across the country when regional administrations may offer more predictable security and economic partnerships? This does not necessarily mean that Western governments have formally abandoned the idea of a unified Somalia. There is no publicly established international doctrine declaring that Somalia should be divided into smaller republics. But geopolitics is often revealed not by official declarations but by where governments put their money, soldiers, diplomats and strategic infrastructure. And that is where the picture becomes increasingly interesting. Three strategic Somalia’s? Somaliland, Puntland and southern Somalia increasingly occupy three very different geopolitical spaces. Somaliland has built its own political and security institutions and controls a strategically located coastline facing the Gulf of Aden. Berbera offers a deep-water port and an expanding transportation corridor connecting the Red Sea region with the Horn of Africa. Puntland occupies another extraordinary strategic position. Its coastline stretches along some of the most important maritime routes connecting the Gulf of Aden with the Indian Ocean. Its territory includes the approaches to the Gulf of Aden and the Guardafui Channel, while its waters are also associated with significant fisheries and potential energy resources. Southern Somalia, meanwhile, remains the principal battleground in the fight against Al-Shabaab. It is also strategically positioned along the western Indian Ocean and the approaches to the Red Sea. These territories therefore offer international powers something that Somalia’s central political institutions have struggled to provide: strategic access combined with local partnerships. Jubaland presents an additional complication because of its geographic proximity to Kenya and its importance to Kenya’s security calculations. The result is a country whose geography may increasingly be more important to foreign governments than the constitutional map drawn in Mogadishu. The uncomfortable question of resources The transformation would not be driven by security alone. Somalia possesses one of Africa’s longest coastlines, potentially valuable fisheries, offshore resources, ports and a geographic position overlooking some of the world’s most important shipping lanes. The Red Sea crisis, the war in the Middle East, competition involving the United States, China, Turkey and Gulf states, and growing concern over maritime security have all increased the strategic value of the Horn of Africa. The question therefore becomes unavoidable: Can the international community afford to ignore Somalia’s coastline simply because Somalia’s political institutions remain dysfunctional? Increasingly, the answer appears to be no. The strategic logic is straightforward. Whoever develops reliable partnerships along Somalia’s coastline will gain influence over one of the most important maritime environments in the world. That makes Somalia not merely a failed-state problem. It makes Somalia a geopolitical prize. For Puntland, this changing environment could represent a remarkable strategic opportunity.Puntland spent years investing politically in the federal system, hoping that federalism would eventually produce a genuine power-sharing arrangement between Mogadishu and the federal member states. Instead, relations have deteriorated. The political confrontation with Mogadishu has pushed Puntland toward a more independent foreign-policy posture, while its geographic position has made it increasingly attractive to external security partners. Any expansion of American security cooperation with Puntland would therefore have significance far beyond counterterrorism. It would signal that Washington sees Puntland’s coastline and geographic position as strategically important in their own right. That could give Puntland greater leverage in negotiations with Mogadishu—but it could also force Puntland to make one of the most consequential political decisions in its history. Does it continue to pursue a unified Somali state through a reformed federal system? Or does it gradually develop the institutions, international partnerships and strategic relationships necessary to function as a separate political entity? Those are two very different futures. The Somaliland precedent. Somaliland provides perhaps the clearest example of what can happen when a territory develops functioning institutions while the internationally recognized central state remains weak. For decades, Somaliland has operated with its own government, security forces, currency and political institutions despite lacking broad international recognition as an independent state. Its strategic location has nevertheless attracted growing international interest. The lesson for Puntland is not necessarily that independence is inevitable. The lesson is more fundamental: In international politics, effective control of territory, institutional capacity and strategic geography can eventually become as important as constitutional claims. Recognition may come later—or not at all. But strategic relevance can arrive much earlier. Southern Somalia: the security problem that refuses to disappear. Southern Somalia presents the opposite challenge. Despite enormous international military assistance, Al-Shabaab remains capable of attacking government positions, infiltrating communities and exploiting political grievances. The fundamental problem is not simply a shortage of weapons. It is the absence of sustainable political authority. A government can capture a town with military assistance. The harder task is keeping it. If local communities do not trust the authorities who arrive after the army, territory can quickly become contested again. This is why Somalia’s repeated cycles of military offensives followed by territorial reversals should concern international policymakers. The country cannot be stabilized by capturing towns alone. It requires legitimate local administration, justice, security, economic opportunity and political inclusion. Without those foundations, military victories remain temporary. Turkey’s expanding role Turkey adds another layer to this increasingly complicated geopolitical landscape. Ankara has developed exceptionally close relations with the Federal Government in Mogadishu, including military, economic and security cooperation. Turkey’s involvement demonstrates that Somalia has become a competitive geopolitical arena rather than merely an international aid project. For Ankara, Somalia offers strategic access to the Indian Ocean and the broader Horn of Africa. For Washington, the priority is counterterrorism, maritime security and limiting the expansion of hostile strategic influence. For Gulf states, ports and maritime trade routes are central. For China, the wider Red Sea and Indian Ocean environment forms part of a much larger strategic network. For Ethiopia, access to the sea is an existential economic and strategic concern. And for Kenya, developments in southern Somalia have direct national-security implications. The result is an extraordinary convergence of interests. Everybody wants something from Somalia. The tragedy is that Somalia itself remains politically divided over what it wants from the outside world. The danger of a geopolitical fragmentation This emerging environment presents both opportunities and enormous dangers. If international powers increasingly deal separately with Somaliland, Puntland, Jubaland and southern administrations, they may unintentionally accelerate Somalia’s political fragmentation. A country that was once struggling to rebuild a central state could gradually become a collection of strategically important territories, each cultivating its own international relationships. That would not necessarily produce immediate formal partition. Instead, something more subtle could emerge: de facto fragmentation without formal recognition. Different territories could have different security partners, different economic agreements and different foreign-policy priorities while continuing to exist nominally within one Somali state. That may be the direction in which events are moving. The Federal Government should therefore pay close attention to this geopolitical transformation. Its greatest danger may not be the formal declaration of independence by another Somali territory. It may be something quieter: the gradual loss of international dependence on Mogadishu. If foreign governments discover that they can protect their interests by dealing directly with regional authorities, the strategic importance of the federal capital could diminish. That would be a devastating political development for any central government. The answer cannot be coercion. Nor can it be attempts to impose political outcomes through military force. The only sustainable alternative is to make the Somali federal government genuinely attractive to its constituent territories. That means constitutional compromise, predictable revenue-sharing, credible elections, respect for federal authority and regional autonomy, accountable security institutions and a foreign policy negotiated with the states rather than imposed upon them. Somalia may therefore be approaching another historic crossroads. One path leads toward the reconstruction of a genuinely negotiated Somali federation—one in which Mogadishu remains important but does not dominate the political system. The second leads toward a looser association of increasingly autonomous territories, each pursuing its own strategic relationships with foreign powers. The third, and most dangerous, is continued confrontation: Mogadishu attempting to impose central authority while regional governments resist, creating a permanent cycle of political crises, armed confrontation and foreign intervention. The Horn of Africa is changing rapidly . The Red Sea crisis, competition among global powers, Ethiopia’s search for maritime access, the expansion of Turkish influence, American strategic repositioning and the growing importance of maritime security have dramatically increased Somalia’s geopolitical value. Somalia may be politically fragmented, but its geography is anything but insignificant. Indeed, geography may ultimately prove stronger than politics. The paradox is striking: the weaker Somalia’s central institutions become, the more valuable its territory may become to competing external powers. That is precisely why the country faces a historic choice. Somalia can either rebuild a political settlement strong enough to make its geography serve one nation—or allow competing powers to negotiate separately with its fragments. The future of the Somali Republic may depend less on who wins the next election in Mogadishu than on whether Somalis can agree on what kind of country they want to build. And that is the geopolitical question the world is increasingly waiting to see answered. Ahmed A. items.title: Baidoa Hospitals Struggle to Treat Wounded Civilians Caught in the Crossfire
items.description: Baidoa (WDN) — The human cost of the latest fighting in Baidoa is becoming painfully clear inside the city’s hospitals, where dozens of wounded people are receiving treatment after heavy clashes erupted across the city and its outskirts on Thursday. The fighting pitted forces loyal to the Federal Government of Somalia and its allies in South West State against militias loyal to former South West President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed (Laftagareen), according to local accounts. The Bay Regional Hospital said it had received 71 wounded people since the fighting began. Among them were 15 women, while one civilian later died from injuries sustained during the violence. Behind those numbers are families facing fear, grief and uncertainty. A City Shaken by Gunfire The fighting began in the early hours of Thursday, with residents reporting the sound of intense gunfire and heavy weapons across parts of Baidoa The clashes brought fear and confusion to a city already burdened by years of conflict and displacement. Some residents fled their homes, while others remained trapped indoors as gunfire echoed through surrounding neighborhoods. For families with loved ones caught in the violence, the hospital became a place of anguish as relatives waited anxiously for news about the condition of the wounded. Some relatives told local sources that several patients remained in serious condition and required medical treatment beyond what is readily available in Baidoa. Doctors and families may ultimately have to consider transferring critically injured patients to Mogadishu, where more specialized surgical and medical services are available. Not everyone admitted to the hospital has required prolonged treatment. Some patients with minor injuries have been discharged after their conditions improved and have returned home. But for families of those who remain seriously injured, the ordeal is far from over. The prospect of transferring a loved one to Mogadishu adds another burden to families already struggling with the consequences of conflict. In a city where humanitarian needs are immense, access to specialized medical care can itself become a matter of survival. Reported: Bay Regional Hospital has directly confirmed the admission of 71 wounded people, including 15 women, and the death of one civilian from injuries sustained during the fighting. The overall number of casualties among the armed sides has not yet been independently established. A Political Crisis Turning Violent The latest clashes come after months of political and security tensions in Baidao involving the Federal Government and political forces aligned with Laftagareen. Federal forces took control of the city in March after Laftagareen left office, but the political dispute has continued to cast a shadow over South West State. What began as a struggle over political authority has now brought armed confrontation into the streets of one of Somalia’s most important cities. Baidoa is the administrative center of Bay region and a key political and security hub for South West State. It is also home to hundreds of thousands of displaced people who depend heavily on humanitarian assistance and already limited health services. A Humanitarian Burden Growing Heavier For a population already living with displacement, poverty and insecurity, renewed fighting carries consequences far beyond the battlefield. Every new casualty adds pressure to hospitals that operate with limited resources. Every family forced to flee another home faces another uncertain future. And every outbreak of violence threatens to disrupt humanitarian services that vulnerable communities depend upon. The tragedy is particularly painful because those bearing the consequences are not necessarily the people making the political decisions that brought the confrontation to Baidoa. The latest violence is a reminder of how quickly Somalia’s political disputes can become human tragedies when they move from negotiations and institutions to armed confrontation. The full toll of Thursday’s fighting remains unclear. But the 71 wounded people reported by Bay Regional Hospital—and the civilian death already confirmed—offer a sobering glimpse of the suffering unfolding behind the political struggle. For the families waiting beside hospital beds in Baidoa, the political arguments are distant. What matters now is whether their loved ones survive, whether they can receive the treatment they need, and whether the guns will finally fall silent. items.title: Dowladda Soomaaliya oo soo saartay habraac cusub oo lagu diiwaangelinayo hay’adaha dhaqanka iyo farshaxanka
items.description: Wasaaradda Warfaafinta, Dhaqanka iyo Dalxiiska ee Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa ku dhawaaqday dhaqan-gelinta Xeer Wasiir Lr. 0001/26, kaas oo lagu ansixiyay Habraaca Kumeelgaarka ah ee Maamulka iyo Diiwaangelinta Hay’adaha Dhaqanka iyo Farshaxanka dalka. Xeerka oo Wasiirku saxiixay 27-kii Luulyo 2026, ayaa khuseeya dhammaan hay’adaha, machadyada, ururrada, golayaasha iyo shakhsiyaadka ka shaqeeya dhinacyada dhaqanka iyo farshaxanka Soomaaliya, kuwaas oo ay ku jiraan hay’adaha maxalliga ah iyo kuwa ajaanibta ah. Wasaaraddu waxay sheegtay in habraacan looga gol leeyahay in la hirgeliyo Siyaasadda Qaranka ee Dhaqanka iyo Farshaxanka, iyadoo la sameynayo nidaam mideysan oo lagu diiwaangeliyo laguna kormeero hay’adaha ka shaqeeya qeybahan. Sidoo kale, habraacu wuxuu diiradda saarayaa ilaalinta iyo horumarinta dhaqanka iyo farshaxanka Soomaaliyeed, xoojinta wada-shaqeynta Wasaaradda iyo hay’adaha ku shaqada leh, iyo hubinta in howlaha dhaqanka iyo farshaxanka dalka ay yeeshaan tayo iyo sharciyeyn rasmi ah. Sida ku cad Qodobka 2-aad ee Xeerka Wasiirka, Wasaaradda Warfaafinta, Dhaqanka iyo Dalxiiska ayaa mas’uul ka noqonaysa diiwaangelinta rukhsadaha iyo heshiisyada, ilaalinta xogta iyo kaydinta dukumentiyada, iyo dabagalka fulinta xeerka. Wasaaraddu waxay dhammaan hay’adaha, ururrada, machadyada iyo shakhsiyaadka uu xeerku khuseeyo ugu baaqday inay si buuxda ula jaanqaadaan habraaca cusub, isla markaana ay Wasaaradda kala soo xiriiraan arrimaha la xiriira diiwaangelinta, rukhsadaha, heshiisyada iyo dukumentiyada hawlahooda. Wasaaradda ayaa sidoo kale caddeysay in Xeer Wasiir Lr. 0001/26 uu dhaqan galay markii uu saxiixay Wasiirka Warfaafinta, Dhaqanka iyo Dalxiiska, iyadoo ku baaqday in dhammaan dhinacyada ay khusayso ay u hoggaansamaan xeerka si loo helo nidaam mideysan oo sharciyeysan oo lagu maamulo laguna horumariyo dhaqanka iyo farshaxanka Soomaaliya.

items.title: Gudoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka oo la dardaarmay Guddiga Doorashooyinka (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Gudoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ee Baarlamaanka Somaliya, Cabdiqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac) ayaa Sabtidan Xafiiskiisa Magaalada Muqdisho kulan kula qaatay Guddiga Doorashooyinka Qaranka. Gudoomiyaha Guddiga Doorashooyinka Qaranka, Cabdikariin Axmed Xasan iyo xubno uu horkacayo ayaa Gudoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka warbixin ka siiyay shaqooyinka guddiga ee la xiriira doorashooyinka dalka iyo marxaladaha hadda ay maraayaan, sida lagu sheegay war ka soo baxay Xafiiska Gudoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka. Gudoomiye Jaamac ayaa xubnaha guddiga ku booriyay, sida warka lagu sheegay in ay dhowraan dhexdhexaadnimada iyo hufnaanta, isla-markaana ay u shaqeeyaan si madaxbannaan, caddaalad ah oo hufan. “Gudoomiye Cabdiqaadir Maxamed Nuur ayaa sheegay in guddiga ay waajib ku tahay inuu howlihiisa iyo go’aannadiisana u guto si waafaqsan shuruucda kale ee dalka, isla-markaana uu u sinnaado dhammaan dhinacyada ururada siyaasadda, musharaxiinta iyo codbixiyeyaasha.” Ayaa lagu yiri warka. Kulanka ayaa imanaya, iyadoo guddigu uu dhawaan guda gelayo qabashada Doorashooyinka Dowlad Goboleedyada Galmudug iyo Hirshabelle. Guddiga ayaa 24-kii bishii August fadeexad kala kulmay Maxkamadda Sare Dalka, ka dib markii ay burisay natiijada doorashadii qof iyo codka ee 30-kii bishii July laga qabtay Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug. Gudoomiyaha Maxkamadda Sare, Garyaqaan Baashe Yuusuf Axmed ayaa waxba kama jiraan ku tilmaamay doorashada ka dhacday Galmudug, ka dib markii uu sheegay inaanan loo maamulin si waafaqsan sharciga, wuxuuna go’aamiyay in doorasho ku celis ah laga qabto Galmudug, taasoo uu guddiguna aqbalay.

items.title: Madaxweynaha Somaliland oo gaadhay dalka Mareykanka
items.description: Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland, Mudane Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro), iyo weftigii ballaadhnaa ee uu hoggaaminayey ayaa si nabad ah uga degay Madaarka Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) ee magaalada Washington, D.C., halkaas oo ay si diirran ugu soo dhaweeyeen bulshada reer Somaliland ee ku dhaqan dalka Maraykanka iyo saaxiibada Somaliland. Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland waxa safarka ku wehelinaya Marwada Koowaad ee Qaranka JSL, iyo xubno kale oo ka tirsan weftiga Madaxweynaha oo ay ka mid yihiin masuuliyiinta hoos ku xusan: 1. Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah 2. Wasiirka Duulista iyo Horumarinta Madaarrada 3. Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga 4. La-taliyaha Sare ee Madaxweynaha ee Arrimaha Dhaqaalaha 5. La-taliyaha Sare ee Madaxweynaha ee Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah . Sidoo kale waftiga Madaxweynaha waxa ku soo biiri doona Guddoomiyaha Golaha Wakiillada JSL, Wasiirka Madaxtooyada iyo La-taliyaha Sare ee Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah . Muddada uu Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland ku guda jiro safarkiisa shaqo ee dalka Maraykanka, waxa uu kulamo iyo wada-hadallo la yeelan doonaa masuuliyiin iyo dhinacyo muhiim ah, isaga oo diiradda saari doona xoojinta xidhiidhka diblomaasiyadeed, iskaashiga amniga iyo dhaqaalaha, maalgashiga, iyo taageerada qaddiyadda aqoonsiga ee Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland. Safarkani ma aha oo keliya booqasho diblomaasiyadeed, balse waa juhdi Qaran oo lagu horumarinayo danaha, sumcadda iyo himilada Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland, iyada oo Madaxweynaha iyo weftigiisu ay Washington u gudbin doonaan aragtida Somaliland, xaqiiqadeeda siyaasadeed, doorkeeda istaraatiijiga ah iyo rabitaanka shacabka Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland oo ah in dalkoodu helo aqoonsi iyo xidhiidh caalami ah oo ku salaysan dano-wadaag iyo iskaashi midho-dhal ah.

items.title: Garbaharey Erupts in Protest as Residents Burn Turkish Flag Over Doolow Attack
items.description: Garbaharey, GEDO (WDN) — In a striking display of public anger, residents of Garbaharey have taken to the streets to protest the attack that took place in Doolow, with demonstrators publicly burning the Turkish flag in a dramatic gesture that appeared to blame Turkey for the violence. Reports from Garbaharey, the administrative capital of Gedo region, say large numbers of residents gathered in a public demonstration following the overnight attack on the residence of Commander Shub in Doolow. The most striking moment came when protesters set fire to the Turkish national flag in a public space—an extraordinary act of condemnation directed at a country that has become one of Somalia’s most prominent military and political partners. Preparations for demonstrations against the Turkish government’s involvement in Somalia’s local politics is said to be underway in other parts of Jubaland, including the port city of Kismayo. A Dramatic Message to Ankara The burning of the Turkish flag appeared to reflect the protesters’ belief that Turkish military aircraft were involved in the Doolow operation or provided support to Somali government forces.Those claims have not been independently verified, but the symbolism of the protest was unmistakable. Turkey has invested heavily in its relationship with Somalia, providing military training, equipment and other forms of security assistance to the Federal Government. The sight of the Turkish flag being burned on the streets of a Somali regional capital therefore carries considerable political weight. The demonstration was not limited to Turkey. Protesters also reportedly burned images of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre, directing their anger at Somalia’s top federal leadership. The images of national leaders being publicly burned alongside the Turkish flag transformed the demonstration into a broader expression of opposition to the federal government’s handling of the Doolow confrontation. The demonstration was eventually broken up by police in Garbaharey, according to local reports.The dispersal came after protesters had publicly expressed their anger over the Doolow attack and what they perceived as the involvement of federal authorities and their foreign military partners. The incident illustrates the depth of emotions surrounding the confrontation in Doolow, where political tensions have increasingly taken on a security dimension. The public burning of a foreign country’s flag is rarely an insignificant act. For Turkey, a country that places considerable importance on its national symbols and has cultivated a highly visible strategic partnership with Somalia, images of its flag being burned in a Somali city are likely to carry particular political significance. Local reports characterize Turkey as highly sensitive to public displays of hostility toward its national symbols. Whether Ankara will respond publicly to the incident remains to be seen. But the images from Garbaharey send a powerful message: a segment of the local population is deeply angry, and Turkey has become part of that anger. From Doolow to Garbaharey What makes the protest particularly striking is that the anger over an incident in Doolow has now spilled into the streets of Garbaharey. The burning of the Turkish flag, followed by the destruction of images of Somalia’s president and prime minister, reflects how quickly a localized security confrontation can evolve into a wider political crisis. If the allegations concerning Turkish military involvement in the Doolow attack are proven, the political consequences could be significant—not only for the Federal Government but also for Turkey’s increasingly prominent role in Somalia. For now, however, the allegations remain contested and require independent verification. What is beyond dispute is the symbolism of the protest itself. In Garbaharey, residents did not simply chant their anger. They set fire to the symbols they associated with the power behind the operation—and in doing so, produced one of the most dramatic public expressions yet of Somalia’s deepening political and security divide. They set fire to the symbols they associated with the power behind the operation—and in doing so, produced one of the most dramatic public expressions yet of Somalia’s deepening political and security divide. items.title: Soomaaliya oo Daahfurtay Siyaasad Qaran oo Lagu Xoojinayo Ilaalinta Rayidka Xilliyada Hawlgallada Milatari
items.description: Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa daahfurtay Siyaasadda Qaranka ee Ilaalinta Rayidka Xilliyada Hawlgallada Milatari iyo Colaadaha Hubeysan, taas oo lagu xoojinayo ilaalinta nolosha, sharafta iyo xuquuqda dadka rayidka ah. Siyaasaddan waxaa si rasmi ah u daahfuray Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya, Axmed Macallin Fiqi, munaasabad ay ka qeybgaleen mas’uuliyiin ka tirsan dowladda federaalka iyo dowlad-goboleedyada, diblomaasiyiin iyo wakiillo ka socday hay’adaha ay khuseyso. Wasiir Fiqi ayaa sheegay in ilaalinta rayidka ay tahay waajib qaran iyo mid dastuuri ah, isaga oo xusay in siyaasaddan ay qeyb muhiim ah ka tahay dhismaha ciidan Soomaaliyeed oo xirfad leh, nidaamsan oo leh isla-xisaabtan. Siyaasadda cusub ayaa dowladda siinaysa hannaan lagu ilaalinayo dadka rayidka ah inta ay socdaan hawlgallada milatari iyo xilliyada colaadaha hubeysan, iyadoo xoogga la saarayo dhowrista sharciga, xuquuqda aadanaha iyo isla-xisaabtanka hay’adaha amniga. Daahfurka siyaasaddan ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli ciidamada dowladda Soomaaliya ay howlgallo ka dhan ah Al-Shabaab ka wadaan qaybo ka mid ah koonfurta iyo bartamaha dalka. Dowladdu waxay sheegtay in ilaalinta rayidka ay muhiim u tahay dhismaha nidaam amni oo ay hoggaaminayaan ciidamada Soomaaliyeed, gaar ahaan xilli masuuliyadda hawlgallada amniga ay si weyn ugu soo wareegeyso ciidamada dalka. Wasiirka Gaashaandhigga ayaa tilmaamay in siyaasaddan ay tallaabo muhiim ah u tahay xoojinta hay’adaha dowladda, ilaalinta xuquuqda shacabka iyo dadaallada lagu gaarayo nabad iyo amni waara. Dowladda Federaalka ayaa mar kale ku celisay inay ka go’an tahay ilaalinta rayidka iyo dhowrista xuquuqdooda inta lagu jiro hawlgallada milatari iyo xaaladaha colaadaha hubeysan.

items.title: Somaliland president Irro arrived in the US for meetings with US officals & international leaders
items.description: Somaliland president Irro arrived in the US for meetings with US officals & international leaders and maybe even a low key UN appearance as part of another countries Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Irro and the delegation accompanying him have arrived in #Washington, D.C., for an official working visit to the United States. The delegation was received at Dulles International Airport by Somaliland government officials led by the Minister of Foreign Affairs, who had arrived earlier, as well as members of the Somaliland diaspora and other diplomats. President Irro is expected to remain in the United States for nearly a month. During his visit, he is expected to hold meetings with senior U.S. officials and other international leaders and diplomats who will be in the United States for the United Nations General Assembly( which starts on september 8th). UN general assembly It is an ideal moment to meet many worldleaders in one place as it is custom for worldleaders to have many sidemeetings with other worldleaders during the UN general assembly whcih starts on september 8th. While Somaliland as a non Un member would on its own not be allowed at UN headquartersin New York, it can get access if a UN member invites him and some teammembers as guest delegation members, members like the US, Israel or UAE could do that. It would give the president and a small team access to the UN delegates lounge (perfect place for unplanned encounters and short talks between world leaders), or to closed side events and bilateral meeting rooms. Also the Somaliland delegation can meet with international figures outside the Un building. Likely he would avoid the main general assembly hall or plenary area to avoid a diplomatic scene if Somalia delegates spot him. Though UN rules allow his presence as apart of another countries delegation and being present on UN grounds does give the benefit his team (wearing the friendly nation’s badge) can scout the lounges first. Once they spot a target leader or a sympathetic foreign minister who is standing alone, they approach them, make the soft pitch, and say, “Our President is just around the corner and would love to say hello for two minutes.” If the leader agrees, the President is brought in for a quick chat, in which the president can try to pitch Somaliland ‘s case and lobby for follow up talks. First working trip to the USA The visit is his first official working trip to the United States since taking office. The visit comes at an important stage in Somaliland’s diplomatic campaign, with Hargeisa seeking to deepen its relations with Washington in the areas of diplomacy, security, economic cooperation and investment, while also advancing its international recognition efforts. It also comes after several high level diplomatic and military US delegations visiting Somaliland in 2025 and 2026. It also build on the work of several Us lawmakers like Us senator Ted Cruz, representatives Scott Perry, Tom Tiffany, Andy Ogles and senator Jim Risch who have advocated for diplomatic recognition in congress. Us interests would likely be in the areas of maritime securtiy, Us military base options (due to complication in Djibouti) and economic cooperation. Somalilands interest would likely be in areas of economic cooperation, access to global financial platforms, security cooperation and most importantly diplomatic recognition. Realistic expectations While sometimes countries can move quite fast like Israel on recogniton, more likely is the path of the UAE who has gradually built cooperation with Somaliland in the areas of trade, development, security and other areas. Given the fact a very recent Us State department report noted both strategic advanteges and opportunities somaliland has to offer it also emphasised, it also stated the US is still only recognising Somalia So i expect for now maybe a first agreement or mou on maritime security cooperation, maybe an mou to explore feasability of a Us base in somaliland or maybe a direct agremeent for a Us base in somaliland. And perhaps on exploring critical resources mining and processing as a core us interest abroad is securing critical resources. Dont see that as a failure,on the contrary any such agrement woudl alreayd be a major win. See them as stepping stones towards recognition which i expect not now but near the end of Trump’s term. As interests and cooperation grow over time that will be a logical point to reach in some years

items.title: Ciidamada Danab oo kor tegay maydadka 14 qof oo…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ciidanka Kumaandooska Danab ee Xoogga Dalka ayaa maanta howlgal qorsheysan ka fuliyay deegaanka Buula Fulaay ee gobolka Baay, halkaas oo ay ku dileen 14 xubnood oo ka tirsan kooxda Al-Shabaab, sida lagu sheegay war kasoo baxay taliska ciidamada xoogga dalka. Howlgalka ayaa lagu beegsaday fariisimo ay kooxda si qarsoodi ah uga sameysatay deegaanka, kuwaas oo la sheegay inay u adeegsanayeen abaabulka iyo qorsheynta howlgallada ay ka fuliyaan deegaannada ku dhow. Ciidanka ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in howlgalka lagu soo furtay hub fara badan oo ay kooxda ku heysatay fariisimaha la beegsaday. Wararka laga helayo howlgalka ayaa intaas ku daraya in ciidamadu ay dul tageen qaar ka mid ah meydadka xubnihii lagu dilay, taasoo muujineysa khasaaraha culus ee Al-Shabaab lagu gaarsiiyay howlgalka. Howlgalka ayaa qeyb ka ah howlgallada qorsheysan ee ciidamada Kumaandooska Danab ay ka fuliyaan deegaannada Gobolka Baay, iyagoo beegsanaya fariisimaha iyo goobaha ay ku dhuumaaleysanayaan xubnaha Khawaarijta. Ujeedka howlgalladan ayaa sidoo kale ah in lagu wiiqo awoodda kooxda, lagana hortago falalka amni-darro ee ay kooxda ka geysan karto deegaannada ay ku sugan yihiin. Dhinaca kale, Ilaa hadda ma jiraan faahfaahin dheeraad ah oo laga bixiyay khasaaraha dhinaca ciidamada ama dadka shacabka ah kasoo gaaray howlgalka. Baay ayaa kamid ah gobolllada ay ku xoogan tahay Khawaarijta waxaana badanaa ka dhacay dagaallo iyo duqeymo ay iska kaashadaan dowladda Soomaaliya iyo saaxibada caalamiga ah.
