items.title: Who Can Stop Me? The Collapse of Digital and Social Boundaries in Somali Society
items.description: By Abdulhakim A Sheik Somali society rebuilt itself after the state fell on trust, privacy and quiet mediation. A generation raised on the smartphones is now testing whether any of that still holds. Picture a house in Mogadishu, or Minneapolis, or Nairobi. A husband and wife are arguing — not violently, but badly, the way tired people argue about money and in-laws. One of them is holding a phone low against the hip. The screen is dark. It is recording. Weeks later, after the marriage has ended, the recording surfaces in a WhatsApp group. Within two days a diaspora commentator plays it on a livestream to tens of thousands of viewers, pausing for effect, inviting the audience to judge. Strangers write verdicts under a clip cut to make one person look worse than they were. The children hear their parents’ worst hour repeated back to them by classmates. This scene is illustrative rather than a report of any particular case. But its components — the secret recording, the group chat, the monetised commentary, the permanence — are no longer exotic. They have become a recognisable genre of Somali online life. The question this essay asks is not who behaved badly in that house. It is why so few limits now stand between a private disagreement and a global audience, and what a society loses when those limits disappear. What a boundary actually is A boundary is not a wall and it is not silence. It is an agreed limit that makes a relationship possible. Boundaries are what allow two people to disagree without destroying each other, and what allow a community to hold competing interests without collapse. They operate at several levels at once. Personal boundaries govern what a person will accept in their own body, time and attention. Family and marital boundaries govern what stays inside the house: the argument, the illness, the debt, the intimate detail. Social boundaries govern how disputes are raised and who is entitled to hear them. Digital boundaries govern what is captured, stored and transmitted. Religious and moral boundaries govern conduct even when no one is watching. Institutional boundaries — courts, schools, professional bodies, mediation councils — decide which conflicts belong in public and which do not. Somali society was never short of boundaries. Xeer, the customary legal tradition, is a boundary system. So is the elder who takes a dispute aside before it becomes a feud, and the aunt who tells a young couple that this conversation ends at her door. What has changed is not that Somalis stopped valuing limits. It is that a technology arrived which routes around every one of them, and no comparable institution arrived to replace what it dissolved. It is worth separating two things that are constantly confused in Somali online argument. A boundary is a limit a person accepts for themselves and negotiates with those closest to them. Censorship is a limit imposed by power on what other people may say. Asking a spouse not to record a private argument is a boundary. Asking the state to silence a critic is censorship. The two are not on the same spectrum, and treating every appeal to restraint as an attack on free speech is a category error that has cost Somali public life a great deal. The global problem, and why it lands harder here The strain is not uniquely Somali. The World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Europe, reporting on a survey of almost 280,000 adolescents across 44 countries, found that signs of problematic social media use — difficulty controlling use, withdrawal, neglect of other activities — rose from 7 per cent in 2018 to 11 per cent in 2022, and were more common among girls. That is a finding about Europe, Central Asia and Canada. There is no equivalent Somali dataset, and the absence is itself part of the argument: we are debating the effects of a technology on our children without having measured them. What we do know is suggestive. DataReportal put Somalia’s internet users at about 5.47 million in late 2025, roughly 28 per cent of the population, with some 3.51 million social media identities — a minority, but a fast-growing, urban and young one. United Nations Population Fund figures cite roughly 46 per cent of Somalis under 15 and about 75 per cent under 30. Put those together. A very young society is coming online quickly, into an information environment with weak regulation, little formal media-literacy instruction, and a state that spent three decades unable to perform the ordinary functions — schooling, licensing, adjudication, consumer protection — through which other societies slowly negotiate their relationship with new technology. Somalis did not get the twenty-year on-ramp. They got the smartphone. When influence replaces institutions Into that vacuum stepped the diaspora, for reasons that are not mysterious. Remittances are the country’s economic backbone: the United States Department of State’s 2025 investment climate report puts them near $2 billion a year, about a quarter of GDP, while IMF-based estimates run lower and informal hawala flows make precision impossible. Money, and with it prestige, flows in one direction. Interpretation followed the money. A man in Ohio explains national politics to people living inside the events he is describing. A woman in London models a standard of life her audience in Baidoa is invited to want and cannot reach. Guidance that ought to be practical — how to use what is actually available here — is replaced by aspiration toward a life that is elsewhere. Living abroad confers proximity to resources. It does not confer knowledge, emotional steadiness or ethical judgement, and it is not a qualification to guide a society. The platforms compound this, because they do not select for wisdom. They select for whatever holds attention, and outrage holds attention better than nuance does. Care is required here. It would be unkind and unfounded to diagnose individual creators or to claim that most influencers are unwell; personal struggle is not disqualifying, and public life has always included people carrying private pain. But the scale is new. A person working through loneliness, grief, a hunger for recognition or a conflicted sense of identity once affected a household. With a large and uncritical audience, the same person can make a coping style look like a value system. When a young Somali watches contempt rewarded with followers, the lesson learned is not about that individual. It is about what works. The serious question is not whether influencers are troubled. It is who is teaching young Somalis to use these tools at all — and the honest answer, in most families, is no one. The phone in the marriage Before a phone becomes a weapon inside a marriage, it has usually already become a wall. Consider the ordinary version, which is undramatic and therefore rarely discussed. A family sits down to eat. The father is half-watching a livestream from another continent. The mother is scrolling. The children are answering people they have never met. Nobody is arguing. Nobody is speaking either. Four people share a table while attending to four separate audiences, none of whom live in the house. Something has been inverted in that room. The people with the strongest claim on one another have become background, and strangers hold the foreground. The cost accumulates quietly, because a couple stops practising the small repairs that keep a marriage working — the aimless talk, the joke, the complaint raised early while it is still small enough to settle. Grievances that are never voiced do not dissolve. They arrive later at full size, in a household that has lost the habit of settling anything privately, and by then both partners have spent months watching other people’s conflicts performed for an audience. From being unable to talk to each other, it is a shorter step than it should be to recording each other. Legally married couples now record each other. Sometimes openly, as a threat; more often secretly, and the material is kept. It is then deployed: as leverage to force a decision, as a method of control, as punishment after separation, as material for public humiliation, and — increasingly — as content, because a marital collapse performs well. Researchers studying image-based abuse describe exactly this pattern. Nicola Henry and colleagues, examining victim-survivor accounts, found that nonconsensual images and recordings function less as “revenge” than as coercive control: surreptitious capture, threats to publish in order to stop a partner leaving, and the use of exposure to dominate rather than merely to retaliate. A multinational survey of more than 16,000 adults across ten countries, published in 2025, found that more than one in five respondents reported experiencing some form of image-based sexual abuse. This is a global phenomenon with a Somali expression, not a Somali invention. Two clarifications matter. First, this is not a male behaviour with female victims, nor the reverse. Men and women both do it, and any account that assigns it to one sex is describing a political preference rather than the situation. Second, not all recording is abuse. Documenting violence, threats or coercion in order to seek help or report to an authority is categorically different from harvesting material for leverage. The distinction is purpose and destination: evidence of harm goes to a trusted person, a mediator, a clinician, a lawyer or the police. It does not go to a feed. What the law permits varies by country and this essay offers no legal advice; anyone in danger should seek qualified help locally. Marriage in the Islamic understanding rests on trust, mercy, mutual protection and the covering of faults. Surveillance is the opposite of that. A spouse who is being recorded is not a spouse; they are a subject under management. And a household in which each partner holds a file on the other has already ended, whatever the paperwork says. Prayer is not the whole of the religion Most Somalis identify as Muslims and many pray five times a day. That is a real achievement, sustained through war and displacement. But it raises an uncomfortable question that this essay cannot avoid: why does so much devotion coexist with so much cruelty online? The question is not original to me. Writing in WardheerNews in August 2026, Dr. Abdurahman Baadiyow asked it at national scale — how a society attached to its religion could remain three decades in collapse — and suggested the fault lies in treating worship as an end in itself rather than as the means by which good people and a good society are formed. His image for it is unforgiving: devotion that yields no moral change is milk churned endlessly that never becomes butter. He reduces the matter to four words: “Has Islam transformed us?” This essay borrows his question and turns it toward a more focused, impactful newer arena — digital and social media. Read more: Who Can Stop Me? The Collapse of Digital and Social Boundaries in Somali Society Abdulhakim A Sheik Email: ahakimsheik7@gmail.com ————— Abdulhakim A Sheik is a software engineer and the author of Understanding Boundaries, part of the Social Development series. He writes on Somali society, ethics and public life.   The post Who Can Stop Me? The Collapse of Digital and Social Boundaries in Somali Society appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: UN Investigation Exposes Transnational Networks Fueling Sudan’s War
items.description: Geneva (WDN) — A new United Nations investigation has found that Sudan’s devastating war has expanded far beyond the country’s borders, with transnational networks operating across the United Arab Emirates, Colombia, Chad, Libya and Somalia allegedly facilitating the movement of fighters, weapons, military equipment, training and logistical support to forces involved in the conflict. The findings were published on September 3, 2026, by the UN Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan, which said it had found reasonable grounds to believe that a cross-border network had provided military support to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which has been fighting Sudan’s armed forces since April 2023. The alleged assistance includes weapons and ammunition, military equipment, training, logistical support and foreign military personnel. One of the report’s most significant findings concerns the recruitment and deployment of former Colombian military personnel. The investigators said hundreds—and potentially as many as 2,000—Colombian fighters were transported to Sudan to work with the RSF. Some were reportedly involved in operating drones, artillery and other advanced weapons systems used by the paramilitary force. The UN findings are consistent with earlier investigations by Human Rights Watch, which reported that an Abu Dhabi-based company recruited Colombian fighters, some of whom received training at facilities in the UAE before being deployed to Sudan. The network reportedly moved personnel through several countries before they reached the battlefield. The UAE has repeatedly denied allegations that it provides military, financial or logistical support to the RSF. Somalia’s Role in the Transit Network Somalia features prominently in the logistical routes identified by investigators, particularly through Bosaso, the commercial hub of Puntland. Human Rights Watch documented the case of a Colombian fighter who travelled from Colombia in 2025 using commercial flights and arrived in Bosaso. He reportedly remained there for approximately 10 days with a group of about 40 other fighters. He was subsequently transported to the United Arab Emirates, then to Chad, before ultimately reaching Nyala in South Darfur. The findings are significant because they place Somalia within a wider international logistics network connected to the Sudan conflict. However, the evidence cited does not establish that the Federal Government of Somalia officially supports the RSF. Rather, it indicates that Somali territory—particularly Bosaso—was allegedly used as a transit point by networks moving personnel toward Sudan. That distinction is important. Libya Route and Chad’s Strategic Position into Darfur Libya has also emerged as a major corridor into Darfur. According to the investigations, Colombian fighters were transported from the UAE by charter aircraft to Benghazi in eastern Libya before continuing overland through the desert toward Darfur. Earlier UN reporting has identified networks operating in southern Libya that facilitate the movement of fighters, weapons and other military supplies toward RSF-controlled areas. The vast and poorly controlled desert frontier has made the region particularly attractive to trafficking and military logistics networks. Chad also occupies a critical position in the network. Investigators found indications that fighters and military equipment moved through N’Djamena, Chad’s capital, before entering Sudan. The Amdjarass airport in eastern Chad has previously been identified as an important transit point for weapons and military supplies allegedly destined for the RSF. The Chadian government maintains that it is neutral in the Sudan conflict and has rejected accusations that it officially supports either side. The UAE at the Center of the Allegations Among the countries identified in the investigations, the United Arab Emirates occupies the most prominent position. The UN and Human Rights Watch have pointed to companies and individuals based in the UAE in connection with the recruitment, training and transportation of foreign fighters. Human Rights Watch has reported that some Colombian recruits received military training in the UAE before being sent to Sudan. The UAE has strongly rejected allegations that it provides military, financial, logistical or political support to the RSF. The competing claims underline the need for further independent investigation into the financing, recruitment and transportation networks sustaining the conflict. The UN Fact-Finding Mission said Sudan’s war has entered a new phase in which advanced weapons and unmanned aerial systems are playing an increasingly important role. Both sides have acquired the ability to conduct long-range attacks, contributing to civilian casualties and damage to critical infrastructure. More than 1,000 people were reportedly killed in drone attacks during the first six months of 2026, according to UN findings. Some attacks struck civilian locations and infrastructure, with investigators warning that certain incidents could constitute war crimes. The report does not place responsibility exclusively on the RSF. While much of the investigation focuses on external support to the RSF, the UN also found evidence that the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have received foreign military assistance. items.title: Jubaland Rejects Scholars Council Bill, Questions Parliament’s Authority to Proceed
items.description: Kismayo (WDN) — Jubaland’s Ministry of Endowments and Religious Affairs has rejected a proposed law establishing a Somali Council of Scholars, arguing that the bill could encroach on responsibilities exercised by Federal Member States and further strain Somalia’s federal system. In a statement, the ministry said the legislation, submitted by the Federal Ministry of Endowments and Religious Affairs, covers religious, cultural and social matters that Jubaland considers to fall within the responsibilities of the states. Jubaland maintains that these matters cannot be regulated at the national level without consultation with the Federal Member States, particularly where a proposed institution could overlap with existing state structures. A Parliament with an Expired Mandate The Federal Parliament’s mandate expired in April 2026, yet it continues to consider legislation with significant political and institutional implications. The Scholars Council bill has reportedly been before Parliament for approximately three years but was not advanced amid concerns over funding and the lack of consultation with the Federal Member States. Jubaland now questions the legitimacy of reviving the legislation under a parliament whose mandate has expired, particularly when the concerns that stalled the bill have not been resolved. Jubaland’s principal concern is that a national council responsible for religious affairs could create overlapping authority with institutions already operating within the Federal Member States. The ministry has called for the bill to be reviewed and discussed with the states before further legislative action is taken. The Federal Government, meanwhile, views the proposed council as a mechanism for coordinating Somali religious scholars and strengthening their role in national religious and social affairs. The disagreement comes amid broader tensions between Mogadishu and several Federal Member States over constitutional amendments, elections, security and the division of political authority. The proposed council has therefore become another test of Somalia’s federal arrangement: whether national institutions can be established unilaterally or must be developed through agreement between the Federal Government and the states. Legitimacy Before Legislation The central issue is not whether Somalia can benefit from a national body representing religious scholars. It is whether this particular bill can legitimately proceed under the current circumstances. Parliament’s mandate expired in April, while the legislation has remained unresolved for years because of funding and consultation concerns. Advancing it without addressing those issues risks creating another institutional dispute. Before proceeding, the authorities should establish the council’s legal foundation, clearly define its powers, resolve its financing and secure meaningful participation from the Federal Member States. That would provide a clearer basis for legislation while reducing the risk of another confrontation over federal authority. The dispute could become another flashpoint in Somalia’s broader political crisis if the Federal Government proceeds without addressing Jubaland’s objections. The proposed council may have a legitimate national purpose, but its creation must be consistent with Somalia’s federal structure. The immediate question is therefore simple: can a parliament whose mandate expired in April legitimately enact legislation that could reshape the relationship between the Federal Government and the states? Jubaland’s answer is no. The ministry has called for the bill to be reconsidered and subjected to a process that includes the Federal Member States before it moves forward. items.title: General Mahad Wounded in Doolow Strike as Turkey’s Somalia Role Comes Under Fire
items.description: Doolow, Gedo (WDN) — Former Somali Custodial Corps Commander General Mahad Abdirahman Adan, widely known as Taliye Shub, and his wife have been evacuated to Nairobi for medical treatment after sustaining injuries in an overnight attack on the house where they were staying in Doolow, Gedo region. The attack has immediately become politically explosive, with Jubaland officials, the national opposition and opposition forces in South West State accusing the Federal Government of targeting General Mahad and alleging that Turkish military aircraft or Turkish-supported capabilities were involved. Those allegations have not been independently verified. The Federal Government has categorically denied responsibility, saying preliminary information gathered by security agencies indicates that the explosions resulted from explosive materials allegedly being prepared inside the house. The government has also announced plans to establish a fact-finding committee to determine what happened, why it happened and who was responsible. The competing accounts have left a central question unanswered: Was General Mahad deliberately targeted, and if so, who ordered and carried out the attack? The residence of Gen. Mahad i n Doolow, after the strike General Mahad is regarded as one of the former Somali military officers associated with armed forces opposing the new administration installed by force by the FGS in South West State. Forces linked to or supported by General Mahad have recently been involved in military operations against the administration led by Speaker Sheikh Adan Mohamed Nur “Adan Madoobe”, which was installed amid a deeply contested political process in South West State. Fighting and armed confrontations have subsequently been reported in Baidoa and surrounding areas, turning the state into one of the most dangerous flashpoints in Somalia’s wider political crisis. General Mahad’s presence in Doolow and the attack on the residence where he was staying have therefore raised questions that the incident was connected to the broader political and military confrontation. Was It an Assassination Attempt? Opposition figures have characterized the attack as an attempted assassination, arguing that General Mahad was deliberately targeted because of his opposition to the Federal Government and the new South West administration. That claim remains proven beyond any doubt. The government’s competing explanation—those explosives inside the residence caused the incident—also is just not possible as the eye witnesses in Doolow confirm that it was a drone. The planned investigation will therefore face an important credibility test. If the government is to investigate allegations that itself have been involved in, the inquiry will need to be sufficiently transparent and independent to convince a deeply divided public. The identities of those killed or wounded, the type of weapon or explosive involved, the trajectory and point of impact, and the circumstances surrounding the residence should all be established through verifiable evidence. The controversy has also placed Turkey’s expanding military relationship with Somalia under unprecedented political scrutiny. Turkey has become one of Somalia’s most important security partners, providing military training, equipment and other forms of security assistance. But as Somalia’s political crisis has intensified, opposition groups increasingly accuse Ankara of abandoning its previously perceived neutrality and becoming too closely aligned with Villa Somalia. Jubaland, Puntland and South West opposition figures have alleged that Turkish military capabilities were involved in operations against their forces and have pointed specifically to Turkish aircraft and drones. These are no more allegations but have been independently established by civilians and government soldiers on the ground. Nevertheless, the political consequences are already significant. For a growing number of Somali opposition figures, Turkey is no longer being viewed simply as a strategic partner helping Somalia rebuild its security institutions. Instead, they increasingly portray Ankara as a government taking sides in Somalia’s internal political confrontation. That perception could become one of the most damaging consequences of Turkey’s current Somalia policy. Turkey’s Image Among Somalis Is Deteriorating Turkey once enjoyed considerable goodwill among Somalis, built partly through humanitarian assistance, infrastructure projects, diplomatic engagement and military cooperation. But that goodwill is now facing a serious political test. The more Turkey becomes identified with the policies and military actions of Villa Somalia, the more difficult it becomes for Ankara to maintain the image of an impartial friend of the Somali people. The opposition’s criticism is increasingly blunt: they accuse Turkey of abandoning neutrality and adopting what they describe as a colonial-style posture by siding with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s government. That accusation is not political rhetoric, but an established fact. But its growing circulation is important because international partnerships ultimately depend not only on government-to-government relations but also on public legitimacy. Somalis have historically been particularly sensitive to any foreign power perceived as attempting to dictate political outcomes or dominate national affairs. If Turkey is increasingly perceived as acting like an extension of Villa Somalia, its long-term relationship with Somali society could suffer regardless of the intentions behind its military partnership. The South West Crisis Could Become Turkey’s Diplomatic Graveyard South West State may now represent the biggest test of Turkish diplomacy in Somalia. The political confrontation in Baidoa has placed Ankara in an uncomfortable position. If Turkey is seen as supporting one side of a deeply disputed domestic political conflict, it risks losing the broader legitimacy it spent years building among Somalis. Turkey’s strategic interests in Somalia extend far beyond one administration or one political faction. A policy that produces short-term influence in Mogadishu could ultimately carry a much higher long-term cost if it alienates opposition forces, Federal Member States and large sections of the Somali public. The South West crisis could therefore become a defining moment for Turkey’s diplomatic legacy in Somalia. The most serious allegations concern armed drones and other sophisticated military capabilities associated with Turkey’s security partnership with Somalia. Opposition figures have questioned whether Turkish-supplied drones are being used in Somalia’s internal political conflicts and whether Turkish personnel based in Mogadishu could have operational knowledge or involvement in their deployment. There is currently no independently verified evidence establishing that Turkish drone operators participated in the Doolow attack but that Turkish drones were used to target General Mahad is verified by people in Doolow. But given the seriousness of the allegations, neither the Somali government nor Turkey should simply dismiss them. If Turkish military equipment was involved, the public deserves to know who authorized its use, under what command structure it was deployed and what safeguards exist to prevent foreign-supplied weapons from being used for domestic political purposes. The controversy also comes against the backdrop of Somalia’s broader constitutional and political crisis. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s government faces continuing disputes over the electoral process, relations with Federal Member States, constitutional changes and the legitimacy of the political roadmap being pursued by Villa Somalia. Critics therefore question why a foreign government would deepen its military relationship with an administration whose political legitimacy and electoral policies are being challenged by major Somali political actors. The question being increasingly asked in opposition circles is blunt: Why would Turkey risk its relationship with the Somali people by becoming so closely associated with one side of Somalia’s political struggle? For Ankara, this is no longer simply a question of military cooperation. It is becoming a question of diplomatic credibility. The danger facing Somalia is greater than any individual military operation. If political disputes increasingly become battles involving armed drones, military aircraft and heavily armed forces, the country risks replacing political competition with militarized confrontation. Somalia needs institutions capable of resolving political disputes through dialogue, constitutional procedures and credible elections. It does not need foreign military capabilities becoming associated with the elimination, intimidation or suppression of political opponents. If the allegations surrounding General Mahad prove false, an independent investigation should establish that clearly. If they prove true, those responsible—including anyone who ordered, facilitated or assisted the operation—should face accountability. The Federal Government has promised an investigation. The credibility of that investigation will depend on whether it answers the questions that matter most. Who carried out the attack? Was General Mahad the intended target? What weapon or explosive caused the damage? Where did it originate? Who authorized the operation? Were Turkish-supplied drones, aircraft or other military capabilities involved? Were Turkish personnel involved in any operational capacity? And why was General Mahad targeted, if he was deliberately targeted? These questions cannot be answered through political statements alone. They require evidence. A Critical Moment for Turkey General Mahad’s evacuation to Nairobi has transformed the Doolow incident into another major test for Somalia’s deeply divided political system—and for Turkey’s increasingly controversial role within it. Turkey still has an opportunity to demonstrate that its relationship with Somalia is with the Somali people and the Somali state, rather than with any individual president or political faction. That would require transparency, neutrality and a clear separation between legitimate national-security assistance and Somalia’s internal political disputes. Editor’s Analysis: If Ankara continues to be perceived as acting in concert with Villa Somalia, the political damage could extend far beyond President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s current administration. Turkey risks losing something much more valuable than influence in Mogadishu: the goodwill of the Somali people. For now, the Doolow attack remains surrounded by competing narratives. General Mahad and his wife are receiving treatment in Nairobi. The government denies responsibility. Opposition forces allege a deliberate attack. Turkey’s alleged role remains unproven in books but its posture as Villa Somalia is clear even to the blind. The only responsible path forward is an investigation capable of establishing the facts. Because in a country already struggling with political division, the perception that foreign military power is being used to settle domestic political disputes could be as destabilizing as the attack itself. items.title: Jubaland Accuses Turkey and Mogadishu of Turning Military Aid Against Somali Opponents
items.description: Doolow, Gedo (WDN) — Jubaland has accused Turkey and Somalia’s Federal Government of using military capabilities supplied for national defence to target political opponents, following an overnight airstrike in Doolow that wounded former Somali Custodial Corps Commander General Mahad Abdirahman Adan and four other civilians. In a strongly worded statement, Jubaland condemned what it described as a deliberate attack by Turkish military aircraft on the house where General Mahad was staying, alleging that the operation was politically motivated because of his opposition to the Federal Government. Jubaland said two missiles were fired during the attack, with one striking the residence of the Doolow district commissioner. General Mahad and four other civilians were reportedly wounded. The allegations have not been independently verified. The Federal Government has denied responsibility and offered a different account of the incident. But Jubaland’s accusation raises a much larger and potentially explosive question: Are foreign-supplied weapons and drones intended to defend Somalia being used instead to settle the country’s political disputes, intimidate opposition figures and impose the Federal Government’s will on Federal Member States? Jubaland argues that General Mahad was targeted not because he posed a security threat, but because he held political views opposed to President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration. That allegation places the Doolow strike within Somalia’s broader political confrontation, particularly the escalating dispute over South West State and the relationship between Villa Somalia and the Federal Member States. Jubaland maintains that General Mahad was deliberately targeted because of his political position and his opposition to the Federal Government. If independently established, such an operation would raise profound questions about the use of state military power against political opponents. The distinction between legitimate national security operations and politically motivated military action is critical in any functioning state. Turkey’s Military Role Under Scrutiny The most serious element of Jubaland’s statement is its direct accusation against Turkey. Ankara has become one of Somalia’s most important military partners, providing training, weapons, equipment, infrastructure and sophisticated military capabilities, including drones. Those capabilities are ostensibly intended to strengthen Somalia’s defence institutions and help the country combat terrorism and other security threats. Jubaland is now accusing the Turkish military relationship of being used for a very different purpose. Editor’s Analysis: If weapons, aircraft or drones supplied through Turkey’s security partnership with Somalia were used in a domestic political confrontation, it would represent a fundamental departure from the stated purpose of such assistance. Military equipment provided to strengthen a national security institution should not become an instrument for eliminating political opponents or coercing Federal Member States. That is an allegation that demands independent scrutiny—not simply competing statements from Mogadishu and its opponents. Somalia has received substantial international military assistance over the years on the understanding that it would be used to defend the country, combat armed extremist groups and strengthen national security institutions. The concern raised by Jubaland is whether that mandate is being stretched into the country’s internal political disputes. If advanced drones and military aircraft are deployed against Somali political actors rather than recognized security threats, the consequences could extend well beyond the Doolow incident. It could undermine confidence in Somalia’s security partnerships and create fears among Federal Member States that military assistance intended to protect the country could instead be turned against them. Jubaland Calls for International Scrutiny Jubaland called on the United Nations, African Union, IGAD, United States and European Union to closely examine what it described as Turkey’s increasingly controversial role in Somalia. The administration argues that Turkey’s involvement is no longer consistent with the interests of the Somali people or regional stability. The statement also called on the United Nations to reconsider the decision to lift the arms embargo on Somalia until there is what Jubaland considers a sufficiently accountable government and reliable safeguards over the use of internationally supplied weapons. That demand reflects a broader concern: who ultimately controls Somalia’s expanding arsenal of foreign-supplied military equipment, and what safeguards prevent its misuse? The controversy could reopen a debate that many international partners considered largely settled when Somalia’s arms embargo was lifted. The purpose of easing restrictions was to allow Somalia to develop stronger national security capabilities and eventually assume greater responsibility for its own defence. But greater access to weapons also requires greater accountability. If credible evidence emerges that internationally supplied weapons or military platforms are being used for political repression, attacks on civilians or coercion of Federal Member States, international partners would face difficult questions about the adequacy of their safeguards. The issue is therefore not simply whether Somalia should possess advanced military equipment. It is who controls that equipment, under what legal authority, for what purpose and with what accountability. A Blow to Turkey’s Mediation Credentials Jubaland also issued a significant diplomatic warning to Ankara. It said Turkey should no longer be regarded as a credible participant in efforts to mediate Somalia’s internal political disputes because, in Jubaland’s view, Ankara has demonstrated that it is aligned with one side. That could become a serious problem for Turkey. Turkey has invested heavily in presenting itself as a strategic partner, mediator and influential diplomatic actor in Somalia. But mediation requires at least a credible perception of neutrality. Editor’s Analysis: A country cannot easily serve as an impartial mediator while being accused of supplying—and allegedly operating—the military capabilities used against one side of Somalia’s political conflict. Even if Turkey rejects the allegation, the perception itself can damage its diplomatic standing. The Doolow incident comes at a particularly sensitive moment for Somalia.Relations between Villa Somalia and several Federal Member States have deteriorated sharply over political authority, elections, constitutional changes and control of security institutions. Against this backdrop, the alleged use of military power against figures aligned with opposing political forces would represent a dangerous escalation. Political disagreements that should be resolved through dialogue, constitutional mechanisms and elections could instead become increasingly militarized. That is precisely the scenario Somalia cannot afford. Federal Member States should not have to calculate whether disagreement with Mogadishu could expose their leaders, officials or communities to military pressure. Nor should foreign military partners become instruments through which one political centre imposes its authority on the rest of the country. What Must Now Be Established The competing accounts surrounding the Doolow attack require an investigation capable of establishing the facts. Among the questions that should be answered are: Was General Mahad deliberately targeted? What weapon caused the explosion? Was an aircraft or drone involved? Was Turkish-supplied military equipment used? Were Turkish personnel involved in operating or supporting the platform? Who authorized the operation? What was the legal basis for the strike? Why was the target selected? Were civilians knowingly placed at risk? These questions cannot credibly be resolved through political accusations alone. They require physical evidence, independent forensic examination, flight or operational records where available, and testimony from witnesses. Jubaland’s accusation goes beyond the fate of one former military commander. It raises a fundamental question about the future of Somalia’s security sector: Will foreign military assistance strengthen the Somali state—or strengthen whoever controls the government at a particular moment? That distinction is essential. Weapons supplied to Somalia should serve the national interest, not the political survival of an administration. Drones purchased or provided to combat terrorism should not become tools for settling political scores. Military partnerships should strengthen institutions, not enable one political faction to dominate its opponents. If the allegations surrounding Doolow are disproved, a credible investigation should establish that clearly. If they are substantiated, however, those responsible must be held accountable—including anyone who authorized, facilitated or participated in the operation. For Turkey, the stakes are equally high. Ankara must decide whether it wants to be remembered as a strategic partner that helped Somalia build a national security capability—or as a foreign power whose military assistance became entangled in Somalia’s internal political war. For Somalia, the choice is even more consequential. A country emerging from decades of conflict cannot build a stable state by turning weapons meant to defend the nation against its own political opponents. Military power must serve the Somali state—not whoever happens to control Villa Somalia. items.title: Somaliland: Our nation,  our choice, our future
items.description: I proudly stand with the people and countries that have chosen to build friendship and cooperation with Somaliland. I deeply respect and appreciate the people of Israel, the United Arab Emirates, and Taiwan. Your friendship, engagement, and willingness to work with Somaliland are deeply valued by many Somalilanders. To the people of Israel, the UAE, and Taiwan: you are our friends, and we welcome you with respect and appreciation. May our relationships continue to grow through cooperation, trade, investment, technology, development, and mutual respect. Somaliland is a peaceful society with its own people, institutions, territory, and aspirations. We believe that our people have the right to determine their own political future and to choose the international partners with whom we wish to build relationships. I strongly reject any government or political force that attempts to deny Somaliland this right or interfere with the relationships Somaliland chooses to establish—particularly the policies of the Government of Somalia and the Government of Turkey. Our message is simple: We choose friendship, not hostility. We choose cooperation, not confrontation. We choose peace, not war. And we will continue to stand for Somaliland’s sovereignty, dignity, and future. To all our friends around the world: thank you for standing with Somaliland. Somaliland first — our nation, our people, our choice, our future. Hamse Ibrahim

items.title: Kheyre oo eedeymo culus u jeediyay Xasan, dushana ka saaray dhacdadii Doolow
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ra’iisul Wasaarihii hore ee Soomaaliya Xasan Cali Kheyre ayaa si adag uga hadlay qaraxa ka dhacay hoyga uu magaalada Doolow ee gobolka Gedo ka degan yahay taliyihii hore ee ciidanka asluubta Soomaaliyeed, Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Taliye Shub). Kheyre ayaa sheegay in guriga Taliye Shub lagu bartilmaameedsaday duqeyn diyaaradeed, xilli dowladda ay sheegtay in qaraxa guriga ka dhacay uu ahaa mid ka dhashay waxyaabo qarxa oo lagu diyaarinayay guriga. Kheyre oo war-saxaafadeedka soo saaray ayaa sheegay inuu cambaareynayo waxa ka dhacay guriga taliyihii hore, isagoo mas’uuliyadeeda dusha u saaray Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh. Kheyre ayaa sheegay in dhacdadan ay tahay arrin aan laga aqbali karin siyaasadda iyo dowladnimada Soomaaliya. “Waxaan si adag u cambaareynayaa duqeynta uu taliska uu hoggaamiyo Madaxweyne hore Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud xalay ku weeraray hoyga uu magaalada Doolow ka deggan yahay taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliyeed Janaraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan,” ayuu yiri Kheyre. Waxa uu intaas kusii daray “Waa ayaandarro iyo dhaqan ugub ku ah dowladnimada Soomaaliya in taliska Madaxweynaha waqtigiisu dhammaaday uu weerarka iyo duqeynta madaxdii u soo shaqeysay qarankan u adeegsanayo hubkii iyo diyaaradihii loogu deeqay Soomaaliya, si loogu adeegsado la-dagaallanka argagaxisada arxanka-daran.” Ra’iisul Wasaarihii hore ayaa xusay in taariikhda Soomaaliya ay muujineyso in khilaafaadka siyaasadeed aan lagu xallin karin awood ciidan, dagaal iyo isku day lagu caburinayo dhinacyada siyaasadda, isagoo ka digay in sii socoshada xaaladdan ay dalka u horseedi karto khasaare hor leh. “Xalka khilaafaadka siyaasadeed marnaba kuma jirin dagaal, ismaquunin iyo ku-takri-falka awoodda dowladnimada,” ayuu yiri Kheyre oo ku baaqay in laga fogaado tallaabo kasta oo sii hurin karta colaadda siyaasadeed. Sidoo kale, Kheyre ayaa sheegay in Soomaaliya aysan xilligan u baahnayn dagaallo siyaasadeed oo sababi kara kala-fogaansho bulsho iyo xasillooni-darro amni, wuxuuna ku baaqay in dhinacyada siyaasadda ay doortaan waddo nabadeed oo lagu wajahayo khilaafaadka jira. Wuxuu ku adkeystay in wada-hadal dhab ah, is-afgarad siyaasadeed iyo heshiis ku saabsan doorasho loo dhan yahay ay yihiin waddada looga gudbi karo xaaladda siyaasadeed ee dalka. Ugu dambeyntiina, Kheyre ayaa sheegay in Soomaaliya ay u baahan tahay doorasho “xor iyo xalaal ah” oo heshiis lagu yahay, si dalka uu u helo hoggaan leh sharciyad buuxda iyo kalsoonida shacabka Soomaaliyeed. items.title: Majaladda Foreign Policy ayaa ku baaqday in Maraykanku aqoonsado Somaliland
items.description: Majaladda Foreign Policy ayaa ku baaqday in Maraykanku aqoonsado Somaliland, iyadoo sheegtay in Hargeysa ay Washington u tahay fursad muhiim ah oo dhinaca istiraatiijiyadda iyo amniga ah. Maqaalka ayaa tilmaamaya in Somaliland ay ku taallo meel muhiim ah oo u dhow Gacanka Cadmeed iyo Badda Cas, halkaas oo danaha Maraykanka ay si weyn ugu xidhan yihiin ilaalinta maraakiibta iyo la tacaalidda khatarta Xuutiyiinta iyo Iran. Foreign Policy waxay si gaar ah u xustay Dekedda Berbera iyo garoonka diyaaradaha, iyadoo sheegtay in Somaliland ay Maraykanka siin karto meel muhiim ah oo uu kaga daba-galo dhaqdhaqaaqa Xuutiyiinta, isla markaana marka loo baahdo cadaadis lagu saaro Xuutiyiinta iyo IRGC-da Iran. Majaladdu waxay qiratay in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu keeni karo cadho iyo diidmo kaga timaadda Turkey, Masar iyo Sucuudiga, oo ah dalal Maraykanku xidhiidh la leeyahay. Hase yeeshee, qoraagu wuxuu ku dooday in saddexdan dal aanay xaq u lahayn inay go’aamiyaan siyaasadda Maraykanka. Wuxuu sheegay in danaha waaweyn ee Washington sida ka hortagga Iran iyo Xuutiyiinta iyo ilaalinta xorriyadda maraakiibta ay ka muhiimsan yihiin walaacyada dalalkaasi qabaan. Dhanka kale wargayska ayaa sheegay, in ay jiraan waxyaabo Somaliland lafteedu ay leedahay oo ay Washington u soo bandhigi karto. Wargeyska ayaa ugu dambayn si cad ugu baaqaya Washington inay ka tanaasusho siyaasadda ku dhisan ilaalinta midnimada dhuleed ee Soomaaliya, isla markaana ay Somaliland u aqoonsato dal madax-bannaan. MMTV

Foreign Policy waxay si gaar ah u xustay Dekedda Berbera iyo garoonka diyaaradaha, iyadoo sheegtay in Somaliland ay Maraykanka siin karto meel muhiim ah oo uu kaga daba-galo dhaqdhaqaaqa Xuutiyiinta, isla markaana marka loo baahdo cadaadis lagu saaro Xuutiyiinta iyo IRGC-da Iran. Majaladdu waxay qiratay in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu keeni karo cadho iyo diidmo kaga timaadda Turkey, Masar iyo Sucuudiga, oo ah dalal Maraykanku xidhiidh la leeyahay. Hase yeeshee, qoraagu wuxuu ku dooday in saddexdan dal aanay xaq u lahayn inay go’aamiyaan siyaasadda Maraykanka. Wuxuu sheegay in danaha waaweyn ee Washington sida ka hortagga Iran iyo Xuutiyiinta iyo ilaalinta xorriyadda maraakiibta ay ka muhiimsan yihiin walaacyada dalalkaasi qabaan. Dhanka kale wargayska ayaa sheegay, in ay jiraan waxyaabo Somaliland lafteedu ay leedahay oo ay Washington u soo bandhigi karto. Wargeyska ayaa ugu dambayn si cad ugu baaqaya Washington inay ka tanaasusho siyaasadda ku dhisan ilaalinta midnimada dhuleed ee Soomaaliya, isla markaana ay Somaliland u aqoonsato dal madax-bannaan. items.title: Turkey accused of war crime after drone strike on former Somali commander
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – A drone strike tore through the residence of General Mahad Abdirahman, Somalia’s former custodial corps chief, in the border town of Dolow on Thursday, and he survived it – but the attack has ignited a political firestorm, with Jubaland authorities pointing at Turkey and warning that a dangerous new front has opened in Somalia’s fracturing security landscape. A video circulating online showed the general receiving treatment at a hospital in the Ethiopian side of Dolow, the twin town separated from its Somali counterpart by the border. A retaliatory strike, hours after Baidoa attack The strike came only hours after Darwish forces loyal to ousted Southwest State President Abdiasis Laftagaren stormed the city of Baidoa on Thursday morning, overrunning army bases and briefly seizing parts of the city’s neighborhoods before fierce clashes. General Mahad is reported to be the backbone of Laftagaren’s resistance against the federal government, which seized Baidoa in a late-March offensive backed from the air by the Turkish air force. He is also Laftagaren’s father-in-law and a prominent figure commanding wide support among the population of Baidoa. The drone strike on his home is reported to be a retaliatory response to Thursday’s assault on Baidoa – a city that has become a battleground since Laftagaren’s ouster, with local forces under new Southwest leader Adan Madobe and federal troops unable to stop the guerrilla-style attacks that keep hitting the town. “Crossing into a very dangerous territory” Adam Aw Hirsi, Somalia’s former minister of state for environment and climate change, condemned the strike in sharp terms. “This is crossing into a very dangerous territory. I do not think the decision to initiate this attack was wise,” he said. He went further, warning that the episode could set off a cycle of retaliation across Somalia’s fractured political map: “If it is confirmed that foreign drones (Somalia has none) at the behest of @TheVillaSomalia attacked a general’s residence in Dollow, give it less than a year before you hear a drone belonging to an FMS or a clan in hinterland Somalia has struck a foreign embassy in Mogadishu.” “Foreigners involved in this need to reassess,” he added. “Somalis are a tough nut to scare. And you are not without competition in this game. Calculate the benefit of one man’s one-day thrill against the alienation of an entire people and squandering their goodwill.” Jubaland points to a Turkish drone, alleges war crime Jubaland State, which administers Dolow, said the strike was carried out by a Turkish drone. The regional administration described the act as a war crime and said it illustrates the dangerous direction in which President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and Turkey are jointly steering Somalia. Jubaland – which is at odds with Mogadishu and has repeatedly clashed with federal forces – said Turkey cannot position itself as part of international efforts to resolve Somalia’s political crisis while conducting such strikes, and it called on international stakeholders to intervene urgently before the fallout unravels the broader political process. Former presidents accuse Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of reckless force Former Somali Presidents Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and Mohamed Abdullahi Farmajo both condemned the attack. They accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of using reckless force through foreign powers to pressure his opponents, characterizing the strike as part of a pattern of assassination attempts against political rivals. Mogadishu distances itself, cites explosives inside the house The federal government distanced itself from the air raid, saying an initial investigation indicates the blast was triggered by explosives planted inside the house. It did not say whether Turkey carried out the attack. Turkey itself has not commented on the allegations. What residents heard and saw Despite Mogadishu’s denial of a drone strike, residents in Dolow told local media they heard the sound of a drone and saw a flash of light in the sky before a missile, apparently fired from above, struck the ground with a loud bang. They said the drone’s sound was heard again after the strike. The strike reportedly targeted with precision the room where General Mahad usually sleeps. He was not inside the room when it was hit. Part of a wider pattern of accusations against Ankara Turkey has faced mounting accusations in recent months of siding unreservedly with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud in his political disputes, a departure from what had long been an international norm under which partners supported Mogadishu on counterterrorism but stayed out of its politicians’ internal disagreements. Ankara has been accused of carrying out deadly drone strikes against Southwest Darwish forces near Baidoa. It has also been linked to suicide drone strikes on buildings housing former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed and former Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire, which came under attack from federal government forces during two days of fighting in Mogadishu in early June. Turkey was further accused of killing 14 civilians in Puntland State under the stated justification of an anti-piracy operation. Ankara has not commented on any of these accusations. Analysts warn Somalia risks becoming a foreign battleground Somali analysts and politicians say the country could soon become a proxy battleground for foreign powers, and that it would not come as a surprise if international partners aligned with various regional states began launching their own drone strikes on government offices in Mogadishu – now that Turkey, in their view, has set the precedent. Former Somali intelligence chief Fahad Yasin drew a historical parallel, calling the strike as dangerous a turning point as the 2006 car bomb attack on President Abdullahi Yusuf Ahmed in Baidoa – the first such explosive attack on a Somali official. He said Friday’s drone strike marks the first drone attack on a former Somali security official who had served the state for a long time. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: Soomaaliya iyo Cumaan oo markii ugu horreysay si toos ah la isugu xiray
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Duulimaad toos ah oo cusub oo isku xiraya magaalooyinka Muqdisho iyo Muscat ee caasimadda dalka Cumaan ayaa si rasmi ah u bilowday, iyadoo Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ay soo dhaweysay duulimaadkii ugu horreeyay ee shirkadda diyaaradaha SalamAir. Duulimaadkan ayaa loo arkaa tallaabo cusub oo fududeynaysa isku socodka dadka iyo ganacsiga Soomaaliya iyo Cumaan, iyadoo shacabka labada dal ay heli doonaan adeeg duulimaad oo toos ah oo isku xiraya labada caasimadood. Munaasabadda lagu daah-furay duulimaadka cusub ayaa waxaa ka qayb-galay Wasiirka Gaadiidka iyo Duulista Rayidka Soomaaliya, Maxamed Faarax Nuux iyo Wasiir ku-xigeenka Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga, Xasan Maxamed Cali (Nadaara). Duulimaadkan cusub ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli uu sii xoogeysanayo xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed iyo iskaashiga u dhexeeya Soomaaliya iyo Cumaan, gaar ahaan kaddib booqashadii uu Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda Soomaaliya ku tagay magaalada Muscat bishii April. Sidoo kale, magacaabista Danjiraha cusub ee Cumaan u fadhiya Soomaaliya ayaa ka mid ah tallaabooyinka muujinaya dadaallada labada dal ay ku xoojinayaan xiriirkooda iyo iskaashiga dhinacyada kala duwan. Wasiir ku-xigeenka Arrimaha Dibadda, Xasan Maxamed Cali (Nadaara) ayaa soo dhaweeyay wafdiga shirkadda SalamAir, isagoo sheegay in Soomaaliya ay ka go’an tahay xoojinta iskaashi wax-ku-ool ah oo sidoo kale u adeegaya dadka safarka ah, isla markaana fursado cusub u abuuraya ganacsiga. Waxaa sidoo kale la filayaa in duulimaadka tooska ah uu kaalin ka qaato fududeynta isu-socodka bulshada iyo ganacsatada labada dal iyo kor u qaadista fursadaha ganacsi iyo dalxiis ee Soomaaliya iyo Cumaan, iyadoo labada dhinac ay yihiin dalal xiriir taariikhi ah iyo mid dhaqan wadaaga. The post Soomaaliya iyo Cumaan oo markii ugu horreysay si toos ah la isugu xiray appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: 5 EU nations agree on model to send rejected migrants to ‘return hubs’ as early as 2027
items.description: Denmark and four other European Union countries agreed Friday on a model for “return hubs” in non-EU nations and hope to begin sending migrants to the facilities as early as 2027, an official said Friday. The announcement, made after a one-day meeting in Copenhagen, is the latest development in an effort by EU states to send people whose asylum requests have been rejected to third countries outside the bloc. “We are moving forward toward what is actually a fundamental transformation of the common European migration and asylum system,” said Morten Bødskov, Denmark’s minister of immigration and integration. He briefed reporters alongside counterparts from Germany, the Netherlands, Austria and Greece. The five countries have been negotiating with governments mainly in Africa over potential sites, pioneering the initiative for the whole of the EU. Human rights groups have criticized plans to deport migrants to centers or prisons in third countries, arguing that European nations cannot guarantee their rights will be respected there. Bødskov rejected the idea that “return hubs” were a euphemism for detention and deportation centers and said the International Organization for Migration and the UN Refugee agency would monitor the centers. “We are not talking about camps, we are talking about opportunities, for a new chance for irregular migrants who cannot return to their own country today and who have no legal grounds to be in our countries,” Bødskov said. The UNHCR told The Associated Press that it “has not been approached with details of such a proposal,” and therefore “cannot comment on the specific arrangements being discussed or on what any potential role for UNHCR might entail.”  ‘Return hubs’ abroad would be first for EU migration policy Although the ministers did not specify which third countries were being considered, Bødskov said they expect to reach their first deal by early 2027. He acknowledged that the concept of “return hubs” was mocked only a few years ago and deemed incompatible with EU and international law. EU laws, however, have changed due to public and political pressure for tougher measures against irregular migration. European lawmakers voted  in June to allow member states to set up centers outside the EU on their own or in small coalitions, and send rejected asylum seekers there instead of to their home countries. “This is something new and it’s groundbreaking,” said Bart van den Brink, the Netherlands’ minister of asylum and migration. Rwanda in negotiations with European nations In early August, a spokesperson for the Rwandan government said it “was natural” for her government to negotiate with European countries and others to potentially host asylum seekers who are not allowed to live elsewhere. Speaking to Royal FM Kigali, Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo cited an emergency transit mechanism established in Gashora in 2018 for people evacuated from Libya, who could stay there until they were resettled in third countries. Bottom of Form Makolo said one of the ideas discussed was to offer a “safe place” where people who have nowhere else to go could get medical care, training and rest while their asylum applications were processed, until they could go back home if safe or get resettled to yet another country. “We want to be part of a solution to a big global problem,” Makolo said. It remained unclear what countries in negotiations with EU nations would gain in return for taking Europe’s rejected migrants. Rights groups concerned about enforcement of law outside EU Migrant rights groups have criticized European efforts to set up migrant centers abroad where it may be difficult to monitor and enforce human rights. In an emailed statement, Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights, Michael O’Flaherty, said “vague assurances of compliance with human rights law are not enough.” “States need to commit to the guardrails necessary to prevent setting up human rights black holes,” he said. The European ministers in Copenhagen emphasized the new hubs would abide by European and international law. Van den Brink, the Dutch immigration minister, said technical talks and missions to potential partner countries would be used “to gain more insight into the human rights situation and the living conditions of the refugees.” “Because we want to do this in a European way, in line with our values and international law and human rights at its core.” Brussels-based rights group PICUM condemned the meeting in Copenhagen. “EU leaders may call these centers an “innovative solution,” but outsourcing migration control is an old tactic to simply move people out of sight and evade human rights obligations,” group director Michele LeVoy said. Ciobanu reported from Warsaw, Poland, and Brito reported from Barcelona, Spain. Philipp Jenne in Vienna and Sam McNeil in Brussels contributed to this report. Source: AP The post 5 EU nations agree on model to send rejected migrants to ‘return hubs’ as early as 2027 appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Muxuu Farmaajo ka yiri qaraxa guriga Taliye SHUB?
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynihii hore ee Soomaaliya, Maxamed Cabdullaahi Farmaajo ayaa ka hadlay qaraxa ka dhacay guriga Taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliya, Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub), kaasi oo dowladda ay sheegtay inuu ahaa mid ka dhashay waxyaabo qarxa oo lagu diyaarinayay guriga, halka garabyada mucaaradka ay sheegeen inay aheyd duqeyn lala beegsaday. War-saxaafadeed uu soo saaray madaxweynihii hore ayaa wuxuu eedeymo ugu jeediyay dowladda Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud oo uu sheegay inay bartilmaameedsatay hoyga uu degmada Doolow ka deggenaa Jananku. “Caafimaad degdeg ah ayaan Alle u weydiinayaa Janaraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan oo kamid noqday Baarlamaanka 11-aad ee JFS, ahaana taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliyeed oo dhaawac ka soo gaaray weerar duqayn ah oo loo adeegsaday DRONE, kaas oo uu nidaamka muddo dhaafka ah ee Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ku bartilmaameedsaday hoygiisa,” ayuu yiri Farmaajo. Waxa uu intaas kusii daray “Weerarkan foosha xun ee lagu qadaay hoyga Janaraal Mahad, oo muddo dheer usoo adeegayey Qaranka Soomaaliyeed waxa uu dhaawac ku yahay dowlad-dhiska dalka iyo dadaallada dib u heshiinta shacabka Soomaaliyeed, waana fal bahalnimo ah oo ay tahay inaan cod midaysan ku diidno.” Farmaajo ayaa dhacdo ugub ah ku tilmaamay waxa ka dhacay guriga Taliye Shub, isagoo Xasan Sheekh ku eedeeyay beegsiga siyaasiyiinta ka aragtida duwan. “Waa dhacdo ugub ah in beegsi noocan ah uu Madaxweynaha muddo xileedkiisu dhammaaday u adeegsado siyaasiyiinta ka arragtida duwan, waxayna tallaabadan gurracani dalka dib ugu celinaysaa kala irdhowgii siyaadadeed ee dhaawacay kalsoonida shacabka Soomaaliyeed,” ayuu Farmaajo ku yiri war-saxaafadeedka. Sidoo kale, Farmaajo ayaa sheegay in mashaakilka ka taagan dowlad-goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed ay tahay in loo maro wadada wada-hadalka iyo dib-u-heshiisiinta, isla markaana xalkeedu uusan ku imaan karin khaarajin siyaasadeed, sida uu hadalka u dhigay “Mashaakilka ka taagan Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed waa mid siyaasadeed oo u baahan in loo maro wadada wadahadalka iyo dib u heshiisiinta, xalkeeduna kuma imaan karo khaarajin siyaasadeed (Political Assassination).” Ugu dambeyntiina wuxuu ku baaqay in baaris deg-deg ah oo madax-bannaan lagu sameeyo waxa ka dhacay guriga Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub). items.title: Fahad Yaasiin oo isku xiray dhacdada Doolow iyo tii Cabdullaahi Yuusuf ee 2006
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Taliyihii hore ee hay’adda NISA, Fahad Yaasiin Xaaji Daahir ayaa isku xiray qarax ka dhacay guriga Taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliya, Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub) oo ku yaalla Doolow iyo weerarkii 2006 lagu qaaday madaxweynihii hore Cabdullaahi Yuusuf Axmed. Fahad Yaasiin ayaa qoraal uu soo saaray ku xusay in dhacdada Doolow ay yeelan karto saameyn ballaaran, isagoo barbar-dhigay dhacdadii Baydhabo ee bishii Sebtembar 2006, xilligaas oo gaari laga soo buuxiyay walxaha qarxa lala beegsaday Cabdullaahi Yuusuf. “Gaarigii qaraxa ahaa ee lala beegsaday Madaxweyne Cabdullaahi Yuusuf waxaa ka dhashay isbeddallo saameyn weyn ku yeeshay dalka 20-kii sano ee la soo dhaafay,” ayuu yiri Fahad Yaasiin. Fahad ayaa sheegay in waxa ka dhacay guriga Taliye Shub uu ahaa weerar diyaaradda aan duuliyaha lahayn ay geysatay, kaasi oo uu sheegay inuu horseedi karo saameyn ka gudubta xuduudaha Soomaaliya. “Diyaaradda Drone-ka ah ee lagu weeraray guriga Taliye Mahad Cabdiraxmaan ee Doolow waxaa ka dhalan doonta saameyn halis ah oo dalka iyo waddamada deriska ah ku sii faafi karta. Wadaac Alla,” ayuu ku yiri qoraalkiisa. Sidoo kale, Fahad Yaasiin ayaa si toos ah u weeraray nidaamka Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, oo uu ku eedeeyay inuu “xuduud kasta dhaafay”, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. “Nidaamka Xasan Sheekh xuduud kasta wuu dhaafay, waxaana khasab ah in dib loogu laabto hannaanka amniga qaranka oo idil,” ayuu yiri Fahad Yaasiin. Hadalkan ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli weli ay taagan tahay dood xooggan oo ka dhalatay qaraxa Doolow, iyadoo dowladda ay sheegtay inuu ahaa mid ka dhashay waxyaabo qarxa oo lagu diyaarinayay guriga, halka siyaasiyiin iyo madax hore ay sheegeen inay aheyd duqeyn lala beegsaday guriga Jeneraal Mahad Shub. The post Fahad Yaasiin oo isku xiray dhacdada Doolow iyo tii Cabdullaahi Yuusuf ee 2006 appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Sheekh Shariif: Xasan Sheekh waxa uu si cad ugu bareeray shirqoolo siyaasadeed
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynihii hore ee Soomaaliya, Shariif Sheekh Axmed ayaa sheegay in Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya uu si cad ugu bareeray shirqoolo siyaasadeed xilli uu maanta si adag u cambaareeyay qarax ka dhacay guriga Taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliyeed, kaasi oo dowladda ku sheegtay inuu ahaa mid ka dhashay waxyaabo qarxa oo lagu diyaarinayay guriga, halka garabyada mucaaradka ay ku doodeen inay aheyd duqeyn lala beegsaday. Shariif ayaa sheegay in dhacdada guriga Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub) ay tahay tii ugu dambeysay ee shirqooladda siyaasadeed ee Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh uu sida weyn u abaabulay, sida uu ku yiri war-saxaafadeed uu soo saaray. “Kani waa fal-dambiyeed abaabulan oo loogu talagalay in lagu khaarajiyo taliyihii hore ee ciidanka Booliska Asluubta Soomaaliyeed Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan,” ayuu Shariif ku yiri qoraalkiisa. Sidoo kale waxa uu nasiib-darro ku tilmaamay “in markii uu fashilmay hadafkii laga lahaa” ay dowladdu isku-daydo in bulshada marin habaabiso, si looga dhuunto xilkasnimada darrada ficilkaas guracan. Shariifka ayaa ka tacsiyeeyay khasaaraha naf iyo maalba leh ee ka dhashay qaraxaan, isagoo ka digay sii socoshada tallaabooyin uu sheegay inay abuurayaan mahadhooyinka bulshada dhexdeeda, isla markaana dhaawacaya kalsoonida taageerada saaxiibada caalamiga ee ku aadan dib u dhiska hay’addaha ammaanka dalka. “Waxaan hay’addaha ammaanka qaranka xusuusinayaa in la soo gaaray marxalad halis badan, oo ay khasab ku tahay inaysan habayaratee ku lug yeelan arrimaha siyaasadda ee cakiran,” ayuu yiri Shariifka. Hoos ka aqriso war-saxaafadeedka oo dhameystiran: Nidaamka muddo xileedkiisu dhammaaday ee Madaxweynaha hore, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud wuxuu si cad ugu bareeray shirqoolo siyaasadeed oo si weyn loo abaabulay, waxaana ugu dambeeyay duullaanka dhinaca cirka ah ee xalay ka dhacay Degmada Doolow ee gobolka Gedo. Kani waa fal-dambiyeed abaabulan oo loogu talagalay in lagu khaarajiyo taliyihii hore ee ciidanka Booliska Asluubta Soomaaliyeed Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan. Waxaa nasiib-darro ah, in markii uu fashilmay hadafkii laga lahaa duqeyntaas wuxuushnimada ahayd uu nidaamka muddo dhaafka ah isku-dayayo inuu bulshada marin habaabiyo si looga dhuunto xilkasnimada darrada ficilkaas guracan. Waxaan ka tacsiyeynayaa khasaaraha naf iyo maalba leh ee ka dhashay weerarkan bahalnimo, waxaana ka digayaa sii socoshada tallaabooyinka nuucaan ah ee abuuraaya mahadhooyinka bulshada dhexdeeda isla markaana dhaawacaya kalsoonida taageerada caalamiga ee ku aadan dib dhiska hay’adaha ammaan dalka. Ugu dambayn, waxaan hay’addaha ammaanka qaranka xusuusinayaa in la soo gaaray marxalad halis badan, oo ay khasab ku tahay inaysan habyaratee ku lug yeelan arrimaha siyaasadda ee cakiran. items.title: Madaxweyne Cirro waxa ay booqashadiisu salka ku haysaa sidii uu aqoonsi u helilahaa dalkiisu
items.description: Sida ay qortay jariiradda caanka ah ee The Economist, Madaxweynaha Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro), ayaa booqanaya Washington si uu Maraykanka ugu qanciyo inuu aqoonsado Somaliland. Maqaalka The Economist waxa lagu xusay muhiimadda Somaliland ay u leedahay gobolka, gaar ahaan Marinka Bab al-Mandab, oo ah marin muhiim u ah maraakiibta ganacsiga adduunka, kaas oo muddooyinkii dambe ay khatar ku hayeen Xuutiyiinta Yemen. Madaxweyne Cirro ayaa laga yaabaa inuu Maraykanka u soo bandhigo isticmaalka saldhigyo milatari oo ku yaalla Somaliland, kuwaas oo Washington u fududayn kara inay wax ka qabato khatarta Xuutiyiinta, sida lagu sheegay warbixinta The Economist. Madaxweyne Cirro ayaa haatan ku rajo weyn inuu arrinta aqoonsiga Somaliland si fool-ka-fool ah ugu bandhigo Madaxweynaha Maraykanka, Donald Trump.

items.title: DF Soomaaliya oo war ka soo saartay dhacdada guriga taliye SHUB, shaacisayna…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa iska fogeysay beegsiga guriga Taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliya, General Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub), iyadoo sheegtay in baaris dhab ah ku sameynayso dhacdadan. War-saxaafadeed lasoo baxay Wasaaradda Warfaafinta Soomaaliya ayaa lagu sheegay in dowladda inaysan wax lug ah ku lahayn dhacdadaasi, iyadoo sheegtay in xogaha horudhaca ah ee ay helayaan hay’adaha amniga muujinayaan in qaraxyadu ay ka dhasheen waxyaabo qarxa oo lagu diyaarinayay guriga. Dowladda ayaa sheegtay inay si degdeg ah u magacaabi doonto guddi xaqiiqo-raadin ah oo baaritaan dhab ah oo dhammaystiran ku sameeya dhacdada, ujeeddadii laga lahaa iyo cidda ka dambaysay. “Degmada Doolow waxay ka mid tahay deegaannada muhiimka u ah amniga iyo isku-socodka gobolka Gedo. Sidaas darteed, Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya waxay mudnaan gaar ah siinaysaa ilaalinta xasilloonida degmada iyo badqabka shacabka ku nool,” ayaa lagu yiri war-saxaafadeedka kasoo baxay wasaaradda. Sidoo kale, Dowladda Federaalka ayaa ka digtay in aan lagu kadsoomin warar ay ku tilmaamtay been abuur, kuwaas oo ka hordhacaya baaritaanka, isla markaana loogu tala-galay in lagu jahwareeriyo shacabka Soomaaliyeed, sida ay sheegtay wasaaradda. “Dowladda waxay caddeynaysaa in natiijada baaritaanka lala wadaagi doono shacabka marka uu soo dhammaado,” ayaa ugu dambeyntiina lagu yiri war-saxaafadeedka wasaaradda warfaafinta Soomaaliya. War-saxaafadeedka dowladda ayaa imanaya xilli maamulka Jubaland uu Dowladda Federaalka iyo Turkiga ku eedeeyay inay ka dambeeyeen duqeyn uu sheegay in lala beegsaday guriga Taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliya, General Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub). Jubaland ayaa ku eedeysay Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya inay taliye Shub u bartilmaameedsatay kaliya inuu ka aragti duwanaaday dhinaca siyaasadda. Maamulka ayaa sidoo kale wuxuu Qaramada Midoobay ugu baaqay inay sida ugu dhaqsaha badan dib ugu eegto go’aankii Soomaaliya lagaga qaaday cuna-qabateynta hubka, “inta laga helayo dowlad mas’uul ah iyo gacmo lagu aamini karo hubka ay dowladaha caalamku ugu deeqayaan Soomaaliya.” The post DF Soomaaliya oo war ka soo saartay dhacdada guriga taliye SHUB, shaacisayna… appeared first on Caasimada Online .

Sidoo kale, Dowladda Federaalka ayaa ka digtay in aan lagu kadsoomin warar ay ku tilmaamtay been abuur, kuwaas oo ka hordhacaya baaritaanka, isla markaana loogu tala-galay in lagu jahwareeriyo shacabka Soomaaliyeed, sida ay sheegtay wasaaradda. “Dowladda waxay caddeynaysaa in natiijada baaritaanka lala wadaagi doono shacabka marka uu soo dhammaado,” ayaa ugu dambeyntiina lagu yiri war-saxaafadeedka wasaaradda warfaafinta Soomaaliya. War-saxaafadeedka dowladda ayaa imanaya xilli maamulka Jubaland uu Dowladda Federaalka iyo Turkiga ku eedeeyay inay ka dambeeyeen duqeyn uu sheegay in lala beegsaday guriga Taliyihii hore ee Ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliya, General Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Aadan (Shub). Jubaland ayaa ku eedeysay Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya inay taliye Shub u bartilmaameedsatay kaliya inuu ka aragti duwanaaday dhinaca siyaasadda. Maamulka ayaa sidoo kale wuxuu Qaramada Midoobay ugu baaqay inay sida ugu dhaqsaha badan dib ugu eegto go’aankii Soomaaliya lagaga qaaday cuna-qabateynta hubka, “inta laga helayo dowlad mas’uul ah iyo gacmo lagu aamini karo hubka ay dowladaha caalamku ugu deeqayaan Soomaaliya.” The post DF Soomaaliya oo war ka soo saartay dhacdada guriga taliye SHUB, shaacisayna… appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Sagal Cabdi-Waali oo safka hore ugu jirta loollanka kursigii Baarlamaanka UK ee Keir Starmer
items.description: London, 3 Sebteembar 2026 — Sagal Cabdi-Waali, oo ah haweeney Soomaaliyeed oo hoggaamisa Golaha Deegaanka Camden, ayaa loo saadaalinayaa inay ka mid noqoto dadka ugu cadcad ee Xisbiga Labour-ku u xulan karo doorashada ku-celiska ah ee deegaanka Holborn and St Pancras. Doorashada ayaa loo qabanayaa kursigii uu banneeyey ra’iisul-wasaarihii hore ee Britain, Keir Starmer, kaas oo 1-dii Sebteembar ku dhawaaqay inuu iska casilay xubinnimada Baarlamaanka. Starmer wuxuu deegaankaas metelayey tan iyo bishii May 2015. Sagal waxay Britain timid horraantii sagaashamaadkii iyadoo carruur ah oo qoyskeedu ka soo qaxay dagaalladii Soomaaliya. Waxay ku kortay Camden, halkaas oo ay markii dambe ka bilowday hawlo bulsho iyo siyaasadeed, sida ay qoreen Evening Standard⁠￼ iyo Eastleigh Voice⁠￼. Waxaa markii ugu horreysay xildhibaan Golaha Camden looga doortay Labour sannadkii 2022. Doorashooyinkii deegaanka ee May 2026 kaddib waxay noqotay hoggaamiyaha Golaha Camden. Waxay sidoo kale hore guddoomiye uga ahayd laanta Labour-ka ee deegaanka Baarlamaanka ee Holborn and St Pancras, taas oo siinaysa aqoon iyo xiriir siyaasadeed oo gudaha degmada ah. Warbaahinta Britain waxay Sagal ku tilmaantay musharrax hore uga soo baxaya loollanka, balse Labour weli si rasmi ah uma magacaabin qofka kursiga ugu tartamaya xisbiga. Codsiyada musharraxnimada waxay xirmayaan duhurnimada 4-ta Sebteembar, halka musharraxa la filayo in la doorto 9-ka Sebteembar, kaddib wareysiyo iyo kulan ay xubnaha deegaanka ku kala xulanayaan tartamayaasha. Loollanka kursiga ayaa sii kululaanaya, iyadoo hoggaamiyaha Xisbiga Green Party, Zack Polanski, uu shaaciyey inuu doonayo inuu u tartamo deegaanka. Inkastoo Holborn and St Pancras muddo dheer loo arkayey saldhig Labour, guulihii Green Party ee doorashooyinkii deegaanka ee May ayaa muujiyey in doorashada ku-celisku noqon karto tartan adag. Reuters⁠￼ iyo The Guardian⁠￼ ayaa xaqiijiyey qorshaha Polanski. Haddii Sagal Cabdi-Waali hesho magacaabista Labour-ka, dabadeedna ku guuleysato doorashada, waxay gaari kartaa taariikh siyaasadeed oo weyn, iyadoo noqon karta haweeneydii ugu horreysay ee asal Soomaali ah ee loo doorto Golaha Shacabka Britain. Guushaasi waxay sidoo kale sare u qaadi lahayd matalaadda Soomaalida iyo qaxootigii hore ee siyaasadda qaranka UK. Si kastaba, xaaladda hadda jirta waa in Sagal ay tahay qof loo saadaalinayo musharraxnimada, ee aysan weli ahayn musharraxa rasmiga ah ee Labour. Natiijada kama-dambaysta ahi waxay ku xirnaan doontaa hannaanka xulashada xisbiga iyo codka xubnaha Labour-ka ee deegaanka.

items.title: Qaramada Midoobay oo Boosaaso oo sheegtay Marin Loo Adeegsaday Taageerada Ciidamada RSF ee Suudaan
items.description: Warbixin cusub oo ay soo saartay Qaramada Midoobay ayaa magaalada Boosaaso ku xustay inay ka mid ahayd marinnada ay adeegsadeen shabakado caalami ah oo lagu taageerayay Ciidamada Gurmadka Degdegga ah ee Suudaan, ee loo yaqaan RSF. Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Xaqiiqo-raadinta Caalamiga ah ee Qaramada Midoobay u qaabilsan Suudaan ayaa sheegay inuu helay sababo macquul ah oo lagu rumaysan karo in shirkado gaar loo leeyahay, dilaaliin saadka iyo hay’ado shaqaaleysiin ay Boosaaso u adeegsadeen goob transit ah. Sida warbixintu tilmaantay, shabakadahan ayaa Boosaaso, chad iyo koonfur-bari Liibiya u maray marinno lagu gaarsiinayay taageero dhinacyo badan leh Ciidamada RSF, oo uu hoggaamiyo Jeneraal Maxamed Xamdaan Daagalo, oo loo yaqaan Xamidti. Guddigu wuxuu sheegay in la diiwaangeliyay ilaa 2,000 oo askari oo hore uga tirsanaa ciidamada milatariga Kolombiya, kuwaas oo lagu xaqiijiyay inay ku biireen cutubyo ka tirsan RSF. Warbixintu waxay sheegtay in ciidamadaasi ay dagaalka ku adeegsadeen qalab casri ah, oo ay ku jiraan diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn, madaafiic iyo hub kale. Dhanka kale, guddiga ayaa sidoo kale xusay in Ciidamada Qalabka Sida ee dowladda Suudaan, ee uu hoggaamiyo Jeneraal Cabdifataax Al-Burhaan, ay adeegsadeen diyaarado drones ah oo laga helay dalal shisheeye, iyadoo duqeymaha qaarkood ay sababeen waxyeello soo gaartay dad rayid ah. Guddiga Qaramada Midoobay ayaa ku baaqay in baaritaanno madax-bannaan lagu sameeyo dhammaan shaqsiyaadka, dowladaha iyo shirkadaha lagu tuhunsan yahay inay amreen, maalgeliyeen ama fududeeyeen marinnada saadka ee loo adeegsaday dagaalka Suudaan. Maamulka Puntland ayaan weli ka hadlin eedeymaha Boosaaso lagu xusay ee ku jira warbixinta Qaramada Midoobay.
