items.title: Have We Somalis Been Deceived in the Name of Religion All Over Again?
items.description: Dr Zakariya Weyrax Warsame Is the Old Somali Sheikh with the Illuminating Faynuus Hidden Under His Garment—Claiming the Power of the Awliya, Invoking Sheikh Jaylani, and Deceiving Us for Money and Influence—Back, Only This Time Speaking Arabic and Selling Houses in Jannah? There are questions a people eventually has to ask itself—questions that are uncomfortable, questions that offend the sensibilities of the pious, and questions whose answers may threaten ideas that have become too sacred to examine. For Somalis, I believe we have arrived at such a moment. Our country has been broken for more than three decades. Since the collapse of the Somali state in 1991, we have endured civil war, clan conflict, displacement, terrorism, political fragmentation, foreign intervention and an almost generational failure to reconcile. We have rebuilt houses, businesses, telecommunications networks, masjids and fragments of government. We have produced new political conferences and new constitutions. We have raised an entire generation in the shadow of war. Yet beneath all this rebuilding, the fundamental wound remains: we have never truly made peace with ourselves. There is something particularly strange about this condition because Somalis are not a people who lack a common identity. Quite the opposite. We possess one of the strongest shared identities in Africa. We share a language, an extraordinary oral tradition, a common history and, above all, a profound attachment to Islam. Indeed, perhaps this last fact is precisely where we need to begin asking difficult questions. Somalis are an intensely Muslim people. Islam is not simply a religion that many Somalis happen to practise; it is woven into our understanding of who we are. It is our vocabulary of morality, our source of ultimate legitimacy and, for many, the unquestionable foundation of personal and collective identity. That depth of faith is a great strength. But every source of authority can also become a source of vulnerability. What if our reverence for Islam has become so absolute that we have become reluctant to question the particular interpretations of Islam presented to us by those who claim religious authority? What if we have become so afraid of questioning an interpretation that we have forgotten that questioning an interpretation is not the same thing as questioning Islam? This is the question I believe Somalis need to confront—not because Islam has failed us, but because we may have failed to ask whether the forms of religious authority that have become increasingly influential in our society are actually helping us confront the extraordinary historical problem before us. It is easier to see what I mean if we consider that history does not always repeat itself in the same form. Sometimes it simply changes its language. Perhaps the best way to understand the question is to look backward before examining what has changed. Do you remember the old stories of another kind of Somali religious authority? Before the civil war, there were men who presented themselves as awliya —holy men possessing extraordinary spiritual powers. Stories were told of sheikhs who would sit before ordinary people with a faynuus hidden beneath their macawiis , creating the impression that something extraordinary was happening. They might invoke Sheikh Jaylani, claim the power of the awliya , perform supposed miracles, or cultivate an aura of sanctity around themselves. Ordinary people, believing they were in the presence of someone specially favoured by Allah, would give them money and gifts. Today, many of us remember these stories almost with amusement. They belong to a religious culture we congratulate ourselves for having outgrown. And perhaps, in some respects, we did. The growth of more scripturally rigorous Salafi-influenced religious movements after the civil war challenged many of these practices. Superstition was attacked. Fabricated miracles were exposed. Claims of supernatural powers were subjected to scrutiny. The Qur’an and Sunnah were brought back to the centre of religious discussion. For many Somalis, this represented genuine religious renewal. It is important to be fair about what this transformation represented. These movements did not emerge in a vacuum. They challenged forms of religious practice that many Somalis regarded as superstition. They questioned claims of supernatural power. They emphasised the Qur’an and Sunnah, attacked fabricated miracles and sought to replace inherited religious customs with what they regarded as a more rigorous and textually grounded understanding of Islam. It would be intellectually dishonest to pretend otherwise. Nor should every Salafi-influenced Somali, or every person associated with Itixaad, Ictisaam or similar movements, be placed into one undifferentiated category. Their politics, scholarship, temperament and objectives have not been identical. But this transformation also created something else: a new kind of religious authority. I say this as someone who is himself a product of that transformation. I grew up within the Salafi-influenced religious tradition, and much of my own religious education and maturity was shaped by it. I owe it a genuine debt for teaching me to question superstition, to take the Qur’an and Sunnah seriously, and to distinguish religious evidence from inherited custom. Precisely because I came through that tradition, I do not believe examining its assumptions, institutions or consequences is an act of hostility toward it. It is, rather, an act of intellectual responsibility. After years of living within this tradition, I have increasingly found myself questioning not simply what it teaches, but whether the system we have built around it is still achieving what it set out to achieve. And perhaps that is precisely why the question that follows is so difficult: what happens when a movement that taught us to question inherited religious authority eventually gives rise to forms of religious authority that become difficult to question themselves? The difficulty lies in a distinction Somali public discourse often refuses to make. There is Islam, and there are Muslims; there is revelation, and there are human interpretations of revelation; there is the Qur’an and Sunnah, and there are people who interpret, explain, prioritise and apply them. To question the latter is not necessarily to question the former. Yet in Somali society, these things are frequently fused together. The preacher who presents an interpretation of religion can acquire a level of moral authority that makes his ideas almost immune from examination. A person who challenges him can quickly find himself accused of ignorance, modernism, Westernisation, disrespect for religion or even disbelief. This creates an intellectual environment in which religious ideas can become insulated from the very scrutiny we routinely apply to every other institution in society. We have no difficulty questioning presidents, politicians, clan elders, foreign governments, businessmen or academics. Yet when a religious interpretation becomes socially powerful, we often lower the intellectual guard we apply everywhere else. The person speaking in the name of religion can become strangely protected from scrutiny simply because his argument is wrapped in religious language. Perhaps that is precisely what we should no longer do. We should be willing to ask not only whether a religious position is textually defensible, but whether it is actually producing the moral and social transformation a society desperately needs. Something can be literaturistically correct while being practically inadequate to the circumstances in which it is being applied. And if a religious framework can remain authoritative despite repeatedly failing to address the problems before us, then we have to ask a more uncomfortable question: what, exactly, is sustaining that authority? You already know the answer, even if you don’t want to say it. The old system. The same promises. The same emptiness. The new authority is sustained by the same vulnerability it claims to have replaced. This is why the comparison is no longer avoidable. So let me ask you plainly: Did we eliminate the old religious deception, or did we merely make religious authority more sophisticated? The trick of the deception is that it no longer looks like deception. It comes dressed as knowledge. The modern religious personality does not need to sit in darkness with a torch beneath him and claim supernatural powers. He does not need to call himself a wali or perform a supposed miracle. He can possess genuine knowledge. He can speak fluent Arabic. He can quote Qur’an and hadith. He can cite classical scholars. He can deliver a sermon entirely convincing on a textual level. Yet none of those things, by themselves, make him immune from human motives, financial incentives or the abuse of authority. This is where the distinction between textual correctness and practical integrity becomes crucial. The old charlatan exploited people’s belief in his supernatural status. The modern religious authority may possess real knowledge and still exploit something else: people’s fear of Allah, their desire for Paradise and their reluctance to question someone speaking in the language of religion. The methods are not the same. The theological claims are not the same. And it would be unfair to suggest that they are. But perhaps the vulnerability being exploited is remarkably similar: the ordinary believer’s assumption that the man standing before him has a special claim upon his conscience. If that is true, then we have to ask whether we have actually escaped the old problem or simply replaced the theatrical miracle with the sophisticated sermon. And this brings us to something even more uncomfortable: what happens when religious authority and money become intertwined? The moment the person delivering the religious message becomes financially dependent upon the audience receiving it, an uncomfortable question emerges: can the message remain completely independent of the money? If the answer is yes, then wonderful. But we should not simply assume it. Look at the world that has developed around some of our most prominent Somali religious personalities. A prominent sheikh may be invited to a congregation and expected to have his flight paid for, accommodation arranged and expenses covered. That is understandable when someone is travelling to provide a service. But increasingly, religious speaking can resemble a professional circuit: one masjid, another city, another conference, another lecture, another fundraising campaign, another invitation, another payment, another audience. Eventually, religious authority can begin to resemble a profession in the ordinary commercial sense. There is nothing inherently wrong with earning a lawful living. But when the product being sold is religious authority, we must ask whether different ethical standards should apply. Historically, the religious scholar was not necessarily dependent upon the congregation for every aspect of his livelihood. In many Muslim societies, scholars had independent means of support, family wealth, endowments or other forms of income that gave them a degree of independence from those to whom they preached. That independence matters. But the financial ecosystem surrounding some of our most prominent religious figures raises a different concern. A sheikh gathers an audience. The audience trusts him because he speaks in the name of religion. He invokes the Qur’an, the Prophet ﷺ, Paradise, Hell, reward and sin. Then he asks the audience for money. Sometimes for a masjid, a madrasa, a well, an orphanage or a humanitarian project. Many of these causes may be completely legitimate. But the mechanism deserves examination because the person asking is not merely another fundraiser. He is a religious authority, and his words carry spiritual weight. The listener is therefore not simply thinking, “Should I donate?” He may also be thinking: “What if I don’t?” That is a completely different psychological proposition. The ordinary fundraiser asks for your money. The religious fundraiser can, intentionally or unintentionally, make you feel that your relationship with Allah is implicated in the decision. That is where the line between persuasion and emotional pressure becomes dangerously thin. For the Somali mother or father living on a modest income, the calculation is not so simple. There is rent, school expenses, elderly parents, children who need clothes, perhaps debt, perhaps a medical bill, and perhaps relatives in Somalia whom they already support. Then a prominent sheikh tells them about a masjid that needs funding. He tells them of the immense reward, reminds them that charity does not diminish wealth, speaks about Paradise and urges them not to miss the opportunity. The decision no longer feels like an ordinary financial choice. It can begin to feel like a test of faith. The imam is not the custodian of Paradise. No Somali sheikh possesses the keys to Allah’s treasury. And no preacher can guarantee a person’s place in Jannah because he donated to his particular masjid. These should be obvious statements. Yet in the emotional atmosphere of religious fundraising, the distinction can become blurred. And this is precisely where we need to stop and ask whether we have actually escaped the old pattern of religious manipulation—or merely given it a more sophisticated vocabulary. I believe Somali religious leaders need to be held to a much higher standard. The poverty and religious devotion of an audience should never become a fundraising mechanism. If a family cannot afford to give, they should not be made to feel that they have failed Allah. If a parent chooses to spend limited income educating their children, feeding their family or caring for an elderly parent, they should not be made to feel that they have somehow missed a greater religious opportunity. And this raises another uncomfortable question: what does Islam actually ask of us when charity comes into conflict with responsibility to our own families? We should be careful here. Islam clearly encourages generosity and charity, and there are different forms and priorities of spending that scholars have discussed in detail. But surely we should be able to acknowledge the basic moral principle that a person’s obligations to those who depend upon him cannot simply disappear because a microphone has been placed in front of him and a fundraising appeal has begun. The Somali parent should not have to choose between feeding his children and proving his faith to a religious audience. Nor should the believer be made to feel that spending money on his child’s education, his family’s health, his elderly parents or his household is somehow spiritually inferior simply because it does not produce the emotional spectacle of a masjid fundraising campaign. A religious leader should never need to make you feel spiritually inadequate in order to fund his institution. Perhaps the more difficult thing for a religious leader to say would sometimes be: “Take care of your family first. Educate your children. Pay your debts. Look after your parents. Give to charity when you can.” That message may raise less money. But perhaps it would reveal more about the integrity of the person delivering it. And if a leader is willing to say that, then surely he should also be willing to ask: do we actually need another masjid? This is a question many Somalis ask privately but rarely say publicly. Why can religious institutions not cooperate? Why does every religious personality, organisation or group seem to require its own masjid, its own fundraising campaign and its own financial apparatus? And then there is the question nobody wants to ask: has the masjid, in some circumstances, become an institution of personal wealth and influence rather than simply an institution of worship? That is an uncomfortable question, and it should remain uncomfortable. But discomfort is not an argument against asking it. When an imam controls fundraising, charitable appeals, religious legitimacy and access to a large community of emotionally receptive believers, there is an enormous concentration of moral and financial authority. Such authority requires accountability. Who audits it? Who examines the accounts? Who protects ordinary Somalis from emotional manipulation? This is not about who is corrupt and who is not. The issue is larger than the masjid, larger than fundraising, and larger than any individual religious leader. It is about whether the religious leadership we have built is still capable of confronting the reality in which we actually live. It must do more than tell us what is permissible. It must understand trauma, history, politics, Somali culture, the economics of the families sitting before it, and the psychology of a population that has lived through thirty-five years of war. It must be capable of asking not merely, “Is this correct?” but also, “What does this produce?” Because that is the question that matters now. After thirty-five years, what has all this religious authority produced? We are still killing one another with a casualness that would shame the dead. Still walking past emaciated children with hollow eyes on the streets of Mogadishu, Kismaayo, Garowe and Hargeisa, their mothers begging while we discuss the finer points of aqeedah and fiqh. Still flying home to Somalia for luxury holidays while families in the camps watch their children fade. Still using the word “brother” as a shield for everything we refuse to do for actual brothers. Still building. Still fundraising. Still preaching. Still reciting. Still debating what is correct. Still congratulating ourselves on our religious seriousness—while a wounded mother sits in the corner of the masjid, waiting for someone to see her. At what point are we allowed to ask whether something has gone wrong? Not whether Islam is wrong. Not whether the Qur’an and Sunnah are wrong. But whether the human system we have built around them is still doing what it was supposed to do. That is where we have arrived. Something is missing. Perhaps the courage to find it begins with asking the questions we have been too afraid to ask. And perhaps the most uncomfortable question of all is this: Did we really rid ourselves of religious deception—or did we simply teach the old awliya charlatans to speak better Arabic, quote more scripture and wear a cleaner robe? The ordinary fundraiser asks for your money. The religious fundraiser can, intentionally or unintentionally, make you feel that your relationship with Allah is implicated in the decision. That is where the line between persuasion and emotional pressure becomes dangerously thin. For the Somali mother or father living on a modest income, the calculation is not so simple. There is rent, school expenses, elderly parents, children who need clothes, perhaps debt, perhaps a medical bill, and perhaps relatives in Somalia whom they already support. Then a prominent sheikh tells them about a masjid that needs funding. He tells them of the immense reward, reminds them that charity does not diminish wealth, speaks about Paradise and urges them not to miss the opportunity. The decision no longer feels like an ordinary financial choice. It can begin to feel like a test of faith. The imam is not the custodian of Paradise. No Somali sheikh possesses the keys to Allah’s treasury. And no preacher can guarantee a person’s place in Jannah because he donated to his particular masjid. These should be obvious statements. Yet in the emotional atmosphere of religious fundraising, the distinction can become blurred. And this is precisely where we need to stop and ask whether we have actually escaped the old pattern of religious manipulation—or merely given it a more sophisticated vocabulary. I believe Somali religious leaders need to be held to a much higher standard. The poverty and religious devotion of an audience should never become a fundraising mechanism. If a family cannot afford to give, they should not be made to feel that they have failed Allah. If a parent chooses to spend limited income educating their children, feeding their family or caring for an elderly parent, they should not be made to feel that they have somehow missed a greater religious opportunity. And this raises another uncomfortable question: what does Islam actually ask of us when charity comes into conflict with responsibility to our own families? We should be careful here. Islam clearly encourages generosity and charity, and there are different forms and priorities of spending that scholars have discussed in detail. But surely we should be able to acknowledge the basic moral principle that a person’s obligations to those who depend upon him cannot simply disappear because a microphone has been placed in front of him and a fundraising appeal has begun. The Somali parent should not have to choose between feeding his children and proving his faith to a religious audience. Nor should the believer be made to feel that spending money on his child’s education, his family’s health, his elderly parents or his household is somehow spiritually inferior simply because it does not produce the emotional spectacle of a masjid fundraising campaign. A religious leader should never need to make you feel spiritually inadequate in order to fund his institution. Perhaps the more difficult thing for a religious leader to say would sometimes be: “Take care of your family first. Educate your children. Pay your debts. Look after your parents. Give to charity when you can.” That message may raise less money. But perhaps it would reveal more about the integrity of the person delivering it. And if a leader is willing to say that, then surely he should also be willing to ask: do we actually need another masjid? This is a question many Somalis ask privately but rarely say publicly. Why can religious institutions not cooperate? Why does every religious personality, organisation or group seem to require its own masjid, its own fundraising campaign and its own financial apparatus? And then there is the question nobody wants to ask: has the masjid, in some circumstances, become an institution of personal wealth and influence rather than simply an institution of worship? That is an uncomfortable question, and it should remain uncomfortable. But discomfort is not an argument against asking it. When an imam controls fundraising, charitable appeals, religious legitimacy and access to a large community of emotionally receptive believers, there is an enormous concentration of moral and financial authority. Such authority requires accountability. Who audits it? Who examines the accounts? Who protects ordinary Somalis from emotional manipulation? This is not about who is corrupt and who is not. The issue is larger than the masjid, larger than fundraising, and larger than any individual religious leader. It is about whether the religious leadership we have built is still capable of confronting the reality in which we actually live. It must do more than tell us what is permissible. It must understand trauma, history, politics, Somali culture, the economics of the families sitting before it, and the psychology of a population that has lived through thirty-five years of war. It must be capable of asking not merely, “Is this correct?” but also, “What does this produce?” Because that is the question that matters now. After thirty-five years, what has all this religious authority produced? We are still killing one another with a casualness that would shame the dead. Still walking past emaciated children with hollow eyes on the streets of Mogadishu, Kismaayo, Garowe and Hargeisa, their mothers begging while we discuss the finer points of aqeedah and fiqh. Still flying home to Somalia for luxury holidays while families in the camps watch their children fade. Still using the word “brother” as a shield for everything we refuse to do for actual brothers. Still building. Still fundraising. Still preaching. Still reciting. Still debating what is correct. Still congratulating ourselves on our religious seriousness—while a wounded mother sits in the corner of the masjid, waiting for someone to see her. At what point are we allowed to ask whether something has gone wrong? Not whether Islam is wrong. Not whether the Qur’an and Sunnah are wrong. But whether the human system we have built around them is still doing what it was supposed to do. That is where we have arrived. Something is missing. Perhaps the courage to find it begins with asking the questions we have been too afraid to ask. And perhaps the most uncomfortable question of all is this: Did we really rid ourselves of religious deception—or did we simply teach the old awliya charlatans to speak better Arabic, quote more scripture and wear a cleaner robe? Maxaa ka jira in ciidamo ka tirsan DF ay u goosteen dowlad-deegaanka Soomaalida?
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa markii ugu horreysay ka hadashay wararka sheegaya inay goosteen qaar kamid ah ciidamadii dhawaan tababarka loogu soo xiray deegaanka Xanan-buure ee gobolka Galgaduud, kuwaas oo la sheegay inay u tallaabeen dhanka dowlad-deegaanka Soomaalida. La-taliyaha amniga qaranka ee Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Danjire Aweys Xaaji Yuusuf oo maanta la hadlay Wariyeyaasha, isaga oo ka qayb-galayay shirweynaha qaran ee amniga gudaha ee ka furmay Muqdisho ayaa beeniyay wararkaasi, wuxuuna tilmaamay in aysan jirin wax ciidan ah oo baxsaday. Aweys Xaaji ayaa meesha ka saaray in ciidamadaasi ay haddda maxaabiis ahaan gacanta ugu hayso Dowlad-deegaanka Soomaalida, balse dowladdu ay siisay fasax, ayna ku maqan yihiin qoysaskooda oo halkaasi deggan. “Ciidamada markii uu tababarka u dhammaaday waxaa la siiyay fasax si u booqdaan ehelladooda annaga raggaas waxay nooga maqan yihiin qoysaskooda, haddii ay carqalado jiraan waa mid aan warbaahinta lasoo wadaagi doono,” ayuu yiri La-taliyaha amniga qaranka ee Madaxweynaha . Waxaa kale oo uu raaciyay “Illaa hadda nama soo gaarin in maxaabiis ahaan loo haysto, balse waxaan xogta ku haynaa inay fasax ku maqan yihiin, waana ogaaneynaa haddii ay wax jiraan sida loo sheegaayana ma aha arrinta”. Ciidamada tababarka ku qaatay deegaanka Xanan-buure ayaa tiradoodu waxa ay gaareysaa ku dhowaad 3,000 oo askari oo ka tirsan Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, kuwaas oo muddo ku dhow hal sano tababar ku qaadanayay xero ku taalla halkaasi. Tirada askarta tababarka dhammeystay ayaa lagu tilmaamay kooxdii ugu ballaarneyd ee heerkan oo kale gudaha Soomaaliya lagu tababaro tan iyo burburkii dowladdii dhexe sanadkii 1991-kii, iyadoo dowladda ay tallaabadan qeyb ka dhigeyso qorshaha dib-u-dhiska ciidamada qaranka. Arrintan ayaa kusoo aadeysa xilli dowladda federaalka ay dooneyso in ciidamada Soomaaliyeed ay si tartiib ah ula wareegaan mas’uuliyadda buuxda ee amniga dalka, iyadoo howlgalka ciidamada Midowga Afrika uu wajahayo qorshe dhimis iyo kala-guur ah. items.title: SolitAir adds Nigeria and Somaliland to its African cargo network
items.description: SolitAir has added Port Harcourt in Nigeria and Hargeisa in Somaliland to its cargo network, taking its African footprint to 20 destinations across 16 countries. The UAE-based cargo carrier will serve Port Harcourt International Airport and Egal International Airport in Hargeisa, marking its first direct presence in both Nigeria and Somaliland. The additions build on SolitAir’s existing East African hub in Nairobi and are intended to strengthen cargo connections between the Gulf and underserved African markets. Port Harcourt International Airport serves Nigeria’s oil and gas economy, while Hargeisa provides access to a market where exports including livestock and time-sensitive agricultural products rely on air freight capacity. The expansion takes SolitAir’s global network to more than 60 destinations across over 35 countries in Asia, Africa and Europe. The carrier operates seven Boeing 737-800BCF freighters, each offering 20 tonnes of cargo capacity, from its hub at Dubai World Central (DWC), Al Maktoum International Airport. The facility has been operational since October 2024. SolitAir is targeting a fleet of 20 aircraft by the end of 2027. Hamdi Osman, founder and chief executive of SolitAir, said: “Nigeria and Somaliland are important additions to our African network, giving us an opportunity to strengthen connections between the Gulf and these markets. “As we continue to expand, we’re focused on identifying destinations where there is clear demand for reliable air cargo services and where we can add value to existing trade flows.” He added: “These routes were built around real customer demand. Port Harcourt and Hargeisa are good examples of how we’re developing the network – by looking at where our partners need to move cargo and building connections that support those trade flows.” Aviation business news

items.title: Qiimo kororka shidaalka iyo canshuur dheeri ah oo nolol xumo galiyay danyarta Hargeysa
items.description: (ERGO) – Nolol xumo ayaa soo wajahday ku dhawaad 100 qoysas danyar ah oo ku nool magaalada Hargeysa, markii ganacsiyo ay masruufka ka heli jireen ay xirmeen 3 bil ee la soo dhaafay. Waxaa sababay canshuuro ay ganacsiyada ku soo rogtay Wasaaaradda Maaliyadda ee Somaliland, badeeco xumo iyo macaamiil yari. Canab Jaamac Furre oo ka mid ah waxay maarayn la’ dahay dhamaan baahiyaha aas-aasiga ah ee qoyskeeda 7 ah kuna ku tiirsanaa keligeed. Haweeynaydaan ayaa tilmaamtay inuu ka xirmay dukaan raashin iyo bagaash ay ku iibin jirtay oo ay reerka ku dabaraysay in ka badan 10 sano. Waxay xustay in meheradeeda ay joogta uga heli jirta $6 illaa $5 oo aan wax canshuur ah laga jarayn. Dhaqaalahan ayay xustay inuu ugu filnaa cunnada, biyaha iyo baahiyaha kale, kuwaas oo ay hadda awoodi la’yihiin, maaddama uu dhaqaalahaasi meesha ka baxay. “Mar keliya ayaan hadda dabka shidana. Mar labaad inaan dabka shidano ma awoodno. Halkaas mar wixii aan helno ayaan isku filnaysiina. Markii hore saddexda waqti ee quraacda, qadada iyo cashada waynu shidanaynaa dabka, balse hadda ganacsigii aan ku tiirsanayn waa naga xirmay.” Canab ayaa sheegtay inay ku tiirsan yihiin dayn aan joogta ahayn iyo kaalmo ay waydiistaan dad ehel ah oo daris la’ ah. Mudadii ay caqabadahan jireen waxay tilmaamtay in reerkeeda ay dabka saaranayeen raashinkii dukaanka u yaallay, kaas oo hadda ka dhamaaday. Waxay xustay in culaysyada haysta ay ka mid yihiin biyo yari. Ugu badnaan jirgaan ay soo baryaan dadka nolol dhaama ayay sheegtay inay ku tiirsan yihiin, maaddaama aysan awoodin $3 oo fuustadii ay iibiiyan booyado keena. Haweeynaydan oo 92 jir ah ayaa sheegtay inaysan awoodin inay shaqooyin xoogsi ah ka raadiso magaalada, maaddaama ay tahay wayeel aan shaqooyinkaasi qaban karin. Dukaanka oo ay ku lahayd guriga dhexdiisa ayay tilmaamtay inuu ahaa waxa keliya ee dhaqaale uga soo saari kartay qoyskeeda. Labo wiil oo ay dhashay ayay tilmaamtay i ay hungoobeen raadinta shaqooyin xamaal ah. Waxay xustay inay ka shalaysan tahay inaysan horray wax kayd ah u samaysan. Waxay cabasho ka muujisay canshuuraha dowladda ku soo rogtay oo ahaa kuwa awoodooda ka badan.  “Dawlada cashuur ayay nagu soo rogtay. Boqolkii doolar waxaa la yiri $2 oo canshuur ah ayaa laga jaraya. Waxaan haynay iyo wixii na soo galayay marka loo eego wax iska kaafin karay ma ahayn. Sidoo kale macaashadii qaali ayay noqotay oo raashinka qiimihiisa cirkuu u kacay. Wax aan alaabo dukaanka ugu soo iibino waa waynay, sidaas ayay nooga xirantay mehradii.” Canab ayaa sheegtay in xaaladdan darteed ay waxbarasho la’aan ka noqdeen saddex carruur ah oo ay ayeeyo u tahay, kuwaas oo ay iyadu masuul ka tahay. Waxay tilmaamtay in bishii Juun laga soo eryay madarasad ay dhigan jireen, markii lagu yeeshay $100 oo isku gaartay oo ay awoodi wayday. Waxaa walwal ku sii kordhinaya $200 oo looga yeeshay dukaamada raashinka ee xaafada magaalo Ugaaso oo ay dagan yihiin.  Waxay awoodi waayeen in ay badeeco soo iibsadaan taas oo sababtay in macaamiishii wax ka iibsan jiray ay u wareegaan bakharadda waawayn ee magaalada. Hoodo Axmed Cabdullahi waxay qoyskeeda oo 12 qof ah sheegtay inay wajahayaan xaaladdii ugu liidatay muddo 7 sano ah kaddib. Waxaa ka xirmay ganacsi dukaan bagaash iyo raashin ah oo ay u iibin jirtay hooyadeed oo waayeel ah, taas oo sidoo kale la dhiban cudurrada sonkorowga iyo dhiig-karka oo ay dhaqaatiirtu ku sheeegeen sanado ka hor. Hal mar ayay sheegtay inay dabka ku shitaan $4 oo uu abbaahooda toddobaadkii mar ka soo helo shaqooyinka dhismaha guriyaha. Waxay tilmaamtay inay tashiishaan hasa yeeshe aysan waxbo ka tarin baahidooda, lakiin ay dantu dhaafi wayday. Cunno xumada waxaa u dheer biyo yari. “Biyihii waxay noqdeen qaali. ma awoodno hadda. Markii hore waa gadan karna lacag walbo la dhaho sababtoo ah waxaan ahayn dad ganacsi ay leeyihiin dhaqaale ka hela. Hadda waxa kaliya ee aan heli karno waa jirgaamo aan dariska ka soo barino.” Hoodo ayaa sheegtay in sidoo kale ay awoodi la’yihiin $50 oo ah kirada labo qol oo jiingad oo ay dagan yihiin. Waxay tilmaamtay in lagu yeeshay $150 oo ah dayn ay saddexdii bil ee la soo dhaafay ku daganaayeen, taas oo ay bixin waayeen. Haweeynaydan ayaa sheegtay in dhanka kale laga jartay korontadii guriga, markii ay bixin waayeen $30 oo laga rabay bishii. Arrintan darteed waxay tilmamtay inay ku qasbanaadeen in habeenkii ay ifsadaan tooshash ay ka soo qateen qoysas ay ehel yihiin oo magaalada kula nool. Hoodo ayaa xustay in nolol xumada haysa ay u dheertahay caafimaad darro hooyadeed oo aysan wax daryeel ah u awoodin. Waxay xustay inay tahay curadda reerka. Shaqooyin nadaafad ah oo ay raadisay marar kala duwan si daawooyinka ay u baahan tahay ugu iibiso ayay sheegtay inay wayday. “Hooyaday ayaa na maarayn jirtay. dhiikar iyo sonkor ayay horray u qabtay, hadda waxaa u raacay xumad daran oo ku soo laalaabatay. Ma awoodi karto inay shaqayso. Sido kale daawadeeda ayaa nagu adag. Awal dad qaarabo ah ayaa naga caawin jiray, haddase iyagiina waxbo kama helno. Hooyaday sidaas ayaa daawo la’aan ku tahay. Wax aan ugu soo iibinana ma heli karn.” Hoodo ayaa sheegtay in dhaqaale xumada haysa ay sidoo kale waxbarasho la’ aan ku sababtay 4 carruur ah oo dugsi hoose dhexe dhiganayay, markii ay bixin waayeen $60 oo kharashkooda waxbarashada ee bisha. Waxay tilmamtay in ganacsiga meesha ka baxay oo qoyskoodu kaalin muhiim ah ugu jiray in markii hore ay ku billawdeen dhaqaale ay dadka ehel u ah ku caawiyeen. Waxay rajo xumo ka muujisay sidii ay markale dib ugu yagleeli doonnaan. Dhanka kale Faadumo Xayd Cali oo ah xoghaya guddi ay ganacsatada yaryar ku midaysan yihiin ayaa Raadiyow Ergo u sheegtay in xaladdan ay saamaysay ku dhawaad boqol ganacsato ahaa, kuwaas oo ay goobahoodii ganacsi ee u ahaa ilahooda kaliya ee dhaqaale ay ka xirmeen. “Shidaalkii, canshuurtii iyo maciishadiiba waa kaceen. Dadkii danyarta ahaa arrintan dhan walbo ayay ka saamaysay. Tangigi biyaha ee $50 la siin jiray $70 ayaa la iibinaya, shidaalka oo qaaliyoobay ayaana keenay, dadkuna ma gadan karaan.” “Dad badan ayaa laga saaray guriyih ay daganaayeen markii ay kirada awoodi waayeen. Waxaan dowladda ka codsanayna inay xaaladda dadkan wax ka qaabtaan.” Fadumo ayaa sheegtay in horray dowladda ay codsi arrintan ku aadan u direen, hasa yeeshee aysan wax jawaab ah ka helin. Waxaa walwal ku sii kordhinaya $200 oo looga yeeshay dukaamada raashinka ee xaafada magaalo Ugaaso oo ay dagan yihiin.  Waxay awoodi waayeen in ay badeeco soo iibsadaan taas oo sababtay in macaamiishii wax ka iibsan jiray ay u wareegaan bakharadda waawayn ee magaalada. Hoodo Axmed Cabdullahi waxay qoyskeeda oo 12 qof ah sheegtay inay wajahayaan xaaladdii ugu liidatay muddo 7 sano ah kaddib. Waxaa ka xirmay ganacsi dukaan bagaash iyo raashin ah oo ay u iibin jirtay hooyadeed oo waayeel ah, taas oo sidoo kale la dhiban cudurrada sonkorowga iyo dhiig-karka oo ay dhaqaatiirtu ku sheeegeen sanado ka hor. Hal mar ayay sheegtay inay dabka ku shitaan $4 oo uu abbaahooda toddobaadkii mar ka soo helo shaqooyinka dhismaha guriyaha. Waxay tilmaamtay inay tashiishaan hasa yeeshe aysan waxbo ka tarin baahidooda, lakiin ay dantu dhaafi wayday. Cunno xumada waxaa u dheer biyo yari. “Biyihii waxay noqdeen qaali. ma awoodno hadda. Markii hore waa gadan karna lacag walbo la dhaho sababtoo ah waxaan ahayn dad ganacsi ay leeyihiin dhaqaale ka hela. Hadda waxa kaliya ee aan heli karno waa jirgaamo aan dariska ka soo barino.” Hoodo ayaa sheegtay in sidoo kale ay awoodi la’yihiin $50 oo ah kirada labo qol oo jiingad oo ay dagan yihiin. Waxay tilmaamtay in lagu yeeshay $150 oo ah dayn ay saddexdii bil ee la soo dhaafay ku daganaayeen, taas oo ay bixin waayeen. Haweeynaydan ayaa sheegtay in dhanka kale laga jartay korontadii guriga, markii ay bixin waayeen $30 oo laga rabay bishii. Arrintan darteed waxay tilmamtay inay ku qasbanaadeen in habeenkii ay ifsadaan tooshash ay ka soo qateen qoysas ay ehel yihiin oo magaalada kula nool. Hoodo ayaa xustay in nolol xumada haysa ay u dheertahay caafimaad darro hooyadeed oo aysan wax daryeel ah u awoodin. Waxay xustay inay tahay curadda reerka. Shaqooyin nadaafad ah oo ay raadisay marar kala duwan si daawooyinka ay u baahan tahay ugu iibiso ayay sheegtay inay wayday. “Hooyaday ayaa na maarayn jirtay. dhiikar iyo sonkor ayay horray u qabtay, hadda waxaa u raacay xumad daran oo ku soo laalaabatay. Ma awoodi karto inay shaqayso. Sido kale daawadeeda ayaa nagu adag. Awal dad qaarabo ah ayaa naga caawin jiray, haddase iyagiina waxbo kama helno. Hooyaday sidaas ayaa daawo la’aan ku tahay. Wax aan ugu soo iibinana ma heli karn.” Hoodo ayaa sheegtay in dhaqaale xumada haysa ay sidoo kale waxbarasho la’ aan ku sababtay 4 carruur ah oo dugsi hoose dhexe dhiganayay, markii ay bixin waayeen $60 oo kharashkooda waxbarashada ee bisha. Waxay tilmamtay in ganacsiga meesha ka baxay oo qoyskoodu kaalin muhiim ah ugu jiray in markii hore ay ku billawdeen dhaqaale ay dadka ehel u ah ku caawiyeen. Waxay rajo xumo ka muujisay sidii ay markale dib ugu yagleeli doonnaan. Dhanka kale Faadumo Xayd Cali oo ah xoghaya guddi ay ganacsatada yaryar ku midaysan yihiin ayaa Raadiyow Ergo u sheegtay in xaladdan ay saamaysay ku dhawaad boqol ganacsato ahaa, kuwaas oo ay goobahoodii ganacsi ee u ahaa ilahooda kaliya ee dhaqaale ay ka xirmeen. “Shidaalkii, canshuurtii iyo maciishadiiba waa kaceen. Dadkii danyarta ahaa arrintan dhan walbo ayay ka saamaysay. Tangigi biyaha ee $50 la siin jiray $70 ayaa la iibinaya, shidaalka oo qaaliyoobay ayaana keenay, dadkuna ma gadan karaan.” “Dad badan ayaa laga saaray guriyih ay daganaayeen markii ay kirada awoodi waayeen. Waxaan dowladda ka codsanayna inay xaaladda dadkan wax ka qaabtaan.” Fadumo ayaa sheegtay in horray dowladda ay codsi arrintan ku aadan u direen, hasa yeeshee aysan wax jawaab ah ka helin. items.title: Maleeshiyaad hubeysan oo la wareegay xarumaha doorashada ee Beledweyne
items.description: Beledweyne (Caasimada Online) – Wararka naga soo gaaraya gobolka Hiiraan ayaa sheegaya in maanta maleeshiyaad hubeysan ay weerar ku qaadeen xarumaha loo asteeyay doorashada ee magaalada Beledweyne, xilli ay halkaas ka jirto xiisad ka dhalatay tabashada ay weli qabaan reer Hiiraan. Maleeshiyada ayaa lagu soo warramayaa inay la wareegtay mid kamid ah goobaha loo asteeyay in lagu qabto diiwaangelinta, maadaama haatan HirShabelle ay isku diyaarineyso doorashooyinka isku sidkan ee Golaha Wakiilada iyo Deegaanka ee maamulkaasi. Cabdulqaadir Yuusuf Cilmi oo isku sheegay hoggaamiyaha maleeshiyaadka la wareegay xarunta doorashada ee Beledweyne ayaa Universal TV u sheegay inay kasoo horjeedaan hannaanka loo wado doorashada HirShabelle. Sidoo kale, wuxuu sheegay inay diidan yihiin in kuraasta loo xiro shaqsiyaad gaar ah, isagoo xusay in loo baahan yahay hannaan doorasho oo loo siman yahay. “Dadka deegaanka oo hubaysan ayaa nahay, waxaan la wareegnay goobtii doorashadda loogu talagalay, dagaal ayaan ka xignaa in Beledweyne doorasho ku sheeg ay ka dhacdo, Xasan Sheekh waxaan la soconaa in kaarka uu siiyay Cali Guudlaawe,” ayuu yiri Cabdulqaadir Yuusuf Cilmi. Dhinaca kale Madaxweynihii hore ee HirShabelle Cali Cosoble oo ka hadlay arrintan ayaa farriin u diray Xildhibaannada kasoo jeeda Hiiraan, isaga oo ugu baaqay inay ka hortagaan qorshaha guddiga doorashooyinka qaranka. “Ku:Xildhibanada Xawadle waxa ay guddiga dorashooyinka ka shaqeynayaan waad aragtaan ee ka hortaga dulmiga ama xilka aad heysaan iska casila,” ayuu yiri Cali Cosoble. Arrintan ayaa kusoo aadeyso, iyada oo maanta guddiga doorashooyinka qaranka uu shaaciyay in 30-ka bisha Sebtember loo asteeyey doorashada Golaha Wakiillada iyo Goleyaasha Deegaanka ee Maamulka HirShabelle. Jadwalku wuxuu sidoo kale dhigayaa in 2-da Sebtember la shaaciyo liiska hordhaca ah ee diiwaanka codbixiyeyaasha, halka 15-ka Sebtember la asteyn doono lana shaacin doono xarumaha iyo goobaha codbixinta. items.title: Shaqaalaha Rayidka Puntland: Maxay Dowladda Uga Aamusantahay Mushaaraadka Aan La Bixin?
items.description: Garoowe (WDN) — Shaqaalaha rayidka ah ee Puntland ayaa wajahaya marxald aadaga taas oo ku aadan su’aal ah: maxay dowladda u bixin la’dahay mushaharaadkooda muddo todoba bilood ka maqan shaqaalaha , iyadoo kharashaad kale oo dowladeed ay weli socdaan? Shaqaalaha dowladda ayaa lagu soo waramayaa in aynan helin wax mushahar ah  ilaa toddobo bilood, iyadoo dhibaatada dib-u-dhaca mushaaraadku la sheegay inay soo bilaabatay bishii Sebtembar, 2023. Muddo sannado ah, mushaaraad iyo xuquuqo shaqo oo kale ayaa ururayay, taas oo qoysas badan gelisay xaalad dhaqaale oo adag. Waxa markii hore ahaa dib-u-dhac mushaar ayaa isu beddelay dhibaato daba dheeraatay, taas oo su’aal gelinaysa awoodda iyo waajibaadka dowladda ee ah inay si joogto ah u daryeesho shaqaalaha hay’adaha dowliga ah. Su’aasha shaqaaluhu qabaan waa mid cad: “Mushaarkayagii xaggee ayuu jiraa, maxaase loo bixin waayay?” Shaqaaluhu waajibaadkoodii way gutaan. Mushaarku ma aha deeq siyaasaddeed ama gunno ikhtiyaari ah; waa xuquuq ay ku leeyihiin shaqada ay u qabtaan dowladda iyo shacabka. Sida lagu sheegay qaab-dhismeedka miisaaniyadda Puntland, mudnaanta bixinta mushaaraadka ayaa lagu kala hormariyaa ciidamada amniga, shaqaalaha rayidka ah, kadibna mas’uuliyiinta siyaasadda sida wasiirrada iyo xildhibaannada. Haddii nidaamkaas si dhab ah loo raacayo, shaqaalaha rayidka ahi waa inay filan karaan in mushaarkooda lagu ilaaliyo qorshaha maaliyadeed ee dowladda. Laakiin xaaladda hadda jirta waxay u muuqataa mid taas ka duwan.Wararka soo gaadhay WardheerNews, waxay tilmaamayaan in shaqaalaha rayidka ahi ay heleen laba jeer oo keliya mushaar intii lagu jiray 2026, kuwaasoo la xiriiray labada ciidood, iyadoo daymaha mushaharaadku weli taagan yihiin. Mushaharaadka aan la bixin ayaa lagu qiyaasayaa ku dhowaad $500,000 bishii. Haddii toddobo bilood la isku leeyahay, wadartu waxay gaari kartaa ku dhowaad $3.5 milyan. Taasi waa lacag weyn, laakiin marka loo eego dakhliga dowladda oo lagu qiyaasay ku dhowaad $10 milyan bishii, waxay dhalinaysaa su’aal muhiim ah: Haddii Puntland ay bil kasta hesho malaayiin doollar oo dakhli ah, maxay u awooddi la’dahay inay hesho $500,000 oo lagu bixiyo mushaaraadka dadka maamula hay’adaha dowladda? Maxaa Dhacaya Marka Shaqaale Mushaharkiisa Weydiiyo? Arinta ugu weyn ee dowladnimadu wuxuu noqon karaa sida maamulka Puntland uga jawaabo shaqaalaha aan la siin xuquuqdii shaqada- mushaharkoodi. Shaqaale weydiiya sababta mushaharkiisa loo siin waayay looma qaadan karo qof aan daacad ahayn, dhib badan ama siyaasad wata. Inaad dalbato mushaharka aad xaqa u leedahay ma aha siyaasad; waa xuquuq shaqo. Dowlad hufan waa inay su’aalahan uga jawaabtaa xog iyo caddeyn: dakhliga ay hesho, kharashaadka ay bixiso, waajibaadka mushaharaadka iyo qorshaha lagu bixinayo lacagaha lagu leeyahay shaqaalaha. Haddii dakhliga dowladda yaraaday, waa in shacabka loo sharxaa. Haddii dhaqaalaha loo weeciyay baahiyo amni oo degdeg ah, waa in taas si cad loo shaaciyaa. Haddii safarro, diyaarado la kireysto, wafdiyo dibadda loo diro ama kharashaad kale ay mudnaan ka heleen mushaharaadka shaqaalaha, shacabka waxay xaq u leeyihiin inay ogaadaan. Aamusnaantu waxay sii kordhinaysaa shakiga. Dowladdi haddii aanay gudan waajibaadkii iyo xuquudii shaqaalaha, iyada oo aan la heyn wax sababa ah sida khataro la soo darsay dalka, waa arin  baal marsan sharciga. Wasaaradda Maaliyadda Oo Su’aalo Adag La Weydiinayo Dhibaatadan waxay si toos ah u gelinaysaa Wasaaradda Maaliyadda Puntland xaalad u baahan isla-xisaabtan. Waxaa wasaaradda lagu eedaynayaa inay mararka qaar u shaqeyso sida “ Mashiinka lacaga ATM-ka madaxtooyada,” iyadoo kharashaadka lagu saleeyo mudnaanta xukuumadda halkii si buuxda loogu hoggaansami lahaa miisaaniyadda la ansixiyay. Tani waa eedeyn culus oo u baahan caddeyn iyo isla-xisaabtan, balse jawaabta saxda ahi waa hufnaan. Dowladdu waa inay soo bandhigtaa dakhligeeda iyo kharashaadkeeda bil kasta, isla markaana sharaxdaa sababta mushaaraadka shaqaalaha loogu leeyahay lacago badan iyadoo kharashaad kale ay weli socdaan. Haddii wararka sheegaya in Xisaabiyaha Guud uu tilmaamay ku dhowaad $12 milyan oo waajibaad shaqaale ah oo aan la bixin ay sax yihiin, baahida loo qabo xog rasmi ah iyo daahfurnaan ayaa sii xoogaysanaysa. Mas’uul sare oo dowladeed haddii uu dhowr bilood mushahar waayo, waxaa laga yaabaa inuu u arko dhibaato dhaqaale. Laakiin shaqaale rayid ah oo mushahar hoose qaata, toddobo bilood oo mushaar la’aan ahi waxay noqon kartaa masiibo. Waxay ka dhigan tahay kirada guryaha oo la bixin waayo, deymo isa soo taraya, kharashaadka waxbarashada qoyska, cunto yari iyo qoysas ku tiirsanaada ehel ama amaah aan rasmi ahayn. Natiijadu waxay noqon kartaa niyad-jab, maqnaansho shaqo iyo hoos u dhac ku yimaada adeegyada dowladda. Dowladdu si macquul ah ugama filan karto shaqaalaheeda inay si buuxda ugu heellan yihiin shaqadooda iyadoo aan la fulin waajibka ugu aasaasiga ah ee loo-shaqeeyaha: in shaqaalaha waqtigooda lagu siiyo mushaharkooda. Shaqaale aan lahayn cod wadajir ah Dhibaatadan daba dheeraatay waxay sidoo kale muujinaysaa baahida loo qabo hannaan madax-bannaan oo shaqaalaha rayidka ahi si sharci ah ugu difaaci karaan xuquuqdooda. Urur shaqaale ama hay’ad xirfadeed oo madax-bannaan, sharci ah oo aan siyaasadda ku milmin ayaa siin kara shaqaalaha madal ay kaga hadlaan mushaharaadka, xaaladaha shaqada iyo u hoggaansanaanta miisaaniyadda. Shaqaaluhu waa inay awoodaan inay helaan islamarkaana weydiin karaan su’aalo ku saabsan xuquuqdooda iyaga oo aan ka baqayn in dalabkooda mushahar loo fasirto mucaaradnimo siyaasaddeed. Dowladdu Jawaab Ayay Leedahay Arrintani ma aha oo keliya muran ku saabsan mushaar. Waa mas’uuliyad dowladnimo. Dowladda Puntland waxaa waajib ku ah inay shacabka u sharaxdo sida loo ururiyo, loo qaybiyo loona isticmaalo lacagta dadweynaha. Shaqaalaha rayidka ahna waxay xaq u leeyihiin inay ogaadaan sababta mushaaraadkooda loo bixin waayay, gaar ahaan haddii miisaaniyadda dowladda ay mudnaan siinayso mushaaraadkooda ka hor wasiirrada iyo xildhibaannada. Haddii shaqaale dowladda ahi yiraahdo: “Maxaad u bixin weydeen mushaharkayga?” Jawaabta dowladdu waa inay noqotaa mid cad oo la xaqiijin karo—ma aha aamusnaan, cabsi gelin ama siyaasaddayn. Lacagtu xaggee ku dambaysay? Xaggee ayaa lagu bixiyay? Yaa go’aamiyay mudnaanta kharashaadka? Goormase la bixinayaa mushaaraadka lagu leeyahay shaqaalaha? Waa su’aalo sharci ah oo mudan jawaab. Inta ay dowladdu ka gaabinayso jawaabtooda, dhibaatada mushaharaadku waxay sii noqonaysaa arin aan ku koobnayn awoodda maaliyadeed ee Puntland, balse taabanaya isla-xisaabtanka, hufnaanta maamulka iyo karaamada dadka u shaqeeya dowladda. Wasaaradda Maaliyadda Oo Su’aalo Adag La Weydiinayo Dhibaatadan waxay si toos ah u gelinaysaa Wasaaradda Maaliyadda Puntland xaalad u baahan isla-xisaabtan. Waxaa wasaaradda lagu eedaynayaa inay mararka qaar u shaqeyso sida “ Mashiinka lacaga ATM-ka madaxtooyada,” iyadoo kharashaadka lagu saleeyo mudnaanta xukuumadda halkii si buuxda loogu hoggaansami lahaa miisaaniyadda la ansixiyay. Tani waa eedeyn culus oo u baahan caddeyn iyo isla-xisaabtan, balse jawaabta saxda ahi waa hufnaan. Dowladdu waa inay soo bandhigtaa dakhligeeda iyo kharashaadkeeda bil kasta, isla markaana sharaxdaa sababta mushaaraadka shaqaalaha loogu leeyahay lacago badan iyadoo kharashaad kale ay weli socdaan. Haddii wararka sheegaya in Xisaabiyaha Guud uu tilmaamay ku dhowaad $12 milyan oo waajibaad shaqaale ah oo aan la bixin ay sax yihiin, baahida loo qabo xog rasmi ah iyo daahfurnaan ayaa sii xoogaysanaysa. Mas’uul sare oo dowladeed haddii uu dhowr bilood mushahar waayo, waxaa laga yaabaa inuu u arko dhibaato dhaqaale. Laakiin shaqaale rayid ah oo mushahar hoose qaata, toddobo bilood oo mushaar la’aan ahi waxay noqon kartaa masiibo. Waxay ka dhigan tahay kirada guryaha oo la bixin waayo, deymo isa soo taraya, kharashaadka waxbarashada qoyska, cunto yari iyo qoysas ku tiirsanaada ehel ama amaah aan rasmi ahayn. Natiijadu waxay noqon kartaa niyad-jab, maqnaansho shaqo iyo hoos u dhac ku yimaada adeegyada dowladda. Dowladdu si macquul ah ugama filan karto shaqaalaheeda inay si buuxda ugu heellan yihiin shaqadooda iyadoo aan la fulin waajibka ugu aasaasiga ah ee loo-shaqeeyaha: in shaqaalaha waqtigooda lagu siiyo mushaharkooda. Shaqaale aan lahayn cod wadajir ah Dhibaatadan daba dheeraatay waxay sidoo kale muujinaysaa baahida loo qabo hannaan madax-bannaan oo shaqaalaha rayidka ahi si sharci ah ugu difaaci karaan xuquuqdooda. Urur shaqaale ama hay’ad xirfadeed oo madax-bannaan, sharci ah oo aan siyaasadda ku milmin ayaa siin kara shaqaalaha madal ay kaga hadlaan mushaharaadka, xaaladaha shaqada iyo u hoggaansanaanta miisaaniyadda. Shaqaaluhu waa inay awoodaan inay helaan islamarkaana weydiin karaan su’aalo ku saabsan xuquuqdooda iyaga oo aan ka baqayn in dalabkooda mushahar loo fasirto mucaaradnimo siyaasaddeed. Dowladdu Jawaab Ayay Leedahay Arrintani ma aha oo keliya muran ku saabsan mushaar. Waa mas’uuliyad dowladnimo. Dowladda Puntland waxaa waajib ku ah inay shacabka u sharaxdo sida loo ururiyo, loo qaybiyo loona isticmaalo lacagta dadweynaha. Shaqaalaha rayidka ahna waxay xaq u leeyihiin inay ogaadaan sababta mushaaraadkooda loo bixin waayay, gaar ahaan haddii miisaaniyadda dowladda ay mudnaan siinayso mushaaraadkooda ka hor wasiirrada iyo xildhibaannada. Haddii shaqaale dowladda ahi yiraahdo: “Maxaad u bixin weydeen mushaharkayga?” Jawaabta dowladdu waa inay noqotaa mid cad oo la xaqiijin karo—ma aha aamusnaan, cabsi gelin ama siyaasaddayn. Lacagtu xaggee ku dambaysay? Xaggee ayaa lagu bixiyay? Yaa go’aamiyay mudnaanta kharashaadka? Goormase la bixinayaa mushaaraadka lagu leeyahay shaqaalaha? Waa su’aalo sharci ah oo mudan jawaab. Inta ay dowladdu ka gaabinayso jawaabtooda, dhibaatada mushaharaadku waxay sii noqonaysaa arin aan ku koobnayn awoodda maaliyadeed ee Puntland, balse taabanaya isla-xisaabtanka, hufnaanta maamulka iyo karaamada dadka u shaqeeya dowladda. items.title: Xamza: Waa khad cas, mana aha wax laga gorgortami karo in…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Soomaaliya, Xamza Cabdi Barre oo wareysi gaar ah siiyay wargeyska Al Sharq ee dalka Qatar ayaa ka hadlay arrimo xasaasi ah oo ku aadan aqoonsiga ay Israel siisay Somaliland. Xamza ayaa shaaca ka qaaday in madax-bannaanida iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee Soomaaliya aysan ahayn arrin laga gorgortami karo, isla markaana Dowladda Federaalka ay ka digeyso faragelin kasta oo wax u dhimaysa midnimada dalka. Sidoo kale wuxuu hoosta ka xariiqay in mowqifka Soomaaliya uu weli sidiisii yahay, isla markaana ay diiddan tahay tallaabo kasta, aqoonsi kasta ama heshiis kasta oo hareer mara Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, waxna u dhimaya midnimada dhuleed ee Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya. Waxaa kale oo uu xusay in aqoonsiga Somaliland uu yahay dano is ballaarin ah oo Israel leedahay, kuwaas oo uu ku tilmaamay in aysan dan ugu jirin shacabka Soomaaliyeed. Ra’iisul wasaaraha ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in Soomaaliya ay diyaar u tahay wada-hadalka lagu xallinayo arrimaha gudaha dalka, balse aan la aqbali karin faragelita shisheeye. “Midnimada Soomaaliya waa khad cas,” ayuu Xamza. Dhanka kale waxa uu tilmaamay in Soomaaliya ay midnimadeeda ku difaaci doonto siyaasad, diblomaasiyad iyo sharci, iyo dhammaan hababka sharciga ah ee waafaqsan xeerarka caalamiga ah iyo mabaadi’da dastuurka Soomaaliya. Ugu dambeyn, wuxuu xusay in Soomaaliya ay ka mid tahay dalalkii dhidibada u taagay Ururka Midowga Afrika, isla markaana ay leedahay xuduudo caalami ahaan loo aqoonsan yahay, sidaas darteedna aysan jirin cid kale oo xaqiiqadaas ku beddeli karta tallaabooyin hal dhinac ah. items.title: Ciidamada Badda Soomaaliya oo Turkiga Tababar Kaga Soo Laabtay
items.description: Muqdisho (Raxanreeb Online): Ciidamo ka tirsan Ciidanka Badda Soomaaliya oo tababar ku soo dhamaystay dalka Turkiga ayaa la filayaa in dhawaan lagu qalabeeyo maraakiib dagaal iyo agab ciidan oo loogu talagalay howlaha badda. Tallaabadan ayaa qeyb ka ah iskaashiga dhinaca difaaca iyo amniga badda ee u dhexeeya Soomaaliya iyo Turkiga, iyadoo la doonayo in kor loo qaado awoodda Ciidanka Badda Soomaaliya. Maraakiibta iyo qalabka la siinayo ciidamada ayaa loo adeegsan doonaa ilaalinta xeebaha Soomaaliya, la-dagaallanka burcad-badeedda iyo ka hortagga kalluumeysiga sharci-darrada ah, oo muddooyinkii dambe caqabado ku ahaa amniga iyo dhaqaalaha badda Soomaaliya. Iskaashiga Soomaaliya iyo Turkiga ee dhinaca badda ayaa sidoo kale qeyb ka ah dadaallada lagu dhisayo ciidan Soomaaliyeed oo awood u leh ilaalinta biyaha territorial-ka dalka iyo khayraadka badda. Faahfaahinta ku saabsan tirada maraakiibta iyo nooca qalabka la siinayo ciidamada weli si rasmi ah looma shaacin. items.title: MW Xasan Sheekh oo Ka Qaybgalay Shirka Dalalka Aan Isbahaysiga Ahayn
items.description: Belgrade, Serbia (Raxanreeb Online): Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa maanta magaalada Belgrade ee dalka Serbia kaga qeyb galay Shirka Dalalka Aan Isbahaysiga Ahayn (Non-Aligned Movement). Madaxweynaha ayaa shirka kusoo bandhigay caqabadaha amniga, siyaasadda iyo dhaqaalaha ee dunidu wajahayo, isagoo adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay xoojinta iskaashiga iyo wada-shaqeynta caalamiga ah. Xasan Sheekh ayaa sidoo kale ka hadlay xaaladda Soomaaliya iyo dadaallada dowladda ee ku aaddan xasilloonida, dib-u-dhiska iyo horumarinta dalka, iyadoo Soomaaliya ay raadineyso iskaashi caalami ah oo wax ka tara amniga iyo horumarka. Shirka Belgrade ayaa diiradda lagu saarayaa sidii dalalka aan isbahaysiga ahayn ay uga wada shaqeyn lahaayeen nabadda, amniga, horumarinta dhaqaalaha iyo xallinta khilaafaadka. items.title: Sawirro: Maxay ka wadahadleen Jaamac iyo safiirka Türkiye?
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ku-simaha Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya, Ahna Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka Mudane Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac) ayaa maanta kulan mira dhal ah la qaatay safiirka Türkiye u fadhiya Soomaaliya Danjire Alper Aktaş, oo ay ka wada-hadleen arrimo muhiim ah. Kulanka labada mas’uul ayaa waxaa looga hadlay xoojinta iyo dardargelinta xiriirka qotada dheer, walaaltinimada iyo iskaashiga istiraatiijiga ah ee ka dhexeeya labada dal ee Soomaaliya iyo Türkiye. Jaamac ayaa sidoo kale uga mahadceliyey dowladda iyo shacabka Türkiye taageerada joogtada ah ee ay la garab taagan yihiin dowladda iyo shacabka Soomaaliyeed, maadaama Ankara ay taageerada ugu badan siiso Soomaaliya. Waxaa kale oo uu rajo wanaagsan ka muujiyey in xiriirka iyo iskaashiga istiraatiijiga ah ee labada dal uu sii xoogeysan doono, si loo gaaro horumar iyo danaha ay wadaagaan labada shacab. Dhankiisa Danjire Alper Aktaş ayaa muujiyey sida ay dowladdiisa uga go’an tahay sii xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga ay la leedahay Soomaaliya, isagoo adkeeyey muhiimadda ay leedahay in la sii ambaqaado wada-shaqeynta labada dal. Jaamac oo aad ugu dhow Türkiye ayaa maalmahan xoojiyay galaangalkiisa, waxaana shalay u diray hambalyo diirran oo ku aadan 30-ka Agoosto, oo ku astaysan Maalinta Guusha ee dalkaasi. “Guushan taariikhiga ah waxay muunad u tahay halganka xorriyadda, madaxbannaanida iyo karaamada, waxayna dhiirrigelin u noqotay shucuub badan oo dunida ku nool,” ayuu yiri Guddoomiye Jaamac. Waxaa kale oo uu sheegay in Soomaaliya ay si qoto dheer u qadarinayso taageerada joogtada ah ee Türkiye, gaar ahaan doorkii taariikhiga ahaa ee Madaxweyne Recep Tayyip Erdoğan iyo iskaashiga xooggan ee labada dal. The post Sawirro: Maxay ka wadahadleen Jaamac iyo safiirka Türkiye? appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Turkish Warplanes Reportedly Strike Near Basra as Somalia’s War Against Al-Shabaab Escalates
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — The skies over central Somalia have reportedly become a new front in the country’s intensifying war against Al-Shabaab, with Turkish F-16 fighter jets said to have carried out airstrikes near Basra, a strategically important area located between the Middle and Lower Shabelle regions, roughly 35 kilometers northwest of Mogadishu. The reported strikes came as Somali government forces launched heavy ground operations against Al-Shabaab in and around Basra, raising the stakes in an offensive aimed at pushing the militant group away from key positions along the Shabelle River. Local sources said the reported Turkish airstrikes targeted Al-Shabaab positions and suspected militant strongholds, particularly around settlements near the river. Initial reports indicated casualties among the militants, although the number of dead and wounded could not be independently verified. The Somali Ministry of Defence separately said government forces were conducting a major offensive in the Basra area and claimed that several Al-Shabaab fighters, including two senior commanders, had been killed and weapons seized. However, neither the Somali nor Turkish government has officially confirmed that Turkish F-16s conducted the reported strikes, leaving questions over the precise nature and extent of Ankara’s direct involvement in the operation. If confirmed, the airstrikes would mark another significant development in Turkey’s expanding military role in Somalia and demonstrate the increasingly international character of the country’s fight against Al-Shabaab. Turkey has emerged as one of Mogadishu’s most important military partners, providing training, equipment and broader security assistance to Somali forces. The reported deployment of F-16 aircraft to Somalia earlier this year further underscored the growing sophistication of Turkey’s military involvement. Basra: A Small Area with Outsized Strategic Importance The fighting around Basra is significant not simply because of the military confrontation taking place there, but because of the area’s geography. Basra sits along an important corridor connecting parts of the Middle and Lower Shabelle regions and lies relatively close to the capital. Control of the surrounding territory can therefore influence movement between rural areas and Mogadishu while providing access toward other strategically important locations. For Al-Shabaab, maintaining positions in the area offers opportunities to disrupt government movements and exert pressure on communities and routes surrounding the capital. items.title: Maxaa Ka Jira: Cali Isaaq Ibraahim oo Lagu Eedeeyay inuu U Goostay Ciidamada Laftagareen?
items.description: Baydhabo (Raxanreeb Online): Warar aan weli si rasmi ah loo xaqiijin ayaa sheegaya in Cali Isaaq Ibraahim, oo ka tirsan Qeybta 60-aad ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, uu u goostay ciidamada taabacsan Madaxweyne Cabdicasiis Laftagareen ee ku sugan duleedka magaalada Baydhabo. Cali Isaaq Ibraahim ayaa la sheegay inuu yahay walaalka Taliyaha Guutada 8-aad ee Qeybta 60-aad, Cabdulle Isaaq, hase yeeshee xogta ku saabsan goosashadiisa iyo sababta uu dhinacaas ugu biiray weli ma hayso xaqiijin rasmi ah. Haddii warkani xaqiiqo noqdo, wuxuu imaanayaa xilli Baydhabo iyo nawaaxigeeda ay ka jiraan xiisado siyaasadeed iyo dhaqdhaqaaqyo ciidan, iyadoo dowladda Federaalka iyo maamulka Koonfur Galbeed ay isku hayaan arrimo siyaasadeed iyo amni. Ilaa hadda ma jiro war rasmi ah oo kasoo baxay Taliska Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, Qeybta 60-aad ama dhinaca ciidamada Laftagareen oo xaqiijinaya ama beeninaya warkan. Sidaas darteed, xogtan waa in loo qaataa war hordhac ah ilaa ilo rasmi ah ay ka hadlaan. items.title: Somalia’s Seven-Month Election Deadline: Breakthrough or Another Political Trap?
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — Somalia’s prolonged political deadlock may be approaching a critical turning point after President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud reportedly accepted three significant proposals during the latest rounds of talks between the Federal Government and opposition groups, negotiations facilitated by international partners. The apparent concessions could signal the first meaningful movement toward a political settlement—but major questions remain unanswered, leaving the fate of Somalia’s electoral process hanging in the balance. The most consequential point concerns the seven-month timeframe for holding elections. President Hassan is reportedly prepared, in principle, to accept elections within seven months. But there is a crucial ambiguity: he has not explicitly committed to holding the presidential election within that period, instead referring broadly to “Federal Government elections.” That distinction could prove decisive. The second point involves the creation of an electoral task force responsible for preparing and coordinating the electoral process. The proposal could provide a mechanism for the competing political forces to participate in shaping the election framework rather than leaving the process entirely in the hands of the federal administration. The President has also reportedly accepted the need for a political agreement with the opposition, potentially creating a pathway out of the constitutional and electoral impasse that has increasingly polarized the country. Yet beneath these apparent breakthroughs lie a more difficult dispute. President Hassan reportedly insists that the international community’s role should be described as “facilitation,” rather than mediation, and has rejected the idea of international actors serving as guarantors of any agreement reached between the government and opposition. That disagreement may sound procedural, but it goes to the heart of the negotiations. For the opposition, international guarantees could provide a degree of confidence that commitments reached at the negotiating table will actually be implemented. For the government, however, accepting external guarantees could be viewed as granting international actors an unusually direct role in Somalia’s domestic political arrangements. As a result, the latest talks appear to have produced movement—but not yet a settlement. The central question now hanging over Mogadishu is deceptively simple: Does “elections within seven months” include the election of the President of the Federal Republic of Somalia? If the answer is yes, the latest understanding could represent the beginning of a credible political exit from the current crisis. If the presidential election is excluded—or the language remains deliberately ambiguous—the seven-month deadline could become little more than another political mechanism for postponing the decisive question. With Somalia already deeply divided over the Constitution, electoral institutions and the legitimacy of the political transition, the wording of this agreement may ultimately matter as much as the agreement itself. The next stage of negotiations will therefore be closely watched. What appears today to be a promising compromise could either become the foundation of a national political settlement—or another chapter in Somalia’s seemingly endless cycle of negotiations, deadlines and unresolved political disputes. items.title: DEG-DEG: Deni oo Amarro Cusub Ka Soo Saaray Amniga iyo Maamulka Puntland
items.description: Boosaaso (Raxanreeb Online): Madaxweynaha Dowladda Puntland, Siciid Cabdullaahi Deni, ayaa maanta magaalada Boosaaso kulan kula qaatay Golaha Wasiirrada, Xildhibaannada iyo masuuliyiin kale oo ka tirsan xukuumaddiisa, isagoo soo saaray amarro cusub oo la xiriira amniga, hubka sharci-darrada ah, ciidamada iyo horumarinta kaabayaasha Puntland. 1. Hubka sharci-darrada ah Madaxweyne Deni ayaa faray in laamaha amniga ay xiraan maleeshiyaadka hubaysan ee ku lug yeesha dagaallada beelaha, isla markaana laga qaado hubka ay wataan, iyadoo hubkaasi lagu wareejinayo dowladda. Wuxuu sidoo kale sheegay in maleeshiyaadka iyo hubka laga qabto lagu soo bandhigo warbaahinta. 2. Ciidamada iyo dadka hubaysan Madaxweynaha ayaa amar ku bixiyay in la xiro dadka hubaysan iyo ciidamada aan shaqada ku jirin ee hubka kula dhex wareega magaalooyinka, isla markaana hubka laga qaado. Deni ayaa sidoo kale uga digay ciidamada dowladda inay ka qeybqaataan dagaallada beelaha, isagoo sheegay in askari ama ciidan lagu helo arrintaasi laga qaadi doono tallaabo. 3. Ilaalada masuuliyiinta Madaxweyne Deni ayaa amar ku bixiyay in la yareeyo tirada ilaalada madaxda dowladda. Sida amarka cusub, wasiir kasta waxaa loo oggolaaday laba askari, halka wasiir ku-xigeenkana loo oggolaaday hal askari. 4. Amniga xeebaha Deni ayaa sheegay in la kordhin doono ciidamada ka hawlgala xeebaha Puntland, isagoo xusay in ujeeddadu tahay kordhinta dakhliga iyo xoojinta dagaalka ka dhanka ah burcad-badeedda. 5. Ballaarinta Dekedda Boosaaso Madaxweynaha ayaa amray in laga bilaabo berri la bilaabo wacyigelinta dadka ku nool xaafadaha ku dhow Dekedda Boosaaso, maadaama la qorsheynayo ballaarinta dekedda. Wuxuu sidoo kale sheegay in Khamiista la bilaabi doono duminta dhismayaasha ku dhow dekedda. 6. Amniga Gaalkacyo iyo Boosaaso Madaxweyne Deni ayaa sheegay in markii uu xilka qabtay Gaalkacyo iyo Boosaaso ay kamid ahaayeen magaalooyinka ugu amni darran Puntland, iyadoo uu sheegay in xilligaasi meelo badan ay joogeen ciidamo iyo dad hubaysan. items.title: MW Xasan Sheekh oo Khudbad Ka Jeediyay Shirka Dalalka Aan Isbahaysiga Ahayn
items.description: Belgrade, Serbia (Raxanreeb Online): Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, ayaa maanta magaalada Belgrade ee dalka Serbia kaga qeyb galay Shirka Dalalka Aan Isbahaysiga Ahayn (Non-Aligned Movement), halkaas oo uu khudbad kaga hadlay xaaladda amni, siyaasadeed iyo dhaqaale ee dunida. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa sheegay in caqabadaha maanta dunidu wajahdo, oo ay kamid yihiin colaadaha, argagixisada, xiisadaha juqraafi-siyaasadeed iyo isbeddelka cimilada, ay u baahan yihiin iskaashi iyo isku-duubni caalami ah. Madaxweynaha ayaa sidoo kale shirka kusoo bandhigay horumarka Soomaaliya iyo dadaallada Dowladda Federaalka ee ku aaddan xasilloonida, dib-u-dhiska iyo horumarinta dalka, isagoo uga mahadceliyay bahwadaagta caalamiga ah taageerada ay si joogto ah u siiyaan Soomaaliya. Xasan Sheekh ayaa adkeeyay in Soomaaliya ay ka go’an tahay dhowrista mabaadi’da Dhaqdhaqaaqa Dalalka Aan Isbahaysiga Ahayn, gaar ahaan madaxbannaanida iyo midnimada dhuleed ee dalalka, caddaaladda, sinnaanta iyo xalinta khilaafaadka si nabad ah. Shirka Belgrade ayaa madaxda iyo wakiillada dalalka ka qeybgalaya siinaya fursad ay kaga wada hadlaan xasilloonida caalamka, iskaashiga dalalka soo koraya iyo sidii loo wajihi lahaa caqabadaha amni, dhaqaale iyo siyaasadeed ee dunida. items.title: Somalia says funding, logistics delay Egyptian troop deployment
items.description: Cairo (Somalia Today) — Funding problems, logistical arrangements and operational requirements are delaying the deployment of Egyptian troops to the African Union mission in Somalia, a senior Somali foreign ministry official has said. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar said Egypt remained ready to deploy its contingent to the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia, or AUSSOM. “Egypt has clearly demonstrated its readiness to deploy its forces,” Omar told Saudi newspaper Asharq Al-Awsat in an interview published on Sunday. He pointed to President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s visit to Egyptian troops preparing for the mission as evidence of Cairo’s readiness. “The crisis is not a lack of Egyptian political commitment or readiness,” Omar said. He said the deployment must take place within agreed African Union and United Nations arrangements, including the sequencing of troop rotations, logistics and operational requirements. Omar also cited the broader challenge of securing sustainable funding for AUSSOM, saying Somalia wanted the remaining arrangements completed as quickly as possible. Long-delayed deployment Egypt is among the countries selected to contribute forces to AUSSOM, which replaced the previous African Union mission in Somalia at the start of 2025. UN planning documents have envisaged the deployment of 1,091 Egyptian troops as part of changes to the mission’s force structure, alongside the withdrawal of Burundian personnel. The African Union reiterated in February that Egypt was ready to contribute troops and called for the acceleration of its deployment alongside the repatriation of Burundian forces and a Ghanaian police unit. Preparations have been under way for more than a year, but the Egyptian contingent has yet to deploy. Egypt’s participation would further expand the security relationship between Cairo and Mogadishu, which has deepened in recent years, including military assistance, training and closer political cooperation. Egyptian troops would also join other AUSSOM contingents to support Somali forces against Al-Shabaab and help with the gradual transfer of security responsibilities to Somali authorities. Funding pressure The delay comes as AUSSOM faces persistent uncertainty over how its operations will be financed. The mission depends heavily on United Nations logistical support for food, fuel, aviation, medical evacuation, transport and other operational needs. For the 2025-26 financial year, AUSSOM required about $190 million for troop reimbursements. However, the African Union had secured only around $120 million in confirmed pledges, Somalia Today reported in July . The UN logistical operation supporting AUSSOM is itself worth hundreds of millions of dollars annually, making predictable donor financing central to the mission’s ability to sustain troops and bases across Somalia. The funding challenge has become more acute as the United States has signalled that it will not support continued UN logistical assistance to AUSSOM beyond the end of 2026. The African Union has repeatedly called for predictable and sustainable financing, warning that continued shortfalls could undermine the mission. The uncertainty comes as AUSSOM continues to support Somali forces fighting Al-Shabaab while Mogadishu seeks to assume greater responsibility for national security. items.title: Puntland and AFRICOM Discuss U.S. Military Presence as Security Threats Intensify
items.description: Bosaso (WDN) — Puntland President Said Abdullahi Deni met in Bosaso with senior officials from the U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM), led by U.S. Special Operations Forces commander for East Africa, Colonel James Rose, for talks centered on security cooperation and the proposed expansion of the U.S. military presence in Puntland. The meeting focused on strengthening cooperation between Puntland and the United States in the areas of counterterrorism, maritime security and military capacity-building. The discussions also included plans to accelerate the development of a U.S. military facility in Bosaso, as well as cooperation against ISIS-Somalia and Al-Shabaab, particularly militants operating in the Cal Miskaad and Calmadow mountain ranges. The timing of a potential U.S. base in Bosaso could prove particularly significant. Puntland faces a combination of security threats that extend beyond terrorism. ISIS and Al-Shabaab remain active in parts of the region, while piracy continues to pose a threat to maritime security along Somalia’s strategically important coastline. For Puntland, a stronger American presence could therefore represent more than a military partnership. It could provide an additional layer of security at a time when the region faces increasingly complex threats on land and at sea. There is also an important economic and political dimension to the proposal. Unlike some foreign military and commercial arrangements that have generated concerns among local communities over who ultimately benefits from the exploitation of Somalia’s strategic location and natural resources, many Puntland residents are likely to expect a U.S. presence to be accompanied by projects that directly benefit local communities. Such expectations could include investment in infrastructure, employment opportunities, vocational training, healthcare, education, water projects and maritime development—particularly in communities located near any future military installation. That expectation could become an important factor in determining how the local population views an expanded American presence. A U.S. facility in Bosaso would also place American forces close to one of the most strategically important maritime corridors in the world. Puntland’s coastline overlooks the Gulf of Aden and the wider approaches to the Red Sea and Indian Ocean, giving the region considerable importance for international shipping and maritime security. For Washington, a presence in Bosaso could potentially improve its ability to monitor and respond to militant activity, piracy and other threats affecting the Gulf of Aden and surrounding waters. For Puntland, meanwhile, the partnership could provide access to advanced military training, intelligence cooperation and counterterrorism capabilities that its security forces have struggled to develop independently. The challenge will be ensuring that the relationship produces benefits beyond the security sector. A foreign military presence that is seen solely as serving external strategic interests could eventually generate local resentment. Conversely, a partnership that combines security cooperation with visible investments in the welfare and economic prospects of surrounding communities could build much stronger public support. President Deni was accompanied at the meeting by members of his cabinet, presidential advisers, senior officials from the Puntland presidency and military officers. The discussions therefore come at a potentially consequential moment for Puntland. With terrorism, piracy and regional instability continuing to threaten the Horn of Africa, a credible U.S. security presence in Bosaso could be welcomed by many local residents as an opportunity to strengthen both security and development—provided that the partnership respects Puntland’s interests and delivers tangible benefits to its people. The question now is not simply whether the United States will establish a stronger military footprint in Bosaso. It is what that presence will mean for the people who live there—and whether American security cooperation can become a catalyst for local development as well as a response to regional threats. items.title: Mahadsanid Madaxweyne Hawlgabku waa fursad Dahabi ah
items.description: ​Waxaynu ogsoonahay in dhiirigelinta iyo fursadaha la siiyo dhalinyarada-cusub (dhalinyarada) ay tahay tallaabada ugu horreysa ee loo qaado dhanka horumarka iyo shaqo abuurka. ​Tartan iyo tamar cusub: Waxay dhalinyarada u bannaynaysaa in ay keenaan fikrado hal-abuur leh oo casri ah. ​Mustaqbal hubaal ah: Waxay horseedaysaa in cududdii shaqo ee dalka lagu soo biiriyo dhiig cusub oo hibo iyo aqoon leh. ​Mas’uuliyad qaran: Waa tallaabo muujinaysa in taladii iyo hawshii dalkaba loo dhiibayo gacmo da’yar oo hufan. ​Mahadnaq iyo bogaadin ayay mudan tahay tallaabadan horusocodka ahi. Waa inoo dhalinyaro hawsha dar-dar gelinaysa oo mustaqbalka hoggaaminaysa! ​ Liibaan Maxamed

items.title: Safiirkii Itoobiya ee Muqdisho ka tegay oo farriin cajiib ah soo diray
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Safiirkii Itoobiya ee Soomaaliya, Suleymaan Dedefo Woshe oo dhawaan soo gaba-gabeeyay howlihii diblomaasiyadeed ee uu ku joogay Muqdisho ayaa fariin ku saabsan xaaladda Soomaaliya u soo diray shacabka iyo hoggaamiyeyaasha dalka. Safiirka ayaa sheegay inuu ka xun yahay dhibaatooyinka amni-darro ee ay weli wajahayaan shacabka Soomaaliyeed, isagoo xusay in nabadgelyadu tahay xuquuq ay mudan yihiin dhammaan dadka Soomaaliyeed. “Waxa aan ka xumahay dhibaatooyinka ay shacabka Soomaaliyeed weli la kulmaan ee amni-darro. Shacabka Soomaaliyeed waxay mudan yihiin nabad,” ayuu yiri Suleymaan Dedefo. Diblomaasiga Itoobiya ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in shacabka Soomaaliya ay xaq u leeyihiin inay helaan amni, xorriyad, sharaf iyo fursado ay ku horumariyaan noloshooda, isagoo carrabka ku adkeeyay baahida loo qabo in dalka laga abuuro xaalad ay dadku ku noolaadaan xasillooni. “Waxay mudan yihiin amni. Waxay mudan yihiin xorriyad, sharaf, fursad iyo barwaaqo,” ayuu hadalkiisa ku sii daray. Suleymaan Dedefo ayaa sheegay inuu rajeynayo in carruurta Soomaaliyeed ay ku koraan waddan ammaan ah oo nabdoon, ayna mustaqbalkooda ku wajahaan rajo halkii ay cabsi ka dareemi lahaayeen. Sidoo kale wuxuu ugu baaqay hoggaamiyeyaasha Soomaaliyeed inay dhinac iska dhigaan khilaafaadka siyaasadeed, isla markaana danta qaranka ka hormariyaan arrimaha kale. “Waxa aan si daacad ah u rajeynayaa in hoggaamiyayaasha Soomaaliyeed ay meel iska dhigaan khilaafka oo danta qaranka ka hor mariyaan wax kasta,” ayuu yiri Dedefo, isagoo xusay in mas’uuliyadda saaran hoggaamiyeyaasha ay tahay mid weyn, ayna hortaal fursad lagu dhisi karo Soomaaliya nabad ah, midaysan, deggan oo barwaaqo ah.
