items.title: Turkiga oo Soomaaliya u soo diray maraakiib dagaal oo DF Soomaaliya ka caawinaya…
items.description: Ankara (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Turkiga ayaa sheegtay inay taageero siineyso mas’uuliyiinta Soomaaliya, kaddib afduubkii markab ee ka dhacay biyaha Soomaaliya, kaasi oo la sheegay in uu Muqdisho usoo siday hub ay leedahay Ankara. Dowladda Turkiga ayaa sheegtay in laba markab oo ka tirsan ciidamada badda Turkiga ay toddobaadka soo socda ku wajahan yihiin Jabuuti, iyagoo qayb ka ah howlgalka badeed ee Ankara ka waddo Soomaaliya iyo nawaaxigeeda. Afhayeenka Wasaaradda Gaashaandhigga Turkiga, Zeki Akturk, ayaa sheegay in maraakiibta TCG Kemalreis iyo TCG Yzb Gungor Durmus ay Jabuuti booqan doonaan 3-da iyo 4-ta September, si ay taageero ugu fidiyaan kooxda howlgalka ciidamada badda Soomaaliya iyo howlaha saadka ee ku wajahan Soomaaliya. Wasaaraddu waxay sidoo kale si gaar ah uga hadashay afduubkii dhowaan dhacay, iyadoo sheegtay in ciidamada Turkiga ee Soomaaliya ay sii wadaan inay Soomaaliya ka caawiyaan xoojinta awooddeeda la-dagaallanka argagixisada iyo burcad-badeednimada, iyadoo loo marayo heshiisyada laba geesoodka ah ee labada dal. “Taageerada lagama maarmaanka ah ayaa la siinayaa mas’uuliyiinta Soomaaliya, iyadoo lala kaashanayo Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda arrinta ka dhacday gudaha biyaha Soomaaliya,” ayey wasaaraddu ku sheegtay bayaan. Wasaaraddu ma aysan magacaabin markabka la afduubtay, mana aysan caddeyn nooca taageero ee Turkigu bixinayo. Sidoo kale, ma aysan sheegin in labada markab ee toddobaadka soo socda tagaya Jabuuti ay ka qayb qaadan doonaan hawlgal la xiriira afduubka. Hadalladan ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli si weyn isha loogu hayo hawl-gallada militari ee Turkiga ee ka socda xeebaha Puntland, halkaas oo burcad-badeeddu ay ku haystaan markabka M/V LUTUF iyo shaqaalihii saarnaa. Markab hub sida oo la afduubtay Burcad-badeeddu waxay 17-kii August qabsadeen markabka LUTUF, oo sita calanka Cameroon, kaas oo xilligaas qiyaastii 3.5 mayl-badeed u jiray deegaanka Marraya ee degmada Eyl ee Puntland, kadibna waxay u jiheeyeen dhanka xeebaha Nugaal. Sarkaal Soomaali ah ayaa wakaaladda wararka AP u sheegay in markabka uu siday hub Turkigu leeyahay, qalab isgaarsiineed iyo nidaamyo dayax-gacmeed, kuwaas oo ku sii jeeday xarunta tababarka ciidamada Turkiga ee Muqdisho. Markabka waxaa saarnaa 10 qof oo shaqaale ah, kuwaas oo kala ah lix Hindi ah, hal Turki ah, hal Georgian ah iyo laba Serbian ah oo ahaa ilaalo amni. Warar soo baxay toddobaadkan ayaa sheegay in burcad-badeedda ay dalbadeen lacag madax-furasho ah oo ku dhow laba milyan oo dollar si ay u sii daayaan markabka. Ilaa hadda ma cadda in wada-hadallo rasmi ah oo madax-furasho ah ay billowdeen iyo in dhinac uu aqbalay bixinta lacagtaas. Afduubka ayaa sidoo kale dhaliyay khilaaf ku saabsan duqeymo dhanka cirka ah oo dhimasho sababay, kuwaas oo ka dhacay meel u dhow goobta lagu hayo markabka. Wasiir-ku-xigeenka Amniga Puntland, Cabdiraxmaan Yuusuf Dujana ayaa Turkiga ku eedeeyay inuu fuliyay laba duqeyn oo uu sheegay inay dileen ugu yaraan 13 qof. Waxa uu sidoo kale ku eedeeyay Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya inay ku lug leedahay, balse ma uusan soo bandhigin caddeyn si madax-bannaan loo xaqiijin karo oo labada dowladood midkood ku xiriirinaysa weerarradaas. Ma jirto dowlad ama ciidan si rasmi ah u sheegtay inay mas’uul ka tahay duqeymaha, halka Caasimada Online aysan si madax-bannaan u xaqiijin eedeymaha Puntland. Wasaaradda Gaashaandhigga Turkiga ayaan si toos ah uga jawaabin eedeymahaas bayaankii ay Khamiistii soo saartay, mana aysan sheegin in ciidamada Turkigu ay duqeymo dhanka cirka ah ka fuliyeen agagaarka markabka la afduubtay. Wasiiru-dowlaha Wasaaradda Gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya, Cumar Cali Cabdi ayaa 22-kii August sheegay in Dowladda Federaalku ay ka warqabto hawl-gallo militari iyo duqeymo ka socda xeebaha Puntland, isla markaana ay diyaarinayso warbixin ku saabsan arrinta. Hase yeeshee ma uusan sheegin ciidanka ama dhinaca fulinaya hawl-gallada, sidoo kalena ma uusan caddeyn in Muqdisho ay fasaxday weerarradaasi. Puntland ayaa dhankeeda ku baaqday in baaritaan lagu sameeyo duqeymaha. Doorka ballaaran ee ciidamada badda Turkiga Turkiga ayaa si tartiib ah u ballaarinayay joogitaankiisa militari iyo midka badeed ee Soomaaliya, iyadoo arrintan ay salka ku hayaan heshiisyo dhowr ah oo dhanka difaaca ah oo dhexmaray Ankara iyo Muqdisho. Baarlamaanka Turkiga ayaa bishii hore kordhiyay muddada ciidamada Turkiga ee Soomaaliya, iyadoo loo oggolaaday inay dalka sii joogaan laba sano oo dheeraad ah, taasoo muddada hawlgalkooda ka dhigaysa mid soconaya ilaa July 2028. Oggolaanshahaasi wuxuu ciidamada Turkiga u saamaxayaa inay ka hawl-galaan goobaha ay Soomaaliya ku heshiisay oo ay ku jiraan biyaha Soomaaliya, isla markaana ay taageeraan dadaallada lagula dagaallamayo argagixisada, burcad-badeednimada, kalluumeysiga sharci-darrada ah, tahriibinta iyo khataraha kale ee amniga. Doorkaasi wuxuu sidoo kale ku saleysan yahay heshiis 10 sano ah oo dhinaca difaaca iyo iskaashiga dhaqaalaha ah, kaas oo la saxiixay 2024, waxaana Turkigu ku ballanqaaday inuu Soomaaliya ka caawiyo dhismaha, tababarka iyo qalabeynta ciidamada badda iyo xoojinta amniga xeebaha dalka. Ciidamada badda Turkiga ayaa durba hawlgallo ilaalin ah ka wada xeebaha Soomaaliya. Bishii Luulyo, Wasaaradda Gaashaandhigga Turkiga ayaa sheegtay in maraakiibta TCG Goksu, TCG Gelibolu iyo TCG Bartin ay ilaalinayeen markabka qodista shidaalka ee Turkiga Cagri Bey iyo saddex markab oo taageero ah oo ka hawlgallayay xeebaha Soomaaliya. Turkigu wuxuu sidoo kale Muqdisho ku leeyahay xarun weyn oo tababar militari, waxaana muddo ka badan toban sano uu tababar iyo qalab siinayay ciidamada ammaanka Soomaaliya. Ballaarinta hawl-gallada badda ee Turkiga ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli burcad-badeednimadu ay mar kale khatar kasoo cusboonaatay biyaha Soomaaliya iyo Gacanka Cadmeed. Hay’adda Caalamiga ah ee Badaha (IMO) ayaa 24-kii August sheegtay in lix markab iyo in ka badan 90 badmaaxiin ah ay kooxo burcad-badeed iyo kooxo hubeysan ku hayaan gobolka. “Ma oggolaan karno in dib-u-soo-noqoshada burcad-badeednimada ee Gacanka Cadmeed iyo biyaha ku hareeraysan aan wax laga qaban,” ayuu yiri Xoghayaha Guud ee IMO, Arsenio Dominguez, isagoo ku baaqay in si degdeg ah loo sii daayo dadka gacanta lagu hayo. Xafiiska Caalamiga ah ee Badaha (IMB) ayaa diiwaangeliyay 38 dhacdo oo burcad-badeednimo iyo dhac hubeysan ah oo dunida ka dhacay lixdii bilood ee ugu horreeyay 2026. Burcad-badeedda Soomaalida ayaa muddadaas lagu eedeeyay inay mas’uul ka ahaayeen 94 boqolkiiba dhammaan shaqaalaha maraakiibta ee la qafaashay. The post Turkiga oo Soomaaliya u soo diray maraakiib dagaal oo DF Soomaaliya ka caawinaya… appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Tallaabada ay qaaday Sweden ee cashirka weyn u ah Soomaaliya
items.description: Stockholm (Caasimada Online) – Sweden oo ah dal ku yaalla Waqooyiga Yurub, isla markaana ay ku nool yihiin ku dhowaad 10 milyan oo qof ayaa si weyn u xoojisay garab istaagga Finland xilli walaaca laga qabo Ruushka uu sare u kacay. Tallaabadan ayaa muujinaysa sida dalalka yaryar ama dhexdhexaadka ah ay mararka qaar u arkaan in difaaca xulafadooda uu yahay qayb ka mid ah difaaca dalkooda, xitaa haddii dagaalku uusan si toos ah uga socon dhulkooda. Su’aasha muhiimka ahi waxay tahay: maxay Sweden ugu degdegaysaa difaaca Finland, iyadoo Finland ay leedahay ciidan iyo nidaam difaac oo u gaar ah? Jawaabtu waxay ku jirtaa juqraafi-strategiga iyo fahamka casriga ah ee amniga. Dalalku ma daneeyaan oo keliya waxa ka dhacaya xuduudahooda, balse waxay si dhow ula socdaan halka ay khataruhu ka soo dhaqaaqi karaan iyo halka lagu joojin karo ka hor inta aysan gaarin dhulkooda. Difaaca hore iyo ka fogaanshaha khatarta Istaraatiijiyad ahaan, marka dal uu wajaho awood ciidan oo ka xoog badan, wuxuu isku dayaa inuu khatarta ka fogeeyo xuduudihiisa. Joogitaanka ciidamada Itoobiya iyo Kenya ee Soomaaliya, iyo sidoo kale ciidamada kale ee Afrikaan ah ee qaybta ka ah hawlgallada amniga, looma fahmi karo oo keliya inay yihiin ciidamo Soomaaliya loogu caawinayo la-dagaallanka Al-Shabaab. Dal kasta oo ciidan dibadda u dira wuxuu leeyahay dano amni, siyaasadeed iyo istaraatiiji ah oo u gaar ah. Soomaaliya iyo danaha dalalka deriska ah Itoobiya iyo Kenya, tusaale ahaan, waxay muddo dheer wajahayeen khatar ka timaadda Al-Shabaab. Sidaas darteed, marka ay ciidamadoodu gudaha Soomaaliya ka hawlgalaan, waxaa jira dano amni oo ka baxsan taageerada Soomaaliya. Ujeeddada ugu weyn waxay noqon kartaa in khatarta lagu qabto gudaha Soomaaliya, halkii ay uga gudbi lahayd xuduudaha oo ay weerarro ka geysan lahayd gudaha Kenya ama Itoobiya. Tani waxay sidoo kale sharrax ka bixin kartaa sababta mararka qaar shacabka Soomaaliyeed ay u dareemaan in natiijada laga filayay ciidamada shisheeye aysan la jaanqaadin kharashaadka iyo muddada ay Soomaaliya joogeen. Soomaalidu waxay inta badan eegaan su’aasha ah: Al-Shabaab ma laga adkaaday? Halka dalalka ay ciidamadu ka yimaadeen ay mararka qaar eegayaan su’aal kale oo ah: khatartii dalkeenna ma laga fogeeyay? Labadaas aragtiyood ayaa aad u kala duwan. Haddii Kenya ay rabto in Al-Shabaab laga fogeeyo xuduuddeeda, Itoobiya ay doonayso in weerarradu aysan gaarin dhulkeeda, halka Soomaaliya ay rabto in kooxda gebi ahaanba laga saaro dhulkeeda, waxaa jiri kara kala duwanaansho ku saabsan qeexidda guusha. Xuduudaha iyo khatarta soo noqoshada Waxaa intaas dheer, Soomaaliya waxay leedahay caqabad gaar ah: xuduudaheeda dhulka iyo badda. Al-Shabaab waa koox ka hawlgasha deegaan aan ku koobnayn hal meel oo go’an, waxaana suurtagal ah in cadaadis ciidan oo xooggan uu dagaalyahannada ku riixo inay u kala gudbaan deegaanno ama xuduudo kale. Sidaas darteed, guul militari oo gudaha Soomaaliya laga gaaro waxay u baahan tahay qorshe lagu hubinayo in kooxda aysan dib uga soo laaban xuduudaha ama aysan u adeegsan dalalka deriska ah meel ay dib uga abaabusho. Tani waa mid ka mid ah sababaha ay Soomaaliya ugu baahan tahay istaraatiijiyad amni oo ka weyn hawlgal ciidan oo gudaha dalka ka socda. Waxaa loo baahan yahay iskaashi xuduudeed, xog-wadaag, ilaalinta xuduudaha, la-dagaallanka maalgelinta argagixisada iyo xakameynta shabakadaha dadka iyo hubka u kala gudbiya Soomaaliya iyo dalalka deriska ah. Dagaalka iyo kala firdhinta awoodda Waxaa sidoo kale jira dhinac kale oo istaraatiiji ah oo aan si weyn looga hadlin: dagaallada waxaa mararka qaar loo isticmaalaa in lagu kala mashquuliyo awoodaha. Haddii dal awood ciidan leh lagu qasbo inuu ciidamo badan geliyo furin ka baxsan xuduudihiisa, waxaa hoos u dhici karta awoodda uu ku wajihi karo khatar kale oo gudaha ama xuduudihiisa ka jirta. Marka dhinacaas laga eego, dagaalka Soomaaliya wuxuu noqon karaa qayb ka mid ah loollan amni oo gobolka ka socda. Dalalka deriska ah waxay rabaan in khatarta laga fogeeyo dhulkooda, halka Soomaaliya ay rabto inay dib ula soo noqoto awoodda buuxda ee dhulkeeda. Labada dano way is waafaqi karaan, balse mararka qaar waxay yeelan karaan mudnaano kala duwan. Maxay quwadaha reer Galbeedku u taageeraan Soomaaliya? Waxaa sidoo kale muhiim ah in la fahmo sababta Mareykanka iyo dalalka Yurub ay boqollaal milyan oo dollar ugu bixiyaan amniga Soomaaliya. Taageeradaasi ma aha oo keliya mid ku saleysan rabitaanka ah in Al-Shabaab laga adkaado, balse waxay sidoo kale la xiriirtaa ilaalinta xasilloonida Geeska Afrika, amniga marinnada ganacsiga, la-dagaallanka argagixisada iyo ka hortagga in Soomaaliya ay noqoto meel ay kooxaha hubeysan ama quwadaha kale ee loollanka kula jira reer Galbeedku ka helaan fursad. Sidaas darteed, haddii hawlgalka AUSSOM ama taageerada reer Galbeedku Soomaaliya sii socoto, waa in la fahmaa in danaha Soomaaliya iyo kuwa taageerayaasheedu ay isku meel ku kulmaan, balse aysan mar walba isku mid ahayn. Soomaaliya waxay u baahan tahay inay ka faa’iidaysato taageeradaas iyadoo isla waqtigaas dhisanaysa awood ciidan iyo mid hay’adeed oo u oggolaanaysa inay mustaqbalka si madax-bannaan u ilaaliso amnigeeda. Casharka Sweden iyo Finland Halkaas ayay ka muuqanaysaa casharka ugu weyn ee laga baran karo Sweden iyo Finland. Sweden waxay fahamsan tahay in haddii khatar weyn ay ka jirto meel ku dhow xuduuddeeda, sugitaanka ilaa khatartu albaabka soo gaarto aysan ahayn istaraatiijiyad wanaagsan. Sidaas darteed, waxay taageerada Finland u aragtaa maalgashi ku saabsan amniga Sweden lafteeda. Sidoo kale, taageerada reer Galbeedka ee Ukraine waxaa lagu fahmi karaa isla aragtidan. Dalalka taageera Ukraine ma eegayaan oo keliya badbaadada Ukraine, balse waxay sidoo kale doonayaan in Ruushka lagu xaddido meel ka fog dalalka NATO, isla markaana aan loo oggolaan inuu si fudud ugu fidiyo awooddiisa militari dalal kale oo Yurub ah. Arrintan waxaa laga dheehan karaa mabda’a loo yaqaan forward defence, oo ah in khatarta lagu joojiyo meel ka fog dhulka aad rabto inaad difaacdo. Taasi waxay ka duwan tahay difaac ku saleysan in la sugo weerarka kadibna laga jawaabo. Soomaaliya maxay ka baran kartaa? Soomaaliya waxay u baahan tahay inay mabda’aas ka barato, balse si waafaqsan xaaladdeeda. Haddii Al-Shabaab lagu ciribtiro gudaha dalka, balse aan la xakameyn xuduudaha, shabakadaha maalgelinta iyo isu-socodka dagaalyahannada, khatartu waxay heli kartaa fursad ay dib ugu soo laabato. Sidaa darteed, guusha dhabta ahi ma noqon karto oo keliya qabsashada magaalo ama tuulo, balse waa in la dhiso nidaam ka hortaga soo noqoshada khatarta. Si kastaba, arrinta Sweden iyo Finland waxay Soomaaliya xusuusinaysaa in amniga qaranku uusan ku koobnayn xadka dalka. Amniga gudaha, amniga xuduudaha, amniga gobolka iyo danaha quwadaha caalamka ayaa si isku xiran u shaqeeya. Soomaaliya haddii ay rabto inay si dhab ah uga adkaato Al-Shabaab waxay u baahan tahay inay ka gudubto qorshe ku saleysan oo keliya hawlgallo militari, una gudubto istaraatiijiyad amni oo isku xirta ciidanka, sirdoonka, xuduudaha, diblomaasiyadda iyo iskaashiga gobolka. Casharka Sweden wuxuu sidaas ku noqonayaa mid fudud: haddii aad rabto inaad dalkaaga ka ilaaliso dagaal, mararka qaar waa inaad dagaalka ku joojisaa meel ka baxsan xuduudahaaga. Soomaaliya se caqabadda hortaalla waxay tahay inay xaqiijiso in dadaalka lagu joojinayo Al-Shabaab gudaha Soomaaliya uu ugu dambeyn u horseedo amni waara oo ay iyadu leedahay, halkii uu noqon lahaa oo keliya hab dalalka kale khatartooda looga fogeeyo. items.title: Turkey sends warships to support Somalia amid ship hijacking
items.description: Ankara (Somalia Today) — Turkey said Friday it was supporting Somali authorities following the hijacking of a vessel in Somali territorial waters, as two Turkish naval ships prepare to visit Djibouti next week as part of Ankara’s expanding maritime mission around Somalia. Turkish Defence Ministry spokesperson Zeki Akturk said the TCG Kemalreis and TCG Yzb. Gungor Durmus would visit Djibouti on September 3-4 to support the Somali Naval Task Group and logistics missions to Somalia. The ministry separately addressed the recent hijacking , saying the Turkish Armed Forces Somalia Task Force continued to help Somalia strengthen its ability to combat terrorism and piracy under bilateral agreements. “Necessary support is being provided to the Somali authorities, in coordination with our Ministry of Foreign Affairs, regarding the incident that occurred in Somali territorial waters,” the ministry said. It did not identify the vessel, specify what assistance Turkey was providing or say whether the two ships due in Djibouti would take part in any operation linked to the hijacking. The comments come amid growing scrutiny of Turkish military activity off Puntland, Somalia’s semi-autonomous northeastern federal member state, where pirates are holding the M/V LUTUF and its crew. Hijacked arms ship Pirates seized the Cameroon-flagged LUTUF on August 17 about 3.5 nautical miles off Marraya in Puntland’s Eyl district before steering it towards the Nugaal coast. A Somali official told the Associated Press that the vessel was carrying Turkish weapons, communications equipment and satellite systems bound for a Turkish military training facility in Mogadishu. Its 10-member crew comprises six Indians, one Turkish national, one Georgian and two Serbian security guards. Somalia Today reported this week that the pirates had demanded about $2 million for the ship’s release. It remains unclear whether formal ransom negotiations have begun or whether any party has agreed to pay. The hijacking has also triggered a dispute over deadly air strikes near the area where the vessel has been held. Puntland Deputy Security Minister Abdirahman Yusuf Dujana accused Turkey of carrying out two strikes that he said killed at least 13 people. He also accused Somalia’s federal government of involvement, but did not provide independently verifiable evidence linking either government to the attacks. No government or military force has publicly claimed responsibility for the strikes, and Somalia Today has not independently verified Puntland’s allegations. Turkey’s Defence Ministry did not directly address the accusations in Thursday’s statement or say whether Turkish forces had conducted air operations around the hijacked ship. Somalia’s State Minister for Defence Omar Ali Abdi said on August 22 that the federal government was aware of military operations and strikes taking place off Puntland and was preparing a report. He did not identify the force involved or say whether Mogadishu had authorised the attacks. Puntland has called for an investigation into the strikes. Wider naval role Turkey has steadily expanded its military and maritime presence in Somalia under a series of defence agreements between Ankara and Mogadishu. The Turkish parliament last month extended the deployment of Turkish forces in Somalia for another two years, keeping the mandate in force until July 2028. The authorisation allows Turkish forces to operate in areas agreed with Somalia, including its maritime zones, and to support efforts against terrorism, piracy, illegal fishing, smuggling and other security threats. That role also rests on a 10-year defence and economic cooperation agreement signed in 2024, under which Turkey agreed to help Somalia build, train and equip its navy and strengthen security along its coastline. Turkish naval forces are already conducting protection missions off Somalia. In July, Turkey’s Defence Ministry said the TCG Goksu, TCG Gelibolu and TCG Bartin were escorting the Turkish drilling ship Cagri Bey and three support vessels operating off the Somali coast. Turkey also runs a major military training facility in Mogadishu and has spent more than a decade training and equipping Somali security forces. The expanded naval activity comes as piracy has again emerged as a threat in waters off Somalia and the Gulf of Aden. The International Maritime Organisation said on August 24 that six vessels and more than 90 seafarers were being held by pirates and armed robbers in the region. “We cannot allow the resurgence of piracy in the Gulf of Aden and surrounding waters to go unaddressed,” IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez said, calling for the immediate release of those being held. The International Maritime Bureau recorded 38 piracy and armed robbery incidents worldwide in the first half of 2026. Somali pirates accounted for 94 per cent of all crew members taken hostage during the period. Somalia’s State Minister for Defence Omar Ali Abdi said on August 22 that the federal government was aware of military operations and strikes taking place off Puntland and was preparing a report. He did not identify the force involved or say whether Mogadishu had authorised the attacks. Puntland has called for an investigation into the strikes. Wider naval role Turkey has steadily expanded its military and maritime presence in Somalia under a series of defence agreements between Ankara and Mogadishu. The Turkish parliament last month extended the deployment of Turkish forces in Somalia for another two years, keeping the mandate in force until July 2028. The authorisation allows Turkish forces to operate in areas agreed with Somalia, including its maritime zones, and to support efforts against terrorism, piracy, illegal fishing, smuggling and other security threats. That role also rests on a 10-year defence and economic cooperation agreement signed in 2024, under which Turkey agreed to help Somalia build, train and equip its navy and strengthen security along its coastline. Turkish naval forces are already conducting protection missions off Somalia. In July, Turkey’s Defence Ministry said the TCG Goksu, TCG Gelibolu and TCG Bartin were escorting the Turkish drilling ship Cagri Bey and three support vessels operating off the Somali coast. Turkey also runs a major military training facility in Mogadishu and has spent more than a decade training and equipping Somali security forces. The expanded naval activity comes as piracy has again emerged as a threat in waters off Somalia and the Gulf of Aden. The International Maritime Organisation said on August 24 that six vessels and more than 90 seafarers were being held by pirates and armed robbers in the region. “We cannot allow the resurgence of piracy in the Gulf of Aden and surrounding waters to go unaddressed,” IMO Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez said, calling for the immediate release of those being held. The International Maritime Bureau recorded 38 piracy and armed robbery incidents worldwide in the first half of 2026. Somali pirates accounted for 94 per cent of all crew members taken hostage during the period. items.title: Somalia at a Defining Moment: Can the Federal Republic Survive Its Political and Geopolitical Storm?
items.description: By Abdullahi A. Nor Somalia is approaching one of the most consequential moments in its modern political history. What began as a dispute over elections and constitutional reform has evolved into a deeper crisis over the very structure, legitimacy and future of the Federal Republic. The danger is no longer simply that Somalia may fail to hold an election on time. The greater danger is that the country could enter a prolonged period in which competing authorities claim political legitimacy, federal states increasingly operate independently of Mogadishu, armed forces become instruments of political competition, and external powers exploit the resulting vacuum. At the centre of this crisis stands President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and a federal government whose constitutional and electoral agenda has been rejected by significant sections of the political opposition and several federal member states. Parliament’s mandate expired in April 2026, while the president’s constitutional term expired in May, according to recent analyses of the crisis. Yet there is still no broadly accepted political settlement governing the country’s transition to the next elections.  That alone should be alarming. A constitutional dispute has become a struggle for the state The fundamental question confronting Somalia is no longer simply when will elections be held? It is who has the authority to determine the rules under which Somalia will be governed? The federal government’s constitutional and electoral reforms have been portrayed by its opponents as an attempt to centralize power in Mogadishu. Puntland has rejected the federal government’s approach, while Jubaland has also remained outside the government’s political framework. The opposition coalition has similarly challenged the legitimacy of the government’s electoral and constitutional process. Puntland’s confrontation with Mogadishu has already moved beyond political statements. In June and July, tensions escalated over federal military appointments and the movement of forces, culminating in clashes involving Puntland forces and units associated with the federal government. This is precisely where constitutional disputes become dangerous: once political disagreements begin to determine where troops move, who controls weapons and which administration commands security forces, the constitutional crisis ceases to be merely political. It becomes a question of state survival. The federal compact is under unprecedented pressure Somalia’s federal system was designed to prevent precisely this kind of concentration of power. Yet today, Somaliland remains outside the federal system and continues to pursue its claim to independence. Puntland has effectively suspended cooperation with Mogadishu over the constitutional and electoral dispute. Jubaland remains deeply opposed to the federal government’s approach. And South West State has become the scene of an increasingly bitter confrontation between the federal government and forces and communities opposed to its intervention. The result is a country in which the political map increasingly looks different from the constitutional map. This is the paradox Somalia now faces: the federal government may control the capital and possess international recognition, but political legitimacy cannot be manufactured through administrative appointments, constitutional amendments or the deployment of security forces. Legitimacy must be negotiated. The crisis in South West State is particularly dangerous because it brings together nearly every unresolved problem in Somalia: federalism, elections, security, constitutional authority and local legitimacy. Critics of the federal government’s intervention argue that Mogadishu has used military force and political engineering to reshape the leadership of South West State. The appointment of Speaker Adan Mohamed Nur—better known as Adan Madoobe—as the political figurehead of the state has been strongly contested by opponents who argue that he lacks sufficient popular legitimacy. Whether one accepts that characterization or not, the underlying political problem is impossible to ignore. A federal government cannot create sustainable political legitimacy in a federal member state simply by controlling its administrative capital. If large sections of the local population regard an administration as imposed rather than elected, the government may possess the buildings, security forces and official titles—but it will struggle to possess genuine authority. That is the lesson Mogadishu should learn before the South West crisis becomes another prolonged Somali conflict. Somalia is not operating in a geopolitical vacuum What makes today’s crisis considerably more dangerous than previous political disputes is Somalia’s geography. Somalia occupies one of the most strategically important positions in Africa. Its coastline stretches along the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean, adjacent to the Bab el-Mandeb, one of the world’s most important maritime gateways. The country sits between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, near Yemen and the Red Sea, while Ethiopia—one of Africa’s most populous countries—remains landlocked and increasingly interested in reliable access to the sea. The strategic importance of this geography has increased dramatically since the outbreak of the U.S.-Iran conflict. The war has disrupted energy markets, shipping routes and security calculations across the Middle East. The Strait of Hormuz has become a major geopolitical pressure point, while the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden have simultaneously become more contested.  For Somalia, this is both an opportunity and a danger. A stable, united Somalia could become one of the most strategically valuable states in the region. A fragmented Somalia could become the opposite: a battlefield of competing regional and global interests. The Iran war has changed the strategic equation The consequences of the Iran war extend well beyond the Persian Gulf. The conflict has demonstrated how quickly maritime chokepoints can become instruments of geopolitical pressure. Shipping companies are already reassessing routes, insurance costs and port infrastructure. Gulf states are investing in alternative transportation corridors as they seek to reduce their vulnerability to disruptions around Hormuz. At the same time, the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden have become increasingly important to competing security and economic strategies. That puts Somalia directly in the middle of the emerging geopolitical contest. Recent piracy incidents off Yemen and Somalia have further illustrated the vulnerability of the maritime corridor. The resurgence of piracy in 2026 has included multiple vessel hijackings across the Gulf of Aden and western Indian Ocean. The message for Somalia should be unmistakable: Geography is becoming Somalia’s greatest strategic asset—and potentially its greatest security liability. When a strategically located country is politically fragmented, other countries rarely remain passive. They seek ports. They seek military access. They seek intelligence partnerships. They seek commercial concessions. They seek political allies. And they seek influence over whoever controls strategic territory. This is already visible throughout the Horn of Africa, where Gulf states, Turkey, Ethiopia, Egypt, the United States, China, Israel and other actors have competing security, commercial and strategic interests. The Iran war has accelerated this competition rather than reducing it. Somalia therefore cannot afford to behave as though its internal political crisis exists in isolation from the international system. Every constitutional dispute in Mogadishu is being watched by actors outside Somalia. Every confrontation between federal and state forces is being assessed through a geopolitical lens. Every port, airport, military base and coastline has strategic value,and every political vacuum creates an opportunity for someone else. The greatest threat may not be Al-Shabaab For years, Somalia’s political establishment has rightly identified Al-Shabaab as the country’s principal security threat. But there is another danger that deserves equal attention: state fragmentation. A weakened central government fighting with federal states is less capable of defeating Al-Shabaab. A federal member state fighting with Mogadishu cannot concentrate fully on economic development. Security forces divided by political loyalties cannot build a professional national army, and a government consumed by electoral survival cannot devote sufficient attention to state reconstruction. This is the vicious circle Somalia risks entering. Political conflict weakens institutions, and weak institutions produce insecurity. Insecurity encourages external intervention. External intervention deepens political competition. Political competition further weakens the state, and the cycle continues. The federal government still has a choice None of this means the Federal Republic is doomed. Somalia’s future remains negotiable. But the window for political compromise is narrowing. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud still has an opportunity to transform the current crisis from a confrontation over political survival into a national settlement over the future of the republic. That would require something more difficult than another political conference. It would require compromise. The government would need to negotiate seriously with Puntland, Jubaland, the opposition and other political actors over the constitutional framework and electoral system. It would need to reduce the use of security forces as instruments of political pressure. And it would need to accept that an election whose rules are rejected by a substantial portion of the country cannot produce the legitimacy Somalia desperately needs. The opposition, for its part, must also recognize that rejecting every federal initiative without presenting a workable national alternative will not resolve the crisis. Somalia needs a political settlement—not merely a political victory for one side. If the current trajectory continues, Somalia could enter a period of prolonged institutional ambiguity. One administration could claim constitutional authority. Federal states could insist that Mogadishu has exceeded its mandate. Opposition leaders could reject the electoral process. Security forces could become increasingly divided. Local administrations could seek greater autonomy. and external powers could deepen their involvement. Such a scenario would not necessarily produce the dramatic collapse of the Somali state overnight. It could be much more dangerous than that. Somalia could gradually become a country that exists as one state on international maps but operates as several competing political and security spaces on the ground. That would be a dream scenario for those seeking strategic influence over Somalia’s coastline and a nightmare for the Somali people. The choice before Somalia Somalia’s strategic geography cannot be changed. Its location beside the Gulf of Aden cannot be moved. Its proximity to Yemen, Ethiopia, the Red Sea and the Arabian Peninsula cannot be negotiated away. But Somalia can decide whether its geography becomes a source of prosperity or a magnet for foreign competition. That decision begins with political unity. Not uniformity. Not centralization. Not the elimination of federal states. It means accepting that constitutional legitimacy cannot be imposed by force, that elections cannot be credible without broad political consent, and that federalism cannot survive if the centre treats member states as subordinate administrative districts. The coming months may therefore determine far more than who governs Somalia next. They may determine whether Somalia’s federal experiment survives at all. The country stands at a crossroads: a negotiated political settlement that preserves the Federal Republic—or a prolonged constitutional crisis that gradually transforms political fragmentation into territorial and institutional fragmentation. And while Somali politicians argue over elections, constitutional clauses and political appointments, the world around them is changing rapidly. The Red Sea is becoming more contested. The Gulf of Aden is becoming more strategic. The consequences of the Iran war are reshaping regional calculations. Foreign powers are reassessing military and commercial access, and Somalia’s coastline is becoming more valuable by the day. The tragedy would be for Somalia to discover too late that while its leaders were fighting over who controls the state, others were preparing for a world in which controlling Somalia’s strategic geography may matter even more than controlling its government. The Federal Republic still has a future—but only if its political leaders choose to save the republic before the geopolitical forces gathering around it decide its future for them. Abdullahi A. items.title: 6.0-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Gulf of Aden, Stirring Concern Along Somalia’s Northeastern Coast
items.description: Garowe (WDN) – A powerful magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck the Gulf of Aden early Friday, sending seismic tremors through a region already known for intense geological activity and raising fresh questions about the vulnerability of Somalia’s northeastern coastline. According to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), the earthquake occurred at 12:07 a.m. local time on Friday, August 28, or 21:07 GMT on Thursday. Its epicenter was located approximately 145 kilometers north of Caluula in Puntland, beneath the Gulf of Aden, at a relatively shallow depth of about 10 kilometers. The quake was strong enough to attract international seismic monitoring, but its offshore location appears to have significantly reduced the immediate risk to populated areas. No deaths, injuries or major structural damage had been reported in the initial assessments. USGS-linked assessments placed the immediate humanitarian risk at a low level. A Region Built on Moving Tectonic Plates The earthquake is a reminder that the Gulf of Aden is far from geologically quiet. The area lies along an active tectonic boundary where the Arabian and Somali plates are pulling apart, producing repeated seismic activity beneath the Gulf and around the surrounding coastlines. The geological forces that created and continue to reshape the Gulf of Aden make earthquakes a recurring feature of the region. And Friday’s earthquake was not an isolated event. On June 25, 2026, a magnitude 5.1 earthquake was recorded in the eastern Gulf of Aden, approximately 152 kilometers north of Caluula, at a depth of 10 kilometers.  The proximity of the two events underscores the continuing seismic activity beneath the waters separating Somalia and Yemen. A magnitude 6.0 earthquake can cause significant damage when it occurs close to densely populated areas, particularly where buildings are poorly constructed. But distance, depth, local geology and construction standards all play a major role in determining the eventual impact. In this case, the epicenter was offshore and roughly 145 kilometers from Caluula, limiting the likelihood of severe destruction along Somalia’s coast. Initial reports indicated no significant casualties or damage. There was also no immediate tsunami warning associated with the event. The available assessments indicated a low tsunami risk, although authorities and seismic monitoring agencies continue to watch for possible changes and aftershocks. A Warning Beneath the Surface For Somalia, however, the significance of the earthquake goes beyond Friday’s relatively limited impact. The country’s northeastern coastline stretches along one of the most geologically active corridors in the region, yet Somalia has comparatively limited earthquake-monitoring infrastructure, public preparedness systems and disaster-response capacity. That creates a potentially serious vulnerability. A similar earthquake occurring much closer to a populated coastal community could produce a dramatically different outcome—particularly in areas where buildings and infrastructure have not been designed with seismic risks in mind. The Gulf of Aden is also one of the world’s strategically important maritime corridors, linking the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. Millions of tonnes of commercial shipping pass through the wider region every year, meaning major geological disruptions could have consequences extending beyond Somalia and Yemen. The Earthquake After the Earthquake For now, there is little evidence that Friday’s earthquake has produced a major humanitarian emergency. But scientists continue to monitor the area for aftershocks, which can follow a significant seismic event. The immediate message from the earthquake is therefore one of caution rather than catastrophe. At magnitude 6.0, the event was powerful. Yet its offshore location appears to have spared Somalia’s northeastern communities from the kind of destruction that such an earthquake could cause if its epicenter were closer to land. Still, the repeated earthquakes recorded near Caluula this year are a reminder that beneath the waters of the Gulf of Aden, powerful geological forces remain active. For a country with limited disaster-preparedness resources, the question is not simply whether another earthquake will occur. It is whether Somalia will be prepared when a stronger one strikes closer to home. items.title: Ethiopia’s Search for Sea Access Raises Bigger Questions for the Horn of Africa
items.description: Addis Ababa (WDN) – Ethiopia’s determination to secure reliable access to the sea is becoming one of the most consequential geopolitical issues in the Horn of Africa. As Africa’s second-most populous country, Addis Ababa has repeatedly argued that remaining landlocked imposes significant economic and strategic costs. Yet its pursuit of maritime access has also generated concern among neighboring coastal states, particularly Somalia, whose political and institutional fragility makes it especially vulnerable to external pressure. Ethiopian lawmaker Fethi Mahdi, Deputy Chair of the Foreign Relations and Peace Affairs Standing Committee of the House of Peoples’ Representatives, said Ethiopia’s demand for sea access goes beyond transportation and trade. He described it as an economic, legal and historical necessity. According to Fethi, approximately 95 percent of Ethiopia’s imports and exports currently pass through a single port- Djibouti, imposing substantial annual costs on the country. He argued that dependence on one maritime corridor increases the price of goods, contributes to inflation and undermines Ethiopia’s export competitiveness. He also invoked Ethiopia’s historical connection to the Red Sea, pointing to the ancient port of Adulis and the maritime links of the Aksumite Kingdom. He argued that Ethiopia historically maintained access to the sea and that its loss was not resolved through a process Addis Ababa considers legitimate. The Ethiopian argument also invokes international maritime law, including the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which recognizes certain rights of landlocked states to access the sea through neighboring countries. But that principle does not give Ethiopia the right to seize another country’s territory or coastline. Any permanent maritime corridor must ultimately rest on negotiated agreements that respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity and borders of coastal states. That distinction is critical. Ethiopia’s search for sea access is understandable from an economic and strategic perspective. But the question facing the region is whether Addis Ababa will pursue that objective through mutually agreed commercial arrangements—or whether the weakness of neighboring states could create incentives for more ambitious territorial or political demands. Somalia is particularly exposed to this pressure. The country continues to struggle with political fragmentation, constitutional disputes, insecurity and weak state institutions. In such an environment, the fear is not simply that Ethiopia wants access to the sea, but that Somalia’s inability to consolidate effective national institutions could make its territory and coastline increasingly vulnerable to external geopolitical competition. The stakes extend beyond Somalia and Ethiopia. Any confrontation over maritime access could destabilize the wider Horn of Africa, affecting trade routes, regional security and relations among Ethiopia, Somalia, Djibouti and Eritrea. Fethi insists that Ethiopia wants a diplomatic solution based on dialogue and mutually beneficial agreements, arguing that sea access could promote regional integration and economic growth. That approach will ultimately be tested by how Ethiopia pursues its objective. For Ethiopia, access to the sea is increasingly portrayed as an economic necessity. For its neighbors, however, the central question is whether that necessity can be satisfied without compromising their sovereignty. items.fullContent: Addis Ababa (WDN) – Ethiopia’s determination to secure reliable access to the sea is becoming one of the most consequential geopolitical issues in the Horn of Africa. As Africa’s second-most populous country, Addis Ababa has repeatedly argued that remaining landlocked imposes significant economic and strategic costs. Yet its pursuit of maritime access has also generated concern among neighboring coastal states, particularly Somalia, whose political and institutional fragility makes it especially vulnerable to external pressure. Ethiopian lawmaker Fethi Mahdi, Deputy Chair of the Foreign Relations and Peace Affairs Standing Committee of the House of Peoples’ Representatives, said Ethiopia’s demand for sea access goes beyond transportation and trade. He described it as an economic, legal and historical necessity. According to Fethi, approximately 95 percent of Ethiopia’s imports and exports currently pass through a single port- Djibouti, imposing substantial annual costs on the country. He argued that dependence on one maritime corridor increases the price of goods, contributes to inflation and undermines Ethiopia’s export competitiveness. He also invoked Ethiopia’s historical connection to the Red Sea, pointing to the ancient port of Adulis and the maritime links of the Aksumite Kingdom. He argued that Ethiopia historically maintained access to the sea and that its loss was not resolved through a process Addis Ababa considers legitimate. The Ethiopian argument also invokes international maritime law, including the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which recognizes certain rights of landlocked states to access the sea through neighboring countries. But that principle does not give Ethiopia the right to seize another country’s territory or coastline. Any permanent maritime corridor must ultimately rest on negotiated agreements that respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity and borders of coastal states. That distinction is critical. Ethiopia’s search for sea access is understandable from an economic and strategic perspective. But the question facing the region is whether Addis Ababa will pursue that objective through mutually agreed commercial arrangements—or whether the weakness of neighboring states could create incentives for more ambitious territorial or political demands. Somalia is particularly exposed to this pressure. The country continues to struggle with political fragmentation, constitutional disputes, insecurity and weak state institutions. In such an environment, the fear is not simply that Ethiopia wants access to the sea, but that Somalia’s inability to consolidate effective national institutions could make its territory and coastline increasingly vulnerable to external geopolitical competition. The stakes extend beyond Somalia and Ethiopia. Any confrontation over maritime access could destabilize the wider Horn of Africa, affecting trade routes, regional security and relations among Ethiopia, Somalia, Djibouti and Eritrea. Fethi insists that Ethiopia wants a diplomatic solution based on dialogue and mutually beneficial agreements, arguing that sea access could promote regional integration and economic growth. That approach will ultimately be tested by how Ethiopia pursues its objective. For Ethiopia, access to the sea is increasingly portrayed as an economic necessity. For its neighbors, however, the central question is whether that necessity can be satisfied without compromising their sovereignty. In a fragile and politically divided Horn of Africa, that distinction could determine whether Ethiopia’s maritime ambitions become an engine of regional integration—or another source of regional instability. items.title: Laftagareen: Is Somalia’s Counterterrorism Mission Being Pulled into a Political War?
items.description: Nairobi (WDN) — Former Southwest State President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen has launched a forceful counterattack against the Federal Government of Somalia, rejecting allegations that he or forces loyal to him have collaborated with Al-Shabaab and warning Ethiopian troops serving under the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) against becoming embroiled in Somalia’s political conflict. In a lengthy statement issued in English, Laftagareen described allegations linking him and his forces to Al-Shabaab as politically motivated and accused the federal government of using counterterrorism rhetoric to justify what he portrays as a military campaign against a regional political opponent. The allegations have not been independently substantiated in the material available, but their political significance is difficult to ignore. The accusation of an Al-Shabaab connection, if used to justify military action against a regional authority, could fundamentally alter the nature of the confrontation—from a political dispute over legitimacy and governance into a counterterrorism operation involving international forces. That is precisely the danger Laftagareen is attempting to expose. Is AUSSOM Becoming Part of the Political Battlefield? Laftagareen’s most consequential warning was directed at AUSSOM, particularly Ethiopian forces stationed in Baidoa. He urged Ethiopia not to allow its troops to become instruments in what he described as an internal political and military struggle in Southwest State. His intervention follows an August 21 statement from AUSSOM acknowledging that it had received a request from the Federal Government for support in counterterrorism operations. That statement raises a fundamental question: where does counterterrorism end and political intervention begin? AUSSOM was created to support Somalia’s security institutions and combat Al-Shabaab. It was not established to determine which Somali political faction controls Baidoa, which regional authority is legitimate, or how political disputes between Mogadishu and the federal member states should be resolved. If international forces become perceived as enforcing the political preferences of one side, their credibility—and potentially their operational effectiveness—could suffer. For Ethiopia, the issue is particularly sensitive. Ethiopian troops have a substantial presence in Southwest State, giving Addis Ababa enormous influence over the security environment surrounding Baidoa. Any perception that Ethiopian forces are taking sides in the political confrontation could transform an already volatile dispute into a broader regional crisis. At the center of the controversy is the dramatic escalation between Mogadishu and Southwest State. Laftagareen has strongly condemned the circumstances surrounding his removal from power, portraying it not as a legitimate political transition but as the product of coercion and military pressure. The federal government, meanwhile, has portrayed the security dimension of the confrontation through the lens of Al-Shabaab and national security. That creates a potentially dangerous political equation: a regional political opponent is accused of links to a terrorist organization, federal forces mobilize, and international troops are asked to provide counterterrorism support. The obvious question is whether the security justification is independently verifiable—or whether counterterrorism language is being used to provide political cover for a struggle over power. No serious government can afford to blur that distinction. The Al-Shabaab Question Laftagareen has categorically denied cooperation with Al-Shabaab, including allegations that his forces have conducted joint operations with the militant group. Those claims and counterclaims require evidence, not political declarations. Al-Shabaab remains Somalia’s most dangerous insurgent organization, and any credible evidence of collaboration between political actors and the group would represent a grave national-security matter. But the opposite is equally important: accusations of terrorism cannot be allowed to become a political weapon without transparent evidence. If the federal government possesses intelligence demonstrating operational cooperation between Laftagareen’s forces and Al-Shabaab, the appropriate response should be to present credible evidence and pursue the matter through lawful national and international mechanisms. If such evidence does not exist, then invoking Al-Shabaab to justify military action against political opponents risks damaging the very institutions that Somalia and its international partners claim to be building. AUSSOM Faces a Test of Neutrality The controversy comes at an especially delicate moment for Somalia’s international security architecture. AUSSOM is operating in a country where political divisions, disputes over federal authority, contested electoral arrangements and security challenges increasingly overlap. The mission therefore faces a difficult balancing act: it must support the Somali government’s fight against Al-Shabaab without becoming entangled in disputes between Mogadishu and the federal member states. That distinction may prove decisive. If AUSSOM is seen by significant sections of the Somali public as taking sides in a political conflict, its legitimacy could erode rapidly. Armed groups could exploit the resulting divisions, while regional authorities could become less willing to cooperate with the mission. The consequences would extend far beyond Baidoa. Laftagareen’s statement ultimately forces a question that Somalia’s international partners cannot afford to ignore: Is the fight against Al-Shabaab being conducted separately from Somalia’s political crisis—or is the war against terrorism gradually becoming entangled with the struggle for political control? The answer matters enormously. Somalia needs international forces to fight Al-Shabaab. It also needs those forces to remain sufficiently neutral to command the confidence of Somalia’s deeply divided political landscape. Turning counterterrorism forces into instruments of political confrontation could achieve a short-term military objective while creating a much larger strategic problem. For now, Laftagareen has put the issue squarely on the table. He denies the allegations against him, challenges the federal government’s justification for military action, and is warning Ethiopia and AUSSOM not to cross the line between supporting Somalia’s security and becoming participants in Somalia’s political war. Whether Mogadishu can provide credible evidence for its accusations—and whether AUSSOM can demonstrate that its operations are driven by counterterrorism imperatives rather than political calculations—may determine what happens next in Baidoa. The most dangerous outcome would be for Somalia’s political battles to acquire the language, weapons and international military machinery of a counterterrorism campaign. items.title: Dowladda Soomaaliya oo dib u furtay garoonka Doolow
items.description: Doolow (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa dib u furtay garoonka diyaaradaha Doolow ee gobolka Gedo, kaas oo muddo ku dhow laba sano u xirnaa khilaafka siyaasadeed ee u dhexeeya Dowladda Federaalka iyo maamulka Jubaland. Dib u furitaanka garoonka ayaa la filayaa inuu dhaqan-galo iyadoo duulimaadkii ugu horreeyay lagu wado inuu berri ka dego Doolow. Xogaha la helayo ayaa sheegaya in dowladda xilligan aysan garoonka ku soo rogin shuruudo cusub oo la xiriira dib u bilaabashada duulimaadyada. Garoonka ayaa dhowr jeer la isku dayay in dib loo furo, balse dadaalladii hore ayaa fashilmay kadib markii la isku fahmi waayay shuruudo iyo dalabaad ay Dowladda Federaalka ku xirtay. Xogaha laga helayo arrintan ayaa sidoo kale sheegaya in saraakiil hore uga tirsanaa Hay’adda Nabad-sugidda iyo Sirdoonka Qaranka (NISA) ay door ku lahaayeen qorshihii xiritaanka garoonka, iyagoo dowladda u gudbiyay aragtiyo la xiriiray saameynta siyaasadeed ee garoonku ku leeyahay magaalada. Sida xogtu tilmaamayso, qorshahaasi ayaa ahaa in cadaadis lagu saaro maamulka deegaanka si Doolow ay si buuxda ugu soo wareegto saameynta Dowladda Federaalka, hase yeeshee maamulka deegaanka iyo gaar ahaan degmada Lafeey ayaa ka horyimid tallaabooyinkaas. Muddooyinkii uu xirnaa garoonka Doolow, bulshada deegaanka ayaa si weyn ugu tiirsaneyd isu socodka dhulka, iyadoo ganacsatada, dadka safarka ah iyo qeybaha kale ee bulshada ay sheegeen in xiritaankiisu uu saameyn ku yeeshay dhaq-dhaqaaqa dhaqaale ee gobolka. Dadka deegaanka ayaa sidoo kale muddo dheer ka cabanayay in garoonka loo adeegsaday loollan siyaasadeed, taas oo sababtay in adeeg muhiim u ahaa bulshada uu muddo dheer hakad galo, iyadoo dhinacyada isku haya arrinta ay isku khilaafeen maamulka iyo mustaqbalka garoonka. Si kastaba, dib u furista garoonka ayaa haddii uu si rasmi ah u dhaqan-galo noqonaya tallaabo wax ka beddeli karta xaaladda isu socodka Doolow, waxaana la filayaa inuu dib u soo celiyo duulimaadyadii, dhaq-dhaqaaqii ganacsi iyo xiriirkii magaalada ay la lahayd deegaannada kale ee dalka. items.title: Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Itoobiya oo Raadinta Marin Baddeed Ka Dhigtay Arrin Saameyn Ku Leh Mustaqbalka Geeska Afrika
items.description: Addis Ababa (WDN) — Go’aanka Itoobiya ee ah inay hesho marin-badeed joogto ah ayaa isu beddelaya mid ka mid ah arrimaha juqraafi-siyaasaddeed ee ugu saamaynta badan Geeska Afrika. Itoobiya oo ah dalka labaad ee ugu dadka badan Afrika, ayaa muddo dheer ku doodaysay in ay xeeb la’aantu ku keento culays dhaqaale iyo mid istiraatiiji ah. Hase yeeshee, dadaalka Addis Ababa ee helitaanka marin-badeed ayaa sidoo kale walaac ka abuuray dalalka deriska ah, gaar ahaan Soomaaliya oo wajahaysa tabar-darro siyaasaddeed iyo hay’adeed oo ka dhigaysa mid si gaar ah ugu nugul cadaadisyada dibadda. Xildhibaan Fethi Mahdi, oo ah ku-xigeenka Guddoomiyaha Guddiga Joogtada ah ee Xiriirka Dibadda iyo Arrimaha Nabadda ee Golaha Wakiillada Shacabka Itoobiya, ayaa sheegay in doonista Itoobiya ee marin-badeedku aysan ku koobnayn gaadiid iyo ganacsi oo keliya, balse ay tahay arrin uu ku tilmaamay baahi dhaqaale, sharci iyo mid taariikhi ah. Sida uu sheegay Fethi, ku dhawaad 95 boqolkiiba badeecadaha Itoobiya soo dejiso ama dhoofiso waxay maraan hal deked, taas oo dalka ku keenta kharash aad u badan. Wuxuu ku doodday in ku-tiirsanaanta hal marin-badeed – Dekad ay sare u qaaddo qiimaha badeecadaha, ay ka qayb qaadato sicir-bararka, isla markaana ay wiiqdo awoodda Itoobiya ee tartanka suuqyada caalamiga ah. Xildhibaanku wuxuu sidoo kale dooddiisa ku saleeyay taariikhda, isaga oo xusay dekeddii qadiimiga ahayd ee Adulis iyo xiriirkii badeed ee boqortooyadii Aksum ay la lahayd Badda Cas. Wuxuu ku doodday in Itoobiya taariikh ahaan lahayd xiriir toos ah oo badeed, isla markaana lumitaanka marin-badeedka dalka uusan ku dhicin hannaan ay Addis Ababa u aragto mid sharci iyo caddaalad ku dhisan. Itoobiya waxay sidoo kale tixraacaysaa sharciga caalamiga ah, gaar ahaan Axdiga Qaramada Midoobay ee Sharciga Badda (UNCLOS), kaas oo aqoonsanaya xuquuqo gaar ah oo ay leeyihiin dalalka aan xeebaha lahayn, oo ay ka mid tahay fursadda ay ku heli karaan marin ay kaga gudbaan dhulalka dalalka deriska ah si ay u gaaraan badda. Hase yeeshee, mabda’aasi ma siinayo Itoobiya xaq ay ku qabsato dhul ama xeeb uu leeyahay dal kale. Marin-badeed joogto ah wuxuu u baahan yahay heshiisyo iyo wada-xaajoodyo dhex mara dowladaha ay arrintu khusayso, iyadoo si buuxda loo dhowrayo madax-bannaanida, xuduudaha iyo dhul-wadaagga dalalka xeebaha leh. Kala duwanaanshahan ayaa ah halka ay arrintu xasaasiyadda ka yeelanayso. Dhinaca Itoobiya, baahida marin-badeedku waxay leedahay sabab dhaqaale iyo istiraatiiji ah oo si fudud loo fahmi karo. Laakiin dhinaca dalalka deriska ah, su’aasha ugu weyn waxay tahay in baahidaas lagu dabooli doono heshiisyo ganacsi iyo diblomaasiyadeed oo labada dhinacba faa’iido u leh, ama in tabar-darrada dowladaha deriska ahi ay abuurto fursad loogu gudbo dano ka ballaaran marin ganacsi. Soomaaliya ayaa si gaar ah ugu nugul xaaladdan. Dalka wuxuu weli la tacaalayaa khilaafaad siyaasadeed, kala qaybsanaan, amni-darro iyo hay’ado dowladeed oo aan weli si buuxda u awoodin inay ilaaliyaan danaha qaranka. Xaaladdan ayaa dhalinaysa walaac ah in arrinta aysan ku ekaan doonista Itoobiya ee marin-badeed, balse tabar-darrada Soomaaliya ay keeni karto in dhulkeeda iyo xeebteeda ay noqdaan goob ay ku tartamaan quwadaha gobolka iyo kuwa caalamka. Arrintani kuma koobna Itoobiya iyo Soomaaliya oo keliya. Khilaaf kasta oo ka dhasha marin-badeedka wuxuu saameyn ku yeelan karaa guud ahaan Geeska Afrika, ganacsiga gobolka, amniga badda iyo xiriirka u dhexeeya Itoobiya, Soomaaliya, Jabuuti iyo Eritrea. Xildhibaan Fethi Mahdi ayaa ku adkeystay in Itoobiya ay doonayso in arrintan lagu xalliyo diblomaasiyad, wada-hadal iyo heshiis labada dhinacba dan u ah, isaga oo ku doodaya in marin-badeedka Itoobiya uu fursad u noqon karo isku-xirka dhaqaale iyo horumarinta gobolka. Hase yeeshee, sida ay arrintu ku dambayn doonto waxay ku xirnaan doontaa habka Addis Ababa u wajahdo hamigeeda. Itoobiya waxay marin-badeedka u aragtaa baahi dhaqaale iyo istiraatiiji ah oo sii kordheysa. Dalalka deriska ahna waxay doonayaan dammaanad ah in baahidaas aan lagu dabooli doonin kharashka madax-bannaanidooda. Geeska Afrika oo ah gobol horey ugu jiray loollan siyaasadeed, amni iyo juqraafi-siyaasadeed, sida loo xalliyo arrintan ayaa go’aamin karta in hamiga Itoobiya uu noqdo albaab u furma is-dhexgal iyo horumar goboleed — ama uu noqdo khilaaf cusub oo dib u qaabeeya khariidadda awoodda Geeska Afrika. Wuxuu ku doodday in Itoobiya taariikh ahaan lahayd xiriir toos ah oo badeed, isla markaana lumitaanka marin-badeedka dalka uusan ku dhicin hannaan ay Addis Ababa u aragto mid sharci iyo caddaalad ku dhisan. Itoobiya waxay sidoo kale tixraacaysaa sharciga caalamiga ah, gaar ahaan Axdiga Qaramada Midoobay ee Sharciga Badda (UNCLOS), kaas oo aqoonsanaya xuquuqo gaar ah oo ay leeyihiin dalalka aan xeebaha lahayn, oo ay ka mid tahay fursadda ay ku heli karaan marin ay kaga gudbaan dhulalka dalalka deriska ah si ay u gaaraan badda. Hase yeeshee, mabda’aasi ma siinayo Itoobiya xaq ay ku qabsato dhul ama xeeb uu leeyahay dal kale. Marin-badeed joogto ah wuxuu u baahan yahay heshiisyo iyo wada-xaajoodyo dhex mara dowladaha ay arrintu khusayso, iyadoo si buuxda loo dhowrayo madax-bannaanida, xuduudaha iyo dhul-wadaagga dalalka xeebaha leh. Kala duwanaanshahan ayaa ah halka ay arrintu xasaasiyadda ka yeelanayso. Dhinaca Itoobiya, baahida marin-badeedku waxay leedahay sabab dhaqaale iyo istiraatiiji ah oo si fudud loo fahmi karo. Laakiin dhinaca dalalka deriska ah, su’aasha ugu weyn waxay tahay in baahidaas lagu dabooli doono heshiisyo ganacsi iyo diblomaasiyadeed oo labada dhinacba faa’iido u leh, ama in tabar-darrada dowladaha deriska ahi ay abuurto fursad loogu gudbo dano ka ballaaran marin ganacsi. Soomaaliya ayaa si gaar ah ugu nugul xaaladdan. Dalka wuxuu weli la tacaalayaa khilaafaad siyaasadeed, kala qaybsanaan, amni-darro iyo hay’ado dowladeed oo aan weli si buuxda u awoodin inay ilaaliyaan danaha qaranka. Xaaladdan ayaa dhalinaysa walaac ah in arrinta aysan ku ekaan doonista Itoobiya ee marin-badeed, balse tabar-darrada Soomaaliya ay keeni karto in dhulkeeda iyo xeebteeda ay noqdaan goob ay ku tartamaan quwadaha gobolka iyo kuwa caalamka. Arrintani kuma koobna Itoobiya iyo Soomaaliya oo keliya. Khilaaf kasta oo ka dhasha marin-badeedka wuxuu saameyn ku yeelan karaa guud ahaan Geeska Afrika, ganacsiga gobolka, amniga badda iyo xiriirka u dhexeeya Itoobiya, Soomaaliya, Jabuuti iyo Eritrea. Xildhibaan Fethi Mahdi ayaa ku adkeystay in Itoobiya ay doonayso in arrintan lagu xalliyo diblomaasiyad, wada-hadal iyo heshiis labada dhinacba dan u ah, isaga oo ku doodaya in marin-badeedka Itoobiya uu fursad u noqon karo isku-xirka dhaqaale iyo horumarinta gobolka. Hase yeeshee, sida ay arrintu ku dambayn doonto waxay ku xirnaan doontaa habka Addis Ababa u wajahdo hamigeeda. Itoobiya waxay marin-badeedka u aragtaa baahi dhaqaale iyo istiraatiiji ah oo sii kordheysa. Dalalka deriska ahna waxay doonayaan dammaanad ah in baahidaas aan lagu dabooli doonin kharashka madax-bannaanidooda. Geeska Afrika oo ah gobol horey ugu jiray loollan siyaasadeed, amni iyo juqraafi-siyaasadeed, sida loo xalliyo arrintan ayaa go’aamin karta in hamiga Itoobiya uu noqdo albaab u furma is-dhexgal iyo horumar goboleed — ama uu noqdo khilaaf cusub oo dib u qaabeeya khariidadda awoodda Geeska Afrika. items.title: MBZ oo boqor Salmaan u diray warqad uusan ogeyn MBS iyo xiisadda oo ka sii dareysa
items.description: Riyadh (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Imaaraadka Carabta, Sheekh Maxamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, ayaa warqad uu si toos ah ugu diray Boqorka Sacuudiga Salman bin Abdulaziz dhalisay hadal-heyn cusub, iyadoo diblomaasiyiin Mareykan iyo Carab ah ay tallaabadan u arkaan isku day uu hoggaamiyaha Imaaraadku ku hareer-marayo Dhaxal-sugaha Sacuudiga Maxamed bin Salman. Warbaahinta rasmiga ah ee Sacuudiga iyo Imaaraadka ayaa Isniintii sheegtay in Sheekh Maxamed bin Zayed uu warqad gacanta lagu qoray u diray Boqor Salman oo 90 jir ah. Wakaaladda wararka Sacuudiga ee SPA ayaa sheegtay in warqaddu la xiriirtay xiriirka labada dal, halka wakaaladda rasmiga ah ee Imaaraadka ee WAM ay sheegtay inay ahayd casuumaad shaqsiyeed oo Boqor Salman loogu fidiyay inuu Abu Dhabi uga qeybgalo shir Qaramada Midoobay taageerto oo ku saabsan biyaha, kaas oo dhacaya bisha December. Hase yeeshee, warbaahinta Middle East Eye ayaa sheegtay in diblomaasiyiin iyo dadka la socda siyaasadda Khaliijka ay warqadda u arkaan astaan muujinaysa heerka xasaasiga ah ee uu marayo xiriirka u dhexeeya Maxamed bin Salman iyo Maxamed bin Zayed. “Imaaraadku waxay dareemeen inaysan haysan waddo kale oo aan ahayn inay si toos ah madaxa ugu tagaan,” ayuu sarkaal reer Galbeed ah oo arrintan xog-ogaal u ah u sheegay Middle East Eye . Sarkaalka ayaa intaas ku daray in Maxamed bin Salman “uusan ku farxi doonin” habkan loo maray Boqor Salman. Boqor Salman ayaa xilka boqortooyada la wareegay sanadkii 2015, kaddib geeridii walaalkiis Boqor Abdullah, balse sannadihii dambe si aad ah ayuu uga yaraaday safarrada iyo hawlaha diblomaasiyadeed ee dibadda. Safarkiisii ugu dambeeyay ee si weyn loo ogyahay wuxuu ahaa Tunisia sanadkii 2019, markaas oo uu ka qeybgalay shir madaxeedka Jaamacadda Carabta. Dhaxal-sugaha Maxamed bin Salman ayaa dhanka kale noqday hoggaamiyaha sida dhabta ah u maamula Sacuudiga, isaga oo gacanta ku haya inta badan hay’adaha iyo siyaasadaha muhiimka ah ee boqortooyada, isla markaana dalka ku matala kulamada heerka sare. Xiriir sii xumaanaya Warqadda Imaaraadka ayaa timid xilli xiriirka Riyadh iyo Abu Dhabi, oo mar ahaa laba xulufo oo aad isugu dhow, uu muddooyinkii dambe galay marxalad ay ka muuqdaan khilaafaad siyaasadeed iyo kuwo istiraatiiji ah. Middle East Eye ayaa sheegtay in khilaafka labada dal uu si weyn u soo shaac baxay bilowgii sanadkan, markii Sacuudigu duqeeyay xoogag gooni-u-goosad ah oo Yemen ka dagaallama oo taageero ka hela Imaaraadka. Labada dal ayaa sidoo kale lagu eedeeyay inay taageerayaan dhinacyada isaga soo horjeeda dagaalka sokeeye ee Sudan, arrintaas oo sii ballaarisay kala fogaanshahooda siyaasadeed. Mareykanka ayaa isku dayay inuu dhex-dhexaadiyo labada dhinac, sida ay sheegtay Middle East Eye , iyadoo sarkaal sare oo Washington ka socda la filayay inuu toddobaadkan booqdo Imaaraadka, balse safarkaasi uusan qabsoomin. Steve Witkoff, ergayga gaarka ah ee Madaxweynaha Mareykanka Donald Trump, ayaa sidoo kale la filayay inuu Imaaraadka tago horaantii bishan, laakiin safarkiisa ayaa la baajiyay. Isbahaysiyo cusub Dagaalka Mareykanka iyo Israel ay la galeen Iran ayaa muddo kooban isu soo dhoweeyay Sacuudiga iyo Imaaraadka, iyadoo labada dal ee Khaliijka ay ku biireen Mareykanka weerarrada Iran, sida lagu sheegay warbixinta. Si kastaba, Riyadh ayaa markii dambe u dhaqaaqday dhanka dadaallada dhex-dhexaadinta oo ay la waddo Pakistan, arrintaas oo la sheegay in Imaaraadku isku dayay inuu hor istaago. Horaantii bishan, Sacuudiga, Pakistan iyo Turkey ayaa ku dhawaaqay heshiis cusub oo difaac wadajir ah oo loo bixiyay “Mecca Pact”. Heshiiskaas ayaa loo arkaa inuu dhisayo hannaan amni oo cusub xilli Imaaraadka iyo Israel ay sii xoojinayaan iskaashigooda. Inkasta oo Sacuudiga iyo xulafadiisu sheegeen in heshiisku uusan cidna ka dhan ahayn isla markaana dalal kale ay ku biiri karaan, haddana falanqeeyayaal Imaaraati ah ayaa si cad u dhaliilay. “Mid ka mid ah shuruudaha guusha isbahaysi kasta waa in la qeexo cadowga la wadaago. Haddaba waa kuma cadowga dalalka isbahaysigan?” ayuu qoray Abdulkhaleq Abdulla, oo ah falanqeeye siyaasadeed isla markaana hore lataliye ugu ahaa Maxamed bin Zayed. Kanaalka Tahnoon Warqadda uu Maxamed bin Zayed u diray Boqor Salman ayaa sidoo kale muhiimad gaar ah yeelatay maadaama ay u muuqato inuu Imaaraadku dhinac maray waddo kale oo wadahadal oo uu hore u soo jeediyay Maxamed bin Salman. Middle East Eye ayaa sanadkan horraantiisii sheegtay in Dhaxal-sugaha Sacuudigu warqad u diray la-taliyaha amniga qaranka Imaaraadka, Sheekh Tahnoon bin Zayed, isaga oo ku faahfaahiyay walaaca Riyadh ay ka qabto dhaq-dhaqaaqyada Imaaraadka ee Yemen iyo Sudan. Warqaddaas ayaa soo jeedisay in labada dhinac ay arrimaha khilaafka ah uga wada hadlaan kanaal rasmi ah oo uu hoggaaminayo Wasiirka Difaaca Sacuudiga Khalid bin Salman, oo ay walaalo yihiin dhaxal-sugaha. Tahnoon bin Zayed, oo ka mid ah dadka ugu awoodda badan Imaaraadka, ayaa muddo dheer door muhiim ah ka ciyaaray hawlaha diblomaasiyadeed iyo kuwa amniga ee Abu Dhabi. Waxa uu hormuud ka ahaa dadaalladii dib loogu soo celiyay xiriirka Qatar kaddib khilaafkii Khaliijka ee billowday 2017. Warbixin ay Reuters hore u baahisay ayaa sidoo kale sheegtay in Tahnoon uu martigeliyay xubno ka tirsan Ilaalada Kacaanka Iran, iyadoo kulamadaasi diiradda lagu saarayay sidii loo joojin lahaa weerarrada ka dhanka ah Imaaraadka. Tallaabada cusub ee Maxamed bin Zayed ayaa sidaas darteed sii xoojisay su’aalaha ku saabsan halka uu ku dambeynayo xiriirka labada quwadood ee ugu awoodda badan Khaliijka, kuwaas oo muddo dheer iska kaashanayay arrimaha gobolka balse hadda ay sii kala fogeynayaan Yemen, Sudan iyo jihada cusub ee isbahaysiyada amni ee Bariga Dhexe. items.title: Soomaaliya iyo Qatar oo saxiixaya heshiis cusub oo ku saabsan dhismaha…
items.description: Doha (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya iyo Qatar ayaa ka wada-hadlay iskaashi ku saabsan dhismaha Akadeemiyadda Qaranka Soomaaliyeed (National Academy of Somalia), taas oo loo qorsheynayo inay noqoto xarun lagu kobciyo hoggaaminta iyo tayada shaqaalaha dowladda. Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah ee Soomaaliya, Cabdisalaam Cali (Dhaay) ayaa xarunta Qatar Leadership Centre ee magaalada Dooxa kulan gaar ah kula yeeshay mas’uuliyiin ka tirsan xarunta, iyadoo diiradda lagu saaray sidii Qatar uga qeyb qaadan lahayd hirgelinta akadeemiyadda. Kulanka ayaa la iskula meel dhigay in labada dhinac ay dhawaan kala saxiixdaan heshiis is-afgarad (MoU) oo qeexaya iskaashiga la xiriira dhismaha iyo horumarinta Akadeemiyadda Qaranka Soomaaliyeed. Wasiirka waxaa kulanka ku weheliyay Xoghayaha Joogtada ah ee Xafiiska Ra’iisul Wasaaraha, Kamaal Daahir Guutaale iyo La-taliyaha Sare ee Ra’iisul Wasaaraha, Dr. Axmednuur Uleex, kuwaas oo qeyb ka ahaa wada-hadallada arrintan ku saabsan. Qatar Leadership Centre oo fadhigeedu yahay Dooxa ayaa ku takhasustay horumarinta hoggaamiyeyaasha, tababarka madaxda iyo sare u qaadista awoodda hay’adaha dowladda, iyadoo bixisa barnaamijyo loogu talagalay madaxda sare, shaqaalaha dowladda iyo hoggaamiyeyaasha soo kacaya. Iskaashiga lala yeelanayo xaruntan ayaa la filayaa inuu gacan ka geysto dhismaha Akadeemiyadda Qaranka Soomaaliyeed, oo loogu talagalay in lagu horumariyo xirfadaha hoggaamineed, maamulka dowliga ah iyo awoodda shaqaalaha hay’adaha dowladda. Dhismaha akadeemiyadda ayaa qeyb ka noqonaya qorshayaasha isbeddelka qaran ee Soomaaliya, gaar ahaan dadaallada lagu xoojinayo hay’adaha dowladda, tayada maamulka iyo diyaarinta jiil cusub oo hoggaan dowladeed leh aqoon iyo xirfad ku filan. Heshiiskan ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli uu dalka Qatar booqasho rasmi ah ku joogo wafdi uu hoggaaminayo Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Soomaaliya, Xamza Cabdi Barre, iyadoo iskaashiga labada dal uu dhinacyo badan ku fidayo. items.title: Somaliland Rebuffs Qatar’s Call For New Talks With Somalia &  The Rejection of Israeli Ties.
items.description: Somaliland Rebuffs Qatar’s Call For New Talks With Somalia & The Rejection of Israeli Ties. Hargeisa,(Qaran news)- According to reliable sources, a high level delegation from the State of Qatar recently visited Hargeysa with the intention of persuading the Somaliland authorities to restart new talks with Somalia and to renege on its diplomatic ties with Israel. According to these reliable sources, both requests were rebuffed by the Somaliland President, Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi “Irro”. The sources confirm that Somaliland sees no benefits in restarting new talks with Somalia after previous engagements in Turkey and Djibouti did not bring forth any concrete results. Regarding Somaliland ties diplomatic with Israel, the first Nation to recognize the restoration of sovereignty on the 26th of December, 2025, the issue is not open for discussion. Somaliland remains firmly and perpetually committed to its relationship with Israel. Qarannews

items.title: Ciidanka Maamulka Somaliland oo Xabsiga u Taxaabay Abwaan Jiheeye
items.description: Xukuumadda Cabdiraxmaan Cirro ayaa lagu eedeeyay inay sii waddo caburin, handadaad iyo tacaddiyo lagula kacayo shacabka, iyadoo maanta xabsiga loo taxaabay Abwaan Jiheeye oo ka mid ah abwaannada caanka ah ee Soomaaliyeed. Abwaan Jiheeye oo daris la ah Cabdiraxmaan Cirro ayaa la sheegay in lagu amray inuu ka guuro hoygiisa, kadib markii uu sheegay inuu wajahayo cadaadis iyo cabsi xooggan oo la xiriirta arrin dhuleed. Abwaanka ayaa sheegay in inta badan dadkii kale ee dariska la ahaa laga iibiyay dhulalkoodii, halka isaga iyo tiro yar oo kale laga maroorsaday dhulkoodii. Abwaanka oo arrintaas ka falceliyay ayaa tiriyay gabay uu Alle uga dacwoonayo hoggaamiyaha Maamulka Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Cirro, isagoo ka hadlay cabashooyinka iyo cadaadiska uu sheegay inuu kala kulmay arrinta dhulka. Wax ka yar 24 saacadood gudahood ayaa xabsiga loo taxaabay Abwaan Jiheeye, taasoo timid kadib markii uu si fagaare ah uga hadlay dhibaatada uu sheegay inay ka soo gaartay arrinta gurigiisa iyo dhulkiisa. Ma ahan markii ugu horreysay ee maamulka Somaliland lagu eedeeyo tacaddi lagula kacay dadka waxgaradka ah, iyadoo hore loo xiray ama loo cadaadiyay culimo, aqoonyahanno iyo wariyayaal.

items.title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Funakoshi
items.description: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Japanese Vice Foreign Minister Funakoshi Office of the Spokesperson The below is attributable to Spokesman Tommy Pigott: Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met today with Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs Funakoshi Takehiro. The Deputy Secretary and the Vice Minister reaffirmed the importance of the U.S.-Japan Alliance and their strong opposition to any actions that undermine regional peace and stability. They reiterated their shared commitment to bolstering deterrence to advance a free and open Indo-Pacific. The senior officials also discussed the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, including the importance of freedom of navigation, and their shared commitment to enhancing global economic security by strengthening secure, reliable supply chains across key industries.

items.title: Siciid Deni oo dalal shisheeye ku eedeeyay shirqool halis ah
items.description: Garacad (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Puntland, Siciid Cabdullaahi Deni ayaa si adag uga hadlay xaaladda burcad-badeedda Soomaalida, isagoo sheegay in dalal shisheeye ay ka dambeeyaan kooxahaas, isla markaana ay doonayaan inay ka faa’iidaystaan khayraadka ku jira xeebaha Puntland. Deni ayaa sheegay in Puntland aysan oggolaan doonin in cudurdaar looga dhigto la-dagaallanka burcad-badeedda, si ciidamo shisheeye loogu soo daadiyo xeebaha maamulka, kadibna arrintaas loogu isticmaalo fursad lagu gurto khayraadka badda. Madaxweynaha ayaa xusay in dadka Puntland aysan aqbali karin in dadkooda lagu dilo xeebaha, iyadoo loo marayo howlgallo ka dhan ah burcad-badeedda, isaga oo ku adkeystay in maamulka uu awood u leeyahay wax ka qabashada arrinta. Deni oo xalay hadal ka jeediyay deegaanka Garacad ayaa sheegay in qorshuhu noqon karo in Puntland lagu tilmaamo maamul ku guuldarreystay la-dagaallanka burcad-badeedda, kadibna arrintaas loo adeegsado in ciidamo shisheeye lagu keeno xeebaha. “Waxaa la rabaa in la yiraahdo Puntland waa difaaci wayday burcad-badeedda, kadibna xeebaha ciidamo la soo dhoobo oo khayraadkeenna gurtaan,” ayuu yiri Siciid Deni. Wuxuu sidoo kale tusaale u soo qaatay ciidamo iyo dalal shisheeye oo hore uga howlgallay xeebaha Soomaaliya, isagoo sheegay in xilligii la sheegayay in bulshada caalamku la dagaallamaysay burcad-badeedda ay dhacday xaalufin lagu sameeyay khayraadka badda Soomaaliya. Deni ayaa ugu dambeyn farriin u diray shacabka Puntland iyo beesha caalamka, isagoo sheegay in maamulkiisu si adag uga shaqeynayo la-dagaallanka burcad-badeedda, isla markaana aysan oggolaan doonin in arrintaas loo adeegsado faragelin ama in khayraadka Puntland laga faa’iidaysto. Maamulka ayaa horey ugu eedeeyay Dowladda Federaalka inay qeyb ka tahay sababaha dib usoo laabashada burcad-badeedda, oo bilihii dambe dhaq-dhaqaaq xooggan ka waday xeebaha dalka.
