items.title: Puntland at 30 and the Leadership Question
items.description: By Abdisaid M. Ali By 2028, Puntland will be thirty years old. Its first three decades were largely about constructing and preserving political order. Its fourth must be about what that order can produce. The founding generation established a functioning political community during one of the most difficult periods in Somalia’s modern history. The task now is to convert that inheritance into capable government, impartial institutions and a more productive economy. Puntland emerged in 1998 through negotiation among communities and political actors who understood that a common political order required accommodation. Authority had to be bargained, competing interests recognised and disputes contained before they threatened the wider settlement. Successive transfers of presidential power reinforced these habits and made political succession one of Puntland’s most valuable achievements. Thirty years of statehood now demand a higher standard, with citizens entitled to expect reliable public services, wider economic opportunity and institutions capable of carrying the state across administrations. Meeting that standard requires disciplined and responsible leaders supported by modern, talented teams. Good leadership combines inclusion, restraint, respect for the law and responsibility for results, while leaving institutions stronger. Elections therefore shape far more than who holds office. They determine how the state uses time, and five years can strengthen institutions, skills, infrastructure and production or leave another period of opportunity behind. Seven Years and a Changing Political Method The Deni presidency provides an important test of this transition. President Said Abdullahi Deni entered office in 2019 with considerable advantages. Puntland had an established political order, an entrepreneurial population, extensive diaspora networks, strategic ports and a record of negotiated political succession. Seven years offered substantial room to deepen that inheritance, yet a recurring feature of the period has been the movement of political disagreement into the security arena. President Deni of Puntland The confrontation surrounding the removal of Parliament Speaker Abdihakim Dhoobo-Daareed turned deadly in Garowe in 2019 . Two years later, disagreement over command of the Puntland Security Force escalated into armed fighting in Bosaso. The pattern became more serious in April 2022, when Somalia’s then Foreign Minister Abdisaid Muse Ali survived an assassination attempt in Gaalkacyo. Armed forces attacked the compound of senior traditional elder Yasin Abdisamad, where the minister and his family had gathered for iftar. One of the minister’s bodyguards was killed and Elder Abdisamad was seriously wounded, injuries that left him permanently disabled. The 2023 electoral dispute again brought armed mobilisation into a contest over political authority, while Gaalkacyo witnessed another armed confrontation involving Puntland forces in August 2026. These episodes arose from different circumstances, but their recurrence is the larger point. Disputes involving parliament, security command, elections, political rivals and relations with Mogadishu have repeatedly acquired an armed dimension. Negotiation eventually returned, often after disagreements had travelled much further than Puntland’s political settlement could comfortably absorb. The deeper concern is the gradual securitisation of political disagreement. Puntland’s historical political method rested on a different instinct. Its founders faced weak formal institutions and profound disagreements, yet bargaining and accommodation entered early because preserving the common order took precedence over immediate political victory. Authority carried recognised limits, and restraint became part of the practical machinery through which Puntland held together. Political culture develops through such repeated practice. Institutions that settle disputes teach political actors to rely on rules, while early negotiation gives restraint political value. Repeated recourse to coercion produces different incentives, drawing security institutions into political competition and gradually making practices once considered exceptional part of ordinary political calculation. This cuts against the political logic through which Puntland was built. Security institutions derive their legitimacy from protecting citizens and constitutional order, while parliament, courts and electoral bodies exist to process political disagreement through law and procedure. Puntland’s institutional maturity therefore depends on strengthening these boundaries and keeping coercive power firmly within its constitutional purpose. From Grievance to Agency A second political habit deserves equal attention. Puntland has legitimate grievances within Somalia’s unsettled federal order, and defending its constitutional interests is part of the responsibility of any Puntland government. The larger question is what political leadership does with those grievances. During the Deni years, Puntland’s cause has increasingly been framed around what Mogadishu has done, what others have denied Puntland and who bears responsibility for its difficulties. Grievance can rally political support, but sustained too long it can also crowd out agency. Research on victimhood offers a useful caution rather than a diagnosis. Work discussed in Scientific American distinguishes genuine experiences of injustice from a mindset organised around continuing victimhood. At both individual and collective levels, persistent attention to injury can encourage rumination, sharpen perceptions of hostile intent and reduce attention to possible solutions. The more constructive response is to turn adversity towards growth, agency and possibility. That distinction matters for Puntland. Its constitutional interests deserve vigorous defence, but Puntland’s political imagination should reach beyond resistance to Mogadishu. The more demanding questions concern what Puntland itself can build, reform and produce. How can its schools develop better skills? How can its cities work better? How can its institutions earn public confidence? How can its ports support production as well as trade? How can young people turn entrepreneurial ability into firms that employ others? Leadership becomes consequential when it converts grievance into a programme of achievement. Puntland’s cause should therefore be defined increasingly by agency. Its strongest defence of autonomy and federalism is the practical value those arrangements create for its people. A Puntland that governs well, produces more, develops capable institutions and creates opportunities for its youth would make a stronger political argument than grievance alone. Its influence across Somalia would then arise from what others can see working. The Cost of Confrontation Political confrontation also carries an opportunity cost because government has finite attention, administrative capacity and political authority. Years absorbed by recurring contests leave less governing energy for public administration, infrastructure, human development and economic transformation. This is where Deni’s political and economic records intersect. Puntland entered his presidency with inherited structural weaknesses. Its productive base was narrow, imports were high and private enterprise operated through thin formal institutions. Yet the foundations for greater ambition were substantial. The diaspora brings capital and expertise, Bosaso and Garacad connect Puntland to regional commerce, livestock and fisheries offer opportunities for value addition, and its cities contain a younger generation increasingly exposed to technology, finance and entrepreneurship. Seven years of political continuity provided an opportunity to connect these assets, yet the scale of transformation remains modest. Investment follows confidence in the future. Entrepreneurs commit capital where rules are predictable, institutions reliable and politics stable. The same calculation shapes diaspora choices about property, education, business and return. Across thousands of households and firms, these decisions determine where capital, skills and enterprise accumulate. Where Puntland’s political and business elites educate their children, buy property and place their major investments therefore offers a revealing measure of how people with choices assess local institutions and long-term prospects. Puntland’s next leaders should ask why an entrepreneur with ambition and resources would establish the next factory, technology company, logistics firm or processing plant in Puntland rather than Nairobi, Addis Ababa or Dubai. The answer lies in the environment created at home, including infrastructure, finance, property security, predictable taxation, useful skills and institutions that inspire confidence. From Commerce to Production Official Puntland statistics illustrate the structural challenge. A decade ago, imports were about 38 per cent of Puntland’s economy. They crossed 60 per cent in 2019, reached 76 per cent in 2022 and remained near 70 per cent through 2024. The figures point to a deeper structural issue. Puntland has developed considerable capacity to finance, import, transport and distribute goods produced elsewhere, while domestic productive capability has expanded more slowly. The next economic task is to turn commercial strength into productive capability. Livestock and fisheries can support processing and value addition, Bosaso and Garacad can connect domestic production to regional markets, and digital services offer another frontier. Much of the underlying potential already exists. The harder task is institutional, creating conditions in which capital, skills, infrastructure and enterprise can combine, grow and accumulate over time. Somali entrepreneurs have shown remarkable adaptability under difficult conditions. Puntland’s next step is to reduce the institutional friction surrounding that enterprise so that secure property rights, predictable rules, credible commercial institutions, reliable infrastructure and access to finance allow businesses to move towards larger firms, long-term investment, technology, value addition and exports. Fiscal policy should reinforce the same objective. A narrow formal economy concentrates revenue collection on a limited group of ports, traders and companies, while a growing productive economy broadens the future revenue base through more firms, jobs, knowledge and taxable wealth. Building businesses is therefore also part of building the state. From Negotiated Authority to Institutional Authority The political and economic arguments ultimately converge on institutions. Puntland’s next transition is from negotiated authority towards institutionalised authority. Negotiation, accommodation and restraint helped construct the state when formal institutions were young. Maturity requires these principles to become embedded in organisations capable of carrying authority across administrations. Courts should command confidence through consistent application of law, parliament should exercise its constitutional responsibilities independently, and the civil service should preserve professional competence across political transitions. Municipalities and tax authorities should operate through predictable rules, while security institutions protect constitutional order impartially. Together, these qualities give citizens, political actors and businesses confidence that public authority rests on institutions rather than personalities. Institutional quality also carries direct economic value. Credible property rights encourage investment, predictable taxation permits planning, reliable courts strengthen contracts and professional administration reduces uncertainty. Political performance should therefore be judged by what remains after an administration leaves office. Stronger institutions, better public services, deeper productive investment, growing firms and greater confidence among citizens and diaspora investors provide a more meaningful measure of governing success. After seven years, these are legitimate tests of the Deni administration and should become the standard applied to whoever governs next. The Leadership Question Puntland now faces a generational choice as its society and the region around it change rapidly. Its population is younger, businesses compete in a more demanding regional economy, capital and professional talent move easily, and technology is reshaping production and government. The institutions created by the founding generation are entering their fourth decade. Political time therefore carries greater value, making the quality of the next leadership especially consequential. That leadership requires a different governing temperament, one that moves political differences early towards negotiation, law and institutions and keeps security forces focused on protecting constitutional order. Public institutions should exercise authority impartially, while economic policy concentrates on enterprise, skills, investment and production. Leaders should accept responsibility for results and surround themselves with modern, talented teams chosen for their ability to govern. The need for renewal lies in the political habits taking root. When coercion and violence become recurring tools of politics, institutions lose authority and political competition grows more dangerous. When economic opportunity remains narrow, capital and talent gravitate towards places offering stronger prospects. Together, these trends weaken confidence in the rules and make future political crises harder to contain. Puntland’s founding generation achieved something historically significant through negotiation, accommodation and restraint, constructing political order during Somalia’s institutional collapse. The generation approaching 2028 inherits a different responsibility. It must convert that political inheritance into impartial institutions, productive enterprise and a state capable of accumulating competence across successive administrations. Puntland’s influence across Somalia should increasingly come from the same source, through institutions that command trust, businesses that create opportunity, cities that function and leaders whose conduct offers an example others can learn from. Puntland now needs renewal in leadership, political method and governing purpose. Its next generation of leaders should move the state from confrontation towards restraint, from grievance towards agency and from commercial resilience towards productive power. The next political cycle will shape how disagreements are settled, how security institutions exercise power, where capital and talent accumulate and whether public institutions grow stronger across changes of government. The founding generation built Puntland by preserving a common political order. The next must secure that inheritance through restraint, stronger institutions and an economy that gives its people compelling reasons to invest their talent, capital and future at home. Abdisaid M. Ali ———– Abdisaid is the chairperson of Lomé Peace and Security Forum, Former Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation and Former National Security Advisor, Somalia. The more demanding questions concern what Puntland itself can build, reform and produce. How can its schools develop better skills? How can its cities work better? How can its institutions earn public confidence? How can its ports support production as well as trade? How can young people turn entrepreneurial ability into firms that employ others? Leadership becomes consequential when it converts grievance into a programme of achievement. Puntland’s cause should therefore be defined increasingly by agency. Its strongest defence of autonomy and federalism is the practical value those arrangements create for its people. A Puntland that governs well, produces more, develops capable institutions and creates opportunities for its youth would make a stronger political argument than grievance alone. Its influence across Somalia would then arise from what others can see working. The Cost of Confrontation Political confrontation also carries an opportunity cost because government has finite attention, administrative capacity and political authority. Years absorbed by recurring contests leave less governing energy for public administration, infrastructure, human development and economic transformation. This is where Deni’s political and economic records intersect. Puntland entered his presidency with inherited structural weaknesses. Its productive base was narrow, imports were high and private enterprise operated through thin formal institutions. Yet the foundations for greater ambition were substantial. The diaspora brings capital and expertise, Bosaso and Garacad connect Puntland to regional commerce, livestock and fisheries offer opportunities for value addition, and its cities contain a younger generation increasingly exposed to technology, finance and entrepreneurship. Seven years of political continuity provided an opportunity to connect these assets, yet the scale of transformation remains modest. Investment follows confidence in the future. Entrepreneurs commit capital where rules are predictable, institutions reliable and politics stable. The same calculation shapes diaspora choices about property, education, business and return. Across thousands of households and firms, these decisions determine where capital, skills and enterprise accumulate. Where Puntland’s political and business elites educate their children, buy property and place their major investments therefore offers a revealing measure of how people with choices assess local institutions and long-term prospects. Puntland’s next leaders should ask why an entrepreneur with ambition and resources would establish the next factory, technology company, logistics firm or processing plant in Puntland rather than Nairobi, Addis Ababa or Dubai. The answer lies in the environment created at home, including infrastructure, finance, property security, predictable taxation, useful skills and institutions that inspire confidence. From Commerce to Production Official Puntland statistics illustrate the structural challenge. A decade ago, imports were about 38 per cent of Puntland’s economy. They crossed 60 per cent in 2019, reached 76 per cent in 2022 and remained near 70 per cent through 2024. The figures point to a deeper structural issue. Puntland has developed considerable capacity to finance, import, transport and distribute goods produced elsewhere, while domestic productive capability has expanded more slowly. The next economic task is to turn commercial strength into productive capability. Livestock and fisheries can support processing and value addition, Bosaso and Garacad can connect domestic production to regional markets, and digital services offer another frontier. Much of the underlying potential already exists. The harder task is institutional, creating conditions in which capital, skills, infrastructure and enterprise can combine, grow and accumulate over time. Somali entrepreneurs have shown remarkable adaptability under difficult conditions. Puntland’s next step is to reduce the institutional friction surrounding that enterprise so that secure property rights, predictable rules, credible commercial institutions, reliable infrastructure and access to finance allow businesses to move towards larger firms, long-term investment, technology, value addition and exports. Fiscal policy should reinforce the same objective. A narrow formal economy concentrates revenue collection on a limited group of ports, traders and companies, while a growing productive economy broadens the future revenue base through more firms, jobs, knowledge and taxable wealth. Building businesses is therefore also part of building the state. From Negotiated Authority to Institutional Authority The political and economic arguments ultimately converge on institutions. Puntland’s next transition is from negotiated authority towards institutionalised authority. Negotiation, accommodation and restraint helped construct the state when formal institutions were young. Maturity requires these principles to become embedded in organisations capable of carrying authority across administrations. Courts should command confidence through consistent application of law, parliament should exercise its constitutional responsibilities independently, and the civil service should preserve professional competence across political transitions. Municipalities and tax authorities should operate through predictable rules, while security institutions protect constitutional order impartially. Together, these qualities give citizens, political actors and businesses confidence that public authority rests on institutions rather than personalities. Institutional quality also carries direct economic value. Credible property rights encourage investment, predictable taxation permits planning, reliable courts strengthen contracts and professional administration reduces uncertainty. Political performance should therefore be judged by what remains after an administration leaves office. Stronger institutions, better public services, deeper productive investment, growing firms and greater confidence among citizens and diaspora investors provide a more meaningful measure of governing success. After seven years, these are legitimate tests of the Deni administration and should become the standard applied to whoever governs next. The Leadership Question Puntland now faces a generational choice as its society and the region around it change rapidly. Its population is younger, businesses compete in a more demanding regional economy, capital and professional talent move easily, and technology is reshaping production and government. The institutions created by the founding generation are entering their fourth decade. Political time therefore carries greater value, making the quality of the next leadership especially consequential. That leadership requires a different governing temperament, one that moves political differences early towards negotiation, law and institutions and keeps security forces focused on protecting constitutional order. Public institutions should exercise authority impartially, while economic policy concentrates on enterprise, skills, investment and production. Leaders should accept responsibility for results and surround themselves with modern, talented teams chosen for their ability to govern. The need for renewal lies in the political habits taking root. When coercion and violence become recurring tools of politics, institutions lose authority and political competition grows more dangerous. When economic opportunity remains narrow, capital and talent gravitate towards places offering stronger prospects. Together, these trends weaken confidence in the rules and make future political crises harder to contain. Puntland’s founding generation achieved something historically significant through negotiation, accommodation and restraint, constructing political order during Somalia’s institutional collapse. The generation approaching 2028 inherits a different responsibility. It must convert that political inheritance into impartial institutions, productive enterprise and a state capable of accumulating competence across successive administrations. Puntland’s influence across Somalia should increasingly come from the same source, through institutions that command trust, businesses that create opportunity, cities that function and leaders whose conduct offers an example others can learn from. Puntland now needs renewal in leadership, political method and governing purpose. Its next generation of leaders should move the state from confrontation towards restraint, from grievance towards agency and from commercial resilience towards productive power. The next political cycle will shape how disagreements are settled, how security institutions exercise power, where capital and talent accumulate and whether public institutions grow stronger across changes of government. The founding generation built Puntland by preserving a common political order. The next must secure that inheritance through restraint, stronger institutions and an economy that gives its people compelling reasons to invest their talent, capital and future at home. Abdisaid M. items.title: Siyaasiyiinta Puntland oo war ka soo saaray xiisadda PSF iyo ciidamada Puntland
items.description: Garoowe (Caasimada Online) – Golaha Siyaasiyiinta iyo Aqoonyahanka Puntland ayaa ku baaqay in si degdeg ah oo nabadeed loo xalliyo xiisadda ka taagan deegaanka Kodmo ee degmada Rako-raaxo, gobolka Karkaar, halkaas oo maalmihii u dambeeyey ay isku horfadhiyeen ciidamada Puntland iyo ciidamo xiriir la leh dowladda federaalka. War-murtiyeed ku taariikhaysan 12-ka Agoosto, oo ay saxiixeen 26 siyaasiyiin, aqoonyahanno iyo mas’uuliyiin hore, ayuu Goluhu maamulka Puntland kula taliyey inuu odayaasha iyo waxgaradka deegaanka kala tashado sidii xal loogu heli lahaa xaaladda, lagana fogaado dagaal cusub oo dhiig ku daato. “Goluhu wuxuu ku talinayaa in maamulku uu kala tashado dhaqanka iyo odayaasha deegaanka xal u helidda xiisadda colaadeed ee Kodmo, si xal nabadeed loogu dhammeeyo,” ayaa lagu yiri war-murtiyeedka. Goluhu wuxuu sidoo kale ku baaqay in wadahadallada socda mudnaanta la siiyo, halkii la qaadi lahaa tallaabo ciidan oo horseedi karta iska hor-imaad. Baaqan ayaa imanaya iyadoo Kodmo ay noqotay goobtii ugu dambeysay ee uu gaaro khilaaf sii xoogeysanaya oo u dhexeeya Puntland iyo dowladda federaalka, kaas oo markii hore ahaa muran siyaasadeed balse toddobaadyadii dambe isu beddelay loollan toos ah oo ku saabsan cidda amar ku leh ciidamada iyo saldhigyada milatari ee gudaha Puntland. Ciidamada hadda ku sugan qaybo ka mid ah Karkaar ayaa 7-dii Agoosto isaga baxay saldhig ay ku lahaayeen Carmo ee gobolka Bari, kadib markii Puntland cadaadis ku saartay ciidamada aan hoos iman taliskeeda inay hubka dhigaan ama ku biiraan hay’adaha amniga Puntland. Ciidamadaas ayaa markaas u dhaqaaqay dhinaca Xumbays iyo deegaanno u dhow Rako-raaxo, taas oo keentay in Puntland-na ay ciidamo u dirto aagga. Odayaal dhaqameed ayaa tan iyo markaas waday dadaallo lagu kala dhex-galayo labada dhinac. Xiisadda Karkaar waxay daba socotaa dagaal 5-tii Agoosto ka dhacay waqooyiga Gaalkacyo, halkaas oo ciidamada Puntland ay la wareegeen saldhig ay haysteen ciidamo la safnaa dowladda federaalka. Puntland waxay sheegtay in howlgalkaas lagu qabtay in ka badan 100 qof, laguna qabsaday hub iyo gaadiid ciidan. Maalin kadib, Golaha Wasiirrada Puntland wuxuu amar ku bixiyey inaan gudaha deegaannada maamulka ka hawlgeli karin ciidamo ama gaadiid ciidan oo aan ka tirsanayn hay’adaha rasmiga ah ee Puntland. Golaha Wasiirradu wuxuu sidoo kale go’aamiyey in siyaasiyiin iyo saraakiil lagu eedeeyo inay qalqal gelinayaan amniga loo gudbiyo hay’adaha garsoorka. Hase yeeshee, Golaha Siyaasiyiinta iyo Aqoonyahanka ayaa hadda ka digaya in qaabka loo wajahayo arrinta Kodmo uu abuuri karo khilaaf ka sii ballaaran kan hadda jira. Goluhu wuxuu si gaar ah u sheegay in hub-ka-dhigis lagu guuleysan karo oo keliya haddii ay ka horreyso heshiis bulsho, wadatashi loo dhan yahay iyo sharci cad oo lagu wada kalsoon yahay. “Goluhu wuxuu ku talinayaa in hannaan kasta oo hub-ka-dhigis ah uu u baahan yahay heshiis bulsho, wadatashi loo dhan yahay iyo shuruuc cad oo hagta,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraalka. Fariintaas waxay si toos ah u taabaneysaa halka uu muranka hadda ka taagan yahay. Puntland waxay ku doodaysaa inaan la aqbali karin ciidamo hubeysan oo gudaha deegaannadeeda ku sugan balse amar ka qaata meel ka baxsan hay’adaha Puntland. Dhinaca kale, ciidamada ay Puntland beegsaneyso qaarkood waxay isu aqoonsadeen ciidamo dowladda federaalka ka tirsan, waxayna diideen inay hoos tagaan taliska Puntland. Khilaafkaas dhinaca amniga ahi wuxuu salka ku hayaa muran siyaasadeed oo muddo soo jiitamayey oo u dhexeeya Garoowe iyo Muqdisho, gaar ahaan sida loo kala leeyahay awoodaha dowladda federaalka iyo dowlad-goboleedyada. Puntland ayaa si weyn uga hortimid isbeddelladii dastuurka ee dowladda federaalka, halka Madaxweyne Saciid Cabdullaahi Deni uu muddooyinkii dambe si joogto ah ugu eedeeyey Villa Somalia inay wiiqeyso nidaamka federaalka. Waxaase xaaladda Kodmo ka dhigaya mid aad uga xasaasi badan murannadii hore in ciidamada iyo dadka deegaanka ay isku dhex jiraan arrimo siyaasadeed, ciidan iyo bulsho. Taasi waxay kordhineysaa khatarta ah in iska hor-imaad u dhexeeya laba ciidan uu isu rogo colaad deegaan oo raadkeedu sii dheeraado. Golaha ayaa taas ku daray walaac kale oo amni, isagoo maamulka xusuusiyey in Puntland aysan weli ka bixin halista kooxaha argagixisada ee ku dhuumaaleysanaya buuraha Calmiskaad. Golaha Siyaasiyiinta iyo Aqoonyahanka ayaa ugu dambeyn ugu baaqay odayaasha dhaqanka, culimada, ganacsatada, siyaasiyiinta iyo qaybaha kale ee bulshada inay ka shaqeeyaan nabadda iyo midnimada. “Waddada ugu habboon ee wax tar u ah amniga, wadajirka, xasilloonida iyo dowladnimada Puntland” ayuu Goluhu ku tilmaamay wadahadal ku dhisan is-qancin iyo isu-tanaasul. Warqadda ayaa waxaa ku saxiixnaa: Wasiir Axmed Ciise Cawad Wasiir Faarax Xali Shire Wasiir Cali X. Warsame Siyaasi Nuradiin Aadan Diiriye Wasiir Cabdiqani Cabdi Jaama (Suumahaye) Aqoonyahan Siyaad Cali Jaamac Aqoonyahan Maxamed Cabdi Baldho Eng. Ciise M. Dholowaa Dr. Aaden Shiikhdoon Cali Dr. Dahir Mire Jibriil Aqoonyahan Cabdirisaaq Jaamac Janogale Aqoonyahan Ruqiyo Maxamed Faarax Dr. Bashiir Maxamed Xuseen Xildhibaan Cabdikariim Xuseen Guure (Shaacuur) Aqoonyahan Maxamed Cabdiqafaar X. Xuseen Wasiir Cabdikhaadar Faarax Shaaciye Aqoonyahan Yuusuf Maxamed Xasan Dr. Bashiir Ashkir Muuse Yasiin Mohamed Beeldaaje Wasiir Maxamuud Beeldaaje Faarax Wasiir Maxamuud X. items.title: Puntland oo ka digtay safarka Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ee Gaalkacyo
items.description: Dowlad Goboleedka Puntland ayaa Madaxweynaha Dowladda Federaalka, Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ku eedeysay in uu colaad cusub ka hurinayo deegaanada Puntland. Madaxtooyada Puntland oo xalay warsaxaafadeed soo saartay ayaa sheegtay in Puntland ay si dhow ula socoto abaabulada qorsheysan bay tiri ee uu Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud wado. Puntland ayaa ka digtay qorshaha safar ay sheegtay in Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuuud uu ku imanayo koonfurta Magaalada Gaalkacyo, iyadoona sheegtay in uu uga gol leeyahay in uu colaad uga abuuro magaaladaasi, oo si nabad iyo xasilloonida ah ay ugu wada nool yihiin labada dhinac ee Puntland iyo Galmudug. Waxay sheegtay Puntland in ay heegan buuxa gelisay ciidamadeeda, waxayna dadka reer Puntland ku wargelisay in ay u diyaargaroobaan in maamulku uu qaadayo tallaabooyin dheeraad ah, oo lagu adkeynayo amniga Magaalada Gaalkacyo iyo deegaanada hoos yimaada. Warsaxaafadeedka Puntland Dowladda Puntland waxay si dhow ula socotaa abaabulada qorsheysan ee uu Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud wado, waxayna ka digeysaa qorshaha safarka Xasan Sheekh uu ku imaanayo koonfurta Gaalkacyo ee Dowladda Galmudug, taas oo uu uga gol leeyahay in uu fidno iyo colaad ka abuuro Magaalada Gaalkacyo oo si nabad iyo xasillooni leh ay ugu wada nool yihiin labada dhinac ee Puntland iyo Galmudug. Dowladda Puntland waxay maamulka iyo shacabka Dowladda Galmudug, gaar ahaan koonfurta Gaalkacyo uga mahadcelineysaa kaalinta weyn ee ay ka qaateen ilaalinta nabadda iyo ka hortagga isku dayadii qorsheysnaa ee Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ku doonayay in uu qalalaase amni ka abuuro Magaalada Gaalkacyo, si uu uga dhigto foodsaar siyaasadeed, waxayna ugu baaqeysaa maamulka iyo shacabka Galmudug ee koonfurta Gaalkacyo in ay ka hortagaan isku dayada cusub ee Xasan Sheekh uu wado. Dowladda Puntland waxay heegan buuxa gelisay Ciidamada Difaaca Puntland, waxayna dadweynaha reer Puntland ku wargelineysaa in ay u diyaargaroobaan in dowladdu qaadeyso tillaabooyin dheeri ah oo lagu adkeynayo amniga guud ahaan Puntland, gaar ahaan amniga Magaalada Gaalkacyo iyo deegaanada hoos yimaada. Sidoo kale, Dowladda Puntland waxay la socodsiineysaa Ummadda Soomaaliyeed, dalalka deriska iyo guud ahaan Beesha Caalamka in Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu qaadayo masuuliyadda ka dhalata fidmada iyo colaadda uu ka abaabulayo Puntland.

Dowladda Puntland waxay maamulka iyo shacabka Dowladda Galmudug, gaar ahaan koonfurta Gaalkacyo uga mahadcelineysaa kaalinta weyn ee ay ka qaateen ilaalinta nabadda iyo ka hortagga isku dayadii qorsheysnaa ee Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ku doonayay in uu qalalaase amni ka abuuro Magaalada Gaalkacyo, si uu uga dhigto foodsaar siyaasadeed, waxayna ugu baaqeysaa maamulka iyo shacabka Galmudug ee koonfurta Gaalkacyo in ay ka hortagaan isku dayada cusub ee Xasan Sheekh uu wado. Dowladda Puntland waxay heegan buuxa gelisay Ciidamada Difaaca Puntland, waxayna dadweynaha reer Puntland ku wargelineysaa in ay u diyaargaroobaan in dowladdu qaadeyso tillaabooyin dheeri ah oo lagu adkeynayo amniga guud ahaan Puntland, gaar ahaan amniga Magaalada Gaalkacyo iyo deegaanada hoos yimaada. Sidoo kale, Dowladda Puntland waxay la socodsiineysaa Ummadda Soomaaliyeed, dalalka deriska iyo guud ahaan Beesha Caalamka in Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu qaadayo masuuliyadda ka dhalata fidmada iyo colaadda uu ka abaabulayo Puntland.

items.title: Puntland Draws a Constitutional Red Line as Somalia’s Political Negotiations Remain Deadlocked
items.description: Garowe (WDN) — Puntland has issued one of its clearest statements yet on the conditions under which it would rejoin a fully agreed Somali federal system, insisting that the country cannot achieve lasting political stability without a constitution endorsed directly by the Somali people. Puntland Minister of Youth and Sports Caydiid Dirir said Puntland would continue to engage with the international community independently until Somalia has a government and political order based on broad national agreement. His remarks come as Somalia’s prolonged political negotiations between President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s Federal Government and opposition forces remain deadlocked after months of internationally supported talks. According to Minister Dirir, Puntland is not opposed to being part of a united Somali state. Rather, he said, Puntland’s position is that such a state must be built on a genuine political agreement and a permanent constitution approved directly by the Somali people. “Puntland is ready to be part of a Somali government that is based on agreement, provided that the country has a constitution that is not provisional and that has been directly approved by the Somali people,” Dirir said. The statement goes to the heart of Somalia’s current political crisis. Negotiations Stalled as Political Maneuvering Continues For months, international partners have attempted to mediate between President Hassan Sheikh’s administration and a broad coalition of opposition leaders over elections, constitutional arrangements, federal-state relations, and the future distribution of political power. Yet the negotiations have repeatedly failed to produce a comprehensive agreement. The central problem is no longer simply disagreement over the technical details of an electoral system. It is a much deeper dispute over who has the authority to determine Somalia’s political rules—and whether those rules can be changed without broad national consent. Critics of the Federal Government accuse President Hassan Sheikh of maintaining an uncompromising negotiating position while simultaneously pursuing a political strategy designed to strengthen his influence outside Mogadishu. They point to developments in several Federal Member States, where opponents allege that the administration has sought to influence regional political processes and install leaderships considered sympathetic to Villa Somalia. For these critics, the contradiction is striking: while international mediators continue trying to bring Somalia’s rival political camps around one negotiating table, political battles over the leadership of Federal Member States continue on the ground. The Federal Member State Question The controversy is particularly significant because Federal Member States are not merely administrative subdivisions. They are central components of Somalia’s federal political architecture. Puntland, Jubaland, South West State, Galmudug and Hirshabelle each possess their own political institutions and security structures, while sharing constitutional responsibilities with the Federal Government. The growing confrontation over regional leadership therefore has national consequences. Critics of President Hassan Sheikh argue that attempts to reshape political leadership in multiple states while negotiations remain unresolved risk undermining the very federal consensus that international mediators are attempting to build. They fear that if regional administrations become politically dependent on Mogadishu, Somalia’s federal system could gradually become centralized around the presidency. Supporters of the Federal Government reject that interpretation, arguing that strengthening national political institutions and encouraging democratic, party-based elections are necessary steps toward building a functioning Somali state. The dispute therefore goes far beyond personalities. It is fundamentally about the future balance between federal authority and regional autonomy. Puntland’s Constitutional Demand Puntland’s latest position reflects a longstanding argument that Somalia’s temporary constitutional arrangements cannot indefinitely serve as the foundation for a permanent political settlement. The demand for a constitution approved directly by the Somali people represents a significant constitutional red line. From Puntland’s perspective, the legitimacy of the country’s future political system must come from a process broad enough to include the Federal Government, Federal Member States, political opposition, traditional leaders, civil society and, ultimately, Somali citizens themselves. Without that consensus, Puntland argues, constitutional changes risk becoming instruments of political competition rather than foundations for stable governance. That position also explains why the current negotiations have become so difficult. The opposing camps are not simply negotiating over how to hold an election. They are negotiating over the rules under which Somalia itself will be governed. The danger is that prolonged negotiations may continue to run in parallel with political developments on the ground. If the Federal Government succeeds in strengthening its influence over several Federal Member States before a national agreement is reached, critics argue, the eventual political settlement could be shaped by a new balance of power rather than by genuine consensus. That could make an eventual agreement even more difficult. Somalia has experienced this cycle before: political competition produces mistrust; mistrust weakens cooperation between Mogadishu and the states; weakened cooperation creates security and political crises; and those crises make national consensus even harder to achieve. Meanwhile, the country faces serious security threats, economic pressures and an uncertain electoral timetable. Every additional month of political paralysis therefore carries a cost. The Choice Before Somalia Puntland’s message is ultimately a challenge to all sides. The Federal Government must decide whether it wants a federal system built around negotiated legitimacy or one increasingly defined by political dominance from the center. The opposition must demonstrate that its alternative is capable of producing functioning institutions rather than simply resisting the incumbent government. And the Federal Member States must determine how they can defend their constitutional powers while remaining part of a viable Somali federation. International partners can facilitate negotiations, provide technical assistance and encourage compromise. But they cannot manufacture the political agreement that Somalia’s leaders themselves have so far failed to reach. The fundamental question is therefore becoming increasingly unavoidable: Will Somalia’s political leaders negotiate a federal settlement broad enough to command national legitimacy—or will political maneuvering continue to deepen the divisions that have kept the country locked in crisis? Puntland’s latest statement suggests that, for now, it is unwilling to accept a political arrangement simply because it has been declared by Mogadishu. Its message is clear: Somalia can be one country, but its political future must be built on agreement, constitutional legitimacy and the consent of its people. items.title: Hassan Sheikh Calls for Rule-Based Politics as Critics Ask Whether His Own Government Is Operating Outside the Rules
items.description: By Abdullahi A. Nor President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has called on Somalia to move beyond personality-driven politics and establish stronger institutions capable of clearly defining who makes national decisions, how those decisions are reached, and which institutions are accountable for implementing them. It is a message that sounds difficult to dispute. Yet coming from a presidency facing persistent accusations of constitutional overreach, political engineering and the concentration of power, it also raises an uncomfortable question: is the President describing the Somalia he wants—or the Somalia his critics say his government is helping to create? Speaking at an event focused on education, national institution-building and the development of Somalia’s human capital, Hassan Sheikh argued that the country cannot achieve sustainable progress while political decision-making remains dominated by individuals and political groups. He urged Somalis to “wake up” and build a political system capable of replacing personality-based politics with institutions governed by clearly defined rules. The President’s argument is that Somalia’s economic and social progress—from expanding commerce to improvements in education and public services—will remain limited unless the country’s political system becomes stable, predictable and institutionally grounded. The argument lands in a deeply polarized political environment. The president’s remarks are seen as nothing more than a performative political rhetoric and empty lip service—an approach to governance that the President has increasingly become accustomed to. The Contradiction at the Center of Somalia’s Crisis Opposition leaders have spent months making almost the opposite argument: that the central problem is not the absence of institutions, but the use of state institutions by the presidency to advance a political agenda. They accuse Hassan Sheikh’s administration of attempting to shape the electoral environment in its own favor, influencing the political leadership of Federal Member States, and pursuing constitutional and electoral changes without the broad consensus they believe Somalia’s federal system requires. These remain political realities, and the government rejects such characterizations. Nevertheless, they expose a striking contradiction at the heart of Somalia’s current crisis. The President says Somalia needs institutions strong enough to prevent individuals from determining the country’s political destiny. His opponents respond that the presidency itself has become too powerful, corrupt and that political institutions are increasingly being used to serve the interests of the incumbent administration. That dispute is particularly significant because Somalia’s political negotiations have remained stalled despite months of engagement between the Federal Government and opposition groups, with international actors attempting to broker an agreement over elections, constitutional arrangements and the country’s political future. While those negotiations continue, political developments in several Federal Member States, SWS, Galmudug, Hirshabeele, have proceeded rapidly, intensifying opposition suspicions that the government is attempting to reshape the political landscape before a national agreement is reached. An Election Designed by Those in Power? One of the most contentious accusations facing the administration concerns the electoral process. Opposition leaders argue that the Federal Government’s preferred model risks allowing the incumbent political establishment to influence the rules, institutions and conditions under which the next election will take place. They have repeatedly called for an electoral framework negotiated among the Federal Government, opposition, Federal Member States and other stakeholders rather than one effectively designed by the government itself. The administration maintains that direct elections and stronger political institutions are essential to ending Somalia’s long dependence on indirect, clan-based political arrangements. The disagreement is therefore not simply about whether Somalia should hold elections. It is about who writes the rules, who controls the institutions administering the process, and whether the political playing field can be considered genuinely neutral. That is the question that continues to haunt Somalia’s political transition. Public Land and the Politics of Accountability The debate also extends beyond elections. Opposition figures and civil society activists have accused this administration in Mogadishu of failing to adequately protect public land and have raised allegations concerning the transfer or sale of valuable government property to politically connected individuals and businesses. Some activists have made particularly disturbing claims involving the encroachment or redevelopment of burial grounds. Such fact requires no investigation or documentary evidence because the eviction of poor people and sale produced nearly living witnesses of 750,000 IDPs, is an established fact. But their persistence reflects a much broader concern over public assets, transparency and accountability in a country where state institutions remain fragile. For critics, the issue is straightforward: a government cannot credibly preach institutional accountability while citizens remain uncertain about how public assets are being allocated and who benefits from them. The specter of kleptocracy, nepotism and the president’s legacy The administration has also faced accusations of nepotism and patronage, with opponents arguing that political appointments and access to state resources have at all times favored individuals with close political, familial or clan connections. Again, the government rejects such accusations. But the broader principle raised by these allegations is important. Strong institutions are not measured by how frequently leaders speak about them. They are measured by whether public appointments, procurement, public land administration, financial management and political decision-making can withstand independent scrutiny. That is where Somalia’s institutional transformation remains unfinished. Hassan Sheikh Mohamud occupies a unique place in Somalia’s political history: he is the first Somali president to return to the presidency after previously serving as head of state. That alone will form an important part of his historical legacy. But history will judge more than the fact that he became the first president elected to two non-consecutive terms. It will also judge what happened to Somalia’s institutions during his tenure. Was the presidency used to strengthen federal institutions or to consolidate political influence? Did constitutional reform produce broader national consensus or deepen political division? Did electoral reform create genuine democratic competition or merely change the mechanism through which political power is distributed? And perhaps most importantly, did Somalia emerge from his presidency with stronger institutions than those he inherited? Those questions are enough to make him the worst president ever in Somalia’s political history. Security, Education and the State Hassan Sheikh also linked political stability to national security and education. Using the metaphor of a farmer preparing the soil before planting, he described security as the foundation upon which education, economic development, dignity and national prosperity must be built. He argued that Somalia’s greatest resource is not oil, minerals, buildings or military hardware but its people and the knowledge they possess. His reference to Japan was intended to illustrate the transformative power of investment in education, research and human capital. That message is difficult to challenge. Somalia desperately needs better schools, universities, skilled professionals, productive businesses and institutions capable of turning knowledge into economic opportunity. But education and security cannot flourish independently of political legitimacy. A university requires predictable institutions. Businesses require enforceable laws. Investors require confidence that contracts and property rights will be respected. Citizens require confidence that government power is constrained by law. President Hassan sold the grounds of the Somali National University including the labs, nursing school among other faculties the medical faculty grounds. In other words, the institutional system the President says Somalia needs is precisely the system his critics argue must first be protected from political interference. A Presidency at a Crossroads The most consequential question facing Hassan Sheikh may therefore be whether his government can reconcile its rhetoric about institutional governance with the political reality confronting the country. Somalia does need to move beyond personality politics. It does need stronger institutions. It does need a predictable constitutional order. It does need transparent elections, accountable government, secure public assets and an independent judiciary. But those principles cannot apply only to political opponents. They must apply equally to the government in power. If Hassan Sheikh succeeds in leaving behind stronger institutions, a credible constitutional settlement and an electoral system trusted by competing political forces, his second presidency could ultimately be remembered as a period of institutional transformation. If, however, political polarization deepens, constitutional disputes remain unresolved, federal relations deteriorate and patronage, corruption and political manipulation continue to dominate public discourse, history may record a very different legacy. The President says Somalia must become a country governed by institutions rather than individuals. That is precisely the standard by which his own presidency should now be measured. The ultimate test is not what the President says about the rule of law. It is whether Somalia’s institutions are strong enough to constrain the President himself. Abdullahi A. items.title: State Department Establishes Task Force to End Birth Tourism
items.description: State Department Establishes Task Force to End Birth Tourism Office of the Spokesperson August 12, 2026 Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s leadership, the Department of State is using all available tools to defend the integrity of U.S. citizenship, ensure nonimmigrant visas are used only for their lawful and intended purposes, and prevent their exploitation through birth tourism. As President Trump has made clear, citizenship is not a commodity to be acquired through the calculated exploitation of U.S. immigration laws. The Department of State is working closely with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to combat birth tourism and protect the integrity of the U.S. immigration system. New Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force To maximize the success of this comprehensive effort, the State Department has established a Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force. The Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force reviews the activities of visa holders worldwide to identify instances of birth tourism, take action to revoke visas of those who engage in or facilitate it, and dismantle the networks that profit from this abuse. The Task Force addresses the abuse by analyzing and connecting information held across the Department and other federal agencies, including the DHS. Thanks to the coordination of the Task Force, the Department of State is addressing birth tourism on a global scale, examining travel histories of individuals from all around the world in order to end this exploitation and abuse. The Birth Tourism taskforce has taken action by revoking more than 600 visas from foreign nationals across the globe to safeguard our nation from this abuse. The Department generally revokes visas when there are indications of a potential ineligibility. The Secretary has broad discretionary authority to revoke visas – and the Trump Administration is committed to exercising that authority to protect the American people and the integrity of our immigration system. Birth Tourism Has Become a For-Profit Industry Facilitators have turned birth tourism into a lucrative, for-profit industry. These facilitators sometimes market themselves as doulas, midwives, or wellness advocates while openly advertising “birth in the U.S.” services, visa coaching, and hospital arrangements. Some forge medical documents or coach clients to conceal their true travel purpose and avoid paying hospital bills, with online marketing promising clients “automatic citizenship” and “a future without borders.” The facts are clear – birth tourism is a pervasive practice that involves nationals from countries spanning every region of the globe. The Department is taking action to dismantle these networks and hold all participants accountable. Birth Tourism Fraud The work of the Bureau of Consular Affairs Task Force and consular officers at U.S. embassies and consulates around the world is exposing widespread patterns of deception. Foreigners who willfully misrepresent the purpose of their travel or entry into the United States may be permanently ineligible for a U.S. visa or entry to the United States. The Department has uncovered patterns that illustrate the lengths some applicants will go to circumvent our laws in order to secure U.S. citizenship for their children – and potentially for themselves in the future. One couple used a conference and a vacation trip to go shopping as cover stories to give birth to two children in the United States, lying about their travel purpose in two separate visa applications. On the second occasion, the couple concealed that they had a child. The visas have been revoked. In another case, a foreign government official requested a visa to travel on behalf of her government for just one week, but instead stayed three months and gave birth in the United States before departing. The Department revoked the visa. Another traveler applied for a visa to go on vacation in Orlando and instead traveled to Los Angeles and gave birth five days after arrival. The Department revoked the visa. Citizenship is not a commodity to be acquired through calculated exploitation and evasion of the immigration laws. items.fullContent: State Department Establishes Task Force to End Birth Tourism Office of the Spokesperson August 12, 2026 Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s leadership, the Department of State is using all available tools to defend the integrity of U.S. citizenship, ensure nonimmigrant visas are used only for their lawful and intended purposes, and prevent their exploitation through birth tourism. As President Trump has made clear, citizenship is not a commodity to be acquired through the calculated exploitation of U.S. immigration laws. The Department of State is working closely with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to combat birth tourism and protect the integrity of the U.S. immigration system. New Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force To maximize the success of this comprehensive effort, the State Department has established a Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force. The Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force reviews the activities of visa holders worldwide to identify instances of birth tourism, take action to revoke visas of those who engage in or facilitate it, and dismantle the networks that profit from this abuse. The Task Force addresses the abuse by analyzing and connecting information held across the Department and other federal agencies, including the DHS. Thanks to the coordination of the Task Force, the Department of State is addressing birth tourism on a global scale, examining travel histories of individuals from all around the world in order to end this exploitation and abuse. The Birth Tourism taskforce has taken action by revoking more than 600 visas from foreign nationals across the globe to safeguard our nation from this abuse. The Department generally revokes visas when there are indications of a potential ineligibility. The Secretary has broad discretionary authority to revoke visas – and the Trump Administration is committed to exercising that authority to protect the American people and the integrity of our immigration system. Birth Tourism Has Become a For-Profit Industry Facilitators have turned birth tourism into a lucrative, for-profit industry. These facilitators sometimes market themselves as doulas, midwives, or wellness advocates while openly advertising “birth in the U.S.” services, visa coaching, and hospital arrangements. Some forge medical documents or coach clients to conceal their true travel purpose and avoid paying hospital bills, with online marketing promising clients “automatic citizenship” and “a future without borders.” The facts are clear – birth tourism is a pervasive practice that involves nationals from countries spanning every region of the globe. The Department is taking action to dismantle these networks and hold all participants accountable. Birth Tourism Fraud The work of the Bureau of Consular Affairs Task Force and consular officers at U.S. embassies and consulates around the world is exposing widespread patterns of deception. Foreigners who willfully misrepresent the purpose of their travel or entry into the United States may be permanently ineligible for a U.S. visa or entry to the United States. The Department has uncovered patterns that illustrate the lengths some applicants will go to circumvent our laws in order to secure U.S. citizenship for their children – and potentially for themselves in the future. One couple used a conference and a vacation trip to go shopping as cover stories to give birth to two children in the United States, lying about their travel purpose in two separate visa applications. On the second occasion, the couple concealed that they had a child. The visas have been revoked. In another case, a foreign government official requested a visa to travel on behalf of her government for just one week, but instead stayed three months and gave birth in the United States before departing. The Department revoked the visa. Another traveler applied for a visa to go on vacation in Orlando and instead traveled to Los Angeles and gave birth five days after arrival. The Department revoked the visa. Citizenship is not a commodity to be acquired through calculated exploitation and evasion of the immigration laws. Foreign nationals who abuse the visa system, and those who help them do so, may lose their visa, their access, and their future in the United States. This is only the beginning.

items.title: Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda Soomaaliya oo ka Jawaabay Eedeymaha Hantidhowrka
items.description: Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah ee Soomaaliya ayaa ka jawaabay eedeymo ka soo baxay Xafiiska Hantidhowrka Guud ee Qaranka, kuwaas oo la xiriiray habraaca diblumaasiyiinta iyo shaqaalaha Wasaaradda loo diro dalalka dibadda. Wasiirka ayaa sheegay in diblumaasiyiinta Soomaaliya u dirtay safaaradaha iyo qunsuliyadaha dalka ay yihiin shaqaale ka tirsan Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda, isagoo meesha ka saaray in dibadda loo diro dad aan hore uga tirsanaan Wasaaradda. Hadalkan ayaa yimid kaddib markii Xafiiska Hantidhowrka Guud ee Qaranka uu warbixin uu soo saaray ku sheegay in Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda ay dibadda u dirtay 14 diblumaasi oo aan marin dhammaan shuruudihii iyo habraacyadii looga baahnaa, halka 19 shaqaale ahna la sheegay in aysan qaadan tababarkii diblumaasiyadeed ee looga baahnaa ka hor inta aan loo dirin howlahooda. Wasiirka ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in arrintan ay wadahadallo uga socdaan Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Xafiiska Hantidhowrka Guud, si loo kala caddeeyo qodobada ay labada dhinac isku khilaafsan yihiin loona saxo wixii khaladaad ah ee jira. Warbixinta Hantidhowrka ayaa ku baaqday in Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda ay hagaajiso habraacyada shaqaaleysiinta, tababarka iyo dirista diblumaasiyiinta, iyadoo sidoo kale ka digtay khataraha ka dhalan kara haddii shaqaale loo diro hawlo diblumaasiyadeed iyaga oo aan helin diyaarintii iyo tababarkii loo baahnaa. Arrintan ayaa hadda noqotay dood ka dhex taagan hay’adaha dowladda, iyadoo la sugayo natiijada wadahadallada u dhexeeya Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Xafiiska Hantidhowrka Guud ee Qaranka iyo haddii ay kasoo baxaan wax tallaabooyin ama caddeyn dheeraad ah.

items.title: FARMAAJO oo si adag uga hadlay dhacdadii maanta
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynihii hore ee Soomaaliya Maxamed Cabdullaahi Farmaajo ayaa si kulul u cambaareeyay barakicinta iyo burburinta guryaha ka socda degmada Waaberi ee magaalada Muqdisho, isaga oo dowladda ku eedeeyay inay awood ciidan u adeegsatay dad ka cabanayay in laga saarayo dhulkooda. Farmaajo ayaa sheegay in tallaabooyinka maanta ka dhacay Waaberi ay meel ka dhac ku yihiin xuquuqda muwaadiniinta iyo waajibaadka dowladda ka saaran ilaalinta shacabka. “Barakicinta, dhul-boobka iyo adeegsiga awoodda ciidan ee ka dhanka ah bulshada ku dhaqan degmada Waaberi ee magaalada Muqdisho waa fal arxan darro ah oo ka soo horjeeda xuquuqda muwaadiniinta iyo waajibaadka hay’adaha dowladda,” ayuu yiri Farmaajo. Madaxweynihii hore ayaa sidoo kale weerar afka ah ku qaaday Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, oo uu ku tilmaamay “madaxweyne muddo-dhaaf ah”, wuxuuna ku eedeeyay in rasaas iyo xoog loo adeegsaday dad si nabad ah uga cabanayay burburinta hantidooda iyo barakicinta qoysaskooda. “Waa nasiib darro in Madaxweynaha muddo dhaafka ah oo caadeystay barakicinta dadka nugul ee caasimadda uu xabad iyo xoog u adeegsado muwaadiniinta sida nabadda ah u muujinayey cabashadooda,” ayuu yiri. Farmaajo wuxuu sheegay in dowladnimadu ay ku dhisan tahay ilaalinta “nafta, maalka iyo karaamada muwaadinka”, isaga oo ciidamada iyo hay’adaha ammaanka ugu baaqay inay dhowraan sharciga, ilaaliyaan shacabka, kana fogaadaan tallaabo kasta oo dhaawaceysa xuquuqda muwaadiniinta. Hadalka Farmaajo ayaa kusoo aadaya iyadoo muranka la xiriira dhulka iyo barakicinta dadka Muqdisho uu bilihii dambe noqday arrin siyaasadeed oo si weyn looga hadal hayo caasimadda. Boqolaal qoys ayaa sanadkan laga saaray goobo kala duwan oo Muqdisho ah, iyadoo qaar ka mid ah dadka la raray ay sheegeen in guryahooda la dumiyay iyaga oo aan helin digniin ku filan ama meel kale oo loo raro. Arrinta ayaa bishii May dhalisay mudaaharaadyo ay mucaaradku taageereen oo ka dhacay qeybo ka mid ah Muqdisho. Hal qof ayaa ku dhintay, kuwo kalena way ku dhaawacmeen kadib markii ciidamada ammaanka ay rasaas ku fureen dibadbaxayaal ku sugnaa degmada Deyniile, sida ay xilligaas sheegeen booliska iyo qabanqaabiyeyaasha dibadbaxa. Dhanka kale, dowladda federaalka ayaa howlaha dib loogula wareegayo dhulalka Muqdisho hore ugu sheegtay kuwo lagu soo celinayo hanti dowladeed oo muddo ay deggenaayeen dad rayid ah ama ay dad kale gacanta ku hayeen. Wasaaradda Howlaha Guud ayaa bishii May sheegtay in dowladda ay waddo qorshe dib-u-dejin loogu sameynayo ilaa 12,000 oo qoys oo ku nool dhul dowladeed, iyadoo la doonayo in qoysaska nugul loo raro deegaanno cusub. Howlaha dib ula wareegidda dhulka ayaa Muqdisho ka dhaliyay muran xooggan, iyadoo dadka laga raro goobaha qaar ay ka cabanayaan qaabka loo fuliyo, halka dowladda ay ku adkeysaneyso xaqa ay u leedahay inay dib ula wareegto hantida dadweynaha. Dowladda ayaa markii dambe sheegtay in la hakiyey howlaha dadka looga saarayo guryaha iyo dhulalka, balse toddobaadyadii u dambeeyey waxaa soo baxay kiisas muujinaya in howlahaasi mar kale dib u billowdeen. Barakicinta ayaa tan iyo markaas qeyb ka noqotay khilaafka sii xoogeysanaya ee u dhexeeya dowladda iyo mucaaradka, iyadoo hoggaamiyeyaasha mucaaradku dowladda ku eedeeyaan dhul-boob iyo caburin, halka muranka doorashooyinka iyo muddo-xileedka madaxweynaha uu isna sii adkeeyay xaaladda siyaasadeed ee Muqdisho. items.title: Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka oo gaaray Dhuusamareeb (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka ee Xoogga Dalka, General Sahal Cabdullaahi Cumar ayaa laba toddobaad ka dib ku laabtay Magaalada Dhuusamareeb ee Xarunta Dowlad Goboleedka Galmudug. Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka oo 27-kii bishii hore ee July gaaray Dhuusamareeb ayaa 29-kii bishaasi soo geba-gabeeyay booqashadii uu ku joogay Galmudug. Taliyaha ayaa gelinkii dambe ee maanta ka degay Garoonka Diyaaradaha Ugaas Nuur ee Dhuusamareeb, halkaas oo ay ku soo dhaweeyeen Saraakiil uu horkacayay Taliyaha Qaybta 21aad ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, Korneyl Maxamed Cabdi Daahir (Maxamed Dhagaweyne). “Soo dhaweynta ka dib, Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed ayaa kulamo gaar-gaar ah la qaatay saraakiisha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ee ku sugan Magaalada Dhuusamareeb.” Ayaa lagu yiri war caawa ka soo baxay Taliska Militariga. Warka ayaa lagu sheegay “Kulamada ayaa diiradda lagu saaray xaaladda iyo howlaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed ee ka hawlgala deegaanada Galmudug.” Ma cadda ujeedka uu haatan Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka u tegay Galmudug, waxaase socda qorshe tababar loogu soo xirayo ciidamo muddooyinkii u dambeeyay uu tababar uga socday Dugsiga Tababarka Ciidamada ee Xananbuure ee waqooyiga Gobolka Galgaduud. Ciidamadan oo boqolaal gaaraya ayaa lagu wadaa in ay ku biiraan Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ee ka hawlgala Gobolada Galgaduud iyo Mudug. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa waxaa suurtagal ah in uu u safro Dhuusamareeb, si uu tababarka ugu soo xiro ciidamadaasi, oo loo diyaariyay inay gacan ka gaystaan hawlgalka dib u xoreynta dalka.

items.title: Taiwanese residents to stay in contact with the Taiwanese office in Somaliland.
items.description: Taiwan calls on nationals to postpone trips to Uganda The Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday called on Taiwanese travelers to postpone trips to Uganda following a new visa incident at the African country’s main airport. In early August, a Taiwanese resident had his passport confiscated at Entebbe International Airport, while a tourist was turned away after being refused entry. In a new incident Wednesday, a Taiwanese business traveler and his two relatives were told to show Chinese passports in order to have their Taiwanese passports returned, the ministry said in a statement. The three travelers were allowed to enter Uganda, but immigration officials told them the request was part of the country’s “one China policy.” The ministry said its representative office in Somaliland and the association of Taiwanese businesses in Uganda immediately provided assistance to the travelers. Even though the Ugandan government has not announced any changes to its visa policies for Taiwanese visitors, the ministry said travelers should evaluate the risks when planning a trip to the East African country. The ministry also advised Taiwanese residents to stay in contact with the Taiwanese office in Somaliland. Nearly 70 Taiwanese nationals reside in Uganda, while around 35 Taiwanese-invested companies operate in the country and create local jobs, the ministry said. Tourism from Taiwan has also been rising in recent years. The ministry called on the Ugandan government to respect Taiwan’s sovereignty and refrain from imposing unreasonable entry restrictions. Taiwan News

items.title: Jaamac oo guddoomiyey kulan maanta lagu ansixiyay…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Guddoomiyaha cusub ee Golaha Shacabka, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac) ayaamnta shir guddoomiyay kulanka Guddiga Joogtada ah ee Golaha Shacabka BFS, kaasi oo ka dhacay xarunta guddoonka iyo guddiyada ee Villa Hargeysa. Guddoomiye Jaamac oo uu wehliyo guddoomiye ku-xigeenka 2-aad ee Golaha Shacabka, Cabdullaahi Cumar Abshirow ayaa warbixinno ka dhageystay Guddiga Joogtada ah, gaar ahaan shuruucda ay gacanta ku hayaan iyo marxaladaha kala duwan ee ay marayaan. Kulanka ayaa si qoto dheer looga dooday dardar-gelinta howlaha sharci-dejinta iyo sidii loo wajihi lahaa howlaha muhiimka ah ee golaha horyaalla inta lagu guda jiro Kalfadhiga 8-aad. Intaas kaddib, xubnaha Guddiga Joogtada ah ayaa ka arrinsaday oo dejiyey ajandayaasha kulamada guud ee Golaha Shacabka ee toddobaadka soo socda, waxayna si wadajir ah u ansixiyeen ajandayaasha kulamada golaha ee todobaadka soo socda. Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka oo kulanka soo xiray ayaa uga mahadceliyey xubnaha Guddiga Joogtada ah doorkooda wax-ku-oolka ah ee ku aadan dejinta ajandayaasha kulamada golaha ee toddobaadka soo socda iyo dardar-gelinta guud ahaan howlaha muhiimka ah ee Golaha horyaalla Kalfadhiga 8-aad. Guddoomiyuhu wuxuu sidoo kale ku boorriyey Guddiyada Golaha inay sii wadaan shaqada muhiimka ah ee loo igmaday, si loo xaqiijiyo in howlaha sharci-dejinta iyo kormeerka golaha ay u socdaan si hufan oo waafaqsan waajibaadka dastuuriga ah ee Golaha Shacabka. Si kastaba, Jaamac ayaa markii uu la wareegay xilka guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ballan-qaaday inuu golaha ku hoggaamin doono si caddaalad, hufnaan iyo wadajir ku dhisan, isagoo xusay in mudnaanta koowaad la siin doono xoojinta shaqada sharci-dejinta, ilaalinta doorka dastuuriga ah ee golaha iyo ka shaqeynta danta guud. Guddoomiyaha ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in Golaha Shacabka uu si wadajir ah uga shaqeyn doono xaqiijinta yoolalka iyo himilooyinka uu hiigsanayo golaha, isagoo ku boorriyey dhammaan xildhibaannada inay si wadajir ah uga qeyb qaataan gudashada waajibaadka dastuuriga ah ee loo igmaday. items.description: Muqdisho (Raxanreeb Online): Madaxweynihii hore ee Soomaaliya, Maxamed Cabdullaahi Farmaajo, ayaa dhaliilay habka dowladda Federaalka ay u wajahday burburinta hantida iyo barakicinta qoysaska ku nool magaalada Muqdisho. Farmaajo ayaa sheegay inay nasiib-darro tahay in Madaxweynaha uu xoog u adeegsado muwaadiniin si nabad ah u muujinayay cabashadooda ku aaddan burburinta hantidooda iyo barakicinta qoysaskooda. items.title: Omar Artan Makes History as First Non-European Referee to Officiate UEFA Super Cup
items.description: Salzburg, Austria (WDN) — Somali referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan has etched his name into European football history after taking charge of the 2026 UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa at Stadion Salzburg on Wednesday night. The landmark appointment made Artan the first non-European referee to officiate the UEFA Super Cup, placing a Somali official at the center of one of European football’s most prestigious fixtures. The match brought together Paris Saint-Germain, the 2025/26 UEFA Champions League winners, and Aston Villa, the 2025/26 UEFA Europa League champions. PSG ultimately prevailed 2–1 to retain the Super Cup title. For Somalia, however, the significance extended far beyond the final score. A Historic Night for Somalia and Africa Artan’s appointment marked an extraordinary breakthrough for African refereeing. UEFA selected the 34-year-old Somali official following consultations with the Confederation of African Football (CAF), highlighting the growing cooperation between the two continental governing bodies. Artan was joined by two African assistant referees: Liban Abdoulrazack Ahmed of Djibouti and Stephen Eleazar Onyango Yiembe of Kenya. Slovenian referee Rade Obrenovič served as fourth official, while Italy’s Marco Di Bello was the Video Assistant Referee (VAR), with Spain’s Guillermo Cuadra Fernández serving as assistant VAR. The all-African core of the on-field officiating team represented a striking demonstration of how football can transcend geographical boundaries and create opportunities beyond the traditional centers of the sport. From FIFA Setback to European Glory The significance of Artan’s achievement was magnified by what happened only weeks earlier. The Somali referee had been selected for the 2026 FIFA World Cup but was unable to participate after being denied entry to the United States while traveling for the tournament. Reports surrounding the incident cited U.S. authorities’ concerns arising from background screening, including alleged associations with suspected members of terrorist organizations. Those allegations were not independently established, and Artan was ultimately unable to take part in the World Cup. Instead of ending his World Cup dream, however, the setback was followed by one of the most remarkable appointments of his career. UEFA announced in June that Artan would referee the Super Cup, explicitly describing him as one of Africa’s leading referees. UEFA President Aleksander Čeferin said football brings people together and emphasized UEFA’s respect for Artan and his refereeing achievements. The appointment transformed a major disappointment into an extraordinary professional opportunity. Artan has been on the FIFA international refereeing list since 2018 and has steadily established himself among Africa’s most prominent officials. His career reached another major milestone in 2025 when he was named CAF Men’s Referee of the Year, recognition that confirmed his status among the continent’s elite referees. UEFA also noted his experience officiating major CAF competitions, including the 2025/26 CAF Champions League final. His selection for the UEFA Super Cup therefore represents not simply a symbolic gesture but recognition of a referee whose career has reached the highest levels of international football. A Moment of Pride for Somalia Artan’s achievement carries particular significance for Somalia, a country whose name is rarely associated with the biggest stages of European football. For decades, Somalia’s international sporting profile has been overshadowed by political instability, conflict and limited sporting infrastructure. Artan’s rise offers a dramatically different image: a Somali professional trusted to control a match involving two of Europe’s most prominent clubs. His performance in Salzburg was closely followed by Somali supporters at home and across the diaspora. The symbolism was impossible to miss. A Somali referee stood at the center of a European final, surrounded by some of the world’s most famous players and watched by millions of football fans. The match itself produced an entertaining contest. PSG took the lead through Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, before Aston Villa equalized through 17-year-old Brian Madjo, who became the youngest scorer in UEFA Super Cup history. PSG eventually regained the lead through Désiré Doué, whose goal was confirmed following a VAR review. PSG’s 2–1 victory made the French champions back-to-back UEFA Super Cup winners, joining an exclusive group of clubs to achieve consecutive victories in the competition. Yet for many Somali viewers, the most memorable figure of the night was not wearing either club’s shirt. He was wearing the referee’s uniform. Beyond One Match Artan’s achievement represents more than an individual career milestone. It demonstrates the possibilities that can emerge when African sporting institutions and European football authorities cooperate to create pathways for talent from outside the traditional football power centers. His appointment was made possible through the growing cooperation between UEFA and CAF, and it could help establish a precedent for greater African representation in major European competitions. For young Somali athletes and officials, the message is equally powerful: the highest levels of international sport are not necessarily beyond reach. Artan’s journey—from FIFA World Cup selection, through a deeply controversial setback, to the center of the UEFA Super Cup—has become an extraordinary story of resilience. On Wednesday night in Salzburg, Omar Abdulkadir Artan did not merely officiate a football match. He made history. And in doing so, he gave Somalia a rare and powerful moment of sporting pride on one of the world’s biggest stages. items.title: Guddiga Xuquuqul Insaanka iyo UNDP oo ka wada hadlay xoojinta iskaashiga
items.description: Guddoomiyaha Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaranka (GMXIQ), Dr. Maryan Qasim, ayaa maanta Muqdisho kulan kula qaadatay Wakiilka cusub ee UNDP Soomaaliya, Christophoros Politis, kaas oo diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta iskaashiga u dhexeeya Guddiga iyo Hay’adda Qaramada Midoobay ee Horumarinta (UNDP). Kulanka ayaa si gaar ah loogu hadlay sidii loo kobcin lahaa awoodda Guddiga, loona xoojin lahaa dadaallada lagu ilaalinayo laguna horumarinayo xuquuqul insaanka Soomaaliya. Labada dhinac ayaa sidoo kale ka wada hadlay muhiimadda ay leedahay isku-duwidda iyo wada-shaqeynta hay’adaha kala duwan ee ka shaqeeya ilaalinta xuquuqda aadanaha, iyo sidii loo abuuri lahaa barnaamijyo wadajir ah oo bulshada Soomaaliyeed wax looga qabanayo. Kulanka waxaa ka qaybgalay Agaasimaha Guud ee Guddiga, Mustafa Axmed Maxamuud, iyo Madaxa Barnaamijyada Dowlad-wanaagga UNDP, Evariste Sibomana. Kulankan ayaa qayb ka ah dadaallada Guddiga Madaxa-bannaan ee Xuquuqul Insaanka Qaranka uu ku xoojinayo hawlihiisa, iskaashiga uu la leeyahay hay’adaha caalamiga ah iyo gudashada waajibaadkiisa qaran ee la xiriira ilaalinta iyo horumarinta xuquuqul insaanka dalka.

items.title: Xilliga la shaacinayo Natiijada Imtixaanka Dugsiga Sare ee Qaranka oo lagu dhawaaqay
items.description: Muqdisho, 13 Agoosto 2026 — Natiijada Imtixaanka Shahaadiga ah ee Dugsiga Sare ee Qaranka ayaa la filayaa in la shaaciyo Sabtida, 15-ka Agoosto 2026, iyadoo kumannaan arday iyo waalidiin ah ay si weyn u sugayaan natiijada imtixaanka. Shaacinta natiijada ayaa noqon doonta marxalad muhiim ah oo soo afjareysa sugitaanka ardayda sanadkan u fariisatay Imtixaanka Qaranka ee Dugsiga Sare, kuwaas oo natiijadoodu go’aamin doonto in ay u gudbaan heerka jaamacadaha iyo waxbarashada sare. Wasaaradda Waxbarashada, Hiddaha iyo Tacliinta Sare ayaa mas’uul ka ah qiimeynta iyo imtixaanaadka shahaadiga ah ee dugsiyada dalka, iyadoo sharciga waxbarashada uu dhigayo in ardayda dhammeysa dugsiga sare ay u fariistaan imtixaanka shahaadiga ah ee dowladda. Ardayda, waalidiinta iyo macallimiinta ayaa si gaar ah isha ugu haya natiijada, iyadoo ay jiri doonto farxad iyo dabaaldegyo ay sameeyaan ardayda ku guuleysata dhibcaha sare, halka kuwa aan natiijada ay filayeen helin ay heli doonaan fursad ay dib ugu qiimeeyaan tallaabada xigta ee waxbarashadooda. Sidoo kale, natiijada sanadkan ayaa la filayaa inay muujiso heerka waxqabadka ardayda iyo guud ahaan xaaladda waxbarashada dugsiyada sare ee dalka. Sabtida, 15-ka Agoosto 2026, ayaa sidaas darteed noqon doonta maalin ay si weyn u sugayaan ardayda iyo qoysaskooda.

items.description: Puntland (Raxanreeb Online): Sida ay SBC ku heshay xog, waxaa heshiis hordhac ah laga gaaray khilaaf ciidan oo u dhexeeyay ciidamada Puntland iyo ciidamo ka amar qaata Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, kuwaas oo dhowr maalmood isku horfadhiyay deegaanka Kur-ilaalo ee degmada Rako-raaxo, gobolka Karkaar.
