items.title: Cumar Cartan oo bog cusub ku qoray magaca Soomaaliya
items.description: Salzburg (Caasimada Online) – Garsooraha Soomaaliyeed Cumar Cabdulqaadir Cartan ayaa waxaa uu noqday garsoorihii ugu horeeyay oo aan Yurubiyaan ahayn ee dhex-dhexaadiya koobka UEFA SUPER CUP, oo ay xalay wada dheeleen Kooxda Paris Saint-Germain F.C. (PSG) iyo Aston Villa. Cartan wuxuu dhigay taariikh cusub oo baal-dabah ah ka gashay xiriirka kubadda Cagta Adduunka, isagoo noqday Garsoorihii ugu horeeyay abid ee loo doortay inuu dhex-dhexaadiyo kulan heer sare ah oo kubadda cagta Yurub ah, wuxuuna magaca Soomaaliya ku qoray bog cusub oo taariikhi ah. Guusha uu xalay gaaray Cumar Cartan kaliya kuma eka tan shaqsiga ah, ee waxa uu calanka Soomaaliya ka lulay masraxyada ugu waaweyn, uguna xiisaha badan dunida kubadda cagta, iyadoo garoonka ay ku cayaarayeen Kooxaha PSG iyo Aston Villa u soo daawasha tageen kumanaan Soomaali ah, markii lasoo gato shucuubtii kale ee dunida, si ay u taageeraan Garsoore Cumar Cartan, una lulaan calamka Jamhuuriyadda. Sidoo kale, dunida Kubadda Cagta ayaa ugu hambalyeysay Garsoore Cumar Cartan sida miisaanka leh ee uu u garsooray ciyaarta weyn ee koobka UEFA SUPER CUP, waxaana ka mid ahaa: Xiriirka Kubadda Cagta Adduunka UEFA oo qoray “Cumar Cartan waxa uu noqday garsoorihii ugu horeeyay ee aan Qaaradda Yurub kasoo jeedin ee Garsoore ka noqda Finalka UEFA SUPER CUP,” magaca Soomaaliya iyo Afrika oo dhan ayuuna ku qoray bogga Taariikhiga ah ee Kubadda Cagta. Dhanka kale, halyeygii hore ee xulka Talyaaniga iyo kooxda Juventus Gianluigi Buffon ayaa ugu hambalyeeyay sida quruxda badan ee Garoore Cumar Cartan u dhex-dhexaadiyay Koobka UEFA SUPER CUP ee ay xalay ku guuleysatay Kooxda reer France ee PSG, isagoo yiri ”Garsooraha Soomaaliyeed Cumar Cartan xalay Kubadda Cagtu waxay siisay mudnaantii uu lahaa.” Xiriirka Kubadda Cagta Afrika ee CAF ayaa isna hambalyo u diray Cumar Cabdulqaadir Cartan guusha taariikhiga ah ee uu xalay ka sameeyay Masraxyada Kubadda Cagta Adduunka iyo sida uu uga soo dhalaalay ciyaartii weyneed ee UEFA SUPER CUP. “Garsoore Cumar Cartan wuxuu Afrika ku metelay Masraxa Kubadda Cagta Adduunka, waana Garsoorihii ugu horeeyay ee Soomaaliyeed ee taariikh ka dhigay Koobka UEFA SUPER CUP, isagoo noqday garsoorihii ugu horeeyay ee Qaaradda Yurub aan kasoo jeedin ee qabta kulankan oo kale, Soomaaliya iyo Afrika ayuuna sharaf ku metelay, guul wayn oo xasuus mudan ayuu Cartan dhigay,” ayaa lagu qoraalka Xiriirka Kubadda Cagta Afrika ee CAF. Cumar Cabduqaadir Cartan oo 34 jir ah ayaa ku jira liiska Garsoorayaasha caalamiga ah ee FIFA tan iyo sannadkii 2018. Sannadkii 2025-ka ayaa loo magacaabay Garsooraha ugu fiican Afrika, isaga oo noqday mid ka mid ah garsoorayaasha ugu sarreeya qaaradda Afrika iyo guud ahaan caalamka, waxaana sidoo kale muddadii uu ku jiray garsoorka uu dhex-dhexaadiyay kulamo badan oo heer caalami ah. Si kastaba, Guusha Cumar Cartan ayaa si gaar ah muhiim u noqotay marka la xuso dhacdadii dhowaan ka horreysay ee uu ku waayay fursaddii uu kaga qeyb geli lahaa Koobka Adduunka 2026, kaddib markii Mareykanka uu u diiday inuu dalka galo, inkastoo uu haystay fiiso sax ah. Mas’uuliyiinta Mareykanka ayaa xilligaas ku sababeeyay go’aanka walaac la xiriiray xaqiijinta xogtiisa, halka FIFA ay markii dambe xaqiijisay inuusan ka qeyb geli karin tartanka. items.title: Duqeymaha Mareykanka ee Yemen oo sababay dhimashada 153 qof
items.description: Qiimeyn ay samaysay Wasaaradda Difaaca Mareykanka ayaa lagu sheegay in duqeymo ay ciidamada Mareykanku ka fuliyeen Yemen sannadkii 2025 ay sababeen dhimashada 153 qof oo rayid ah, halka 243 qof oo kale ay ku dhaawacmeen. Warbixinta Pentagon-ka oo aan sir ahayn ayaa muujinaysa in dhammaan khasaaraha rayidka ah ee ay ciidamada Mareykanku diiwaangeliyeen sannadkaas uu ka dhashay saddex weerar oo dhacay bishii Abriil 2025. Saddexda duqeymood ayaa lagu bartilmaameedsaday goobo ay ku sugnaayeen ciidamada Xuutiyiinta iyo deegaanada ku dhow caasimadda Sanca, iyo sidoo kale dekedda shidaalka ee Ras Ciise ee gobolka Xudeyda. Weerarkii ugu khasaaraha badnaa wuxuu ka dhacay dekedda Ras Ciise, halkaas oo sida qiimeynta Pentagon-ka lagu sheegay ay ku dhinteen 80 qof, halka 171 kalena ay ku dhaawacmeen. Ciidamada Mareykanka ayaa xilligaas sheegay in weerarka Ras Ciise uu ahaa mid lagu jarayay il shidaal iyo dhaqaale oo ay Xuutiyiintu ka heli jireen dekedda, ayadoo Taliska Dhexe ee Mareykanka (CENTCOM) uu sidoo kale sheegay in ujeeddadu aysan ahayn waxyeellada shacabka Yemen. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, qiimeyntii Pentagon-ka ayaa markii dambe lagu ogaaday in saddexda weerar ay u badan tahay inay sababeen waxyeello loo geystay rayid, iyadoo qiimeynta lagu saleeyay xog sirdoon, sawirro iyo warbixinno laga helay ilo furan. Tirada khasaaraha ayaa si weyn uga badan tii sanadkii 2024, markaas oo Pentagon-ku qiimeeyay in hawlgallada ciidamada Mareykanka ay Yemen ka fuliyeen ay dileen laba qof oo rayid ah, halka laba kalena ay dhaawacmeen. Pentagon-ku wuxuu sidoo kale sheegay in aan la bixin magdhowga tacsiyeed ee loo yaqaan condolence payments dadka ku dhintay ama qoysaskooda, inkastoo warbixintu aysan si faahfaahsan u sharxin sababta go’aankaas. Dhanka kale, khasaaraha rayidka ah ee ka dhashay duqeymaha Mareykanka ee Yemen ayaa laga yaabaa inuu kordho, iyadoo CENTCOM ay ilaa Febraayo 2026 dib u eegis ku waday 15 dhacdo oo kale oo hay’adaha aan dowliga ahayn ay ku soo warrameen inay ahayd khasaaro rayid. Duqeymaha Mareykanka ee Yemen waxay billowdeen xilligii madaxweyne Joe Biden, kaddib markii Xuutiyiintu bilaabeen weerarro gantaallo iyo diyaarado aan duuliye lahayn ah oo lagu qaaday maraakiib ganacsi oo mara Badda Cas. Qiimeyntan cusub ee Pentagon-ka ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli si weyn loo eegayo saameynta rayidka ee hawlgallada milatari ee Mareykanka, gaar ahaan siyaasadda maamulka madaxweyne Donald Trump ee ku aaddan weerarrada dibadda.

Pentagon-ku wuxuu sidoo kale sheegay in aan la bixin magdhowga tacsiyeed ee loo yaqaan condolence payments dadka ku dhintay ama qoysaskooda, inkastoo warbixintu aysan si faahfaahsan u sharxin sababta go’aankaas. Dhanka kale, khasaaraha rayidka ah ee ka dhashay duqeymaha Mareykanka ee Yemen ayaa laga yaabaa inuu kordho, iyadoo CENTCOM ay ilaa Febraayo 2026 dib u eegis ku waday 15 dhacdo oo kale oo hay’adaha aan dowliga ahayn ay ku soo warrameen inay ahayd khasaaro rayid. Duqeymaha Mareykanka ee Yemen waxay billowdeen xilligii madaxweyne Joe Biden, kaddib markii Xuutiyiintu bilaabeen weerarro gantaallo iyo diyaarado aan duuliye lahayn ah oo lagu qaaday maraakiib ganacsi oo mara Badda Cas. Qiimeyntan cusub ee Pentagon-ka ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli si weyn loo eegayo saameynta rayidka ee hawlgallada milatari ee Mareykanka, gaar ahaan siyaasadda maamulka madaxweyne Donald Trump ee ku aaddan weerarrada dibadda.

items.title: Faahfaahinno dheeraad ah oo ka soo baxaya Howlgal ka dhacay degmada Maxaas ee Gobolka Hiiraan
items.description: Ciidanka Hay’adda Sirdoonka iyo Nabadsugidda Qaranka (NISA), oo taageero ka helaya saaxiibada caalamka, ayaa xalay howlgal ka fuliyay degmada Maxaas ee Gobolka Hiiraan, sida lagu sheegay war ay soo saartay NISA. Howlgalka ayaa lagu bartilmaameedsaday guri la sheegay in ay ku sugnaayeen xubno sare oo ka tirsan kooxda Al-Shabaab, kuwaas oo sida ay NISA sheegtay muddooyinkii u dambeeyay ka waday deegaannada gobolka qorsheyn iyo abaabul la xiriira dagaallo. Wararka kasoo baxay hay’adda ayaa sheegaya in howlgalka lagu gaarsiiyay kooxda khasaaro xooggan, iyadoo bartilmaameedku ahaa xubno muhiim u ahaa hoggaanka iyo isku-dubbaridka howlgallada kooxda ee gobolka. Howlgalka ayaa qeyb ka ah howlgallo sirdoon oo ciidamada ammaanka Soomaaliya ay ka wadaan qaybo ka mid ah dalka, gaar ahaan deegaannada Bartamaha iyo Koonfurta dalka. NISA ayaa bilihii u dambeeyay dhowr jeer sheegtay in howlgallo noocan ah lagu bartilmaameedsaday xubno sare iyo xarumo ay kooxda ku lahayd Gobolka Hiiraan iyo meelo kale.

items.title: Qorrax-madoobaad buuxa oo Yurub qaybo ka mid ah mugdi geliyay
items.description: Malaayiin qof ayaa Arbacadii u soo baxay inay daawadaan dhacdo naadir ah oo cirka ah, kaddib markii qorrax-madoobaad buuxa uu daboolay qaybo ka mid ah Yurub, maalintiina isu beddeshay mugdi. Qorrax-madoobaadkan ayaa ahaa kii ugu horreeyay ee noociisa ah ee laga arko qaaradda Yurub tan iyo 1999-kii, iyadoo madoobaadku uu ka soo gudbay dhulka Arctic-ga, Greenland iyo Iceland, ka hor inta uusan gaarin waqooyiga Spain iyo qayb yar oo waqooyi-bari boortaqiiska ah. Markii dayaxu uu si buuxda u hor istaagay qorraxda, meelaha ku jiray jidka madoobaadka waxaa muddo ku dhow laba daqiiqo ka dhacay mugdi aan caadi ahayn, waxaana cirka ka muuqday hareeraha iftiinka qorraxda ee loo yaqaan corona. Qorrax-madoobaadka qayb ahaan ah ayaa isna laga arkay qaybo badan oo Yurub ah iyo meelo ka tirsan Waqooyiga Afrika iyo Waqooyiga Ameerika. Spain ayaa ka mid ahayd meelihii ugu muhiimsanaa ee lagu daawaday dhacdadan, ayadoo kumannaan dad ah ay isugu soo baxeen goobo kala duwan, halka qaar badan ay safarro gaar ah ku tageen dhulka uu maro jidka madoobaadka buuxa. Wararka laga helayo Spain ayaa sheegay in dadku ay si weyn ugu riyaaqeen markii cirka uu mugdi galay, waxaana loo arkayay dhacdo taariikhi ah oo dhif iyo naadir ah. Dhanka Iceland, dad badan ayaa iyaguna sugayay qorrax-madoobaadka, inkastoo xaaladaha cimiladu meelaha qaar ay adkeeyeen in si cad loo daawado. Qaybo ka mid ah dalka ayaa helay fursad wanaagsan oo lagu arko dhacdada, halka daruuruhu ay meelaha kale daboolayeen muuqaalka. Qorrax-madoobaadku wuxuu sidoo kale soo jiitay indhaha khubarada cilmiga xiddigiska, sawir-qaadayaasha iyo dalxiisayaasha, kuwaas oo fursad u helay inay diiwaangeliyaan mid ka mid ah dhacdooyinka cirka ee ugu cajiibsan sannadka 2026. Dhacdadan ayaa xusuus gaar ah ku yeelatay dadka ku nool Yurub, maadaama qorrax-madoobaad buuxa oo qaaradda laga arko uu yahay dhacdo aan si joogto ah u dhicin. Si kastaba ha ahaatee qorrax-madoobaadka 12-ka Agoosto 2026 wuxuu noqday muuqaal dabiici ah oo malaayiin qof ay si toos ah ama sawirro iyo muuqaallo uga daawadeen, iyadoo qaybo ka mid ah Yurub ay muddo kooban la kulmeen mugdi ku dhacay bartamaha maalinta.

items.title: As the Iran-backed Houthis step up their threat to Red Sea shipping, analysts say the U.S. could consider a major change in strategy.
items.description: JOHANNESBURG: As the Iran-backed Houthis step up their threat to Red Sea shipping, analysts say the U.S. could consider a major change in strategy. Houthi attacks on ships passing through a vital chokepoint may lead Washington to cement relations with more reliable partners along Africa ’s coastline. Somaliland is a pro-U.S. outpost, having broken away from war-torn Somalia in 1991, and is offering the U.S. the use of one of the longest runways in Africa, an air base and a deep sea port on the Red Sea. IRAN AND HOUTHI TERROR PROXY FACING RED SEA THREAT FROM PRO-US AFRICAN NATION An aerial view of The Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a sea route connecting the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea via the Suez Canal. (Gallo Images/Orbital Horizon/Copernicus Sentinel Data 2021) The Houthis have vowed to close the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait, a narrow waterway through which Saudi Arabia exports up to 7 million barrels of oil a day, now that access to the Strait of Hormuz is severely restricted. In the past month in the Red Sea, the Houthis have reportedly attacked Saudi-flagged ships, are said to have sunk an Indian commercial cargo vessel and, on Aug. 13, an Egyptian cargo ship was hit, with at least four of its crew killed. The U.S. already has a large military base on the Red Sea in Djibouti, but this is claimed to be increasingly problematic. “China is significantly expanding its military and commercial presence in Djibouti, ” Edmund Fitton-Brown previously told Fox News Digital. Fitton-Brown, the former British ambassador to the Houthis’ home country, Yemen, and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, (FDD), added, “There is a sense that Djibouti is not a reliable ally for the U.S. So Somaliland’s time has probably come.”Major General Ken Ekman, who retired last year from being the Department of War’s West Africa Coordination Element Lead, said, in essence, the Houthis could force the U.S. into recognizing Somaliland as an independent state. “The Houthis could compel a different U.S. strategy in Africa.” Fox News

items.title: Strategic shift:  Could Somaliland be the key to U.S. strategy in the Horn of Africa?
items.description: As Iran-backed Houthi attacks disrupt Red Sea shipping and traditional allies like Djibouti align closer with China, experts argue Washington needs a strategic pivot. Speaking to Fox News Digital, Bashir Goth, Somaliland Representative to the U.S., highlighted Somaliland’s potential role as a key regional partner: “Somaliland is that partner and our defense officials have been in active dialogue with AFRICOM on Red Sea security. Somaliland has the geography, the stability and the will to work closely with Washington — and will continue to do so.” Fox news

items.title: Somaliland iyo Israel oo yeeshay wada-hadallo cusub
items.description: Dubai (Caasimada Online) – Safiirka Israa’iil u fadhiya Imaaraadka Carabta, Yossi Shelley iyo Wakiilka Somaliland ee Imaaraadka, Mascuud Cabdi Cali ayaa yeeshay kulan ay uga wada-hadleen fursadaha ka abuurmay xiriirka cusub ee u dhexeeya maamulka Somaliland iyo Israa’iil. Shelley ayaa qoraal uu ku baahiyay barta X ku sheegay in kulanka lagu gorfeeyay xoojinta iskaashiga dhaqaale iyo sidii loo horumarin lahaa xiriirka labada dhinac, kaddib markii Israa’iil ay noqotay waddankii ugu horreeyay ee si rasmi ah u aqoonsada maamulka Somaliland inuu yahay dal madax-bannaan. Safiirka ayaa sheegay in wakiilka Somaliland uu si weyn u soo dhaweeyay go’aanka Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Israa’iil Benjamin Netanyahu ee aqoonsiga Somaliland. Wuxuu tallaabadaasi ku tilmaamay mid geesinimo leh oo muhiim u ah dadaalka Somaliland ee raadinta aqoonsi caalami ah. Shelley ayaa sidoo kale shaaciyay in Mascuud Cabdi Cali uu u fidiyay martiqaad uu ku booqdo Somaliland. Safiirka ayaa xusay rajadiisa in dalal kale ay ku daydaan tallaabada ay Israa’iil qaaday, ayna Somaliland aqoonsadaan, inkastoo Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ay si adag uga hortagayso in dalal kale ku dhiiraadaan tallaabada Tel Aviv oo kale. “Waxaan rajeynayaa in aan dhisno iskaashi xooggan oo aan ku horumarino xasilloonida gobolka,” ayuu yiri Yossi Shelley. Kulanka ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli maamulka Somaliland uu waddo dadaallo diblomaasiyadeed oo uu doonayo inuu ku helo aqoonsi caalami ah, iyadoo xiriirro cusub la sameysanaysa dalal iyo dhinacyo kala duwan oo caalami ah. Si kastaba, Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa si adag uga soo horjeedda aqoonsiga Somaliland, waxayna waddaa dadaallo diblomaasiyadeed oo looga hortagayo in dalal kale ay raacaan tallaabada Israa’iil, iyadoo Muqdisho ku adkaysanayso midnimada iyo madax-bannaanida dhuleed ee Soomaaliya. The post Somaliland iyo Israel oo yeeshay wada-hadallo cusub appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Ethiopia’s Tigray Crisis Could Reshape Somalia’s Security Landscape as Regional Fault Lines Deepen
items.description: By Abdikarim H. Abdi Buh A dangerous new chapter may be opening in the Horn of Africa. Renewed tensions between Ethiopia’s federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) are raising fears of another major conflict in northern Ethiopia—one that could extend far beyond Tigray and potentially reshape the security architecture of neighboring Somalia. For Somalia, the question is particularly consequential: what happens if Ethiopia suddenly needs thousands of troops that are currently deployed across the border? That possibility is no longer merely an abstract strategic concern. Tensions between Addis Ababa and the TPLF have intensified following the TPLF’s return to political dominance in Tigray and the weakening of the transitional administration supported by the federal government. The developments have further strained the fragile political understanding created by the 2022 Pretoria peace agreement, which ended two years of devastating war. New clashes in western Tigray have added to concerns that the peace agreement is under its most serious pressure since it was signed. A return to full-scale war would be disastrous for Ethiopia. But its consequences could also be felt across the wider region—including in Somalia, where Ethiopian troops remain a critical component of the country’s security architecture. The Somalia Question Ethiopia has maintained a substantial military presence in Somalia for years, including forces operating along the two countries’ border and troops participating in the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia, AUSSOM. Those forces have become an important part of the regional security equation. Somalia remains heavily dependent on international security assistance while its own security forces continue the difficult process of assuming responsibility for national security. AUSSOM remains a key component of that transition. This creates an uncomfortable strategic reality. If fighting in Tigray escalates to the point where Addis Ababa requires additional troops at home, Ethiopian commanders may face difficult choices about force deployments outside the country. Some Ethiopian troops currently serving in Somalia could potentially be reassigned to domestic priorities. There is, however, no confirmed evidence that Ethiopia has decided to withdraw its forces from Somalia because of the Tigray crisis. Any large-scale redeployment should therefore be treated as a potential scenario rather than an established policy. But in geopolitics, possibilities can be consequential long before they become official decisions. A reduction in Ethiopian forces could create additional pressure on Somalia’s already fragile security transition—particularly at a time when the future financing and international support structure surrounding AUSSOM remains uncertain. A Regional Crisis Waiting to Connect The Tigray crisis cannot be viewed in isolation. One of the most worrying dimensions is the rapidly deteriorating relationship between Ethiopia and Eritrea. The two countries were once close military partners during the 2020–2022 Tigray war, when Eritrean forces fought alongside Ethiopian federal forces against the TPLF. That alliance has since collapsed. Relations between Addis Ababa and Asmara have deteriorated sharply, with disputes involving Eritrean troops in Ethiopian territory, border questions, and Ethiopia’s increasingly explicit interest in securing reliable access to the Red Sea. For Eritrea, Ethiopia’s ambitions on the Red Sea are not simply an economic question. They touch directly on sovereignty and national security. Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea became independent, making reliable access to a Red Sea port strategically important to Addis Ababa. Asmara, meanwhile, has every reason to be wary of an increasingly powerful neighbor seeking a permanent maritime foothold. That makes the Tigray crisis particularly dangerous. A confrontation between Addis Ababa and the TPLF could create opportunities for Eritrea to exert pressure on Ethiopia indirectly—or potentially become involved more directly if its security interests are threatened. The result could be a regional equation in which former enemies become temporary partners because their interests happen to converge. The Enemy of My Enemy? The irony is striking. Eritrea and the TPLF spent decades as bitter enemies. Their confrontation culminated in the devastating 1998–2000 Ethiopia-Eritrea war and later the Tigray conflict. Yet today’s geopolitical landscape is radically different. The principal strategic relationship is no longer simply Eritrea versus TPLF. It is increasingly Eritrea versus an Ethiopian government whose regional ambitions have become a source of concern in Asmara. That distinction matters. TPLF’s political and military resurgence, combined with worsening Ethiopia-Eritrea relations, could create an unexpected convergence of interests—even if no formal alliance exists between the parties. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has repeatedly warned about external and internal forces seeking to destabilize his government, with Tigray and Eritrea featuring prominently in the government’s security calculations. Meanwhile, reports and assessments have pointed to renewed military mobilization inside Tigray, adding to fears that the Pretoria agreement could be approaching a critical breaking point. Sudan Adds Another Layer of Danger Then there is Sudan. The Horn of Africa’s security crises increasingly overlap. Tigray, Eritrea and Sudan sit within a strategic triangle connecting the Nile Basin, the Red Sea and the wider Horn of Africa. A renewed Ethiopian conflict could therefore interact with Sudan’s devastating civil war and produce consequences that are difficult to contain. A new war in Tigray could generate additional displacement, disrupt cross-border trade, increase arms flows and create new opportunities for armed groups operating across porous borders. What begins as an Ethiopian domestic conflict could rapidly acquire regional characteristics. That is precisely what makes the current situation so alarming. For Somalia, the first and most immediate concern would be security. If Ethiopia were forced to move substantial numbers of troops from Somalia back toward Tigray or other vulnerable areas, Somalia could face a reduction in one of the most significant external military contingents supporting its security environment. That would happen at a particularly difficult moment. Somalia is still confronting Al-Shabaab, while its security institutions remain heavily dependent on international assistance, training, intelligence and logistical support. A sudden reduction in Ethiopian forces could therefore create security gaps in areas where Somali forces are not yet capable of independently replacing them. It could also complicate AUSSOM’s broader transition strategy. The mission is already operating in an environment where questions about financing, troop contributions and long-term international support remain unresolved. A major Ethiopian redeployment would add another layer of uncertainty. The Bigger Horn of Africa Picture The implications extend beyond troop numbers. Ethiopia is one of the most powerful states in the Horn of Africa. Eritrea controls a strategically important stretch of Red Sea coastline. Sudan is engulfed in a devastating civil war. Somalia sits beside the Gulf of Aden and the Bab el-Mandeb, one of the world’s most important maritime corridors. Together, these countries form a geopolitical chain linking East Africa, the Red Sea, the Arabian Peninsula and the Indian Ocean. A major conflict in one part of that chain rarely remains isolated for long. For Somalia, the danger is particularly acute because the country is still rebuilding its security institutions while simultaneously confronting a persistent insurgency. The last thing Mogadishu needs is a sudden deterioration in the regional security environment or a significant reduction in the foreign forces currently helping to contain militant threats. No War Yet—but the Warning Signs Are Growing. It would be premature to declare that Ethiopia is heading inevitably toward another full-scale Tigray war. The federal government retains substantial military capabilities, and political and diplomatic mechanisms remain available to prevent further escalation. But the warning signs are difficult to ignore. The Pretoria agreement was supposed to close the chapter on Ethiopia’s devastating internal war. Instead, the region is now watching to see whether its fragile peace can survive a new generation of political and military confrontation. For Somalia, the stakes could hardly be higher. If war returns to Tigray, Somalia may discover that a conflict hundreds of kilometers away can suddenly become a crisis on its own doorstep. And in the Horn of Africa, that distance can disappear remarkably quickly. Abdikarim H. items.fullContent: By Abdikarim H. Abdi Buh A dangerous new chapter may be opening in the Horn of Africa. Renewed tensions between Ethiopia’s federal government and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) are raising fears of another major conflict in northern Ethiopia—one that could extend far beyond Tigray and potentially reshape the security architecture of neighboring Somalia. For Somalia, the question is particularly consequential: what happens if Ethiopia suddenly needs thousands of troops that are currently deployed across the border? That possibility is no longer merely an abstract strategic concern. Tensions between Addis Ababa and the TPLF have intensified following the TPLF’s return to political dominance in Tigray and the weakening of the transitional administration supported by the federal government. The developments have further strained the fragile political understanding created by the 2022 Pretoria peace agreement, which ended two years of devastating war. New clashes in western Tigray have added to concerns that the peace agreement is under its most serious pressure since it was signed. A return to full-scale war would be disastrous for Ethiopia. But its consequences could also be felt across the wider region—including in Somalia, where Ethiopian troops remain a critical component of the country’s security architecture. The Somalia Question Ethiopia has maintained a substantial military presence in Somalia for years, including forces operating along the two countries’ border and troops participating in the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia, AUSSOM. Those forces have become an important part of the regional security equation. Somalia remains heavily dependent on international security assistance while its own security forces continue the difficult process of assuming responsibility for national security. AUSSOM remains a key component of that transition. This creates an uncomfortable strategic reality. If fighting in Tigray escalates to the point where Addis Ababa requires additional troops at home, Ethiopian commanders may face difficult choices about force deployments outside the country. Some Ethiopian troops currently serving in Somalia could potentially be reassigned to domestic priorities. There is, however, no confirmed evidence that Ethiopia has decided to withdraw its forces from Somalia because of the Tigray crisis. Any large-scale redeployment should therefore be treated as a potential scenario rather than an established policy. But in geopolitics, possibilities can be consequential long before they become official decisions. A reduction in Ethiopian forces could create additional pressure on Somalia’s already fragile security transition—particularly at a time when the future financing and international support structure surrounding AUSSOM remains uncertain. A Regional Crisis Waiting to Connect The Tigray crisis cannot be viewed in isolation. One of the most worrying dimensions is the rapidly deteriorating relationship between Ethiopia and Eritrea. The two countries were once close military partners during the 2020–2022 Tigray war, when Eritrean forces fought alongside Ethiopian federal forces against the TPLF. That alliance has since collapsed. Relations between Addis Ababa and Asmara have deteriorated sharply, with disputes involving Eritrean troops in Ethiopian territory, border questions, and Ethiopia’s increasingly explicit interest in securing reliable access to the Red Sea. For Eritrea, Ethiopia’s ambitions on the Red Sea are not simply an economic question. They touch directly on sovereignty and national security. Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea became independent, making reliable access to a Red Sea port strategically important to Addis Ababa. Asmara, meanwhile, has every reason to be wary of an increasingly powerful neighbor seeking a permanent maritime foothold. That makes the Tigray crisis particularly dangerous. A confrontation between Addis Ababa and the TPLF could create opportunities for Eritrea to exert pressure on Ethiopia indirectly—or potentially become involved more directly if its security interests are threatened. The result could be a regional equation in which former enemies become temporary partners because their interests happen to converge. The Enemy of My Enemy? The irony is striking. Eritrea and the TPLF spent decades as bitter enemies. Their confrontation culminated in the devastating 1998–2000 Ethiopia-Eritrea war and later the Tigray conflict. Yet today’s geopolitical landscape is radically different. The principal strategic relationship is no longer simply Eritrea versus TPLF. It is increasingly Eritrea versus an Ethiopian government whose regional ambitions have become a source of concern in Asmara. That distinction matters. TPLF’s political and military resurgence, combined with worsening Ethiopia-Eritrea relations, could create an unexpected convergence of interests—even if no formal alliance exists between the parties. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has repeatedly warned about external and internal forces seeking to destabilize his government, with Tigray and Eritrea featuring prominently in the government’s security calculations. Meanwhile, reports and assessments have pointed to renewed military mobilization inside Tigray, adding to fears that the Pretoria agreement could be approaching a critical breaking point. Sudan Adds Another Layer of Danger Then there is Sudan. The Horn of Africa’s security crises increasingly overlap. Tigray, Eritrea and Sudan sit within a strategic triangle connecting the Nile Basin, the Red Sea and the wider Horn of Africa. A renewed Ethiopian conflict could therefore interact with Sudan’s devastating civil war and produce consequences that are difficult to contain. A new war in Tigray could generate additional displacement, disrupt cross-border trade, increase arms flows and create new opportunities for armed groups operating across porous borders. What begins as an Ethiopian domestic conflict could rapidly acquire regional characteristics. That is precisely what makes the current situation so alarming. For Somalia, the first and most immediate concern would be security. That would happen at a particularly difficult moment. It could also complicate AUSSOM’s broader transition strategy. The mission is already operating in an environment where questions about financing, troop contributions and long-term international support remain unresolved. A major Ethiopian redeployment would add another layer of uncertainty. The Bigger Horn of Africa Picture The implications extend beyond troop numbers. Ethiopia is one of the most powerful states in the Horn of Africa. Eritrea controls a strategically important stretch of Red Sea coastline. Sudan is engulfed in a devastating civil war. Somalia sits beside the Gulf of Aden and the Bab el-Mandeb, one of the world’s most important maritime corridors. Together, these countries form a geopolitical chain linking East Africa, the Red Sea, the Arabian Peninsula and the Indian Ocean. A major conflict in one part of that chain rarely remains isolated for long. items.title: Xasan oo weeraray mucaaradka, kuna tilmaamay hoggaamiye kooxeed
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa si weyn u weeraray siyaasiyiinta mucaaradka oo ayagu kasoo horjeeda hanaanka doorasho ee dowladda wado. Madaxweynaha ayaa sheegay in Soomaaliya ay u baahan tahay nidaam qeexaya cidda dalka mas’uulka ka ah iyo habka go’aannada loo gaarayo, isagoo muujiyay aragtidiisa in la dhiso nidaam siyaasadeed oo cad iyo hay’ado awood leh oo qaata go’aannada qaranka. Xasan ayaa tilmaamay in weli ay jiraan siyaasiyiin uu sheegay inay ku faanayaan inay yihiin hoggaamiye-kooxeedyo, taas oo uu tilmaamay inay jahawareer ku keeni karto hannaanka siyaasadeed ee dalka iyo cidda leh awoodda sharciyeed ee go’aannada qaranka. “Dadka Soomaaliyeed waxaan leeyahay kaca oo baraaruga, kaca oo baraaruga. Nidaam sameysta. Siyaasaddu waa waxa aad haysataan. Dhaqaaluhu wuu socdaa, dadku way ganacsanayaan, tacliintuna way sii horumareysaa, laakiin meeshii ay gaari lahayd weli ma gaarin,” ayuu Madaxweyne Xasan ka sheegay munaasabad ka qabsoomtay magaalada Muqdisho. Sidoo kale wuxuu carrabka ku adkeeyay in siyaasadda iyo arrimaha kale ee dalka aysan ku socon karin go’aanno shaqsiyeed, balse loo baahan yahay hannaan iyo hay’ado awood u leh inay si cad u qaataan mas’uuliyadda go’aannada dalka. “Haddii aynaan toosin siyaasadda dalka, haddii aynaan aqoon cidda dalka masuulka ka ah, qof ma aha, hay’adda masuulka ka ah ee go’aanka u gaaraysa ummadda iyo sida ay ugu gaarayso, horumar ma gaari karno,” ayuu yiri. Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in amnigu yahay saldhigga lagu dhisi karo waxbarashada, dhaqaalaha iyo horumarka bulshada. “Amnigu waa geed-qaadkii beerta lagu diyaarinayay. Kadib ayaan beeraynaa waxbarasho, dhaqaale, sharaf iyo karaamo,” ayuu yiri madaxweynaha. Ugu dambeyntiina, Madaxweynaha ayaa sheegay in awoodda ugu weyn ee ummaddu aysan ku jirin oo keliya kheyraadka dabiiciga ah, dhismayaasha dhaadheer ama hubka, balse ay ku jirto aqoonta iyo tayada dadkeeda, isagoo tusaale u soo qaatay Japan oo uu sheegay inay horumarkeeda ku dhistay dadka iyo aqoonta. The post Xasan oo weeraray mucaaradka, kuna tilmaamay hoggaamiye kooxeed appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Ethiopia Reportedly Asks AU to Accelerate Withdrawal of Its Troops from Somalia
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — In a potentially significant shift in Somalia’s security landscape, Ethiopia has reportedly asked the African Union to accelerate the withdrawal and redeployment of some of its troops serving under the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), prompting the AU to reconsider its previously agreed force-redeployment timetable. The reported request has caught observers by surprise because Ethiopia was not initially expected to significantly reduce its military footprint in Somalia at this stage of the AUSSOM transition. Under the earlier planning framework, greater attention had been placed on reducing Ugandan forces and completing the withdrawal of the remaining Burundian contingent, while Ethiopian forces were expected to maintain a substantial presence in several strategically important areas. That calculation now appears to be changing. According to information emerging from diplomatic and security circles, Addis Ababa’s request is linked to mounting security pressures inside Ethiopia, forcing the government to reassess how many troops it can continue to deploy abroad and where those forces are most urgently required. The first visible indication of the reported shift came on 8 August, when Ethiopian forces formally handed responsibility for one of their military positions in Buurhakaba to Somali security forces. The handover is being viewed as part of a broader restructuring of Ethiopia’s military deployment in Somalia, with additional positions reportedly under consideration for transfer to Somali forces. There are also indications that the number of Ethiopian troops stationed in Baidoa, one of the most strategically important cities in Southwest State, could be reduced. That development is particularly significant given the continuing security threat posed by Al-Shabaab in Bay and surrounding areas. Why Ethiopia Wants Its Troops Back Ethiopia has maintained a substantial military presence in Somalia for years, particularly in areas close to its border and in regions where Somali and international forces have been conducting operations against Al-Shabaab. But Addis Ababa is now confronting its own complicated security environment. Internal security pressures, military commitments and regional tensions are placing new demands on Ethiopia’s armed forces. If those pressures continue to intensify, maintaining a large overseas deployment in Somalia could become increasingly difficult. The reported request therefore appears to reflect a broader reassessment of Ethiopia’s military priorities rather than simply a routine adjustment to the AUSSOM rotation schedule. The timing could hardly be more sensitive. AUSSOM is already undergoing a complicated transition aimed at gradually transferring greater responsibility for national security to Somali forces. Any accelerated reduction by one of the mission’s major troop-contributing countries could disrupt that carefully calibrated process. Ethiopian forces constitute one of the most significant military components supporting Somalia’s security architecture. Their departure from strategically important bases would therefore raise immediate questions about who will take over those positions and whether Somali forces are adequately prepared to assume full responsibility. The concern is particularly acute around Baidoa and the wider Southwest State, where Al-Shabaab continues to maintain operational capabilities and exploit gaps in state security. Could Al-Shabaab Exploit the Vacuum? For Somalia, the greatest danger is not simply the departure of Ethiopian soldiers. It is what happens after they leave. If Ethiopian forces withdraw from strategically important locations faster than Somali forces can replace them, Al-Shabaab could attempt to exploit the resulting security gaps. The Somali government may consequently be forced to accelerate the deployment of national forces to positions vacated by Ethiopian troops. Other AUSSOM contingents could also face pressure to increase their presence in vulnerable areas if the AU wants to prevent a sudden deterioration in security. That would, however, place additional pressure on an already financially and logistically constrained mission. A Significant Test for Somalia’s Security Transition The reported Ethiopian request comes at a particularly delicate moment for Somalia. The Federal Government is under increasing pressure to demonstrate that its security forces can progressively assume responsibility for the country’s security as international forces reduce their presence. For years, Ethiopia’s military has provided a crucial layer of security in parts of Somalia that Somali forces have struggled to secure independently. A substantial and accelerated Ethiopian redeployment would therefore represent one of the most consequential tests yet of Somalia’s security transition. The immediate questions are now becoming increasingly urgent: How many Ethiopian troops will actually leave? Which bases will be transferred? When will Somali forces take over? And will other AUSSOM contingents compensate for the reduction? For now, neither the African Union nor the Somali Federal Government has publicly confirmed the full scale of the reported Ethiopian request. If the reports are confirmed, however, Ethiopia’s decision could mark a major change in the architecture of AUSSOM—one that comes at precisely the moment Somalia can least afford an unexpected security gap. The real test will not be Ethiopia’s decision to reduce its deployment. It will be whether Somalia is ready to fill the space Ethiopia leaves behind. items.title: Sacdiya Bajaaj Released After Appeals Court Overturns Prison Term
items.description: MOGADISHU — The Banadir Regional Court of Appeal has overturned a three-year prison sentence imposed on Sacdiya Macallin Ali, widely known as Sacdiya Bajaaj, leading to her release from custody on Wednesday. Sacdiya was sentenced to three years in prison in late June following an earlier court ruling. Her legal team subsequently appealed the decision, requesting that the appellate court review and overturn the sentence. The Banadir Regional Court of Appeal recently heard submissions from Sacdiya’s lawyers, who presented the grounds for their appeal and challenged the earlier judgment. Following its review of the case, the court announced on Wednesday that it had annulled the previous ruling, effectively restoring Sacdiya’s freedom. Hours before the decision was announced, members of Sacdiya’s family had appealed to the Banadir Regional Court of Appeal to overturn the earlier sentence and order her release. The ruling marks a significant development in the case, bringing an end to the three-year sentence previously imposed on Sacdiya Bajaaj. items.title: Maxay mucaaradka DF ka yiraahdeen sii-deynta Sacdiyo Bajaaj?
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Hoggaamiyeyaasha mucaaradka ayaa si diirran u soo dhaweeyay sii-deynta Sacdiyo Macallin Cali (Sacdiyo Bajaaj) oo maanta dib u heshay xoriyadeeda. Madaxweynihii hore ee dalka, Shariif Sheekh Axmed ayaa sheegay in adkeysiga Sacdiyo uu shidaal cusub ku sii shubayo dhallinyarada Soomaaliyeed ee u taagan inay si xor ah u muujiyaan, dareenkooda iyo aragtidooda ku aaddan hab-nololeedkooda iyada oo aysan joojin karin awood sheegasho kasta oo lagu lagula kaco. “Waxaan ku faraxsanahay in Sacdiya Macallin Cali ay maanta xorriyadeeda dib u heshay, kadib muddo afar bilood ah oo ay si dulmi ah ugu xirneed nidaamka muddo-xileedkiisu dhammaaday,” ayuu yiri Shariifka. Waxa uu intaas kusii daray: “Waxaan sidoo kale oo u mahadcelinayaa dhallinyarada caasimadda, warbaahinta iyo cid kasta oo garab-istaag u muujisay Sacdiyo Macallin islamarkaana ka dhiidhisay ku takri-falka iyo cabburinta Madaxweynihii hore Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu ku hayo shacabka gaar ahaan dhallinyarada.” Shariif ayaa sidoo kale waxa uu ku dhiirrigaliyay dhallinyarada Soomaaliyeed meel walba oo ay joogaan inay muujiyaan isku duubni, adkeysi iyo midnimo. Dhanka kale, Cabdiraxmaan Cabdishakuur Warsame oo kamid ah siyaasiyiinta mucaaradka ayaa isna soo dhaweeyay sii-deynta Sacdiyo, isagoo eedeymo u jeediyay hoggaanka tallada haya ee Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud. “Adkaysiga Sacdiyo, iyo ku dhaca Garsoore Cabdifitaax waxay abuurayaan rajo iyo yididiilo. Waxay ina tusayaan in Soomaaliya ay weli leedahay dhalinyaro wanaagsan, mabda’ leh oo geesiyaal ah, kuwaas oo aan damiirkooda iyo mabaadi’dooda ku iibsan xil, xoolo ama dano gaar ah,” ayuu yiri Cabdiraxmaan Cabdishakuur. Waxa uu intaas kusii daray: “Waxaa jira kuwa la mid ah Garsoore Cabdifitaax oo ku jira garsoorka, shaqaalaha rayidka ah, diblomaasiyadda iyo ciidamada oo aaminsan in sharciga, caddaaladda iyo danta qaranku ay ka weyn yihiin qof iyo xukunkiis. Taasi waa dhiirrigelin, waa rajo, waana yididiilo.” Go’aanka Guddoomiyaha Maxkamadda Racfaanka Gobolka Banaadir ayuu sheegay inuu cashar weyn ugu jiro “kuwa sharaftooda iyo damiirkooda u loogay raalli-gelinta taliska Xasan Sheekh si ay xil, xoolo iyo awood u helaan,” sida uu hadalka u dhigay. items.title: After 122 Days Behind Bars, “Sacdiya Bajaaj” Walks Free
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — After spending 122 days in detention, nearly four months behind bars , Somali social media personality Sacdiya Macallin Ali, widely known as “Sacdiya Bajaaj,” has regained her freedom after the Banadir Regional Court of Appeal overturned a three-year prison sentence imposed against her by a lower court. The Appeals Court ruled that the earlier sentence was not consistent with the law, effectively bringing Sacdiya’s prolonged detention to an end. Her release comes after months of mounting public concern over her case, which became a powerful flashpoint in Somalia’s increasingly contentious debate over freedom of expression, political accountability, and the limits of government power. Sacdiya’s detention drew particular attention because of her outspoken presence on social media. Opposition politicians, civil society groups, and supporters repeatedly demanded her release, arguing that her imprisonment was unjust and that citizens should not face criminal prosecution simply for expressing criticism of government policies or alleged wrongdoing. The case has therefore become larger than one individual. It has raised uncomfortable questions about the shrinking space for public criticism in Somalia at a time when President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s government faces growing accusations from opponents over corruption, political repression, and the use of state institutions against critics. Among the most explosive issues in Mogadishu is the continuing controversy surrounding public land. Opposition figures and activists have alleged that valuable public land in the capital has been transferred or sold to politically connected businessmen and powerful investors, with critics describing the process as one of the country’s most serious forms of institutionalized corruption. Some allegations have gone even further, claiming that cemeteries and burial grounds have been cleared or otherwise encroached upon for commercial development. Those allegations can’t be contested but should be independently verified. But their very presence in public discourse illustrates the growing anger surrounding land ownership and the management of public property in Mogadishu. For critics of the government, Sacdiya’s case has become symbolic of a broader concern: that citizens who publicly challenge powerful interests risk intimidation, detention, or prosecution. The government’s supporters, however, argue that individuals must remain accountable under the law and that criticism does not place anyone above legal proceedings. That argument now faces an important test. By overturning the three-year sentence, the Appeals Court has not merely released Sacdiya; it has also raised questions about the legal basis of the original conviction and the circumstances under which she was detained for more than four months. Sacdiya, a mother, became one of the most widely discussed detainees in Somalia during her imprisonment. Opposition leaders held press conferences and public demonstrations calling for her release, while supporters urged the judiciary to reconsider the original verdict. The court has now done so. Her release represents a significant moment for a country struggling to balance state authority with freedom of expression and political accountability. Yet the broader questions remain unresolved. Can Somalis openly discuss allegations of corruption without fear of detention? Can journalists, activists, and ordinary citizens investigate the controversial disposal of public land? And can Somalia’s institutions protect citizens who challenge powerful political and economic interests? Those questions matter far beyond Sacdiya Bajaaj. For many Somalis, the significance of today’s ruling lies not simply in the fact that one woman has walked out of prison after 122 days. It lies in whether the case becomes a reminder that government power must remain subject to the law—and that criticism, however uncomfortable, is not itself a crime. items.title: Ugandan Commander Sounds Alarm at Carbiska Base, Warns Troops to Stay Ready for Al-Shabaab Attacks
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — A senior Ugandan commander serving with the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) has issued a stark warning to troops stationed at the Carbiska operational base, ordering them to maintain heightened vigilance and remain prepared for possible attacks by Al-Shabaab. Colonel Saul Nabimanya, commander of Uganda’s 46th Battalion under AUSSOM’s First Sector, delivered the warning during an address to soldiers at the Carbiska base, praising their commitment while emphasizing the continuing security risks facing African Union and Somali forces operating around the capital. Nabimanya commended the troops for their discipline and dedication to their mission, but urged them not to become complacent. He instructed soldiers to maintain high levels of professionalism, discipline and operational readiness, stressing that they must be capable of responding rapidly to any emerging security threat while carrying out their duties in Somalia. Al-Shabaab Threat Remains The commander’s warning comes amid continuing concerns over Al-Shabaab activity in areas surrounding Mogadishu and along major roads linking the capital with surrounding communities. Although Somali and AUSSOM forces have intensified joint security operations in recent months, Al-Shabaab continues to retain the ability to conduct ambushes, hit-and-run attacks and other forms of asymmetric warfare against government and international forces. Carbiska is considered a strategically important location within the wider security architecture around Mogadishu. The base supports operations aimed at strengthening security and assisting Somali forces as they gradually assume greater responsibility for protecting the country. For the troops stationed there, the message from their commander was therefore direct: the transition toward greater Somali security responsibility does not mean the threat has disappeared. In an unusual addition to his security-focused message, Colonel Nabimanya also urged his troops to think beyond their immediate military responsibilities. He reminded the soldiers that their deployment in Somalia is temporary and encouraged them to consider the lives and responsibilities that await them when they eventually leave the mission and return home. The commander urged the troops to manage their finances responsibly and make sound decisions that would improve their long-term welfare. His message was effectively twofold: remain alert on the battlefield, but also prepare for life after the battlefield. Nabimanya emphasized that responsible financial management, professional discipline and forward planning should be treated as part of a soldier’s broader responsibility to himself, his family and his future. Uganda’s Continuing Role in Somalia Uganda remains one of the principal troop-contributing countries to the African Union’s Somalia mission and has maintained a major military presence in Somalia for many years. Ugandan forces have operated in several strategically important areas, supporting Somali security forces in counterinsurgency operations and helping protect key population centers and transportation corridors. AUSSOM’s broader mandate includes supporting Somalia’s fight against Al-Shabaab, strengthening national security institutions and helping create the conditions for a gradual transfer of security responsibilities from African Union forces to Somali authorities. That transition, however, remains a delicate undertaking. Somali forces are increasingly expected to take the lead, while AUSSOM contingents continue to provide operational support, training, coordination and security assistance. Colonel Nabimanya’s latest message highlights the difficult reality facing troops at Carbiska and elsewhere in Somalia. The international security presence may eventually decline, but Al-Shabaab’s ability to exploit vulnerabilities has not disappeared. For now, the Ugandan contingent at Carbiska remains on alert, operating alongside Somali forces in an environment where a quiet day can quickly become a security emergency. The commander’s message was therefore more than a routine briefing. It was a reminder that as Somalia moves toward greater national ownership of its security, the forces supporting that transition must remain prepared for the possibility that Al-Shabaab will test them at every opportunity. items.title: Janan Joins Jubaland Forces as Federal & Regional Rivalry Deepens in Gedo
items.description: Kismayo (WDN) — A major shift in the political and security balance of Somalia’s Gedo region is taking shape after former Federal Government security chief Abdirashid Janan in Gedo region, reportedly joined the Jubaland administration following days of talks with Jubaland President Ahmed Mohamed Islam (Ahmed Madobe). Janan, who previously commanded Federal Government forces in Gedo, is reported to have aligned himself and his troops with Jubaland, potentially delivering a significant blow to Mogadishu’s efforts to consolidate federal control over the strategically important region. According to reports, Janan assembled Federal Government forces under his command at the UK military camp outside Beledxaawo and informed them that his long-running dispute with Jubaland had now ended. The reported realignment could fundamentally alter the balance of power in Gedo, where Mogadishu and Kismaayo have spent years competing over political authority, security forces and control of key border areas. A New Blow to Mogadishu’s Strategy Sources told WardheerNews that Jubaland has agreed to assume responsibility for the salaries of the troops, who have reportedly gone for an extended period without receiving regular pay from the Federal Government. Janan is also reported to have told his forces that Mogadishu had failed to demonstrate genuine commitment to Jubaland’s interests, accusing some federal officials of approaching the country’s political disputes through narrow personal and clan-based calculations. The allegations have not been independently verified, but they reflect the increasingly bitter political confrontation between the Federal Government and Jubaland. The reported defection is particularly significant because it comes amid a broader struggle by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s administration to reshape the political landscape of Somalia’s Federal Member States. Critics of the President accuse Villa Somalia of pursuing a strategy aimed at bringing regional administrations under tighter federal political control—an approach they argue has already produced severe instability in South West State, Galmudug and Hirshabelle. From this perspective, the confrontation with Jubaland and Puntland is not simply a disagreement over administrative authority. It is part of a much larger battle over whether Somalia’s federal system will remain genuinely decentralized or gradually become dominated by the political preferences of the Federal Government. From Political Dispute to Security Confrontation The danger is that political competition is increasingly being conducted through security forces. Rather than resolving disagreements through negotiated federal arrangements, rival administrations have repeatedly sought to build competing military and political structures. Gedo is perhaps the clearest example. Beledxaawo occupies a strategically important position near the Somalia–Kenya border, making control of the area significant not only politically but also for trade, security and cross-border movement. Janan’s reported decision to align with Jubaland could therefore give Kismaayo greater leverage in the region while complicating Mogadishu’s ability to deploy and maintain federal forces there. It could also force the Federal Government to reconsider its wider security strategy in Gedo at a time when Somalia is already struggling with the threat posed by Al-Shabaab and the gradual transition from African Union forces to Somali national security institutions. The episode raises a question that extends far beyond Janan or Gedo: What happens when political disagreements between Mogadishu and federal member states become disputes over armed forces? Supporters of President Hassan Sheikh argue that the Federal Government has a constitutional responsibility to strengthen national institutions and prevent regional administrations from maintaining autonomous security structures outside a unified national framework. Opponents counter that Mogadishu’s approach risks destroying the very federal balance it claims to be protecting. They point to the experiences of South West State, Galmudug and Hirshabelle, arguing that federal political intervention has increasingly produced regional administrations closely aligned with Villa Somalia. Their concern is that Puntland and Jubaland could eventually face similar pressure. Jubaland, however, has demonstrated that it is prepared to resist. Puntland has likewise maintained a firm political distance from Mogadishu, creating an increasingly polarized federal landscape in which cooperation between the center and the regions is becoming more difficult. Janan’s reported realignment is therefore more than the movement of one commander and his troops. It is a reminder that Somalia’s political struggle is increasingly being fought through the institutions and security forces that are supposed to protect the federal system. For now, the immediate consequences will be felt in Gedo. But the political message is much broader: attempts to impose political uniformity on a federal system can produce resistance—and when that resistance acquires an armed dimension, the consequences can extend far beyond the original dispute. items.title: Sidee loo Maareeyaa Marka ay iska Hor Yimaaddaan Jinsiga Jidheed iyo Jinsiga Afeed?
items.description: Waxa jirta dood ka dhalatay qoraal aan bartayda Faysbuug ku baahiyay. Iyada oo ay sidaas tahay ayaa haddana waxa jira mawduucyo aan aqoon ahaan weli meel la saarin sida “sababta ay afafka qaar jinsi u leeyihiin”. Marka ilme inoo dhasho waxaynu u bixinnaa magac. Waxaynu ilmaha magaca ugu bixinnaa in lagu garto. Eeg markanna labo wax baynu ka hadalnay. Waa ilmaha iyo waxa lagu garanayo. Sidaas baa marka aynu afka ka hadlayno labadaas fahan oo iska turjumayaa isu saaran yihiin. Waa shey oo aynu lafdiga waxa laga hadlayo ka wadno iyo sumad oo aynu magaca lagu aqoonsanayo ka wadno. Waa uun shey iyo taarikadiis. Haddaba, labadan fahan ee aynu ka soo hadalnay mid walbi jinsi buu leeyahay. Waxana aynu u kala qaadan karnaa jinsi jidheed iyo jinsi afeed. Jinsiga jidheed waa jinsiga sheyga lafdigiisa ka muuqda. Marka aynu aragno “lax” iyo “wan” isbarbar taagan, waynu kala garannaa tan “lax” ah iyo kan “wan” ah. Waxaynu ku kala garannaa qayb ka mid ah xubnaha jidhkooda. Kaasi waa jinsi jidheed, waxana yeesha noolaha. Waxa isna jira jinsi afeed. Marka aynu jinsi maqalno, waa ay iska caddahay in aynu wax nool ka hadlayno, waxase layaab ah in marka afka la joogo ereyadu jinsi yeeshaan. Layaabku waxa weeye in ereyga “waddo” uu dheddig yahay, ereyga “dhagax” uu isna lab yahay. Lama garan karo sida labadaas erey ama xataa labada wax ee ay ku magcaaban yihiin ay jinsi u yeelan karaan! Afku muxuu jinsi u leeyahay waa mawduuc aan war badan laga hayn, waxase la filayaa in dadku iyagu afka lahaayeen, sidaas darteedna ay jinsiga ugu sameeyeen sida ay iyaba lab iyo dheddig u yihiin. Waa innaga niraahna “Saca caanihiisa”. Ma niraahno “Saca caanaheeda”, sidaas darteed, “sacu” jidh ahaan waa neef dheddig ah, magac ahaanna wuxuu leeyahay magac lab ah. Waxan filayaa in noolaha aynu “sac” u naqaanno uu ina kaga filan yahay in aan kala fahanno jinsi jidheed iyo jinsi afeed. Maaddaama ay labada jinsi wada shaqeeyaan oo isku dul dhisan yihiin, waxa dhaca: B. Mar labada jinsi iswaafaqaan. T. Mar labada jinsi aanu mid caddayn. J. Mar labada jinsi iska hor yimaaddaan. X. Mar jinsiga afeed iska hor yimaaddo. B. Marka labada jinsi iswaafaqaan: Mar jinsiga jidheed iyo jinsiga afeed ayaa iswaafaqa, waana marka jinsi jidh ahaan lab ama dheddig ah loo bixiyo magac lab ah ama dheddig ah, sida ay u kala horreeyaan. Noolaha aynu “hal” u naqaanno jidh ahaan waa dheddig, magac ahaanna waa dheddig. Waa innaga niraahna “Hasha caanaheeda”. Sida oo kale, noolaha aynu “nin” u naqaanno jidh ahaan waa lab, magac ahaanna waa lab. Labadan marba waa ay iswaafeqeen jinsiga jidheed iyo jinsiga afeed. T. Marka aanu jinsiga afeed caddayn : Waxa dhacda in mararka qaar aanu caddayn mid jinsiyada ka mid ahi. Sida aynu soo sheegnay jinsiga jidheed waxa uun yeelan kara waxyaabaha noolaha ah, balse dhinaca kale afku wuxuu jinsi u sameeyaa wax aan noolaba ahayn. Sidaas darteed, waxa dhacda mar uu kaba gaabsado afku jinsiga sheyga. Afku sidee jinsiga u sheegaa? Afku saddex qaab buu jinsiga sheyga u sheegaa, waana; mar uu dheddig ku sheego, mar uu lab ku sheego iyo mar aanu midna ku sheegin. Meesha la galo ee “guri” afku wuxuu u yaqaannaa wax lab, xubinta jidhka ee “kelli” iyana wuxuu u yaqaannaa wax dheddig. Mar kale afku wuxuu jinsiga ku caddeeyaa xarfaha ereyga u danbeeya. Ereyada kelida ah ee shaqalka “O” ku dhammaada afku wuxuu u yaqaannaa kuwo dheddig. Waa magacyada ay ka midka yihiin (Dhalo, waddo, Canbaro, Geelo IWM). Dhinaca kale, ereyada ku dhammaada shaqalka “E” iyana afku wuxuu u yaqaannaa kuwo lab. Waa kuwa ay ka midka yihiin (cambe, qare, Barre, Geelle IWM). Labadan waxa soo raaca magacyada “ey” ku dhammaada sida “Caddey, Badey IWM) oo dheddig ah iyo kuwa ku dhammaada “ow” sida (Calasow, Fiidow IWM). Haddaba, wixii magacyada sare ka soo hadha afku wuxuu u aqoonsan yahay in ay lab iyo dheddigba noqon karaan oo hadba sidii la doono loogu dhawaaqi karo. Waxa iyana jirta in marka magacyada gaarka ah la joogo aanu dhawaaqu kala saari karin magacyadan. Tusaale ahaan, magaca “Shugri” marka uu nin yahay iyo marka uu naag yahay ma kala cadda codkiisu in uu lab yahay iyo in uu dheddig yahay. -Shugri baa yimi. -Shugri baa timi. Magaca “Shugri” ragga iyo dumarkaba waa loo bixiyaa. Marka aynu magacan afka ku eegno rag iyo dumarba wuu u yaqaannaa oo ma kala saari karo kan loo jeedo. Haddaba, si labada loo kala saaro waxa loo noqdaa lafdiga sheyga ama jinsiga jidheed. Halkaas ayaa lagu soo go’aamiyaa magacani fal lab ah iyo fal dheddig ah kan uu qaadanayo. J. Sida aynu soo sheegnay noolaha “sac” jidh ahaan waa dheddig, balse afku jinsi labeed buu u yeelay. Marka sidan oo kale labada jinsi iska hor yimaaddaan, lafdiguna aanu dad ahayn waxa la qaataa jinsiga afeed. Waxa kale oo dhacda in qof lab ah loo bixiyo magac dheddig. Tusaale ahaan, magacyada “Siilaanyo iyo Caddo” waxa lahaa labo madaxweyne oo mid Soomaalilaan soo hoggaamiyay midna Budlaan, sida ay u kala horreeyaan. Markan waxa la qaadanayaa lafdiga sheyga ama jinsiga jidheed, waxana la kala siinayaa falal lab ah. Waxa la oranayaa: -Siilaanyo wuxuu ahaa… -Caddo wuxuu ahaa… Caddo iyo Siilaanyo keliya maahee magacyada noocan ahi waa kuwo baahsan. Waxa ka mid ah (Subxaanyo, Dureemo, Dhalo…). Waa run oo marba mid baynu qaadannay. Innagu ma qaadan ee dadka oo dhan baa sidaas sameeya, sababtuna waxay noqon kartaa in marka “dadka” laga hadlayo aanay afka marti ka ahayn oo ay yihiin kuwii afkaba lahaa. Sidaas darteed, waxyaabaha kale in labkooda la caddeeyo ama aan la caddayn dadka uma laha muhiimad weyn oo u dhiganta marka arrinku iyaga joogo. X. Tusaale ahaan, mar anigaygan qoraalka qorayaa waxan ahay “nin”, mar kalana “Maxamed”. Mid waa magac guud, midna gaar baan u leeyahay. Waxa dhacda mar labadani iska hor yimaaddaan. Sidan si la mid ah waxa dhacda in meel loo yaqaanno “magaalo ama degmo” oo dheddig ah, haddana magac af ahaan lab ah la siiyo. Halkan waxa iska hor yimi labadii qodob ee afku jinsigiisa xarfo ahaan ugu caddayn jirey. Sida aynu hore u soo sheegnay waa yeedhaha “O iyo E” oo dheddig iyo lab u kala taagnaa, sida ay u kala horreeyaan. Meeshu waa magaalo ama waa degmo oo shaqalka “O” buu magac walba ku dhammaadaa, haddana dhinaca kale, waxa la siiyay magacyo lab ah oo shaqalka “E” u danbeeyo. Markan maxaa la falayaa? Ma waxaynu oranaynaa: Jamaame ayaa badisay mise badiyay? Buulaburde ayaa qaadday mise qaaday? Sida muuqata markan waxaynu qaadanaynaa magaca lafdiga xiga ee guud ee “magaalo ama degmo”. Sideedaba, meeshani awel waxay ahayd dheddig oo waxay haysataa magac dheddig, magaca cusub ee soo kordhayna waxba ka beddeli maayo jinsigeedii maaddaama aanay awelba jinsi jidheed lahayn. Sidaas darteed, waxaynu oranaynaa: -Jamaame ayaa badisay. -Buulaburde ayaa qaadday. Gabagabadii, marka ay iswaafaqaan jinsiga jidheed iyo midka afeed wax mushkilad ahi ma jirto, marka aan mid caddaynna waxa la qaadanayaa kan muuqda, halka marka ay si toos ah labadu isaga hor yimaaddaan ama mid gudihiis iska hor yimaaddana ay xalalku kala duwan yihiin una muuqan karaan iska-hor-imaad. Marka dadku meesha ku jiro isaga ayaa cad oo la qaadanayaa, balse marka shey kale la caddaynayo wuu isbeddeli karaa. Markan danbe waxan tixgeliyay fegradda guud ee afka oo dadku bilow ilaa dhamaad isagu samaystay. Haddii aad u fiirsatid “carruurta dhurwaagu ama iduhu magacyo gaar ah inoo ma kala laha” sababtuna waa in aanu iyaga afku aad u khusayn in la eg inta uu dadka khuseeyo. Tixraacyo Mansuur, Barashada Naxwaha Af Soomaaliga. Keenaddiid, Qaamuuska Af Soomaaliga. Dirir, Habqoraalka Farsoomaaliga. Meeshu waa magaalo ama waa degmo oo shaqalka “O” buu magac walba ku dhammaadaa, haddana dhinaca kale, waxa la siiyay magacyo lab ah oo shaqalka “E” u danbeeyo. Markan maxaa la falayaa? Ma waxaynu oranaynaa: Jamaame ayaa badisay mise badiyay? Buulaburde ayaa qaadday mise qaaday? Sida muuqata markan waxaynu qaadanaynaa magaca lafdiga xiga ee guud ee “magaalo ama degmo”. Sideedaba, meeshani awel waxay ahayd dheddig oo waxay haysataa magac dheddig, magaca cusub ee soo kordhayna waxba ka beddeli maayo jinsigeedii maaddaama aanay awelba jinsi jidheed lahayn. Sidaas darteed, waxaynu oranaynaa: -Jamaame ayaa badisay. -Buulaburde ayaa qaadday. Gabagabadii, marka ay iswaafaqaan jinsiga jidheed iyo midka afeed wax mushkilad ahi ma jirto, marka aan mid caddaynna waxa la qaadanayaa kan muuqda, halka marka ay si toos ah labadu isaga hor yimaaddaan ama mid gudihiis iska hor yimaaddana ay xalalku kala duwan yihiin una muuqan karaan iska-hor-imaad. Marka dadku meesha ku jiro isaga ayaa cad oo la qaadanayaa, balse marka shey kale la caddaynayo wuu isbeddeli karaa. Markan danbe waxan tixgeliyay fegradda guud ee afka oo dadku bilow ilaa dhamaad isagu samaystay. Haddii aad u fiirsatid “carruurta dhurwaagu ama iduhu magacyo gaar ah inoo ma kala laha” sababtuna waa in aanu iyaga afku aad u khusayn in la eg inta uu dadka khuseeyo. Tixraacyo Mansuur, Barashada Naxwaha Af Soomaaliga. Keenaddiid, Qaamuuska Af Soomaaliga. Dirir, Habqoraalka Farsoomaaliga. items.title: Soomaaliya oo si adag uga hortimid dal aqoonsaday madax-bannaanida Israa’iil ee…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa si adag u cambaareysay go’aanka ay Dowladda Kolombiya ku aqoonsatay sheegashada Israa’iil ee ku aaddan madax-bannaanida Buuraleyda Golan. Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in aqoonsi kasta oo noocaas ah uu yahay mid aan waxba ka jirin, isla markaana uu ka hor imanayo sharciga caalamiga ah iyo Axdiga Qaramada Midoobay. Dowladda Soomaaliya waxay adkaysay in Buuraleyda Golan uu yahay dhul Suuriyaan ah oo ay Israa’iil haysato, iyadoo diidday tallaabo kasta oo lagu aqoonsanayo sheegashada Israa’iil ee dhulkaasi. Soomaaliya waxay sidoo kale ku baaqday in khilaafka u dhexeeya Israa’iil iyo Suuriya lagu xalliyo wada-hadal iyo hab nabadeed, iyadoo la dhowrayo mabaadi’da sharciga caalamiga ah. Dowladdu waxay xustay muhiimadda ay leeyihiin qaraarrada Qaramada Midoobay ee khuseeya Buuraleyda Golan, kuwaas oo xaqiijinaya xaqa Suuriya u leedahay dhulkeeda. Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in dhulka Suuriya lagu haysto ay tahay in si buuxda loogu soo celiyo dalkaasi, iyadoo lagu salaynayo xuduudihii jiray ka hor dagaalkii 1967. Dowladda Federaalka ayaa ugu dambeyn ugu baaqday dhammaan dowladaha, oo ay ku jirto Kolombiya, inay dhowraan sharciga caalamiga ah, ixtiraamaan madaxbannaanida iyo midnimada dhuleed ee dowladaha, ayna ka fogaadaan aqoonsiga dhulalka la haysto. items.title: Thousands flee yearslong drought in Somalia as hunger deepens and aid shrinks
items.description: After nearly two weeks on the road with her five children, Luul Mohamed finally arrived in the southwestern Somali city of Baidoa with no food and little sense of what would happen next. Drought conditions had forced Mohamed and her family to leave Saakoow, a town in the Middle Jubba region more than 300 kilometers (186 miles) away. They moved from village to village before arriving in Baidoa, now a major hub for people fleeing drought, insecurity and food shortages, on Aug. 3. “We are very hungry and in a desperate situation,” Mohamed said. “We have nothing to eat and can only place our hope in God, as He is the one who sustains us through this ordeal that culminated in our trip.” The family’s journey is one example of a deepening humanitarian emergency in Somalia, where years of drought, conflict and economic pressures are pushing more families from rural communities into displacement camps as hunger rises and humanitarian funding shrinks. About 2 million people are facing emergency levels of food insecurity, more than double the number recorded last year, according to Plan International, which has provided assistance to more than 200,000 people in Somalia this year. The humanitarian group and Somalia’s Disaster Management Agency are calling for increased international assistance, with concern that the crisis could be compounded by another climate shock later this year. The U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization has projected a greater than 90% probability of El Nino conditions developing from mid-2026 and intensifying during Somalia’s October-to-December rainy season, bringing the severe risk of flooding. Somalia is highly vulnerable to extreme weather and has experienced repeated cycles of prolonged drought followed by destructive flooding. The shocks have eroded livelihoods, displaced communities, contributed to disease outbreaks and worsened food insecurity. In Baidoa, hundreds of thousands of people fleeing prolonged drought have gathered in sprawling displacement settlements on the outskirts of the city. One of them, Habiba Adan, fled her settlement in Awdiinle in the Bay region after four consecutive years of drought destroyed crops and killed livestock. She eventually moved to Baidoa with her two older daughters and now lives in a displacement camp. Adan would like to return home, but she said continuing drought and failed harvests there have left families with little prospect of rebuilding their lives. “The drought we are experiencing has stretched for four consecutive years, and this year, most crops have again been decimated,” Adan said. “Farmers were only able to harvest enough to sow their fields for the next season, leaving our future bleak. Here in these camps, we lack food and essential support. We have no food, water, or money, and we sit idly.” According to Plan International, the city is hosting about 1.6 million people, nearly half of them displaced. It says one in five families lacks reliable access to water, among the most immediate challenges facing displaced families. They are increasingly forced to buy trucked water at steep prices that many simply cannot afford. Families have nothing left after years of drought Reena Ghelani, the global CEO of Plan International, visited Baidoa last week, meeting drought-displaced families and visiting a malnutrition ward in the Bay region. Ghelani said many of the families she met had tried to remain in their communities through successive years of drought, leaving only when their resources were exhausted. Many fled “after waiting and waiting year after year of drought and just surviving,” Ghelani said. “And now they say there’s nothing left. They have no water. They have no stocks. The animals have died. There is literally nothing left anymore.” She said rising prices are placing additional pressure on families already struggling to find enough food. Children are suffering from malnutrition Data released in May by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, a global hunger monitoring system, showed that about half of children under 5 in Somalia were facing acute malnutrition. Plan International, citing Save the Children, said the number of children receiving treatment for the most dangerous form of malnutrition in Baidoa had nearly tripled over six months. Dr. Omar Abdikarin, a nutritionist in Baidoa, said patients are arriving for treatment from the Bay as well as the neighboring Bakool and Gedo regions. “Malnutrition is prevalent in this region, and the majority of patients treated at this hospital suffer from malnourishment,” Abdikarin said. The health risks extend beyond malnutrition. Ghelani said she encountered children affected by outbreaks of diphtheria, measles, malaria, cholera and acute diarrhea. The prospect of heavy rainfall later this year presents a new threat to communities facing multiple crises. Intense rainfall and flooding could wash away homes and farmland, contaminate drinking water and force families to move again. Aid agencies warn that the expected El Nino conditions will compound the crisis for countless families before they have had time to recover from prolonged drought conditions. For families arriving in Baidoa such as Mohamed’s, the most urgent question is where to find clean water and food. Mohamed said her husband had left for farms on the outskirts of the city, in search of work or something for their children to eat. A day after arriving in the city, she was still waiting to find out whether her husband would return with good news. AP.
